text: 基于Atlas A3集群的DeepSeek-R1模型decode阶段推理性能优化 概述 本文主要介绍基于Atlas A3 系列产品的DeepSeek-R1模型decode阶段的并行部署和性能优化策略。本文将介绍如何在Atlas A3 系列产品上进行大EP（Expert Parallel）推理，及其他并行技术和优化方案。 性能优化 通用优化 DeepSeek-R1结构中的非MoE部分与Llama类似，通用优化点可参考 Llama 的改动，如固定KV Cache大小、cos/sin优化、AddRMSNorm融合、全量优化LM Head计算量等。 MLA (Multi-Head Latent Attention)低秩压缩优化 使能融合算子 参考 Deepseek论文 中提及的低秩压缩方法，可以减少KV cache占用的内存，提升推理效率。在实现MLA低秩压缩后，可以通过使能融合kernel实现性能优化，相关实现可以参考DeepseekV3Attention类中的 forwardpageattentionmlaprolog 函数。 MLA前置计算性能优化：使能 npumlaprologv3 融合kernel，替换attention计算前的计算，其中包含Q、K、V的线性层计算、旋转位置编码 (ROPE)、RmsNorm计算及KV Cache更新等计算处理； Attention性能优化：使能 npufusedinferattentionscore 融合kernel，实现对MLA计算的加速。 MoE模块实现Expert Parallel (EP)及使能融合算子 在MoE模块中，如采用原始的MoE实现，将通过for循环处理expertnum个FFN专家，效率较低。针对MoE层中的token路由和专家计算等操作，CANN提供了一系列融合算子，提升计算效率。 Router计算优化：使用 torchnpu.npumoegatingtopk 算子，对router计算的结果排序，并选取前top-k个专家； 高性能专家计算：使用 torchnpu.npugroupedmatmul 算子，可以同时处理多个专家的计算，提高计算和搬运效率； 多卡间高性能通信路由：使能 torchnpu.npumoedistributedispatchv2 和 torchnpu.npumoedistributecombinev2 算子，实现EP并行下多卡间的通信。在使用前可参考上述的算子文档，检查HCCLBUFFSIZE等环境变量的配置是否合理，了解该算子的使用场景和约束。 MLP线性层计算合并 原始DeepseekV3MLP实现中，存在gateproj、upproj与downproj三个matmul运算，可通过将gateproj与upproj进行合并计算，得到gateupproj提升整体计算效率。 torchair图模式 Decode场景一般时延要求较高，在pytorch的eagermode下，算子很可能面临比较严重的host下发bound，此时可以通过torch.compile使能图模式进行优化。TorchAir（Torch Ascend Intermediate Representation）是Ascend Extension for PyTorch（torchnpu）的图模式能力扩展库，提供了昇腾设备亲和的torch.compile图模式后端，实现了PyTorch网络在昇腾NPU上的图模式推理加速以及性能优化。 TorchAir提供了max-autotune和reduce-overhead两种实现模式，具体可参考 文档 。本样例在decode场景下对这两种模式都支持，可以通过配置yaml文件中exemode使能，其中gegraph对应max-autotune模式，aclgraph对应reduce-overhead模式。 支持Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) 根据Deepseek论文中介绍的MTP方法，实现了MTP投机推理，在未达到计算bound的场景下，MTP计算可以实现较好的推理加速效果。可通过nextn参数使能MTP。 集合通信使能AIV展开 利用Device的Vector Core计算单元来加速通信操作的执行，可参考 HCCLOPEXPANSIONMODE环境变量 ： shell export HCCLOPEXPANSIONMODE=AIV SuperKernel优化 在decode使能gegraph图模式的场景下，支持对模型的计算图按照用户定义的范围，进行SuperKernel优化。SuperKernel技术的详细介绍，请参考 官方文档 。在本示例中，可通过enablesuperkernel开关使能，支持将所有的decode layers优化在一个SuperKernel scope内，实现对任务调度的等待时间和调度开销的优化，提升整体性能。如希望修改SuperKernel scope的范围，可以在 modelingdeepseek.py 中调整，示例如下： python from executor.utils import superkernelscope switch = enablesuperkernel scope = f"scopename" options = f"scopeoptions" with superkernelscope(switch, scope, options): your modules 其中scope表示当前融合范围的SuperKernel名称，options表示SuperKernel编译的自定义选项。关于scope和options的具体描述和使用范围请参考 SuperKernel文档 。 Benchmark 基于Atlas A3，本实践对DeepSeek-R1 W8A8C8 量化版本进行了性能Benchmark测试。 Quant Mode Global Batch Size Seq Length Chips TPOT (ms) Throughput (tokens/p/s) ------- ----------------- ---------- ----- --------- ----------------------- W8A8C8 6144 4096 64 44.9 2138 注：性能数据基于 MTP1 与 perfect eplb 配置采集，平均 1 个 draft token 中 accept token 为 0.7 个。 -- 附录 环境部署以及样例执行

Decode-Stage Inference Performance Optimization for DeepSeek-R1 on an Atlas A3 Cluster Overview This document describes parallel deployment and performance optimization strategies for the decode stage of DeepSeek-R1 on Atlas A3 series products. It explains how to perform large-scale Expert Parallel (EP) inference on Atlas A3 series products and introduces other parallel techniques and optimization solutions. Performance Optimization General Optimization The non-MoE part of DeepSeek-R1 has a structure similar to Llama. For general optimizations, refer to the changes in Llama , such as fixing the KV Cache size, optimizing cos/sin, fusing AddRMSNorm, and fully optimizing the LM Head computation workload. MLA (Multi-Head Latent Attention) Low-Rank Compression Optimization Enabling Fused Operators The low-rank compression method described in the DeepSeek paper reduces the memory occupied by the KV cache and improves inference efficiency. After MLA low-rank compression is implemented, enable fused kernels to optimize performance. For the related implementation, refer to the forwardpageattentionmlaprolog function in the DeepseekV3Attention class. MLA prolog computation performance optimization: Enable the npumlaprologv3 (Chinese) fused kernel to replace computations before attention. These computations include the Q, K, and V linear layers, rotary position encoding (ROPE), RmsNorm, and KV Cache updates. Attention performance optimization: Enable the npufusedinferattentionscore (Chinese) fused kernel to accelerate MLA computation. Implementing Expert Parallel (EP) and Enabling Fused Operators for the MoE Module If the original MoE implementation is used in the MoE module, a for loop processes expertnum FFN experts, which is inefficient. CANN provides a series of fused operators for token routing, expert computation, and other operations in the MoE layer to improve computation efficiency. Router computation optimization: Use the torchnpu.npumoegatingtopk (Chinese) operator to sort the router computation results and select the top-k experts. High-performance expert computation: Use the torchnpu.npugroupedmatmul (Chinese) operator to process the computations of multiple experts simultaneously, improving computation and data movement efficiency. High-performance communication routing across multiple cards: Enable the torchnpu.npumoedistributedispatchv2 (Chinese) and torchnpu.npumoedistributecombinev2 (Chinese) operators to implement communication across multiple cards under EP. Before using these operators, refer to their documentation to check whether environment variables such as HCCLBUFFSIZE are properly configured and to understand their use cases and constraints. Merging MLP Linear Layer Computations The original DeepseekV3MLP implementation contains three matmul operations: gateproj, upproj, and downproj. Merge the gateproj and upproj computations to obtain gateupproj and improve overall computation efficiency. TorchAir Graph Mode The decode scenario generally has strict latency requirements. In PyTorch eagermode, operators may encounter a severe host delivery bottleneck. Enable graph mode through torch.compile to optimize performance. TorchAir (Torch Ascend Intermediate Representation) extends the graph mode capabilities of Ascend Extension for PyTorch (torchnpu). It provides an Ascend device-friendly torch.compile graph mode backend to accelerate and optimize PyTorch network inference in graph mode on Ascend NPUs. TorchAir provides the max-autotune and reduce-overhead modes. For details, refer to the documentation (Chinese). This sample supports both modes in the decode scenario. Enable a mode by configuring exemode in the YAML file. gegraph corresponds to max-autotune, and aclgraph corresponds to reduce-overhead. Supporting Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) The sample implements MTP speculative inference based on the MTP method described in the DeepSeek paper. When the scenario has not reached the computation bottleneck, MTP computation can provide effective inference acceleration. Set the nextn parameter to enable MTP. Enabling AIV Expansion for Collective Communication Use the Vector Core compute units on the device to accelerate communication operations. For details, refer to the HCCLOPEXPANSIONMODE environment variable (Chinese): shell export HCCLOPEXPANSIONMODE=AIV SuperKernel Optimization When gegraph graph mode is enabled for decode, the sample supports SuperKernel optimization of the model computation graph within a user-defined scope. For details about SuperKernel, refer to the official documentation (Chinese). In this sample, set enablesuperkernel to enable the feature. The sample can optimize all decode layers within one SuperKernel scope, reducing task scheduling wait time and scheduling overhead to improve overall performance. To change the SuperKernel scope, modify modelingdeepseek.py as follows: python from executor.utils import superkernelscope switch = enablesuperkernel scope = f"scopename" options = f"scopeoptions" with superkernelscope(switch, scope, options): your modules Here, scope indicates the SuperKernel name of the current fusion scope, and options indicates the custom SuperKernel compilation options. For details about the descriptions and usage scopes of scope and options, refer to the SuperKernel documentation (Chinese). Benchmark This practice benchmarks the performance of the DeepSeek-R1 W8A8C8 quantized version on Atlas A3. Quant Mode Global Batch Size Seq Length Chips TPOT (ms) Throughput (tokens/p/s) ------- ----------------- ---------- ----- --------- ----------------------- W8A8C8 6144 4096 64 44.9 2138 Note: The performance data is collected with the MTP1 and perfect eplb configurations. On average, 0.7 tokens are accepted from one draft token. -- Appendix Environment Deployment and Sample Execution (Chinese)

基于Atlas A3集群的DeepSeek-R1模型prefill阶段推理性能优化实践 概述 本文主要介绍基于Atlas A3 系列产品的DeepSeek-R1模型prefill阶段并行部署和性能优化策略。主要采用了混合切分策略、Double-Routing、micro-batch等关键优化技术，最终在Atlas A3 系列产品实现perfect eplb下6.5k tokens/卡/s的吞吐性能。 MLA (Multi-Head Latent Attention)部署策略优化 DP (Data Parallelism)切分策略 prefill在MLA部分可以采用纯DP计算策略，每卡部署完整模型权重，不对模型做任何切分，该策略有以下优点： 1. 纯DP切分可以避免多卡冗余KV-Cache (Key-Value Cache)，每卡只需要存储本卡所接收请求的KV-Cache数据量，各卡之间的KV-Cache互不相同，无冗余数据。 2. MLA部分无通信算子，可以避免通信开销，prefill阶段更容易用满算力，在请求数据量较大时更易获得高吞吐。 但是该切分策略会导致以下问题： 1. 计算负载不均：实际场景中，输入请求的序列长度往往参差不齐，处理较短序列的卡会提前完成计算，随后必须等待批次中最长序列的处理完成，导致计算周期被浪费。 2. TTFT (Time to First Token)被延长：若实时请求数量低于卡数，部分卡将处于空闲状态；若为凑齐完整批次而延迟处理，会延长首token生成时间；若直接处理不完整批次，则会导致计算资源利用不充分。 针对上述问题，通过对TP (Tensor Parallelism)切分策略改进，本样例提出SP-TP-SP (Sequence Parallelism, SP)混合切分策略，对以上问题进行优化。 SP-TP-SP混合切分策略 针对输入序列，采用batch和seqlen合轴的方式，转换为token数量，对token进行SP切分，均匀的分发到各个卡上，计算过程如下图所示： 1. 将多个请求序列拼接后并padding到卡数的最小整数倍，进行SP切分，此时每张卡获取的token数相同。 2. FlashAttention（FA）计算部分采用TP策略，通过将Attention head均匀分布到每张计算卡上来实现，确保计算负载在多卡间均衡分布。 3. FlashAttention计算完成之后，通过AlltoAll通信，将TP转换为SP切分，通信算子的通信量更小，性能更优；此时，oproj由于需要全载权重，占用内存会变高。 上述切分策略，每张卡的MLA阶段计算量相等，计算负载均匀。假设有3个输入input0，input1和input2，把batch和seqlen合轴后，将token均匀分布到Rank0Rank3上，downproj包含qaproj和kvaproj计算，qupproj和kvupproj分别表示qbproj和kvbproj计算，此时每张卡计算数据量一致，计算负载均匀。具体计算流程如下图所示： 上述策略有以下优势： 1. TTFT更短：尤其是长序列场景，比如1个128K的请求，此时可以将计算均匀分布到各个卡上完成计算，获得更短时延。 2. MLA部分的计算负载均匀：输入序列只需要padding到卡数的倍数即可，各个卡的计算量相等，几乎无冗余计算。 但是该策略会引入以下问题，需要通过相应的优化手段解决： 1. 每卡需要存储完整的KV-Cache，各卡之间的KV-Cache存在冗余，占用内存高，可通过将KV-Cache数据分卡存储进行规避。 2. 相对于纯DP策略，MLA计算引入AllGather和AlltoAll通信，该通信时间可以进一步通过micro-batch进行优化。 总结：当前在prefill场景中，当请求量较大或KV-Cache内存占用较高时，可以考虑采用DP切分策略，以提升吞吐量；当请求数量较少、分布不均匀或单次请求序列长度较长时，可以考虑采用SP-TP-SP混合切分策略，以降低时延。 MoE (Mixture of Experts)部署策略优化 MoE计算阶段采用EP (Expert Parallelism)切分策略，即将路由专家均匀分布到每张卡上，同时每张卡上同步存放一个共享专家。路由专家采用Double-Routing的计算策略完成计算，其核心在于每张卡需要完成2次init-routing和finalize-routing操作。该方案有以下优点： 1. 当负载相对较均匀时，相对于AllGather的方案，峰值内存较低，每张卡只需要获取对应专家计算的token即可，不存在数据冗余。 2. 相比于每张卡上获取完整token数据量，通信量更低，通信耗时更优。 该方案的主要计算流程如下图所示： 主要计算步骤如下： 1. 调用npumoeinitroutingv2接口，对本卡上的token进行expand并排序得到expandx，同时获取每个专家需要计算的token个数即tokensperexpert，以及用于恢复token原始排序的参数expandedrowidx（第一次routing操作）。 python expandedx, expandedrowidx, tokensperexpert, = torchnpu.npumoeinitroutingv2(...) 2. 通过对tokensperexpert进行AlltoAll操作和ReduceSum操作，获得每张卡需要向其他卡发送的token数量(inputsplits)，以及每张卡需要从其他卡上拿到的tokens数量（outputsplit），该参数主要用于AlltoAll通信，各卡分别获取对应的token。 3. 调用AlltoAll通信接口，对每张卡上的token进行交互，每张卡上的专家获取本专家需要计算的token。 python dist.alltoallsingle(gatheredtokens, expandedx, outputsplits, inputsplits, group=moeepgroup) 4. 此时每张卡上已经获取到本卡专家需要计算的token，但是处于乱序。因此，本卡需要再完成一次rerouting操作，得到排序后的token分布即hiddenstatesorderedbyexperts，以及本卡上每个专家需要计算的token数量tokensperlocalexpert，同时得到用于恢复本卡token顺序的参数gatheredidsunsort（第二次routing操作）。 python hiddenstatesorderedbyexperts, , gatheredidsunsort, tokensperlocalexpert = torchnpu.npumoererouting(...) 5. 完成路由专家和共享专家计算。 python hiddenstatesorderedbyexperts = experts(args) 6. 对完成计算的token进行排序恢复（第一次finalize-routing操作，与第二次routing操作相对应），此处采用torch.indexselect()接口性能更优。 python newx = torch.indexselect(hiddenstatesorderedbyexperts, 0, gatheredidsunsort.float().argsort().int()) 7. 调用AlltoAll通信接口，进行token多卡交互，把本卡上的token获取回来。 python dist.alltoallsingle(gatheredtokens, newx, inputsplits, outputsplits, group=moeepgroup) 8. 调用finalizerouting接口，对本张卡上的token进行顺序恢复，得到原始排序的token（第二次finalize-routing操作，与第一次routing操作相对应），同时可直接通过该接口完成路由专家和共享专家的加权求和。 python hiddenstates = torchnpu.npumoefinalizerouting( gatheredtokens, skip1=hiddenstatesshare, skip2=None, bias=None, scales=topkweight.to(gatheredtokens.dtype), expandedsrctodstrow=expandedrowidx, exportforsourcerow=None, droppadmode=2 ) TND格式支持 常规FlashAttention采用BNSD的格式（[batch, numofhead, seqlen, headdim]）计算，而对于每个请求长度均不确定的场景，可能需要padding操作，导致计算资源的浪费。而TND格式可以对batch和seqlen进行合轴处理即[batchseqlen, numofhead, headdim]，转换为token数，无需padding数据即可完成计算，此功能依赖于FlashAttention的功能支持。 针对TND（[token, numofhead, headdim]）格式，需要把所有输入的请求合成一个list进行处理。假设有4个请求，seqlen长度分别为128，256，512和1024，在FlashAttention计算时，需要把所有的请求合成一个list，即actualseqlengthskv=[128, 256, 512, 1024]即可完成对应计算，无需把请求padding到统一的长度。 尤其对于不定长输入的场景，TND格式解决了易用性以及计算资源浪费的问题。但是，实际计算时，TND格式会引入以下问题： 1. 数据排布不亲和：对于FlashAttention计算不亲和，数据访问不连续，FlashAttention带宽效率较低。 2. 引入额外计算开销：原始BNSD的格式需要使用transpose变成TND格式，引入一些非必要的计算开销。 为避免上述问题，实际在FlashAttention计算中采用NTD的格式，提升带宽效率的同时，也减少了transpose等计算开销。在prefill阶段MLA部分实际的计算流程如下图所示： 采用该计算方式的优点如下： 1. 相对于TND格式，FlashAttention的计算效率提升15%。 2. 配合matmul权重拆分以及FlashAttention支持独立的NoPE(No Positional Encoding)和RoPE(Rotary Positional Encoding)输入，可以完全消除split/concat/transpose等额外计算开销，提升MLA阶段的计算效率。 micro-batch优化 prefill阶段通常属于计算bound的场景，同时又有一定比例的通信耗时开销，通信耗时占比可达30%。而计算和通信由不同的硬件单元完成，如果此时计算和通信能够并行运行，将进一步提升prefill阶段的性能。理想情况下，通信耗时可以完全被计算掩盖，这样计算效率将极大提升。 因此，可以把输入拆分成两个micro-batch，采用双流的方式，构造两条流水线，通过定制化的流水排布，把计算和通信并行起来，最大化prefill阶段的计算效率。 将输入拆分成两个micro-batch，数据被一分为二，会改变prefill阶段每一层计算的shape，shape的变动会导致计算和通信的效率发生变化；同时在eager模式下，task下发的数量也会多一倍，对host要求更高。因此在prefill阶段做micro-batch优化时，需要确认以下问题的影响： 1. 计算和通信性能线性度较好：要求输入数据切分前计算和通信的性能，近似等于切分后两份数据的计算和通信性能加和，这样可以最小化避免因shape变化导致的性能劣化。 2. 计算未出现host bound：如果模型本身就是host bound场景，此时通过双流实现micro-batch会导致host性能劣化，整体耗时劣化。 MLA-DP和MoE-EP场景micro-batch策略 MLA采用DP切分的情况下，整个prefill阶段的通信算子主要来源于MoE阶段的AlltoAll通信（dispatch阶段和combine阶段）。因此，该阶段micro-batch的核心目标就是通过计算掩盖dispatch和combine两个阶段的通信耗时，最大化prefill阶段的计算效率。 该场景的流水排布如下图所示： 其主要步骤如下： 1. 计算和通信划分：将prefill的计算划分为6个阶段，分别为：atten、initrouting、dispatch、mlp、combine、finalizerouting， 图中： atten主要包含MLA和oproj计算，dispatch主要包含将token分发到对应专家的AlltoAll通信，mlp主要包含路由专家和共享专家计算，combine主要包含把token恢复到各卡上的AlltoAll通信。 2. micro-batch预处理：将输入划分成2个micro-batch进行处理，假设每卡上面有2个4k请求，则每个micro-batch处理1个4k请求，当2个micro-batch全部计算完成时，则完成所有的计算处理。 3. 通信处理：由于通信和计算并行，此时不能使能HCCLOPEXPANSIONMODE的AIV模式，采用默认SDMA模式。如果采用AIV模式，则会导致通信和计算硬件资源抢占，时延变长。 4. 创建流：针对DP+EP的切分策略场景，将所有的计算放在默认计算流上。 python currstream = torch.npu.currentstream() 新建一条流，用于通信： python stream1 = torch.npu.Stream() 5. 流水排布：将计算放到当前流上进行，如下所示： python with torch.npu.stream(currstream): # 在currstream进行atten计算 atten() 将通信放到stream1上进行计算： python with torch.npu.stream(stream1): # 在stream1进行atten计算 dispatch() 针对需要同步的位置，可以采用以下方式进行两条流的同步操作： python event0 = currstream.recordevent() ... stream1.waitevent(event0) Prefill-Stage Inference Performance Optimization for DeepSeek-R1 on an Atlas A3 Cluster Overview This document describes parallel deployment and performance optimization strategies for the prefill stage of DeepSeek-R1 on Atlas A3 series products. It primarily uses key optimization techniques such as a hybrid partitioning strategy, Double-Routing, and micro-batch. It ultimately achieves a throughput of 6.5k tokens/card/s with perfect eplb on Atlas A3 series products. MLA (Multi-Head Latent Attention) Deployment Strategy Optimization DP (Data Parallelism) Partitioning Strategy The MLA part of prefill can use a pure DP computation strategy. Each card deploys the complete model weights without partitioning the model. This strategy has the following advantages: 1. Pure DP partitioning avoids redundant KV-Cache (Key-Value Cache) across multiple cards. Each card stores only the KV-Cache data for the requests received by that card. The KV-Cache data differs across cards, so no redundant data exists. 2. The MLA part has no communication operators, which avoids communication overhead. The prefill stage can more easily fully use the computing power and achieve high throughput when processing a large amount of request data. However, this partitioning strategy causes the following issues: 1. Uneven computation load: In actual scenarios, input requests often have different sequence lengths. Cards that process shorter sequences complete computation earlier and must then wait for the longest sequence in the batch, wasting computation cycles. 2. Increased TTFT (Time to First Token): If the number of real-time requests is smaller than the number of cards, some cards remain idle. Delaying processing to form a complete batch increases the time required to generate the first token. Directly processing an incomplete batch underutilizes computing resources. To address these issues, this sample improves the TP (Tensor Parallelism) partitioning strategy and proposes an SP-TP-SP (Sequence Parallelism, SP) hybrid partitioning strategy. SP-TP-SP Hybrid Partitioning Strategy For input sequences, combine the batch and seqlen axes to convert the input into a token count. Apply SP partitioning to the tokens and evenly distribute them across cards. The following figure shows the computation process: 1. Concatenate multiple request sequences, pad them to the smallest multiple of the number of cards, and apply SP partitioning. Each card then receives the same number of tokens. 2. The FlashAttention (FA) computation uses the TP strategy. It evenly distributes Attention heads across compute cards to balance the computation load across multiple cards. 3. After FlashAttention computation is complete, use AlltoAll communication to convert TP partitioning to SP partitioning. This communication operator transfers less data and provides better performance. At this point, oproj consumes more memory because it must load the complete weights. With this partitioning strategy, each card has the same MLA-stage computation workload, resulting in a balanced computation load. Assume that there are three inputs: input0, input1, and input2. After combining the batch and seqlen axes, evenly distribute the tokens across Rank0 to Rank3. downproj includes the qaproj and kvaproj computations. qupproj and kvupproj represent the qbproj and kvbproj computations, respectively. Each card then processes the same amount of data and has a balanced computation load. The following figure shows the detailed computation process: The preceding strategy has the following advantages: 1. Shorter TTFT: This advantage is especially significant for long-sequence scenarios. For example, for one 128K request, computation can be evenly distributed across cards to reduce latency. 2. Balanced computation load in the MLA part: Input sequences only need to be padded to a multiple of the number of cards. Each card has the same computation workload, with almost no redundant computation. However, this strategy introduces the following issues, which require corresponding optimizations: 1. Each card must store the complete KV-Cache. The KV-Cache is redundant across cards and consumes a large amount of memory. Store KV-Cache data across separate cards to avoid this issue. 2. Compared with the pure DP strategy, MLA computation introduces AllGather and AlltoAll communication. Use micro-batch to further optimize the communication time. Summary: In the current prefill scenario, consider the DP partitioning strategy to improve throughput when there are many requests or KV-Cache occupies a large amount of memory. Consider the SP-TP-SP hybrid partitioning strategy to reduce latency when there are few requests, the request distribution is uneven, or a single request has a long sequence. MoE (Mixture of Experts) Deployment Strategy Optimization The MoE computation stage uses the EP (Expert Parallelism) partitioning strategy. It evenly distributes routed experts across cards, while each card also stores one shared expert. Routed expert computation uses the Double-Routing strategy. Each card performs init-routing and finalize-routing operations twice. This solution has the following advantages: 1. When the load is relatively balanced, this solution has lower peak memory than the AllGather solution. Each card obtains only the tokens required by its experts, so no redundant data exists. 2. Compared with obtaining the complete token data on each card, this solution transfers less data and reduces communication time. The following figure shows the main computation process of this solution: The main computation steps are as follows: 1. Call npumoeinitroutingv2 to expand and sort the tokens on the current card to obtain expandedx. The interface also obtains tokensperexpert, which is the number of tokens each expert processes, and expandedrowidx, which restores the original token order (first routing operation). python expandedx, expandedrowidx, tokensperexpert, = torchnpu.npumoeinitroutingv2(...) 2. Perform AlltoAll and ReduceSum operations on tokensperexpert to obtain the number of tokens that each card sends to other cards (inputsplits) and the number of tokens that each card receives from other cards (outputsplit). These parameters are primarily used for AlltoAll communication so that each card obtains its corresponding tokens. 3. Call the AlltoAll communication interface to exchange tokens across cards. The experts on each card obtain the tokens they need to process. python dist.alltoallsingle(gatheredtokens, expandedx, outputsplits, inputsplits, group=moeepgroup) 4. At this point, each card has obtained the tokens required by its local experts, but the tokens are out of order. Therefore, the card performs another rerouting operation to obtain the sorted token distribution hiddenstatesorderedbyexperts, the number of tokens processed by each local expert tokensperlocalexpert, and gatheredidsunsort, which restores the token order on the current card (second routing operation). python hiddenstatesorderedbyexperts, , gatheredidsunsort, tokensperlocalexpert = torchnpu.npumoererouting(...) 5. Complete the routed expert and shared expert computations. python hiddenstatesorderedbyexperts = experts(args) 6. Restore the order of the computed tokens (first finalize-routing operation, corresponding to the second routing operation). The torch.indexselect() interface provides better performance here. python newx = torch.indexselect(hiddenstatesorderedbyexperts, 0, gatheredidsunsort.float().argsort().int()) 7. Call the AlltoAll communication interface to exchange tokens across cards and retrieve the tokens for the current card. python dist.alltoallsingle(gatheredtokens, newx, inputsplits, outputsplits, group=moeepgroup) 8. Call finalizerouting to restore the token order on the current card and obtain the tokens in their original order (second finalize-routing operation, corresponding to the first routing operation). This interface can also directly compute the weighted sum of routed expert and shared expert outputs. python hiddenstates = torchnpu.npumoefinalizerouting( gatheredtokens, skip1=hiddenstatesshare, skip2=None, bias=None, scales=topkweight.to(gatheredtokens.dtype), expandedsrctodstrow=expandedrowidx, exportforsourcerow=None, droppadmode=2 ) TND Format Support Conventional FlashAttention uses the BNSD format ([batch, numofhead, seqlen, headdim]) for computation. When each request has an uncertain length, padding may be required, which wastes computing resources. The TND format combines the batch and seqlen axes into [batchseqlen, numofhead, headdim] and converts the input into a token count, enabling computation without padding. This function depends on FlashAttention support. For the TND ([token, numofhead, headdim]) format, combine all input requests into a list for processing. Assume that there are four requests with seqlen values of 128, 256, 512, and 1024. During FlashAttention computation, combine all requests into a list and set actualseqlengthskv=[128, 256, 512, 1024] to complete the corresponding computation without padding the requests to a uniform length. The TND format addresses usability and computing resource waste issues, especially for variable-length input scenarios. However, during actual computation, the TND format introduces the following issues: 1. Unfriendly data layout: The data layout is unfriendly to FlashAttention computation, data accesses are discontinuous, and FlashAttention has low bandwidth efficiency. 2. Additional computation overhead: The original BNSD format must use transpose to convert to the TND format, introducing unnecessary computation overhead. To avoid these issues, actual FlashAttention computation uses the NTD format. This format improves bandwidth efficiency and reduces computation overhead from operations such as transpose. The following figure shows the actual computation process of the MLA part during the prefill stage: This computation method has the following advantages: 1. Compared with the TND format, FlashAttention computation efficiency improves by 15%. 2. Combined with matmul weight partitioning and FlashAttention support for separate NoPE (No Positional Encoding) and RoPE (Rotary Positional Encoding) inputs, this method completely eliminates additional computation overhead from split, concat, and transpose operations and improves MLA-stage computation efficiency. Micro-Batch Optimization The prefill stage is usually computation-bound and also has some communication overhead, which can account for up to 30% of the total time. Different hardware units perform computation and communication. Running computation and communication in parallel further improves prefill-stage performance. Ideally, computation completely hides communication time and greatly improves computation efficiency. Therefore, split the input into two micro-batches, use two streams to construct two pipelines, and run computation and communication in parallel through a customized pipeline layout. This approach maximizes prefill-stage computation efficiency. Splitting the input into two micro-batches divides the data in half and changes the shape of each layer computation during the prefill stage. Shape changes affect computation and communication efficiency. In eager mode, the number of delivered tasks also doubles, imposing higher requirements on the host. Therefore, when optimizing micro-batch during the prefill stage, confirm the impact of the following issues: 1. Good linearity of computation and communication performance: The computation and communication performance before input partitioning must be approximately equal to the sum of the performance for the two partitions. This requirement minimizes performance degradation caused by shape changes. 2. Computation is not host-bound: If the model itself is host-bound, implementing micro-batch through two streams degrades host performance and increases the overall duration. Micro-Batch Strategy for the MLA-DP and MoE-EP Scenario When MLA uses DP partitioning, communication operators throughout the prefill stage mainly come from AlltoAll communication in the MoE stage, including the dispatch and combine stages. Therefore, the core objective of micro-batch in this stage is to use computation to hide communication time in the dispatch and combine stages and maximize prefill-stage computation efficiency. The following figure shows the pipeline layout for this scenario: The main steps are as follows: 1. Computation and communication division: Divide prefill computation into six stages: atten, initrouting, dispatch, mlp, combine, and finalizerouting. In the figure, atten mainly includes MLA and oproj computation. dispatch mainly includes AlltoAll communication that distributes tokens to the corresponding experts. mlp mainly includes routed expert and shared expert computation. combine mainly includes AlltoAll communication that restores tokens to each card. 2. Micro-batch preprocessing: Divide the input into two micro-batches for processing. Assume that each card has two 4k requests. Each micro-batch processes one 4k request. All computation is complete when both micro-batches finish. 3. Communication processing: Because communication and computation run in parallel, do not enable the AIV mode of HCCLOPEXPANSIONMODE. Use the default SDMA mode. AIV mode causes communication and computation to compete for hardware resources, increasing latency. 4. Creating streams: For the DP+EP partitioning strategy, place all computations on the default computation stream. python currstream = torch.npu.currentstream() Create a stream for communication: python stream1 = torch.npu.Stream() 5. Pipeline layout: Place computation on the current stream as follows: python with torch.npu.stream(currstream): # Run atten computation on currstream. atten() Place communication on stream1 as follows: python with torch.npu.stream(stream1): # Run atten computation on stream1. dispatch() At synchronization points, synchronize the two streams as follows: python event0 = currstream.recordevent() ... stream1.waitevent(event0) After micro-batch computation is enabled, computation completely hides communication in the dispatch and combine stages. The entire prefill stage is computation-bound, and the chip has no idle time. Therefore, end-to-end computation efficiency improves. On Atlas A3 series products, prefill uses a two-node, 16-card deployment with an input sequence of 644K. Assuming that the expert load of the MoE layer is balanced, the performance test results are as follows: Partitioning Strategy Latency (ms) Total Throughput (tokens/s) Average Throughput (tokens/card/s) ------------------------ MLA-DP32 + MoE-EP32 3128 83805 5237 MLA-DP32 + MoE-EP32 + micro-batch 2512 104356 6522 With this partitioning strategy, enabling micro-batch improves performance by 25%. Enabling the weightNZ Format for Matmul Operators For Matmul computations in DeepSeek, process the weight Tensor of the model weights into the weightNZ format, which is friendly to Ascend AI Processors, to further improve Matmul computation efficiency. The weightNZ format uses 512-byte alignment, which effectively improves hardware bandwidth access efficiency. For example, an int8 Tensor with a shape of [16384, 7168] is converted to [224, 1024, 16, 32] in the NZ format. Appendix Environment Deployment and Sample Execution (Chinese)

计算已经融入LightningIndexer算子，相较于 Top-$k$ 外置收益大约20%；SparseFlashAttention则是针对稀疏 Attention 场景进行了特殊优化的 Attention 算子。 A3 中的 Cube 核与 Vector 核数比为 $1:2$，每1个 Cube 核与2个 Vector 核构成一个组核 (一个 AICore)，其中一个组核的结构如下图所示，其中 L1、L0A、L0B、L0C 为 Cube 核的片上 Buffer，UB 为 Vector 核的片上 Buffer。具体介绍可参考： 基本架构 。 在本篇技术报告中，我们将对两个融合算子在 A3 上的具体优化进行细致地阐述，包括：具体的算子 Tiling 设计、Cube 核与 Vector 核间的流水优化、计算流程的实现优化、以及下一步即将开展的优化等内容；同时将介绍当前融合算子在提升易用性上的进展。 Highlights 细致的算子 Tiling 及 Pipeline 设计，发挥融合算子优势 充分利用硬件特性，基于 Ascend C API 高效实现 聚合访存，减少指令下发，提高离散访存性能 算子开发及调测的易用性提升 LightningIndexerQuant量化支持，Mat-Duce 算法充分利用 Cube 核 Outline NPU DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp Ascend C 融合算子优化 Highlights Outline LightningIndexer LI 算子 Tiling 设计 LI Pipeline 设计 ReLU 随路实现 Top-k 指令实现 LI 量化支持 Mat-Duce 算法 SparseFlashAttention SFA 算子 Tiling 设计 SFA Pipeline 设计 访存优化 SFA Next Feature 易用性提升 TilingKey 模板化 分核计算下沉 LightningIndexer LightningIndexer基于一系列操作得到每一个 token 对应的 Top-$k$ 个位置。对于某个 token 对应的 Index Query $Q{index}\in\R^{g\times d}$，给定上下文 Index Key $K{index}\in\R^{S{k}\times d},W\in\R^{g\times 1}$，其中 $g$ 为 GQA 对应的 group size，$d$ 为每一个头的维度，$S{k}$ 是上下文的长度，LightningIndexer的具体计算公式如下： $$ \text{Top-}k\left\{[1]{1\times g}@\left[(W@[1]{1\times S{k}})\odot\text{ReLU}\left(Q{index}@K{index}^T\right)\right]\right\} $$ 可拆分为如下计算流程： 1. 计算矩阵乘法：$S = Q{index}@K{index}^T$； 2. 计算激活函数：$S'=\text{ReLU}(S)$； 3. 计算广播乘法：$SW=(W@[1]{1\times S{k}})\odot S'$； 4. 沿G轴进行Reduce操作：$Score=[1]{1\times g}@ SW$； 5. 对 $Score$ 进行 $\text{Top-}k$ 计算，即获取数值排序前 $k$ 个的结果，并返回其对应的 Index， 在 Prefill 或开启 MTP 的 Decode 场景，多个 token 对应的 $Q{index}$ 会被合并统一计算，本文后续部分不对单/多个 token 对应的 $Q{index}$ 加以区分。 实际开发中需要充分利用昇腾硬件的特征以实现更好的性能，以下将详细介绍当前的解决方案及具体实现方式。 LI 算子 Tiling 设计 算子的 Tiling 设计决定了储存空间是否被充分利用，进而影响整体的算力利用率以及算子性能。针对LightningIndexer，本章分别阐述核间和核内的 Tiling 设计。 由于片上 Buffer 空间有限，任何计算本质上都需要进行切块，因此需要确定一次迭代计算的基本块大小，即核间的 Tiling 设计。当前LightningIndexer算子将基本块大小设置为$(512,512)$：即一次迭代计算完成512行以减少右矩阵的重复搬运 (以$g=64$为例，一次会合并8个token统一计算)；同时会完成 $S{k}$ 方向上粒度为512的计算，这个值的选取可以保证流水线头尾开销可控以及 Cube 核与 Vector 核之间同步开销可被计算掩盖。 核内 Tiling 设计采用了如下方案： L1 空间划分为如下部分： $Q{index}$ 矩阵常驻：$512\times 128\times2\text{ Bytes}=128\text{ KB}$，L1层级基本块为 $(512,128)$，在实际计算时可做更细致的搬运，即一次只搬运$(256,128)$大小的数据到L1以降低搬运头开销； $K{index}$ 矩阵 3-Buffer 循环复用：$3\times256\times 128\times2\text{ Bytes}=192\text{ KB}$，L1层级基本块为 $(256,128)$。 L0A，L0B，L0C 使能 Double Buffer，分别划分为$2\times32\text{ KB},2\times32\text{ KB},2\times64\text{ KB}$，一次搬入 L0A 和 L0B 的矩阵块大小都为$(128,128)$，这是一种对昇腾硬件较为亲和的设置，可以提高算力利用率。 这样的方式可以保证在计算过程中 $Q{index}$ 只需要搬运一次，并且降低 $K{index}$ 矩阵的重复搬运次数：假设 $Q{index}$ 矩阵 L1 层级基本块大小为 $(128,128)$，而行方向总的 token 数为 $Sq$，那么 $K{index}$ 矩阵需要重复搬运 $\lceil Sq/128\rceil$ 次；选取基本块大小为 $(512,128)$ 可将重复搬运次数降低到 $\lceil Sq/512\rceil$。由于第一个计算过程矩阵乘的启动需要右矩阵的搬运，为右矩阵分配多块 Buffer 可消除计算流程因为 Buffer 占用造成的阻塞，所以为 $K{index}$ 分配 3-Buffer 可以提升带宽爬坡期的搬运效率。 LI Pipeline 设计 LightningIndexer的计算流程只有两个阶段：即矩阵乘和 ReLU 操作 ($C1$) 以及后续的多个向量计算 ($V1$)。为了防止多个阶段的串行执行，需要提前下发 (Preload) 一次 $C1$ 以实现流水的互相掩盖。 ReLU 随路实现 LightningIndexer首先需要进行矩阵乘法，并对结果进行ReLU计算。由于矩阵乘法和 ReLU 计算分别发生在不同的计算单元，朴素的实现需要将矩阵乘法的结果从 Cube 核搬运至 Vector 核进行。而昇腾NPU上 Cube 核的 FixP 组件提供随路 ReLU 能力，即可以在矩阵乘法完成之后直接在数据搬运的过程中随路完成 ReLU 操作，不需要显式进行 ReLU 计算。除 ReLU 之外，FixP 组件还有更多强大功能，具体可参考 基础API: FixP相关 。 Top-k 指令实现 LightningIndexer融合算子的核心是在长达数十万的序列中，为每个 token 高效地筛选出分数最高的 $k$（例如2048）个索引。同时，对于算子而言，Top-$k$ 的计算必须是准确无误的，不能采用近似算法求解。 当前的实现方案基于昇腾支持的排序指令进行全量排序，Top-$k$ 计算方案过程分为三步： 分组排序：通过VBS32指令将每32个 token 按照其 $Score$ 进行稳定降序排列，输出其排序向量以及对应索引向量，直到将整个序列的 token 分组排序完毕。 归并：通过VMS4v2指令将至多4组（可为2/3组）长度为32、128、512的已排序向量进行归并，直到合并后的向量长度达到2048。合并排列仍然按照其对应 $Score$ 进行稳定降序排列，最终输出的向量长度为4组输入向量长度之和，同时输出其对应索引向量。 规约：采用VMS4v2指令的耗尽模式 (当某个输入向量的可用数据已全部读取完毕，排序指令立即暂停执行)，将至多4组长度为2048已排序的向量进行归并。取出前 $k=2048$ 个参数组成的向量与另外未参与合并排序的有序向量重复进行 Top-$k$ 计算，直到将所有长度为2048的有序向量比较完毕，得到最终所有向量中得分最高的2048个对应的 Index。 假设上下文长度为 $Sk$ ，分组排序与归并步骤的计算量为 $4Sk$。规约步骤的计算量无法精确评估，采用正态分布结合蒙特卡洛法模拟，结果显示第一次的计算量接近 $4k$ ，从第二次开始，由于已经有了 $k$ 个较大数的向量参与运算，计算量开始大幅减少直到逼近耗尽极限 $k$ 。该部分计算量经过模拟分析后可表示为 $0.36Sk+3.32k$ 。因此Top-$k$ 流程总计算量 $totalCount = 4.36Sk + 3.32k$。 LI 量化支持 当前LightningIndexer算子已支持 Per-Token-Head 量化 输入，即输入的 $Q{index}$ 和 $K{index}$ 都被量化为 INT8 数据类型，以此应对长序列场景下显存占用过大的问题。 支持量化输入的LightningIndexerQuant对于某个 token 对应的 Index Query $Q{index}^{INT8}\in\R^{g\times d}$ 及其反量化系数$Scale{Q}\in\R^{g\times1}$，给定上下文 Index Key $K{index}^{INT8}\in\R^{S{k}\times d}$ 及其反量化系数$Scale{K}\in\R^{S{k}\times1}$, $W\in\R^{g\times 1}$，其中 $g$ 为 GQA 对应的 group size，$d$ 为每一个头的维度，$S{k}$ 是上下文的长度，LightningIndexerQuant的具体计算公式如下： $$ \text{Top-}k\left\{[1]{1\times g}@\left[(W@[1]{1\times S{k}})\odot\text{ReLU}\left(\left(ScaleQ@ScaleK^T\right)\odot\left(Q{index}^{INT8}@{(K{index}^{INT8})}^T\right)\right)\right]\right\} $$ Mat-Duce 算法 LightningIndexerQuant算子采用了 Mat-Duce 算法，利用数学变换调整计算逻辑，用矩阵乘法实现规约计算。该算法充分利用 A3 芯片 Cube 核的随路能力，将LightningIndexerQuant算子中的大部分计算都在 Cube 核内实现。 由于 $ScaleQ,ScaleK\ge0$，令 $\tilde{W} = ScaleQ \odot W \in \mathbb{R}^{g\times1}$，LightningIndexerQuant计算公式可等价变换为： $$\text{Top-}k\left\{\tilde{W}^T @ \text{ReLU}(Q{index}^{INT8}@(K{index}^{INT8})^T) \odot ScaleK^T\right\}.$$ 对应的具体计算流程为： 1. 预处理，在 UB 上计算 $\tilde{W} = ScaleQ \odot W$，CAST 到 FP16 写出到 GM; 2. 在 Cube 核内计算 $S^{INT32} = Q{index}^{INT8}@(K{index}^{INT8})^T$，$S$ 数据类型为 INT32； 3. 利用 FixP 的 DEQF16 指令，计算 $S^{FP16}=\text{FP16}(S^{INT32}/1024)$，将 INT32 结果与 $1/1024$ 相乘并转化为 FP16 数据类型，此处 $1/1024$ 可以防止数值溢出，且不会影响最终 Top-$k$ 的结果； 4. 继续利用 FixP 的随路 ReLU 功能，计算 $S'=\text{ReLU}(S^{FP16})$ 并将结果搬运至 L1 以进行下一次矩阵乘法计算； 5. 在 Cube 核内执行 $P=\tilde{W}^T@S'$， 将结果写出到 GM 上。这一步骤同时完成了关于 $ScaleQ$ 的反量化、关于 $W$ 的行方向放缩以及不同头结果的求和操作； 6. 将 $P$ 从 GM 读入到 Vector 核内并进行关于 $ScaleK$ 的反量化，$Score = P \odot ScaleK^T$； 7. 在 Vector 核内对 $Score$ 计算 Top-$k$。 计算流程如下图所示 这一方案相比标准实现方案，将大部分向量操作通过数学变换以 Cube 核实现 (步骤5)，同时充分利用了 FixP 随路量化激活搬运 能力，将量化矩阵乘法的结果从 INT32 数据类型转化为 FP16 数据类型 (步骤3，4) 得以进行第二次半精度的矩阵乘法操作，显著提升了算子性能。 SparseFlashAttention 随着大模型上下文长度的增加，Sparse Attention 的重要性与日俱增，这一技术通过“只计算关键部分”大幅减少计算量，然而会引入大量的离散访存，造成数据搬运时间增加，进而影响整体性能。Sparse Attention 计算可表示为 $$ \text{softmax}(\frac{Q@\tilde{K}^T}{\sqrt{dk}})@\tilde{V} $$ 其中 $\tilde{K},\tilde{V}$ 为基于某种选择算法 (如LightningIndexer) 得到的重要性较高的 Key 和 Value，一般具有稀疏或分块稀疏的特征，$dk$ 为 $Q,\tilde{K}$ 每一个头的维度。 本次公布的SparseFlashAttention是面向 Sparse Attention 的全新算子，针对离散访存进行了指令缩减及搬运聚合的细致优化。SparseFlashAttention算子沿用 FlashAttention 的计算流程，分为四个阶段： $C1$：$Q@K^T$； $V1$：online softmax； $C2$：$P@V$； $V2$：rescaling $O$。 SFA 算子 Tiling 设计 SparseFlashAttention一次迭代计算的基本块大小为$(256,512)$。 算子核内 Tiling 设计如下： L1 空间划分为如下部分： $Q/P$ $K/V$ 矩阵 3-Buffer 循环复用：$3\times128\times 288\times2\text{ Bytes}=216\text{ KB}$，其中$K$矩阵每次的搬运大小为$(128,288)$，$V$矩阵每次的搬运大小为$(256,128)$。 L0A，L0B，L0C使能 Double Buffer，分别划分为$2\times32\text{ KB},2\times32\text{ KB},2\times64\text{ KB}$，在 $C1$ 阶段一次搬入 L0A 和 L0B的矩阵块大小分别为 $(128,96),(96,128)$；在 $C2$ 阶段一次搬入 L0A 和 L0B 的矩阵块大小都为 $(128,128)$。 SFA Pipeline 设计 对于复杂的融合算子而言，Cube 核和 Vector 算法，SparseFlashAttention除最终的归一化操作外只有三个计算阶段$C1,V1,C2$。相较于LightningIndexer算子而言，SparseFlashAttention算子的计算流程更为复杂，依赖关系更多，朴素的流水排布会导致计算过程中出现大量的空泡。如下图的上半部分所示，由于计算流程中的不同阶段之间存在数据依赖，不论是 Cube 流或 Vector 流上都出现了很多的空闲部分，导致算力利用率较低。本算子采用 Preload 流水排布以消除依赖，实现了除头尾以外的平台期部分 Cube 流完美掩盖 Vector 流，效果如下图下半部分所示，可以看到这种方式相较于朴素的流水排布有较大的性能收益。 访存优化 实际的访存行为可以分为两个步骤：指令下发及数据搬运。对于非 Sparse 场景的 Attention 算子，数据访存一般是连续的，因此单次数据搬运耗时相较于指令下发耗时更长，可实现连续的多次访存，达到较高的访存带宽。然而对于 Sparse Attention 的离散访存而言，单次访存的耗时大幅下降，甚至可能小于指令下发的耗时，这就会导致严重的指令下发阻塞，如下图所示。 Attention 计算从 Cube 核发起，访存指令也由 Cube 核发射。基于 A3 芯片 Cube 核和 Vector 核数比为 $1:2$ 的特性，利用 Vector 核发射访存指令，将指令的下发效率提高一倍。另一方面，单次访存的数据量本身也会影响实际达到的带宽，而离散访存单次的访存量较小，这会导致数据搬运本身的耗时高于预期。针对这一问题，可以将离散的数据点两两聚合，利用 srcGap 参数实现成对的数据访存，提升访存带宽，如图所示。 SFA Next Feature 后续将探索SparseFlashAttention算子的量化支持以应对长上下文场景下显存占用过大的挑战。 易用性提升 TilingKey 模板化 TilingKey 是算子区分不同的实现而将代码进行区分的方法，目标是以不同的分支处理不同的特性。然而 TilingKey 本身不易于记忆和理解，因为它们通常是较长又没有明确含义的数字，严重影响代码的可读性和可编程性。 为了提高算子代码的可读性，降低开发难度，本次开源的两个全新算子均采用 Ascend C 的 Tiling 模板编程方法替代传统的 TilingKey 编程，只需要定义模板参数及其对应的组合即可实现分支管理，减少对 TilingKey 具体数值的依赖，提高代码的管理效率。详细内容可参考 Tiling模板编程 。 分核计算下沉 Tiling 是算子执行前的预处理阶段，在此阶段 Host 侧会计算 workspace 占用以及分核策略等算子执行需要的内容，在单算子模式下，可能会出现 Host Bound 的情况。通过 静态图下沉技术 ，我们规避了这种情况。 然而对于 Attention 类算子而言，实际输入的不同 Batch 对应的上下文长度可能不同，因此 Tiling 中分核策略的计算对具体上下文长度 (actualSeqLengths) 存在值依赖，这使得 Attention 类算子无法完全下沉到静态图执行，导致整网产生过多小的静态子图，引入大量静态子图调度开销；同时，进行分核计算时需要将对应的数据从 Device 侧向 Host 侧拷贝，造成整网性能较差。 针对这一问题，Attention 类算子采用了 Tiling 下沉的解决方案，将分核计算下沉到 Device 侧的 AICPU 进行。整网运行时，分核计算依赖的数据就绪后即可启动，且可以与算子执行流并行进行。然而，对于分核计算依赖前序算子的情况，这种方法依然无法避免执行断流。从具体使用的角度看，这种处理方式引入了额外的 AICPU Tiling 逻辑，在自定义算子流程中需要另外开发对应的 Tiling func，并配合下沉图执行调度实现，功能复杂、链条较长，导致自定义开发和调测难度较高。 本次发布的LightningIndexer及SparseFlashAttention算子进行了进一步的 Tiling 下沉优化，将分核计算流程从 AICPU 下沉到 AICore 内部执行，简化调用链条，消除 Tiling 依赖前序算子引入的调度开销，开发和调试流程得到了简化。

NPU DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp Ascend C Fused Operator Optimization For the DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp architecture, this release provides two new fused operators: LightningIndexer (LI) and SparseFlashAttention (SFA). The LightningIndexer operator is one of the most distinctive parts of the new DeepSeek architecture and sparsely selects important context. The Top-$k$ computation is currently integrated into the LightningIndexer operator, providing an improvement of approximately 20% compared with an external Top-$k$ implementation. SparseFlashAttention is an Attention operator specifically optimized for sparse Attention scenarios. The ratio of Cube cores to Vector cores in A3 is $1:2$. Each Cube core and two Vector cores form a core group (one AICore). The following figure shows the structure of a core group. L1, L0A, L0B, and L0C are on-chip buffers of the Cube core, and UB is the on-chip buffer of the Vector core. For details, refer to Basic Architecture (Chinese). This technical report describes the detailed optimizations of the two fused operators on A3, including operator tiling design, pipeline optimization between Cube and Vector cores, implementation optimization of the computation process, and planned optimizations. It also introduces the current progress in improving the usability of fused operators. Highlights Detailed operator tiling and pipeline designs that fully use the advantages of fused operators Efficient implementation based on Ascend C APIs that fully uses hardware features Aggregated memory access that reduces instruction delivery and improves discrete memory access performance Improved usability for operator development and debugging Quantization support for LightningIndexerQuant and full use of Cube cores by the Mat-Duce algorithm Outline NPU DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp Ascend C Fused Operator Optimization Highlights Outline LightningIndexer LI Operator Tiling Design LI Pipeline Design In-Path ReLU Implementation Top-k Instruction Implementation LI Quantization Support Mat-Duce Algorithm SparseFlashAttention SFA Operator Tiling Design SFA Pipeline Design Memory Access Optimization SFA Next Feature Usability Improvements TilingKey Templating Core Partition Computation Offloading LightningIndexer LightningIndexer performs a series of operations to obtain the Top-$k$ positions corresponding to each token. For the Index Query $Q{index}\in\R^{g\times d}$ of a token, given the context Index Key $K{index}\in\R^{S{k}\times d},W\in\R^{g\times 1}$, where $g$ is the group size corresponding to GQA, $d$ is the dimension of each head, and $S{k}$ is the context length, the LightningIndexer computation formula is as follows: $$ \text{Top-}k\left\{[1]{1\times g}@\left[(W@[1]{1\times S{k}})\odot\text{ReLU}\left(Q{index}@K{index}^T\right)\right]\right\} $$ The computation can be divided into the following process: 1. Compute the matrix multiplication: $S = Q{index}@K{index}^T$. 2. Compute the activation function: $S'=\text{ReLU}(S)$. 3. Compute the broadcast multiplication: $SW=(W@[1]{1\times S{k}})\odot S'$. 4. Perform a Reduce operation along the G axis: $Score=[1]{1\times g}@ SW$. 5. Perform the $\text{Top-}k$ computation on $Score$. Obtain the top $k$ values and return their corresponding indexes. In the Prefill scenario or the Decode scenario with MTP enabled, the $Q{index}$ values corresponding to multiple tokens are combined for unified computation. The following sections do not distinguish between $Q{index}$ values for one token and multiple tokens. Actual development must fully use the features of Ascend hardware to achieve better performance. The following sections describe the current solution and its implementation in detail. LI Operator Tiling Design The operator tiling design determines whether storage space is fully used and therefore affects overall computing power utilization and operator performance. For LightningIndexer, this section describes inter-core and intra-core tiling designs. Because the on-chip buffer space is limited, every computation must be partitioned into blocks. Therefore, the basic block size for one iteration, namely the inter-core tiling design, must be determined. The current LightningIndexer operator sets the basic block size to $(512,512)$. One iteration computes 512 rows to reduce repeated movement of the right matrix. For example, when $g=64$, eight tokens are combined for unified computation. The iteration also completes computation at a granularity of 512 in the $S{k}$ direction. This value keeps pipeline startup and completion overhead controllable and allows computation to hide the synchronization overhead between Cube and Vector cores. The intra-core tiling design uses the following solution: The L1 space is divided into the following parts: The $Q{index}$ matrix remains resident: $512\times 128\times2\text{ Bytes}=128\text{ KB}$. The basic block at the L1 level is $(512,128)$. During actual computation, data can be moved at a finer granularity. Each operation moves only $(256,128)$ data to L1 to reduce movement startup overhead. The $K{index}$ matrix uses three buffers cyclically: $3\times256\times 128\times2\text{ Bytes}=192\text{ KB}$. The basic block at the L1 level is $(256,128)$. L0A, L0B, and L0C enable double buffering and are divided into $2\times32\text{ KB},2\times32\text{ KB},2\times64\text{ KB}$, respectively. The matrix block sizes moved into L0A and L0B each time are both $(128,128)$. This setting is friendly to Ascend hardware and improves computing power utilization. This method ensures that $Q{index}$ only needs to be moved once during computation and reduces repeated movement of the $K{index}$ matrix. Assume that the basic block size of the $Q{index}$ matrix at the L1 level is $(128,128)$ and the total number of tokens in the row direction is $Sq$. The $K{index}$ matrix must then be moved $\lceil Sq/128\rceil$ times. Selecting a basic block size of $(512,128)$ reduces the number of repeated movements to $\lceil Sq/512\rceil$. Starting the matrix multiplication in the first computation process requires moving the right matrix. Allocating multiple buffers to the right matrix removes computation process stalls caused by buffer occupancy. Therefore, allocating three buffers to $K{index}$ improves movement efficiency during the bandwidth ramp-up period. LI Pipeline Design The LightningIndexer computation process has only two stages: matrix multiplication and ReLU operations ($C1$), followed by multiple vector computations ($V1$). To prevent serial execution of the stages, preload $C1$ once so that the pipelines hide each other. In-Path ReLU Implementation LightningIndexer first performs matrix multiplication and then applies ReLU to the result. Because matrix multiplication and ReLU run on different compute units, a basic implementation must move the matrix multiplication result from the Cube core to the Vector core. However, the FixP component of the Cube core on the Ascend NPU provides in-path ReLU. After matrix multiplication is complete, ReLU can run directly during data movement without an explicit ReLU computation. In addition to ReLU, the FixP component provides more powerful functions. For details, refer to Basic API: FixP (Chinese). Top-k Instruction Implementation The core function of the LightningIndexer fused operator is to efficiently select the $k$ indexes with the highest scores, such as 2048 indexes, for each token in a sequence containing hundreds of thousands of tokens. The operator must compute Top-$k$ accurately and cannot use an approximation algorithm. The current solution performs a full sort based on sorting instructions supported by Ascend. The Top-$k$ computation has three steps: Group sorting: Use the VBS32 instruction to perform a stable descending sort of every 32 tokens by $Score$. Output the sorted vector and corresponding index vector until all tokens in the sequence are sorted in groups. Merging: Use the VMS4v2 instruction to merge up to four groups, which can also be two or three groups, of sorted vectors with lengths of 32, 128, or 512 until the merged vector length reaches 2048. The merged vectors remain in stable descending order by $Score$. The length of the output vector equals the sum of the four input vector lengths. The instruction also outputs the corresponding index vector. Reduction: Use the exhaustion mode of the VMS4v2 instruction. When all available data in an input vector has been read, the sorting instruction immediately pauses. Merge up to four sorted vectors with a length of 2048. Extract the vector consisting of the first $k=2048$ parameters and repeatedly perform Top-$k$ computation with the remaining sorted vectors that have not participated in the merge sort. Continue until all sorted vectors with a length of 2048 have been compared to obtain the indexes corresponding to the 2048 highest scores across all vectors. Assume that the context length is $Sk$. The computation workload of the group sorting and merging steps is $4Sk$. The computation workload of the reduction step cannot be evaluated precisely. A simulation using a normal distribution and the Monte Carlo method shows that the first computation workload is close to $4k$. Starting from the second computation, a vector containing $k$ larger values already participates in the computation, so the computation workload decreases sharply until it approaches the exhaustion limit $k$. Simulation analysis expresses the workload of this part as $0.36Sk+3.32k$. Therefore, the total computation workload of the Top-$k$ process is $totalCount = 4.36Sk + 3.32k$. LI Quantization Support The current LightningIndexer operator supports Per-Token-Head quantized inputs. Both the input $Q{index}$ and $K{index}$ are quantized to the INT8 data type to address excessive memory usage in long-sequence scenarios. For a token, LightningIndexerQuant, which supports quantized inputs, receives the Index Query $Q{index}^{INT8}\in\R^{g\times d}$ and its dequantization coefficient $Scale{Q}\in\R^{g\times1}$. Given the context Index Key $K{index}^{INT8}\in\R^{S{k}\times d}$ and its dequantization coefficient $Scale{K}\in\R^{S{k}\times1}$, and $W\in\R^{g\times 1}$, where $g$ is the group size corresponding to GQA, $d$ is the dimension of each head, and $S{k}$ is the context length, the LightningIndexerQuant computation formula is as follows: $$ \text{Top-}k\left\{[1]{1\times g}@\left[(W@[1]{1\times S{k}})\odot\text{ReLU}\left(\left(ScaleQ@ScaleK^T\right)\odot\left(Q{index}^{INT8}@{(K{index}^{INT8})}^T\right)\right)\right]\right\} $$ Mat-Duce Algorithm The LightningIndexerQuant operator uses the Mat-Duce algorithm. This algorithm applies mathematical transformations to adjust the computation logic and uses matrix multiplication to implement reduction computation. It fully uses the in-path capabilities of the Cube cores on the A3 chip and implements most computations of LightningIndexerQuant within the Cube cores. Because $ScaleQ,ScaleK\ge0$, let $\tilde{W} = ScaleQ \odot W \in \mathbb{R}^{g\times1}$. The LightningIndexerQuant computation formula can be equivalently transformed as follows: $$\text{Top-}k\left\{\tilde{W}^T @ \text{ReLU}(Q{index}^{INT8}@(K{index}^{INT8})^T) \odot ScaleK^T\right\}.$$ The corresponding computation process is as follows: 1. Preprocess the data. Compute $\tilde{W} = ScaleQ \odot W$ in the UB, cast the result to FP16, and write it to the GM. 2. Compute $S^{INT32} = Q{index}^{INT8}@(K{index}^{INT8})^T$ in the Cube core. The data type of $S$ is INT32. 3. Use the FixP DEQF16 instruction to compute $S^{FP16}=\text{FP16}(S^{INT32}/1024)$. Multiply the INT32 result by $1/1024$ and convert it to the FP16 data type. Here, $1/1024$ prevents numeric overflow without affecting the final Top-$k$ result. 4. Continue using the in-path ReLU function of FixP to compute $S'=\text{ReLU}(S^{FP16})$ and move the result to L1 for the next matrix multiplication. 5. Compute $P=\tilde{W}^T@S'$ in the Cube core and write the result to the GM. This step simultaneously performs dequantization for $ScaleQ$, row-wise scaling for $W$, and summation of the results from different heads. 6. Read $P$ from the GM into the Vector core and perform dequantization for $ScaleK$: $Score = P \odot ScaleK^T$. 7. Compute Top-$k$ for $Score$ in the Vector core. The following figure shows the computation process: Compared with the standard implementation, this solution uses mathematical transformations to implement most vector operations in the Cube core in step 5. It also fully uses the FixP in-path quantization, activation, and movement (Chinese) capabilities to convert the quantized matrix multiplication result from INT32 to FP16 in steps 3 and 4, enabling the second half-precision matrix multiplication and significantly improving operator performance. SparseFlashAttention As the context length of large models increases, Sparse Attention becomes increasingly important. This technique substantially reduces the computation workload by computing only critical parts. However, it introduces extensive discrete memory access, increasing data movement time and affecting overall performance. Sparse Attention computation can be expressed as follows: $$ \text{softmax}(\frac{Q@\tilde{K}^T}{\sqrt{dk}})@\tilde{V} $$ Here, $\tilde{K},\tilde{V}$ are important Key and Value values obtained by a selection algorithm such as LightningIndexer. They generally have sparse or block-sparse characteristics. $dk$ is the dimension of each head of $Q,\tilde{K}$. The released SparseFlashAttention operator is a new operator for Sparse Attention. It provides detailed optimizations for discrete memory access by reducing instructions and aggregating data movement. The SparseFlashAttention operator uses the computation process of FlashAttention , which consists of four stages: $C1$: $Q@K^T$. $V1$: online softmax. $C2$: $P@V$. $V2$: rescaling $O$. SFA Operator Tiling Design The basic block size for one SparseFlashAttention iteration is $(256,512)$. The intra-core tiling design of the operator is as follows: The L1 space is divided into the following parts: The $Q/P$ matrices reuse the space at different times, where the $P$ matrix is the softmax result: $4\times128\times 288\times2\text{ Bytes}=288\text{ KB}$. In a $C1$ or $C2$ stage, the left matrix is moved to L1 four times and remains resident in L1 during one iteration. Each movement of the $Q$ matrix has a size of $(128,288)$, and each movement of the $P$ matrix has a size of $(128,256)$. The $K/V$ matrices use three buffers cyclically: $3\times128\times 288\times2\text{ Bytes}=216\text{ KB}$. Each movement of the $K$ matrix has a size of $(128,288)$, and each movement of the $V$ matrix has a size of $(256,128)$. L0A, L0B, and L0C enable double buffering and are divided into $2\times32\text{ KB},2\times32\text{ KB},2\times64\text{ KB}$, respectively. In the $C1$ stage, the matrix block sizes moved into L0A and L0B are $(128,96)$ and $(96,128)$, respectively. In the $C2$ stage, the matrix block sizes moved into L0A and L0B are both $(128,128)$. SFA Pipeline Design For complex fused operators, efficient collaboration between Cube and Vector cores is the main challenge in fully using hardware computing power. Pipeline overlapping is the core scheduling mechanism that connects the two types of cores, and its design directly determines operator performance. Because SparseFlashAttention uses the AMLA (Chinese) algorithm, it has only three computation stages, $C1,V1,C2$, in addition to the final normalization operation. Compared with LightningIndexer, SparseFlashAttention has a more complex computation process with more dependencies. A basic pipeline layout introduces many bubbles during computation. As shown in the upper half of the following figure, data dependencies between different stages of the computation process introduce many idle periods in both Cube and Vector streams, resulting in low computing power utilization. This operator uses a preload pipeline layout to eliminate dependencies. During the steady-state period, excluding pipeline startup and completion, the Cube stream completely hides the Vector stream. The lower half of the following figure shows the result. This method provides a significant performance improvement compared with the basic pipeline layout. Memory Access Optimization Actual memory access behavior can be divided into instruction delivery and data movement. For an Attention operator in a non-sparse scenario, data access is generally continuous. Therefore, one data movement takes longer than instruction delivery, enabling multiple continuous memory accesses and high memory access bandwidth. For discrete memory access in Sparse Attention, however, the duration of a single memory access decreases substantially and may be shorter than instruction delivery. This causes severe instruction delivery stalls, as shown in the following figure. Attention computation starts from the Cube core, which also issues the memory access instructions. Based on the $1:2$ ratio of Cube cores to Vector cores on the A3 chip, use Vector cores to issue memory access instructions and double the instruction delivery efficiency. The amount of data in a single memory access also affects the actual bandwidth. A discrete memory access transfers a small amount of data, which causes the data movement itself to take longer than expected. To address this issue, aggregate discrete data points in pairs and use the srcGap (Chinese) parameter to implement paired data access and improve memory access bandwidth, as shown in the figure. SFA Next Feature Future work will explore quantization support for the SparseFlashAttention operator to address excessive memory usage in long-context scenarios. Usability Improvements TilingKey Templating TilingKey distinguishes different operator implementations by separating code so that different branches process different features. However, TilingKey values are difficult to remember and understand because they are usually long numbers without clear meanings, which severely affects code readability and programmability. To improve operator code readability and reduce development difficulty, the two new open-source operators use the Ascend C tiling template programming method instead of conventional TilingKey programming. Developers only need to define template parameters and their combinations to manage branches. This method reduces dependency on specific TilingKey values and improves code management efficiency. For details, refer to Tiling Template Programming (Chinese). Core Partition Computation Offloading Tiling is the preprocessing stage before operator execution. During this stage, the host computes the workspace usage, core partitioning strategy, and other information required for operator execution. Host-bound issues may occur in single-operator mode. Static graph offloading (Chinese) avoids this issue. However, for Attention operators, different batches in the actual input may have different context lengths. Therefore, computing the core partitioning strategy during tiling has a value dependency on the specific context length (actualSeqLengths). This prevents Attention operators from being completely offloaded to static graph execution, producing too many small static subgraphs in the entire network and introducing substantial static subgraph scheduling overhead. Core partition computation also requires copying the corresponding data from the device to the host, resulting in poor end-to-end network performance. To address this issue, Attention operators use a tiling offloading solution that offloads core partition computation to the AICPU on the device. During end-to-end network execution, core partition computation starts when its dependent data is ready and can run in parallel with the operator execution stream. However, when core partition computation depends on a preceding operator, this method still cannot prevent an execution interruption. From a usage perspective, this approach introduces additional AICPU tiling logic. The custom operator process must separately develop the corresponding tiling function and work with offloaded graph execution scheduling. The function is complex and the invocation chain is long, making custom development and debugging difficult. The released LightningIndexer and SparseFlashAttention operators further optimize tiling offloading by offloading the core partition computation process from the AICPU to the AICore. This optimization simplifies the invocation chain, eliminates scheduling overhead caused by tiling dependencies on preceding operators, and simplifies development and debugging.

A3推荐部署策略如下图所示，Prefill使用M个节点部署，Decode使用N个节点部署，每个节点包含8卡。其中BF16场景下，推荐根据资源数量、SLA等约束，M在48，N在416内动态调整。 Prefill并行策略 DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp新增的DSA主要面向长序列推理场景，Prefill阶段设备内存OOM风险较高，而且推理服务部署时TTFT也会面临巨大的挑战，因此优化内存占用和TTFT是并行策略设计的主要目的。 如果沿用DeepSeek R1 Blog里的Attention DP策略，每个rank都需要推理不同的超长序列，总计算量较大，TTFT较高，用户体验较差。 Tensor Parallel(TP)是优化推理TTFT的重要手段，但DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp中DSA新增的Indexer模块计算量和$S^2$成正比，是长序列场景下的主要瓶颈，该模块针对head轴做了Reduce Sum操作，TP切分会产生大量的通信开销，影响整网性能。 综合上述两点，DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp模型Prefill Attention选用Context Parallel(CP)并行，多个rank均摊长序列的计算，单rank的计算量和activation内存都较小，TTFT较为可控，用户体验更好。MoE模块则沿用DeepSeek-V3.1的EP并行，兼顾吞吐与时延。 Prefill的并行策略可以设计为下图形式： Embedding并行策略 为了节省Embedding Table的内存占用，Embedding计算使用TP并行，tpsize控制在单Node内，之后通过AllReduce聚合。 Attention并行策略 Attention整体选用CP并行，以64K输入推理为例，每个rank处理64K/cpsize=1K个token，在计算完kv之后，对所有CP域的kv token进行AllGather，得到完整的kv结果。每个rank拿到64K/cpsize的q token和完整的kv token，进行后续的Attention计算。 Attention计算需要遵循因果注意力，如果CP简单按照rank顺序进行切片可能会面临计算负载均衡问题。如第一个rank关注到的历史kv token很少，计算量较小；最后一个rank关注到的历史kv token较多，计算量较大。为了降低负载不均带来的影响，需要将输入的inputids按照cpsize2进行切片，如上图右侧所示，每个rank负责计算头尾对称的两个切片，每层Lightning Indexer和Sparse Flash Attention计算前通过Token重排将kv还原回因果顺序。 考虑到Oproj模块内存占用较大，本实践选择对其局部进行TP切分，因此Oproj前后引入AlltoAll和ReduceScatter算子。 MoE并行策略 MoE模块沿用了和DeepSeekV3相同的EP并行部署，EP复用CP通信域。 LM Head并行策略 为了节省LM Head的内存占用，LM Head选用TP切分，tpsize控制在单Node内。 LMHead模块采用TP切分，同样需要在TP域内做AllGather，但此处为整个CP域内的AllGather，并通过Token重排将最终输入LMHead的feature map还原到原始序列排布。 Decode并行策略 Decode阶段依旧沿用DeepSeek-V3.1的部署策略，选用Attention DP + MoE EP部署。 特别地，由于Oproj和LMHead权重内存较大，且在Decode阶段表现为明显的访存瓶颈，本实践选用局部TP并行。同时为了降低设备内存占用，Embedding层同样使用TP切分。为了尽可能地减小TP并行带来的通信开销，TP域控制在高速互联HCCS域内。 MTP DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp依然提供了原生的Multi-Token Prediction(MTP)机制，MTP机制允许在一次主模型推理过程中同时推理多个Token，在相似的数据搬运下，进行更多的计算，以充分利用芯片的算力，提升模型等效时延和吞吐。 DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp由于采用了新的DSA结构，MTP加速相对于DeepSeek-V3.1会更复杂。Full Attention场景的MLA无论是否使用MTP，其KV 使能W8A8C8量化后，由于受限于设备内存，在长序列场景 batch size依然无法进一步提升。为了解决设备内存紧张问题，可将占比较高的MLA Full KVCache内存卸载到Host内存上，完成KVCache的Offload，释放设备内存压力，达到提高batch size的目的。 KVCache Offload方案涉及Prefill阶段和Decode阶段。 Prefill Stage Prefill阶段，在设备上只申请一层MLA KVCache，同时每卡在Host内存上申请61层KVCache内存。MLA计算完后，通过多流的方式将当前层设备上的KVCache卸载到Host侧的内存上。 Decode Stage Decode阶段，每一层计算得到的当前Token的Cache更新到Host内存上，新增的 GatherSelectionKvCache 算子，根据Lightning Indexer模块返回的TopK个相关Token的位置信息，从Host侧的Full KVCache选出对应的需要参与计算的kv token，送给后续的SFA计算。 其中 GatherSelectionKvCache 算子充分利用了前后Token在同一层上TopK 命中率（相似度）特性，将已经在设备上的Cache做了复用。也即如果当前步的TopK=2048个kv token和前一步的TopK=2048个kv token有60%一样，那只需要从Host侧读取40%的没有复用的kv token，60%可以复用的kv token直接从设备上读取，从而减少了H2D的耗时。 Benchmark W8A8C8 基于 Atlas A3，本实践对 DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp 与 DeepSeek-V3.1 W8A8C8 版本进行了性能Benchmark NPU DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp Inference Optimization Practice The DeepSeek team released its latest model, DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp. The model uses the sparse DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA) architecture to improve long-sequence computation efficiency and reduce inference costs. Long-context scenarios and the new DSA structure jointly introduce new requirements for inference optimization systems. This document describes Prefill and Decode inference optimizations for DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp on an A3 cluster. It first analyzes the structural characteristics of DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp, implements a model parallel strategy friendly to long sequences, and designs new NPU fused kernels and multi-stream parallel optimizations. Based on these optimizations, this practice deployed the DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp BF16 model on day 0 and the W8A8C16 model on day 1. It currently supports C8 quantization and will continue to implement low-bit quantization algorithms. Conventional 4K to 8K sequences inherit the existing DeepSeek-V3.1 optimizations. In long-sequence inference scenarios from 16K to 166K, DSA sparsity provides benefits and enables performance that exceeds DeepSeek-V3.1. Both the model and fused kernels are open source. For the new Lightning Indexer (LI) and Sparse Flash Attention (SFA) operators in the DSA structure, this open-source release includes not only an AscendC implementation but also the first release of the in-house PyPTO implementation. Developers can program dynamic-shape operators with only a few hundred lines of code. PyPTO is a programming system for large fused operators released by CANN and provides a MegaKernel-oriented programming paradigm. Its core concept uses Tensor/Tile as the basic data representation and describes and assembles a complete computation process through a series of basic Tensor operations. A human-in-the-loop and white-box approach fully uses SRAM space and enables efficient use of multiple cores. The open-source TileLang community has also integrated with the CANN software stack and supports the new LI and SFA operators in the DSA structure. Highlights The overall deployment strategy retains the large-EP parallel solution of DeepSeek. For the sparse DSA structure, it adds a CP parallel strategy friendly to long sequences to balance latency and throughput. The model inference code (Chinese) is open source and has also been adapted to the mainstream open-source inference frameworks vLLM and SGLang. NPU LI and SFA fused kernels are implemented in AscendC to realize the potential of sparse computation. The AscendC kernel technical documentation and code are open source in the corresponding operator directories of the CANN/ops-transformer repository , including Lightning Indexer and Sparse Flash Attention . NPU DSA is implemented based on the in-house PyPTO framework to improve fused operator programming usability. It implements not only an LI fused kernel but also a larger Decode Attention fusion scope. The PyPTO kernel technical documentation and code (Chinese) are open source. The open-source TileLang community supports the LI and SFA operators in the DSA structure. The TileLang kernel technical documentation and code (Chinese) are open source. Based on the preceding optimizations, CANN supported DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp BF16 inference deployment on day 0 and Int8 quantization on day 1. The reference performance for Prefill and Decode is as follows: using lossless BF16 precision, the TTFT of a 128K long sequence on 64 cards is less than 2 seconds without a cache hit, and TPOT is less than 30 ms. In the W8A8C8 quantization scenario, TPOT for a 128K long sequence on 64 cards is less than 20 ms. Outline DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp vs V3.1 Parallel Strategies MTP Fused Kernels Quantization Strategy Multi-Stream Parallel Optimization KVCache Offload Benchmark Future Plan DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp vs V3.1 Compared with DeepSeek-V3.1, DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp primarily adds the sparse Lightning Indexer module, which sparsely selects the TopK tokens from a long sequence for attention computation. Weight memory analysis Lightning Indexer is a lightweight MQA-like structure that adds three Linear layers: qb proj, wk proj, and weight proj. Their weight sizes are as follows: $$ \begin{aligned} \mathrm{Param}{\mathrm{q\b\proj}}&=\mathrm{q\lora\rank} \times \mathrm{Indexer\head\num} \times \mathrm{Indexer\head\dim} \\ \mathrm{Param}{\mathrm{wk\proj}} &= \mathrm{hidden\size} \times \mathrm{Indexer\head\dim}\\ \mathrm{Param}{\mathrm{weight\proj}} &= \mathrm{hidden\size} \times \mathrm{Indexer\head\num} \end{aligned} $$ Across all layers, the number of weight parameters increases by approximately 0.85B. KVCache memory analysis To preserve model quality, DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp still caches the complete MLA Full KVCache. To improve inference efficiency and prevent repeated computation of the Indexer Key during Decode, it must also add an Indexer Key Cache. Its memory size is as follows: $$ \mathrm{batch\size}\times \mathrm{kv\length} \times \mathrm{Indexer\head\dim} \times \mathrm{storage\bytes} \times \mathrm{num\layers} $$ For example, when each rank processes four batches with a sequence length of 64K, the additional Indexer Key Cache in the BF16 scenario is approximately 4 GB. MLA Naive vs Absorb During Prefill, using one batch of 64K inference as an example, Lightning Indexer selects TopK=2048 KV tokens for each Q token. The MLA computation process has three options: Solution 1: MLA Naive + Sparse Mask. Prefill MLA uses Naive mode, consistent with the original DeepSeek V3. Each Q token computes Attention with all historical KV tokens. An Attention Mask filters out tokens that do not belong to TopK before softmax. The shapes of the two BatchMatmul operations in Attention are as follows: Solution 1 Batch M K N :---------: :---: :--: :--: :--: BMM1(QK^T) 1128 64K 192 64K BMM2(PV) 1128 64K 64K 128 This solution has the same computation workload as the original Full Attention, but it cannot obtain the sparse computation benefits of DSA and has poor performance in long-sequence scenarios. Solution 2: MLA Naive + Sparse Attention. Prefill MLA uses Naive mode, and each Q token computes Attention with TopK=2048 KV tokens. Solution 2 Batch M K N :---------: :--------: :--: :--: :--: BMM1(QK^T) 1\64K128 1 192 2048 BMM2(PV) 1\64K128 1 2048 128 Solution 2 has a smaller BMM computation workload, which is 64K/2048=32 times smaller than the original Full Attention, but it has the following issues: The M axis of BMM is 1, resulting in low matrix multiplication efficiency. Compared with the original Full Attention, the HBM memory access volume of BMM increases by 2048 times, causing a memory access bottleneck. Solution 3: MLA Absorb + Sparse Attention. Prefill MLA uses Absorb mode, consistent with Decode. Similarly, each Q token computes Attention with TopK=2048 KV tokens. Solution 3 Batch M K N :---------: :----: :--: :--: :--: BMM1(QK^T) 1\64K 128 576 2048 BMM2(PV) 1\64K 128 2048 512 Solution 3 and Solution 2 differ as follows: Solution 3 increases the computation workload by approximately three times, but its BMM M axis is 128, which is more friendly to matrix multiplication. Solution 3 reduces HBM memory access by dozens of times compared with Solution 2, resulting in a shorter memory access duration. Considering computation and memory access time and long-sequence application scenarios, this practice uses Solution 3, MLA Absorb + Sparse Attention, for Prefill deployment. This solution unifies the MLA computation flows of Prefill and Decode. To achieve better inference latency and throughput for long sequences and DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp, this practice designs an NPU-friendly parallel strategy and implements NPU Lightning Indexer (LI) and Sparse Flash Attention (SFA) fused kernels. The following sections provide details. Parallel Strategies The following figure shows the recommended deployment strategy for Atlas A3. Prefill uses M nodes, Decode uses N nodes, and each node contains eight cards. In the BF16 scenario, dynamically adjust M within 4 to 8 and N within 4 to 16 based on constraints such as the number of resources and the SLA. Prefill Parallel Strategy The new DSA in DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp primarily targets long-sequence inference scenarios. During Prefill, device memory has a high OOM risk, and TTFT also presents a major challenge when deploying inference services. Therefore, the main goals of parallel strategy design are to optimize memory usage and TTFT. If the Attention DP strategy in the DeepSeek R1 Blog is retained, each rank must infer a different ultra-long sequence. This approach has a large total computation workload, high TTFT, and a poor user experience. Tensor Parallel (TP) is an important method for optimizing inference TTFT. However, the computation workload of the new Indexer module in DSA is proportional to $S^2$, making it the main bottleneck in long-sequence scenarios. This module performs a Reduce Sum operation along the head axis. TP partitioning produces substantial communication overhead and affects end-to-end network performance. Considering these two points, Prefill Attention in DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp uses Context Parallel (CP). Multiple ranks share long-sequence computation. Each rank has a smaller computation workload and activation memory, resulting in controllable TTFT and a better user experience. The MoE module retains the EP parallelism of DeepSeek-V3.1 to balance throughput and latency. The Prefill parallel strategy can be designed as follows: Embedding parallel strategy To reduce the memory occupied by the Embedding Table, Embedding computation uses TP parallelism. tpsize remains within a single node, followed by AllReduce aggregation. Attention parallel strategy Attention uses CP parallelism as a whole. Using inference with a 64K input as an example, each rank processes 64K/cpsize=1K tokens. After KV computation, perform AllGather on the KV tokens in all CP domains to obtain the complete KV result. Each rank receives 64K/cpsize Q tokens and the complete KV tokens for subsequent Attention computation. Attention computation must follow causal attention. If CP simply partitions data in rank order, the computation load may be unbalanced. For example, the first rank attends to fewer historical KV tokens and has a smaller computation workload, while the last rank attends to more historical KV tokens and has a larger computation workload. To reduce the impact of load imbalance, partition the input inputids by cpsize2. As shown on the right of the preceding figure, each rank computes two symmetric partitions at the beginning and end. Before Lightning Indexer and Sparse Flash Attention compute in each layer, token rearrangement restores KV to causal order. Because the Oproj module occupies a large amount of memory, this practice applies local TP partitioning to it. Therefore, AlltoAll and ReduceScatter operators are introduced before and after Oproj. MoE parallel strategy The MoE module retains the EP parallel deployment used by DeepSeekV3. EP reuses the CP communication domain. LM Head parallel strategy To reduce LM Head memory usage, LM Head uses TP partitioning, and tpsize remains within a single node. The LMHead module uses TP partitioning and also requires AllGather within the TP domain. However, this operation is an AllGather across the entire CP domain. Token rearrangement restores the feature map finally input to LMHead to the original sequence layout. Decode Parallel Strategy The Decode stage retains the deployment strategy of DeepSeek-V3.1 and uses Attention DP + MoE EP deployment. In particular, the Oproj and LMHead weights occupy a large amount of memory and present clear memory access bottlenecks during Decode. This practice uses local TP parallelism. The Embedding layer also uses TP partitioning to reduce device memory usage. To minimize communication overhead from TP parallelism, the TP domain remains within the high-speed HCCS interconnect domain. MTP DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp still provides a native Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) mechanism. MTP allows multiple tokens to be inferred during one main-model inference process. With similar data movement, it performs more computation to fully use chip computing power and improve the effective model latency and throughput. Because DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp uses the new DSA structure, MTP acceleration is more complex than in DeepSeek-V3.1. In a Full Attention scenario, MLA moves the same amount of KV Cache data with or without MTP. Therefore, MTP increases the computation-to-memory-access ratio and improves computing power utilization. The computing power utilization of the MLA operator in CANN can exceed 70% in the MTP1 scenario. For Sparse Flash Attention in DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp, however, each Q token selects 2048 active KV tokens. In an extreme case, the MTP1 scenario must move twice as much KV Cache data as the non-MTP scenario, increasing the cost of discrete memory access. Its K Cache movement is similar to dense MLA, so the MTP mechanism can increase the computation-to-memory-access ratio. In addition, sparse DSA computation significantly reduces the long-sequence computation workload and decreases the proportion of Attention in the complete inference process. The remaining operators, such as Matmul, can achieve better computation-to-memory-access ratios. Therefore, MTP provides significant acceleration for the complete inference process. Fused Kernels The DSA computation process consists of five parts: MLAProlog, IndexerProlog, Lightning Indexer, Sparse Flash Attention, and MLAEpilog, as shown in the following figure: Lightning Indexer: It includes Score Batchmatmul, ReLU, ReduceSum, TopK, and other operations. In long-sequence scenarios, the TopK operation becomes a bottleneck. Pipeline overlapping can use the TopK computation time to hide the time of other operations and obtain computation pipeline benefits. Sparse Flash Attention: It selects TopK related tokens from the complete KVCache and computes sparse Flash Attention. The main duration bottleneck is discrete aggregated memory access. Pipeline parallel acceleration can use this duration to hide the time of other operations. MLAProlog and IndexerProlog: They include Q/KV LoRA, RoPE, Norm, KVCache updates, and other operations, providing substantial pipeline parallelism between Cube and Vector cores. MLAEpilog: It includes Oproj and V dimension expansion operations. The NPU implementations of lightningindexer , its quantized version quantlightningindexer , sparseflashattention , and its quantized version kvquantsparseflashattention are implemented and open source in the CANN/ops-transformer repository. Quantization Strategy Compared with BF16 inference, Int8 quantization effectively reduces end-to-end latency and improves system throughput. This practice currently supports W8A8C8/W4A8C8 quantization. The quantization architecture is as follows: The four quantized fused operators MLAProlog, MLAEpilog, IndexerProlog, and LightningIndexer are as follows: MLAProlog: All Linear operations except Qbproj, which uses W8A8, are not quantized. KVCache is quantized to C8. Sparse Flash Attention: KVCache uses Int8 storage and BF16 computation. IndexerProlog: All Linear operations except Qbproj, which uses W8A8, are not quantized. Indexer Q uses A8 quantization, and Indexer Cache uses C8 quantization. Lightning Indexer: BatchMatmtul uses Int8 computation. MoE: Routed experts use W8A8/W4A8 quantization, and shared experts use W8A8 quantization. MLAEpilog: Oproj uses W8A8 quantization. LMHead: It is not currently quantized. Note: W8A8: W8 indicates that weights use static Per-Channel Int8 quantization, and A8 indicates that data uses dynamic Per-Token Int8 quantization. A8C8: A8 indicates that Q in Lightning Indexer uses dynamic Per-Token-Head Int8 quantization, and Indexer Cache uses dynamic Per-Token-Head Int8 quantization. MLAEpilog: Oproj uses W8A8 quantization. KVCache C8: KVCache uses dynamic Per-Token-Head-Tile-128 Int8 quantization. W8A8C8 quantizes fewer linear layers. For MLA linear layers, only qbproj and woproj are quantized. For Indexer linear layers, only wqbproj is quantized. The main reason is that the IndexerProlog fused operator is designed to output FP16 from weightsproj without quantization. Therefore, Linear operations associated with the MLA input are not quantized, allowing the same BF16 data to be input to IndexerProlog and MLAProlog. In addition, the MLAProlog KVCache quantization strategy dynamically stores data in 8-bit precision and computes in 16-bit precision. In ultra-long-sequence scenarios, W8A8C8 quantization has nearly lossless precision while reducing weight memory usage by two times. MLA C8 storage and 16-bit computation provide memory benefits and enable high throughput. LightningIndexer A8C8 provides computation benefits, reduces LI computation latency, and also optimizes TTFT and TPOT. For DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp, the W4A8C8 quantized version uses a learning-based quantization algorithm to optimize the Clamp parameter, mitigating the difficulty of quantizing W4A8 outliers and achieving high quantized model accuracy. The W4A8C8 version also reduces MoE weight memory by two times compared with W8A8C8. Therefore, in a large-EP scenario, the W4A8 MoEGMM operator allows one card to store more experts, reducing resource usage, optimizing the computation-to-memory-access ratio, and enabling single-node deployment.
