NPU DeepSeek-V4 AutoFuse Automatic Operator Fusion Optimization As AI model architectures become increasingly complex, dynamic, fine-grained small-operator combinations have become a mainstream design pattern, especially in MoE (Mixture of Experts) and multimodal architectures. In the latest model released by DeepSeek, hcPre and hcPost use flexible small-operator structures, and similar structures will also become common in future multimodal scenarios. These operator structures are flexible and varied and can be combined in many ways. If optimization depends on conventional manually written fused operators, development efficiency cannot keep pace with rapid model iteration. Therefore, automatic operator fusion is technically necessary and urgent. The Inductor component of the PyTorch framework provides basic operator-fusion and compilation capabilities in graph mode. Its design is compatible with the existing PyTorch ecosystem and provides good software continuity. However, NPUs and GPUs differ fundamentally in memory architecture, compute units, and parallel mechanisms. Directly reusing GPU-oriented optimization strategies cannot fully use NPU hardware potential. To implement efficient NPU-specific fusion while retaining the overall Inductor workflow and interfaces, just-in-time (JIT) operator-generation capabilities for NPUs are required. The AutoFuse component integrated into the CANN framework is therefore deeply optimized for NPU architecture features and automatically maps and generates efficient NPU operator code from computation graphs. This component maintains collaboration and compatibility with Inductor and further uses architecture-aware fusion strategies, memory-access optimization, and instruction scheduling to substantially improve operator-fusion efficiency on NPUs, supporting high-performance deployment of complex models on NPU platforms. This technical report describes automatic Vector-operator fusion for NPUs and integration with Inductor. It also briefly introduces model benefits and enablement methods. Highlights Easy to use: Add one line of code to the PyTorch frontend to enable the feature. Performance improvement: Use NPU-friendly operator-generation technologies to improve out-of-the-box model performance. NPU-friendly, template-normalized schedule technology. Hardware-modeling-based operator Tiling technology with dynamic solving. AscendC operator kernel code-generation technology expressed in AscendLoopIR. Generalization and completeness: Currently, 46 of the 152 LoopIR operations are supported. The remaining operations will be added progressively to achieve complete parity with LoopIR. Outline NPU DeepSeek-V4 AutoFuse Automatic Operator Fusion Optimization Highlights Outline Inductor and AutoFuse Integration Operator-Generation Capabilities of AutoFuse JIT NPU-Friendly, Template-Normalized Schedule Technology Hardware-Modeling-Based Operator Tiling Technology with Dynamic Solving AscendC Operator Kernel Code-Generation Capabilities Expressed in AscendLoopIR Introduction to AscendLoopIR Inductor and AutoFuse Integration We extended Inductor's Codegen backend on NPUs. It converts InductorLoopIR to AscendLoopIR and invokes the AutoFuse module to select Schedule templates, reuse the UB, and tune Tiling, generating an efficient AscendC Kernel implementation. Reference implementation for Inductor integration with AutoFuse: inductornpuext Enabling in a Script 1. Import inductornpuext at the beginning of the script to register the AutoFuse-based Inductor compilation-backend extension. python import inductornpuext 2. Add the @torch.compile decorator to a function to compile it. Select the Inductor compilation scope based on the following rules: The graph structure within the compilation scope is stable and does not contain runtime branch selection, .item() memory synchronization, or similar behavior, preventing excessive Graph Breaks. Avoid an excessively large compilation scope. A large compilation scope is more likely to trigger recompilation because dynamo guards accumulate. Select a scope containing many Pointwise/Reduce computations. Inductor fuses such computations effectively and provides performance benefits with low compilation cost. Benefits for a Typical Code Segment In the DeepSeek-V4 model, the hcpost segment contains multiple small-operator combinations and is suitable for fusion optimization through AutoFuse. Compiling the hcpost function with the @torch.compile decorator substantially improves its execution performance. python @torch.compile def hcpost(x: torch.Tensor, residual: torch.Tensor, post: torch.Tensor, comb:torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor: y = post.unsqueeze(-1) x.unsqueeze(-2) + torch.sum(comb.unsqueeze(-1) residual.unsqueeze(-2), dim=2) return y.typeas(x) Performance data was tested on Ascend A3 using typical input shapes for hcpost execution. Model Component Uncompiled Latency Compiled Latency (dynamic=False) Performance Improvement Compiled Latency (dynamic=True) Performance Improvement -------- ---------- ------------------------- -------- ------------------------ -------- hcpost 30 us 7.5 us 4x 10 us 3x Operator-Generation Capabilities of AutoFuse JIT The core operator deliverables mainly contain kernel source code and Tiling source code. The AutoFuse module abstracts the operator code-generation process into several stages: 1. AscendLoopIR is the expression IR that abstracts the operator computation process and describes information such as the computation process, partitioning axes, and UB memory. 2. The Schedule component processes the Hint graph. Based on actual hardware capabilities, it provides a complete set of axis-partitioning strategies that cover all shape scenarios. Each specific partitioning strategy is carried by an AscendLoopIR called an impl graph. A set of impl graphs is used as input for the subsequent ATT and Codegen components. 3. The ATT component generates Tiling code for each impl graph. At runtime, the Tiling code evaluates the performance of the kernel template corresponding to each impl graph based on the specific shape, selects the optimal template, calculates partitioning parameters, and passes them to the kernel through tilingdata. 4. The Codegen component generates kernel code for each impl graph. Each impl graph corresponds to a template implementation. At runtime, tilingdata parameters determine the actual template to execute and the specific parameters for looped movement. The AutoFuse module source code is open-sourced and available here . NPU-Friendly, Template-Normalized Schedule Technology On an NPU, one hardware-unit operation can complete vector operations on a batch of data. To fully use hardware features, the vector-operation axis must be selected accurately. Given the hardware's multi-core capabilities and limited memory, the axis for inter-core partitioning and the axis for UB partitioning must also be selected. Correct selection of these three axes has a major impact on functionality and execution performance. Incorrect selection can easily cause functional problems such as UB overload or severe performance degradation. Different input shapes are usually best suited to different partitioning strategies. An operator implementation for a specific partitioning strategy is usually called a template. A general template simplifies the problem but cannot provide optimal performance. A detailed and extensive template library can provide maximum performance for different scenarios but makes template selection and code maintenance difficult. As a JIT operator-fusion technology, AutoFuse uses a balanced template-design solution. It provides multiple templates but abstracts and normalizes their applicable scenarios to control the template count. A limited number of templates provides excellent performance for most shapes. The Schedule module generates a set of ImplGraphs from the HintGraph, with each ImplGraph corresponding to one template implementation. Reduce Multi-Template Example Reduce fusion is one of the most common deep-learning scenarios and involves reduction operations such as Sum, Max, Min, Mean, Prod, Any, and All. Its core challenges are: Different handling of reduction and non-reduction axes. Multi-core load balancing. Optimization of subsequent computation after reduction. To support partitioning strategies for different shapes, the following three primary templates are summarized for different applicable scenarios. Template Type Trigger Condition Scheduling Characteristics Applicable Scenario --------------------- ----------------------------- ---------------------- -------------------- Full-load template Nodes after Reduce ≤4 and in AR/ARA mode Does not need to partition the Reduce axis Small data volume and simple graph structure General template Default selection UB partitioning + Block partitioning Medium-scale general scenarios R-axis inter-core template Large and partitionable data volume Uses the Reduce axis as the multi-core partitioning axis Large Reduce axis For a large R axis, designing only a general template causes UB overload. For small-data scenarios, selecting a general template affects performance because of high core-launch overhead. AutoSchedule Implementation The core idea of AutoSchedule is to abstract computation nodes in a fused graph into several ComputeTypes. Based on the NPU-specific partitioning method of each type, AxisGroup semantically groups axes, and Merge rules generate a common AxisGroup applicable to all nodes, ultimately producing multiple candidate partitioning solutions (TilingCases). ComputeType Abstraction and NPU Partitioning Methods Computation nodes in a fused graph are abstracted into several ComputeTypes, each with an optimal NPU-specific partitioning method: ComputeType Typical Operator NPU Partitioning Characteristics Axis-Grouping Characteristics --------------------- ---------------- -------------------------- ---------------------- Elementwise Add, Mul, Relu, and others Can be partitioned along any dimension and supports vectorization All axes are assigned to the Y group Broadcast Broadcast operator Must handle alignment across different shapes Computation axes are assigned to the Y group Reduce Sum, Max, Min, and others Reduction axes require special handling Reduction axes are assigned to the R group; non-reduction axes are assigned to the Y group Concat Concatenation The concatenation dimension cannot be partitioned Non-concatenation axes are assigned to the Y group AxisGroup Axis Grouping and Merge Rules To support the partitioning requirements of different ComputeTypes, define an AxisGroup structure for semantically grouping axes: X group: Axes that require complete data, such as a Concat concatenation axis. Data integrity must be preserved after partitioning. Y group: Primitive-operator computation axes, such as Elementwise, that can be flexibly partitioned in the UB. R group: Reduce reduction axes that use a dedicated multi-core reduction strategy. Because a fused graph may contain multiple ComputeTypes, Merge rules generate a common AxisGroup applicable to all nodes: Rule Type Merge Condition Result Description -------- ------------- ---------- ------------------------ Y+Y Both nodes are in the Y group Keep the Y group The computation characteristics are the same, so the groups can be merged directly Y+R A Y group encounters an R group Upgrade to the R group Reduce has a higher priority Y+YR A Y group encounters a YR group Extend to the YR group Supports reduction and non-reduction computation Generating TilingCase Candidate Solutions Based on the common AxisGroup, generate multiple candidate partitioning solutions (TilingCases). Each TilingCase defines a set of specific partitioning parameters: UB partitioning: Specifies the axis used to partition the UB Buffer. Block partitioning: Specifies the axis used for multi-core parallelism. Special Reduce handling: Specifies whether to enable multi-core partitioning along the R axis. Schedule Transformations Schedule performs specific scheduling transformations on each TilingCase, converting abstract partitioning solutions into specific scheduling operations: Transformation Type Description Effect --------------------------- -------------- ------------------------ TileSplit UB-level partitioning Loads data into the UB Buffer in blocks BlockSplit Block-level partitioning Implements multi-core parallelism ReduceBlockTiling Reduce-specific partitioning Optimizes multi-core execution of reduction operations Vectorization Identifies vectorizable axes Improves computation throughput Hardware-Modeling-Based Operator Tiling Technology with Dynamic Solving At compile time, Schedule technology provides a normalized template set for different shapes. At runtime, supporting technology must correctly select a template and output inter-core and UB partitioning results. Incorrect calculation results directly cause out-of-bounds UB access or severe performance degradation. In the AutoFuse component, ATT (Auto Tiling) performs this work. Preset performance modeling and multiple solution strategies ensure functional correctness and general performance in generalized scenarios while balancing solution accuracy and solution speed. Automatic Tiling Challenges 1. Difficulty of performance evaluation: Different templates output by Schedule vary substantially in GM discontinuity, UB discontinuity, whether vectorization-width alignment is used, loop count, computation bottleneck, and movement bottleneck. Therefore, their performance differs across fusion scenarios and Shapes. Automatic Tiling must accurately evaluate the execution performance of different templates. 2. Tradeoff between inter-core and block partitioning: Increasing the number of cores introduces additional core-launch overhead, including hardware and software overhead. Reducing the number of cores creates excessive single-core load. Therefore, balancing the number of cores and Tile block size is a key challenge. Core Functions of Automatic Tiling Automatic Tiling finds a Tiling strategy that provides optimal Kernel execution performance. Its core functions include: 1. Find the optimal partitioning result: Find the optimal partitioning result for each ImplGraph, determining the number of cores used during Kernel execution, the amount of data moved from GM to UB each time, the number of loops in the UB, the amount of data calculated in the UB each time, and the number of movements from UB to GM. 2. Select the optimal template: Based on the optimal partitioning solution of each ImplGraph, evaluate Kernel execution performance as accurately as possible and select the optimal template. Core Workflow of Automatic Tiling Kernel execution logic is expressed in IR. Automatic Tiling extracts key information from the IR graph expression, including: Symbolic expression of constraints: LocalBuffer usage constraint: During Automatic Tiling solving, the usage of each LocalBuffer level must remain within the hardware-permitted range. For example, the total size of TQue/TBuf and temporary Buffers requested by the Kernel cannot exceed the hardware UB limit. IR expresses each Tensor's location (GM or UB) and reuse relationships between Tensors. Automatic Tiling uses this information to symbolically express constraints for each LocalBuffer level. Core-usage constraint: Automatic Tiling generates a symbolic expression for the actual number of cores based on axis-partitioning methods. At Tiling runtime, it determines whether the constraint is satisfied based on actual hardware constraints and determined symbolic values. Partitioning constraints: For example, constraints that ensure a child-axis size is no greater than the parent-axis size and that a partitioning axis is aligned to 32 B. Symbolic expression of each pipeline's latency Automatic Tiling performs performance modeling for each API and symbolically expresses the performance of these APIs on each pipeline. It determines the number of API invocations from the loop axes expressed in IR and derives the total latency of all APIs in the IR on each pipeline. Here, execution of the bottleneck pipeline is assumed to effectively overlap execution of non-bottleneck pipelines (simplified bottleneck-pipeline theory). Therefore, total task-execution latency is mainly the bottleneck-pipeline latency. The following figure contains three pipelines. AIVMTE2 is the bottleneck pipeline. During execution, AIVMTE2 overlaps AIVMTE3 and AIVVEC, so total task-execution latency is represented by AIVMTE2 execution latency. Pipeline Diagram Automatic Tiling generates Tiling solver code from the extracted key information and generates an axis-ordering Tiling solver by default. This solver uses "storage usage during operator implementation does not exceed physical storage at each NPU level" as a constraint. Based on different IR expressions, it selects the most appropriate Tiling algorithm to ensure baseline-solution performance. It then uses "minimize the latency of the bottleneck execution unit" as the optimization objective and solves through performance modeling to improve the solution's performance ceiling. The system also provides an optionally configured heuristic iterative solver. This solver uses a heuristic solving method. Starting from an initial solution, it searches the solution space that satisfies memory requirements within the feasible region that meets constraints, following the gradient-descent direction of performance-formula modeling. When the modeled formula value reaches its minimum, the optimization process exits and returns the optimal Tiling. Key Technologies Performance formula modeling: Purpose: The simulation accuracy of the performance formula determines: Accuracy of template selection from Schedule output. Accuracy of core-count adjustment through axis ordering and intra-core loop selection. Accuracy of heuristic iterative solving. Therefore, each type of API must be modeled as accurately as possible. Movement API modeling implementation: 1. Identify the primary factors that affect movement performance. Examples include data volume, GM discontinuity, UB discontinuity, whether vectorization-width alignment is used, number of cores, Pipe initial overhead, API initial overhead, and API invocation count. 2. Design a performance formula based on the primary factors that affect movement performance and their impact on performance. For example, assume that MTE2 overhead is Cost(MTE2), where API initial overhead is h, data volume is DataSize, API invocation count is Count, Pipe initial overhead is H, and bandwidth is T: Cost(MTE2) = ((DataSize / T + h) Count) + H Here, bandwidth is a dependent variable related to whether vectorization-width alignment is used, number of cores, GM discontinuity, and UB discontinuity. 3. Based on the assumed performance model, experimentally verify actual movement performance as different primary factors change. 4. Establish the relationship between movement performance and primary factors and express it through symbolic technology. Computation API modeling implementation: 1. For AscendC stable basic APIs, the Automatic Tiling module collects performance data for different inputs, obtains the relationship between performance and input, establishes a performance model, and expresses it symbolically. 2. For AscendC variable APIs, the Automatic Tiling module calculates their invocation parameters and invocation count based on API invocation logic and generates a complete performance model for the API, producing relatively accurate performance modeling. Based on movement API modeling, computation API modeling, and the simplified bottleneck-pipeline theory, the two core problems of Automatic Tiling can be simplified to: 1. How to adjust Tiling to minimize the bottleneck-pipeline formula value. 2. Select the template with the minimum bottleneck-pipeline formula value as the optimal template. Axis-ordering solver: Purpose: The Tiling solver determines appropriate inter-core and block partitioning sizes based on the input Shape to provide the best possible Kernel performance. The heuristic priority-ordering rules supported by the axis-ordering solver (priority means an axis that should preferably not be partitioned) and basic algorithms, such as the UB-usage/core-usage tradeoff algorithm, UB-first greedy algorithm, and symmetric partitioning, effectively ensure baseline-solution performance. Combining them with performance-modeling expressions also improves the Kernel performance ceiling. Implementation: Determine partitioning-axis priorities: First, determine the priority of each partitioning axis based on the API in the following order: A parent axis has a higher priority than a child axis (hard functional constraint). A reduction-type axis has a higher priority than a non-reduction-type axis (heuristic rule). A broadcast axis has a higher priority than a non-broadcast axis (heuristic rule). A non-innermost axis has a higher priority than the innermost axis (heuristic rule). The last axes of movement APIs have equal priority (heuristic rule). Inter-core and intra-core partitioning: Next, partition in two parts: intra-core Tiling and inter-core Tiling. The UB-first greedy algorithm is used as an example and is suitable for scenarios with high initial API overhead: Intra-core Tiling: Traverse in reverse axis order, first adjust a variable to its maximum value, and determine whether it satisfies hardware constraints. If not, use binary search to adjust the variable until it meets hardware constraints. Then adjust the next intra-core Tiling variable until all variables satisfy hardware constraints. For example, s1tt2, s1tt, s1t, and s2t are Tiling-related axes. Their partitioning workflow is shown as follows: Inter-core Tiling: Identify multi-core-related variables and traverse them in descending order to locate records that use more cores. Return if the physical-core count is exceeded. In the following figure, bngs1T is the multi-core partitioning axis, and its partitioning workflow is shown. The selection strategy is to prefer the record that uses more cores when the core usages differ. Based on this strategy, the final selected core usage is 47. The specific workflow is as follows: First traverse s2t and adjust it to the maximum value 1024, which satisfies hardware constraints. Then traverse s1t and adjust it to the maximum value 256, which also satisfies hardware constraints. Then sequentially adjust the next variables s1tt>s1tt2 until all variables satisfy hardware constraints. Other algorithms: UB-usage/core-usage tradeoff algorithm: Suitable for scenarios that require fine-grained control of core usage and UB usage (with a preset value; the number of cores can be dynamically adjusted based on the performance formula). Symmetric partitioning: Suitable for last-axis transpose scenarios. It ensures that multiple last axes used by movement APIs can be partitioned with equal priority. Cache Compress)，减少Attention的计算和访存开销，可以大幅提升长序列的计算效率，降低推理的成本。本实践0 Day支持了DeepSeek-V4的模型推理部署，并适配支持Atlas-A3 Pod和950PR/DT多代际昇腾芯片，提供长达1M序列的高性能推理能力。 2026) KV Cache内存分析 在DeepSeek-V4中，通过多种算法有效降低KV Cache占用的内存。SWA仅需保留slidingwindow大小的KV Cache；在压缩Cache的层中，KV Cache中存储压缩后的KV，内存大小为： $$ \mathrm{batch\size}\times (\mathrm{kv\length} // \mathrm{compress\ratio} ) \times \mathrm{head\dim} \times \mathrm{storage\bytes} \times \mathrm{num\compress\layers} $$ 未满足压缩长度，暂时不被压缩的kvstate和对应的scorestate，会被保存在remainder中。因此remainder的最大大小为： $$ \mathrm{batch\size}\times (\mathrm{compress\ratio - 1}) \times \mathrm{compress\dim} \times \mathrm{storage\bytes} \times \mathrm{num\compress\layers} $$ 在压缩倍率为4的层中（CSA），采用了LI进一步稀疏KV Cache，因此与DeepSeek-V3.2类似，LI需要保留对应的Indexer Cache。为了与KV Cache的压缩对应，在LI中也通过Compressor模块进行了4倍压缩，因此Indexer Cache的存储数据量也为压缩后的长度，如当前的kvlength不满足压缩长度，则会暂存在indexerkvstate和indexerscorestate中。 综合来看，得益于滑窗和高倍率压缩，不保留Full Cache可以使得KV Cache整体存储的数据量明显降低，如128k序列，在128倍压缩（HCA）后，仅需保留1k KV；在4倍压缩（CSA）后，保留32k KV，对于长序列下的内存压力得以显著缓解。 针对上述的差异和模型特点，本实践设计了NPU亲和的并行策略，并实现了SAS, Compressor, LI, GatingTopK, mHC等融合Kernel，详细介绍请参考后续章节。 融合Kernel 使用融合Kernel可以获得算子间的数据流优化、流水并行、减少算子调度开销等优化收益。在DeepSeek-V4中，本次开源的融合算子覆盖Attention、MoE、mHC等各模块。 Compressor：包含了KV/Gate的Linear计算和kvstate/scorestate更新，并选取对应的数据（CSA场景存在Overlap）计算压缩KV并输出； KvCompressEpilog：包含对压缩后的压缩KV的量化、量化后压缩KV和其Scale的拼接，和刷新到KV Cache的操作； IndexerCompressEpilog：包含Indexer Cache的量化、刷新操作； mHC模块的融合算子由hcpre和hcpost组成，其中hcpre融合算子同步提供 AscendC、PyPTO 两种实现版本，融合范围如下图所示： 上述NPU融合Kernel均已开源，使用方式参见 融合Kernel执行指导 。 并行策略 针对Decode场景，在950DT平台下，可以采用8卡或16卡部署，获取极低单用户时延；在Atlas-A3 Pod平台采用64卡大EP部署，获得高吞吐性能收益。针对Prefill场景，在950PR平台下，采用8卡或16卡部署，针对长短序列可以分别选用DP或CP并行，提升TTFT。 Prefill并行策略 DeepSeek-V4主要面向长序列推理场景，Prefill阶段的内存占用和TTFT会面临巨大挑战，因此优化内存占用和TTFT是并行策略设计的主要目的。如果采用Attention DP (Data Parallel) 策略，每个Rank都需要推理超长序列，总体计算量较大，TTFT较高，用户体验较差。因此，针对长序列场景，在Attention部分设计选用Context Parallel（CP）并行，通过多Rank分摊计算和访存开销，提升整体性能。 由于LI采用causalmask，越往后的Context Chunk访存和计算量越大，在CP切分时，可以沿用之前Recipes在DeepSeek-V3.2使用的zigzag切分方式，将首尾的序列块放在同一Rank上，使得CP后各卡间的计算量相对均衡。 此外，在切分序列时，还需要考虑Attention模块采用的Window Attention和KV Cache压缩。 SWA层计算时，每个Chunk需要获取到前序winsize=128长度的KV； 在HCA层中，可以通过切分使得前序Rank上的序列为128对齐，则无需传递额外的Token给后续chunk所在的Rank，同时除最后一个chunk以外，其余chunk不需要处理remainder； 在CSA层中，由于Compressor需要处理Token Overlap的信息，因此需要获取到前序4个Token来实现Overlap压缩；假设前序chunk的序列长度为128对齐，则除最后一个chunk所在的Rank外，无remainder。 因此在Attention模块执行时，需要从前序序列获取的最大Token长度为128（满足Window Cache），每个chunk向后续chunk传递128个Token。通过全局的allgather通信算子，获取所有Rank最后的128个Tokens，并通过对应的receiveidx裁切出各chunk所需的数据。首个序列块chunk0不需要获取额外的Token。 因此在Attention模块会引入2次通信： 在MQA模块起始做一次通信，通信128大小的hiddenstates。此时MLAProlog的计算量会略有冗余，但实现较为简洁； 在Compressor计算后，由于Query已进行CP切分，需要对Compress Cache进行CP域的allgather，获取到完整的压缩后的Cache，用于LI和SAS的计算。针对zigzag场景，在allgather后需要对Cache进行顺序重排。 Prediction(MTP)机制，MTP机制允许在一次主模型推理过程中同时计算验证多个Token，在未达到计算瓶颈前，可以通过较少的时延增加，有机会获得更多的输出Token，从而降低单Token的推理耗时。DeepSeek-V4涉及的滑窗/压缩/稀疏Hybrid Attention算法复杂度较高，为适配MTP带来了新的挑战。 Main Model方案 Cache设计：本模型针对Window KV和Compressor模块的kvstate/scorestate设计了Ring Buffer，可以通过blocktable与slotmapping实现对少数几块Cache的内存复用；其余KV Cache的内存按照压缩后的最大长度申请。 两种Cache管理方式的对比实现，如下图所示： MTP场景适配：假如主模型在Decode阶段每个Step每个Batch需要额外验证nextn个Token。在每个Step的推理过程中，算子正常在kvlength维度递进，如果满足CSA/HCA的压缩条件就进行压缩。这一场景需要沿用LI和SAS算子内置的梯形掩码，确保待验证Token的压缩Cache不参与主模型Token的计算。假如有MTP Token校验不被接受，需要在下一个Step重新推导该Token。重新推导的场景需要为Compressor的kvstate/scorestate额外缓存。如下图所示，左侧是kvstate/scorestate缓存范围，右侧是Indexer/Attention计算使用梯形掩码。 结合本模型的Ring Buffer设计，只需要提前申请更大的Buffer，就可以自然实现额外缓存的动作。需要缓存的Cache大小可以以compressratio个Token为一组进行统计，具体多少组Token的计算公式为 $$ \mathrm{num\ratio\group} = (1 \ \mathrm{if} \ \mathrm{next\n}\ == 0 \ \mathrm{else}\ 2) + \mathrm{overlap} $$ 其中overlap在CSA等于1，在HCA等于0。numratiogroup里预留了余数Token和可能需要重新压缩的前序Token。每个Batch需要的Cache Block个数为 $$ \mathrm{ceil}(\mathrm{num\ratio\group} \mathrm{ratio} \ / \ \mathrm{block\size}) $$ MTP Spec Model方案 模型结构：MTP模型仅使用Window Attention (SWA)。 Cache结构：在当前实现中，nextn个Draft Token共享一份MTP权重和KV Cache。 性能分析 MTP机制允许Decode在一次主模型推理过程中同时对小模型投机的nextn个Token批量Verify，在相似的数据搬运下，有机会能得到更多的预测Token，提高了Decode推理阶段的计算访存比； Attention部分：在MTP场景下，CSA的FA计算在极端情况下需要搬运的KV Cache数据量是非MTP场景的nextn + 1倍，一定程度上增加了离散访存代价。但是SWA/HCA/LI的Cache搬运量与非MTP场景几乎一致，能够自然地提升计算访存比。 其余算子，如Matmul等，在MTP机制下可以复用权重搬运，达到更好的计算访存比，因此MTP有比较可观的加速比。 在高吞吐场景下，使用多个Draft Token很容易触及计算瓶颈，因此可采用MTP1进行加速；在低时延场景下，计算密度更小，可采用MTP3获得更大加速比； IndexerProlog：qbproj使用W8A8，indexerweight不量化；indexerq使用A8量化；Indexer Cache使用C8量化； LightningIndexer: batchmatmul使用Int8计算； Compressor: Linear不量化； MLAEpilog：oaproj不量化，obproj使用W8A8量化； MoE：路由和共享专家的Linear使用W8A8量化； LMHead：不量化。 注： W8A8：W8指权重使用静态Per-Channel Int8量化，A8指数据使用动态Per-Token Int8量化； A8C8：A8表示LI中的Q使用动态Per-Token-Head Int8量化，Indexer Cache使用动态Per-Token-Head Int8量化。 出于性能考虑，只对参数量较多的部分Linear模块进行量化。因此Linear模块里只对MLA的qbproj, obproj和Indexer的qbproj进行量化，KV Cache暂时维持BF16存算。LI通过A8C8量化进一步降低计算时延，同步优化TTFT和TPOT。 Hybrid INT8-INT4 (推荐DeepSeekV4-Pro模型使用) 由于DeepSeekV4-Pro模型的参数量较大，MoE部分使用W8A8推理会面临较大的内存和访存瓶颈。本实践针对DeepSeekV4-Pro模型设计了Hybrid INT8-INT4的量化。整体量化策略同上，主要对MoE部分采用INT4量化，相比较纯INT8量化策略，Hybrid INT8-INT4可显著降低MoE部分的存储和访存开销。与INT8量化策略区分点： MoE：路由专家的Linear使用W4A8量化，共享专家的Linear使用W8A8量化； 注： W4A8：W4指权重使用静态Per-Channel Int4量化，A8指数据使用动态Per-Token Int8量化； Ascend 950PR/DT Hybrid MXFP8-MXFP4 (推荐DeepSeekV4-Flash/Pro模型使用) 本实践支持了原生Hybrid NPU DeepSeek-V4 Inference Optimization Practice The DeepSeek team released the latest DeepSeek-V4 model series, which includes the DeepSeek-V4 Flash and DeepSeek-V4 Pro specifications. Building on DeepSeek Sparse Attention in DeepSeek-V3.2, the model further uses a KV Cache sliding window (Window Cache) and compression algorithm (KV Cache Compress) across different layers to reduce Attention computation and memory-access overhead, substantially improving computation efficiency for long sequences and reducing inference costs. This practice provides Day-0 support for DeepSeek-V4 model inference deployment, adapts to multiple generations of Ascend chips, including Atlas-A3 Pod and 950PR/DT, and provides high-performance inference for sequences of up to 1M tokens. Based on the new model structure, this practice provides a low-latency, high-throughput deployment solution and innovatively designs high-performance NPU fused kernels and a multi-stream parallelism solution to substantially improve inference performance. For quantization, this practice adapts the W8A8C16 (Int8) quantization solution on the Atlas-A3 Pod platform. On the 950PR/DT platform, it supports the native Hybrid FP8-MXFP4 mixed-quantization mode and the hardware-friendly Hybrid MXFP8-MXFP4 and Hybrid HiF8-MXFP8-MXFP4 modes to fully use the computing capabilities of different hardware. This practice also open-sources TileLang and PyPTO implementations, providing directly reusable examples for efficient operator development. Complex fused kernels can be developed with only a few hundred lines of code. For the new DeepSeek-V4 model structure, this open-source release provides a series of high-performance fused operators, including: A unified SparseAttnSharedKV (SAS) interface for Window/Sparse/Compress Attention interleaved across multiple layers, supporting multiple Attention computations. Compressor and CompressEpilog fused operators for different Compress Ratios, enabling efficient Cache compression and updates. Enhanced LightningIndexer (LI) functionality with support for the Compress Ratio feature. HCPre and HCPost fused operators for the mHC (Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections) architecture. The AscendC implementations of these fused operators were all open-sourced on Day 0. This release also provides PyPTO and TileLang implementations as directly reusable examples for efficient operator development. Complex fused kernels can be developed with only a few hundred lines of code. Highlights The overall deployment strategy follows DeepSeek's EP parallelism solution. Based on the structural features of the new model, this practice designs and implements an NPU-friendly parallelism strategy, supports deployment on multiple generations of Ascend chips, including Atlas-A3 Pod and 950PR/DT, and provides high-performance inference for sequences of up to 1M tokens. The model inference code (Chinese) is open-sourced in cann-recipes-infer, and mainstream open-source inference frameworks vLLM and SGLang are also adapted. AscendC-based HC Pre and HC Post fused operators are open-sourced to efficiently compute the preprocessing and postprocessing workflows of mHC. The AscendC kernel technical document and code (Chinese) are open-sourced. Self-developed PyPTO-based HC Pre and MLAProlog fused operators are released to improve fused-operator programmability. The operator frontend does not need to be aware of chip-generation differences. The backend distinguishes them through pass IR and PTOISA instructions to provide cross-generation compatibility. The PyPTO kernel technical document , PTO ISA user guide , and code (Chinese) are open-sourced. The TileLang open-source community also supports development of all new operators in DeepSeek-V4. These operators correspond to the Expert and Developer development modes of TileLang-Ascend and provide two integration levels, AscendC basic instructions and PTO AS, offering multi-level open interfaces for various programming frontend languages and compilers. They are released in the TileAI open-source community. The TileLang kernel technical document and code (Chinese) are also open-sourced. The NpuGraphEx backend combines unique features such as the dynamo compilation cache and static compilation to fully use Ascend computing power and deliver maximum graph-mode acceleration. 950PR/DT supports the native Hybrid FP8-MXFP4 mixed-quantization mode, enabling smooth and lossless weight migration. This practice also supports replacing native FP8 computation with MXFP8 to further improve computation efficiency in high-throughput Prefill or Decode scenarios. Based on the preceding optimizations, CANN provides Day-0 support for DeepSeek-V4 inference deployment. Reference Decode performance: For DeepSeek-V4 Flash on 950DT, TPOT is less than 10 ms with 16 cards and a 128K sequence. On Atlas-A3 Pod, single-card Decode throughput is 4388 TPS@30 ms with 64 cards and an 8K sequence. Compared with DeepSeek-V3.2, DeepSeek-V4 retains the LI sparse attention mechanism in the Attention component and adds Window Attention and KV Cache compression. These additions keep overall Attention computation and memory access low compared with a Full Cache, substantially improving performance for long sequences. The DeepSeek-V4 model architecture is shown in the following figure: Due to space limitations, the figure provides a simplified representation of some structures. Attention Sparsity and Compression In the first two model layers, DeepSeek-V4 Flash uses Window Attention (SWA) with a KV Cache of slidingwindow=128, effectively reducing Attention computation and KV Cache memory usage. DeepSeek-V4 Pro uses a Compress Ratio of 128 and compresses the Full Cache by 128 times through Compressor (HCA). In subsequent layers, Compressed Sparse Attention (CSA) and Heavily Compressed Attention (HCA) are used alternately. Compressor compresses the Full Cache by 4 times (CSA) or 128 times (HCA). In CSA layers, LI applies KV Cache sparsity on the compressed Cache and selects the Top 512 KV pairs for Attention computation, further improving performance for long sequences. Attention computation uses MQA (Multi-Query Attention) instead of MLA. It no longer distinguishes between the Prefill and Decode computation flows (naive or absorb) and introduces the attentionsink parameter. Six routed experts and one shared expert are activated each time. For expert selection, the first three layers use hash routing, while the subsequent 40 layers use learnable soft routing. mHC (Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections) mHC extends conventional residual connections. It expands hiddenstate from one path to multiple paths and merges them back into one path through Pre Mapping before Attention/MoE computation, leaving the Attention/MoE computation process unchanged. The Attention and MoE outputs are then expanded back into multiple paths through Post Mapping. Meanwhile, the multi-path residuals are fused through Res Mapping. The fused result is added to the Post Mapping result to produce the mHC output. The image is from the mHC paper Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections (Xie et al., 2026) . KV Cache Memory Analysis In DeepSeek-V4, multiple algorithms effectively reduce the memory occupied by the KV Cache. SWA only needs to retain a KV Cache of size slidingwindow. In layers with Cache compression, the KV Cache stores compressed KV data, and its memory size is: $$ \mathrm{batch\size}\times (\mathrm{kv\length} // \mathrm{compress\ratio} ) \times \mathrm{head\dim} \times \mathrm{storage\bytes} \times \mathrm{num\compress\layers} $$ kvstate data that has not reached the required compression length and therefore has not yet been compressed, together with the corresponding scorestate, is retained in remainder. Therefore, the maximum size of remainder is: $$ \mathrm{batch\size}\times (\mathrm{compress\ratio - 1}) \times \mathrm{compress\dim} \times \mathrm{storage\bytes} \times \mathrm{num\compress\layers} $$ In layers with a compression ratio of 4 (CSA), LI further sparsifies the KV Cache. Therefore, as in DeepSeek-V3.2, LI must retain the corresponding Indexer Cache. To match KV Cache compression, the Compressor module also compresses LI data by 4 times. Therefore, the amount of data stored in the Indexer Cache is also the compressed length. If the current kvlength does not meet the compression length, data is temporarily retained in indexerkvstate and indexerscorestate. Overall, because of the sliding window and high-ratio compression, not retaining the Full Cache substantially reduces the total amount of data stored in the KV Cache. For example, for a 128K sequence, only 1K KV data must be retained after 128x compression (HCA), and 32K KV data is retained after 4x compression (CSA), significantly relieving memory pressure for long sequences. Based on these differences and model characteristics, this practice designs an NPU-friendly parallelism strategy and implements fused kernels such as SAS, Compressor, LI, GatingTopK, and mHC. For details, see the following sections. Fused Kernels Fused kernels provide optimization benefits such as inter-operator data-flow optimization, pipeline parallelism, and reduced operator scheduling overhead. In DeepSeek-V4, the open-sourced fused operators cover modules such as Attention, MoE, and mHC. The fused operators in the Attention component include Compressor, LI, KvCompressEpilog, IndexerCompressEpilog, and SAS. Compressor: Includes KV/Gate Linear computation and kvstate/scorestate updates, selects the corresponding data (with Overlap in the CSA scenario), and computes and outputs compressed KV data. KvCompressEpilog: Includes quantization of compressed KV data, concatenation of the quantized compressed KV data and its Scale, and refresh of the KV Cache. IndexerCompressEpilog: Includes Indexer Cache quantization and refresh operations. LightningIndexer: Includes operations such as scorebatchmatmul, relu, reducesum, and topk. In long-sequence scenarios, the topk operation becomes a bottleneck. The topk computation time can overlap other operations in the pipeline to provide pipeline-computation benefits. SparseAttentionSharedKV: Includes Sparse Attention, Compress Attention, and Window Attention computation. The fused operators in the mHC module consist of hcpre and hcpost. Parallelism Strategy For Decode scenarios, 8-card or 16-card deployment can be used on the 950DT platform to achieve extremely low single-user latency. On the Atlas-A3 Pod platform, 64-card large-scale EP deployment provides high-throughput performance benefits. For Prefill scenarios on the 950PR platform, 8-card or 16-card deployment can be used. DP or CP parallelism can be selected for short or long sequences, respectively, to improve TTFT. Prefill Parallelism Strategy DeepSeek-V4 primarily targets long-sequence inference scenarios. Memory usage and TTFT during Prefill pose major challenges, so optimizing memory usage and TTFT is the main objective of the parallelism strategy. If the Attention DP (Data Parallel) strategy is used, each rank must infer an ultra-long sequence, resulting in a large total computation volume, high TTFT, and a poor user experience. Therefore, for long-sequence scenarios, Context Parallel (CP) parallelism is used in the Attention component. Multiple ranks share the computation and memory-access overhead to improve overall performance. Because LI uses causalmask, later Context Chunks require more memory access and computation. During CP partitioning, the zigzag partitioning method previously used by Recipes for DeepSeek-V3.2 can be reused. It places the first and last sequence blocks on the same rank, making the computation load across cards relatively balanced after CP partitioning. In addition, Window Attention and KV Cache compression in the Attention module must be considered when partitioning the sequence. During SWA-layer computation, each chunk must obtain KV data of length winsize=128 from the preceding sequence. In HCA layers, partitioning can align the sequence on the preceding rank to 128. No additional tokens then need to be transferred to the rank containing a subsequent chunk, and no chunk except the last one needs to process remainder. In CSA layers, the Compressor must process Token Overlap information, so it must obtain the preceding four tokens to implement Overlap compression. If the sequence length of the preceding chunk is aligned to 128, no rank except the rank containing the last chunk has a remainder. Therefore, when the Attention module runs, the maximum token length that must be obtained from the preceding sequence is 128 to satisfy the Window Cache. Each chunk transfers 128 tokens to the subsequent chunk. A global allgather communication operator obtains the last 128 tokens from all ranks, and the corresponding receiveidx slices out the data required by each chunk. The first sequence block, chunk0, does not need additional tokens. Therefore, the Attention module introduces two communication operations: One communication operation is performed at the beginning of the MQA module to communicate hiddenstates of size 128. MLAProlog performs slightly redundant computation in this case, but the implementation is simpler. After Compressor computation, Query has been partitioned by CP, so allgather must be performed on the Compress Cache in the CP domain to obtain the complete compressed Cache for LI and SAS computation. In the zigzag scenario, the Cache must be reordered after allgather. The CSA implementation is shown in the following figure: The two Compressors can run in parallel, and the CSA Compressor only requires the information of four Overlap tokens. Therefore, the data required by Window Attention and Compressor can also be communicated separately to overlap computation with communication while introducing little redundant computation. After Compressor, allgather communication must also be performed on the Compressed Cache in the CP domain. The CSA implementation is shown in the following figure: Decode Parallelism Strategy During Decode, the parallelism strategy follows the solutions used for DeepSeek-R1 and DeepSeek-V3.2: Attention uses Data Parallel (DP) parallelism. MoE uses Expert Parallel (EP) parallelism. LMhead uses Tensor Parallel (TP) parallelism. In the Output Projection after Attention, oaproj has a large weight and long memory-access latency. In low-latency scenarios, TP partitioning can be used selectively so that multiple ranks share the memory-access overhead in parallel. The alltoall and reducescatter communication operators convert between DP and TP, as shown in the following figure: MTP DeepSeek-V4 continues to provide a native Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) mechanism. MTP allows multiple tokens to be calculated and verified during one main-model inference operation. Before the computation bottleneck is reached, more output tokens may be obtained with only a small increase in latency, reducing the inference latency per token. The sliding-window/compression/sparsity Hybrid Attention algorithm in DeepSeek-V4 is highly complex, presenting new challenges for MTP adaptation. Main Model Solution Cache design: This model implements a Ring Buffer for Window KV and the kvstate/scorestate of the Compressor module. blocktable and slotmapping enable memory reuse across a small number of Cache blocks. Memory for the remaining KV Cache is allocated based on the maximum compressed length. A comparison of the two Cache-management implementations is shown in the following figure: MTP scenario adaptation: Assume that during Decode, the main model must additionally verify nextn tokens for each batch in each step. During inference in each step, operators advance normally along the kvlength dimension and perform compression when the CSA/HCA compression condition is met. This scenario must continue using the trapezoidal masks built into the LI and SAS operators to ensure that the compressed Cache of tokens to be verified does not participate in computation for the main-model token. If an MTP token is not accepted during verification, the token must be inferred again in the next step. Reinference requires an additional cache for the Compressor's kvstate/scorestate. In the following figure, the left side shows the kvstate/scorestate cache range, and the right side shows the trapezoidal mask used for Indexer/Attention computation. With this model's Ring Buffer design, additional caching can be implemented naturally by allocating a larger Buffer in advance. The required Cache size can be counted in groups of compressratio tokens. The formula for calculating the number of token groups is: $$ \mathrm{num\ratio\group} = (1 \ \mathrm{if} \ \mathrm{next\n}\ == 0 \ \mathrm{else}\ 2) + \mathrm{overlap} $$ Here, overlap equals 1 in CSA and 0 in HCA. numratiogroup reserves space for remainder tokens and preceding tokens that may need to be compressed again. The number of Cache Blocks required by each batch is: $$ \mathrm{ceil}(\mathrm{num\ratio\group} \mathrm{ratio} \ / \ \mathrm{block\size}) $$ MTP Spec Model Solution Model structure: The MTP model uses only Window Attention (SWA). Cache structure: In the current implementation, nextn Draft Tokens share one set of MTP weights and KV Cache. Performance Analysis MTP allows Decode to batch-verify nextn tokens speculated by the small model during one main-model inference operation. With a similar amount of data movement, more predicted tokens may be obtained, improving the computation-to-memory-access ratio during Decode inference. Attention component: In the MTP scenario, under extreme conditions, CSA FA computation must move nextn + 1 times as much KV Cache data as in the non-MTP scenario, increasing discrete memory-access overhead to some extent. However, the Cache movement volume of SWA/HCA/LI is almost the same as in the non-MTP scenario, naturally improving the computation-to-memory-access ratio. Other operators, such as Matmul, can reuse weight movement under MTP to achieve a better computation-to-memory-access ratio. Therefore, MTP provides a considerable speedup. In high-throughput scenarios, using multiple Draft Tokens can easily reach the computation bottleneck, so MTP1 can be used for acceleration. In low-latency scenarios, computation density is lower, so MTP3 can provide a larger speedup. Quantization Strategy Atlas-A3 Pod Int8 (Recommended for the DeepSeekV4-Flash Model) Based on the native Hybrid FP8-MXFP4 weights, this practice supports Int8 W8A8 quantization. Compared with BF16 inference, W8A8 quantization effectively reduces end-to-end latency and improves system throughput. The quantization strategy is as follows: MLAProlog: qbproj uses W8A8 quantization. Other Linear operations are not quantized. The KV Cache uses C16. IndexerProlog: qbproj uses W8A8, while indexerweight is not quantized. indexerq uses A8 quantization. The Indexer Cache uses C8 quantization. LightningIndexer: batchmatmul uses Int8 computation. Compressor: Linear operations are not quantized. MLAEpilog: oaproj is not quantized, while obproj uses W8A8 quantization. MoE: Linear operations of routed and shared experts use W8A8 quantization. LMHead: Not quantized. Note: W8A8: W8 indicates that weights use static Per-Channel Int8 quantization, and A8 indicates that data uses dynamic Per-Token Int8 quantization. A8C8: A8 indicates that Q in LI uses dynamic Per-Token-Head Int8 quantization, and the Indexer Cache uses dynamic Per-Token-Head Int8 quantization. For performance considerations, only some Linear modules with a large number of parameters are quantized. Therefore, among the Linear modules, only MLA's qbproj and obproj and Indexer's qbproj are quantized. The KV Cache temporarily retains BF16 storage and computation. LI uses A8C8 quantization to further reduce computation latency and optimize both TTFT and TPOT. Hybrid INT8-INT4 (Recommended for the DeepSeekV4-Pro Model) Because the DeepSeekV4-Pro model has a large number of parameters, using W8A8 inference in the MoE component creates major memory and memory-access bottlenecks. This practice designs Hybrid INT8-INT4 quantization for the DeepSeekV4-Pro model. The overall quantization strategy is the same as described previously, but INT4 quantization is primarily used for the MoE component. Compared with the pure INT8 quantization strategy, Hybrid INT8-INT4 significantly reduces storage and memory-access overhead in the MoE component. The difference from the INT8 quantization strategy is: MoE: Linear operations of routed experts use W4A8 quantization, while Linear operations of shared experts use W8A8 quantization. Note: W4A8: W4 indicates that weights use static Per-Channel Int4 quantization, and A8 indicates that data uses dynamic Per-Token Int8 quantization. Ascend 950PR/DT Hybrid MXFP8-MXFP4 (Recommended for the DeepSeekV4-Flash/Pro Models) This practice supports the native Hybrid FP8-MXFP4 quantization method. It also supports replacing Linear modules in the native FP8 format with MXFP8 or HiF8, which can further improve compute utilization and overall performance in high-throughput Prefill and Decode scenarios. The overall Hybrid MXFP8-MXFP4 quantization strategy is as follows: MLAProlog: qaproj, qbproj, and kvproj use W8A8 quantization. The KV Cache uses C8 pseudo-quantization. IndexerProlog: qbproj uses W8A8, while indexerweight is not quantized. indexerq uses A8 quantization. The Indexer Cache uses C8 quantization. LightningIndexer: batchmatmul uses FP8 computation. Compressor: Linear operations are not quantized. MLAEpilog: oaproj and obproj use W8A8 quantization. MoE: Linear operations of routed experts use W4A8 quantization, while Linear operations of shared experts use W8A8 quantization. LMHead: Not quantized. Note: W8A8: W8 and A8 indicate MXFP8 quantization. LI A8C8: A8 indicates that Q in LI uses dynamic Per-Token-Head FP8 quantization with FP32 Scale. The Indexer Cache uses dynamic Per-Token-Head FP8 quantization with FP32 Scale. KV Cache C8: Indicates that the KV Cache uses dynamic Per-Group-64 FP8 quantization with E8M0 Scale. The MLAProlog KV Cache quantization strategy uses dynamic 8-bit storage and 16-bit computation. For ultra-long sequences, the C8 KV Cache reduces memory usage by 2 times. LI uses A8C8 for computation benefits, reducing LI computation latency and optimizing both TTFT and TPOT. Hybrid HiF8-MXFP8-MXFP4 (Recommended for the DeepSeekV4-Flash/Pro Models) This practice also supports Hybrid HiF8-MXFP8-MXFP4. The overall quantization strategy is as follows: MLAProlog: qaproj, qbproj, and kvproj use HiF W8A8 quantization. The KV Cache uses HiF A8 quantization. IndexerProlog: qbproj and indexerweight use HiF W8A8 quantization. indexerq and the Indexer Cache use HiF A8 quantization. LightningIndexer: batchmatmul uses HiF8 computation. Compressor: wkv and wgate use HiF W8A8 quantization. MLAEpilog: oaproj and obproj use HiF W8A8 quantization. MoE: Linear operations of routed experts use MXFP W4A8 quantization, while Linear operations of shared experts use MXFP W8A8 quantization. LMHead: Not quantized. Note: HiF W8A8: A8 indicates that activations use Per-Tensor HiF8 quantization, W8 indicates that weights use offline Per-Channel HiF8 quantization, and the Scale format is FP32. MoE MXFP W4A8/W8A8: Uses the same MoE quantization strategy as Hybrid MXFP8-MXFP4. Multi-Stream Parallelism Optimization Attention Multi-Stream Parallelism In the MLAProlog module before Attention computation, the Query computation flow and KV computation flow can run in parallel. In CSA, LI and CSA Compressor have no data dependency and can also run in parallel. Therefore, the operator core-control and multi-stream parallelism technologies provided by the CANN software stack can provide fine-grained computation-flow control for the Attention module and improve inference performance. For CSA, the following solution can be implemented: Matmul operations such as kvproj and qbproj in MLAProlog are computed on Cube cores and can run in parallel with operators such as qrmsnorm that are computed on Vector cores. rmsnorm and rope after qbproj can run in parallel with LI's liqbproj. For LI and the CSA Compressor module, CV core control ensures that operators are assigned appropriate numbers of Cube and Vector cores. This reduces the performance impact of competition for computing resources during multi-stream parallelism and fully overlaps the CSA Compressor. HCA does not contain LI, so MLAProlog computation can directly overlap part of the Compressor. Some logic is represented in simplified form. The length of an operator box does not represent its actual execution time and is used only for illustration. Multi-Stream Parallelism for Shared and Routed MoE Experts In the MoE module, shared and routed experts also provide opportunities to parallelize computation with computation and computation with communication. Multi-stream parallelism can overlap the computation latency of shared experts with almost no impact on routed experts. This practice implements expert multi-stream parallelism for Int8 and MXFP8 quantization scenarios and provides significant benefits. The implementation is shown in the following figure: Multi-Stream Parallelism for AICPU Scheduler Operators Operators such as Attention and LI depend on the actual context length during computation. This practice provides corresponding AICPU Scheduler operators that calculate the core-partitioning strategy before operator execution, reducing the execution burden and improving performance. Using SparseAttnSharedkv as an example, the following interfaces are provided: npu\sparse\attn\sharedkv\metadata: Obtains Tiling containing key load-balancing information based on operator inputs such as cuseqlensq, sequsedkv, and cmpratio. npu\sparse\attn\sharedkv: Performs Attention computation based on the tiling information output by npusparseattnsharedkvmetadata. During one full-network inference iteration, the AICPU Scheduler operator on which each SAS (SWA, CSA, or HCA) and LI operator depends only needs to run once, and Tiling information can be reused across operators in different layers. Therefore, Tiling computation can run in parallel with Embedding and MLAProlog computation. Multi-stream parallelism effectively overlaps the Tiling computation latency. NPU DeepSeek-V4模型 PyPTO 融合算子优化 面向 DeepSeek-V4架构，本次发布多个全新的融合算子：hcpre ，Compressor 和三个 FA 类算子：SWA, CFA和SCFA；MlaProlog 和 IndexerProlog 也针对新架构进行了适配。其中hcpre是本次 DeepSeek 新架构中 Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC) 的一部分。 本篇技术报告中，我们将对这些融合算子在 PyPTO 上的具体的实现和优化进行概述。同时，我们也会介绍 PTO-ISA（PTO 虚拟指令集）帮助 PyPTO 实现跨代际兼容。若对 PyPTO 高性能编程框架代码感兴趣，可参考 PyPTO 仓库： Cann-PyPTO 。 以下是单 die 64 batch, MTP1，序列长度 8k 下各算子的实测性能数据以及各算子的代码规模，可以看出 PyPTO 可以以较少的代码量，高效的开发效率（3-7天）完成复杂融合算子的开发，且能取得不错的基础性能： 算子 代码行数(KLOC) B S1 S2 D cmpratio coff start pos Duration(us) slidingwindowattention 0.3 64 2 8192 512 N/A N/A N/A 65 compressedflashattention 0.2 64 2 8192 512 128 N/A N/A 90 sparsecompressedflashattention 0.2 64 2 8192 512 4 N/A N/A 160 compressorc4li 0.9 64 2 N/A 128 4 2 8192 55 compressorc4a 64 2 N/A 512 4 2 8192 80 compressorc128a 64 2 N/A 512 128 1 8192 55 compressorc4li 64 2 N/A 128 4 2 8191 75 compressorc4a 64 2 N/A 512 4 2 8191 95 compressorc128a 64 2 N/A 512 128 1 8191 125 mlaprolog 0.5 64 2 N/A N/A N/A N/A N/A 130 hcpre 0.4 64 2 N/A N/A N/A N/A N/A 70 lightningindexerprolog 0.3 64 2 N/A N/A N/A N/A N/A 101 hcpre hcpre 在每层会调用两次，分别在 attention 和 ffn 的计算前。 计算过程 1. 计算 RMSNorm 的分母 $$ rsqrt = \sqrt{\frac{1}{\frac{1}{n}\sum{i=1}^n xi^2 + \epsilon}} $$ 2. 计算 mixes $$ mixes = (x @ hc\fn) \odot rsqrt $$ 3. Sinkhorn-Knopp 算法 $$ pre, post, comb = sinkhorn(mixes, hc\scale, hc\base, hc\mult, hc\sinkhorn\iters) $$ Sinkhorn-Knopp 算法每次迭代会进行逐行归一化，再做逐列归一化，hcsinkhorniters 控制迭代次数。 4. 利用 pre 和 x 计算 y $$ y = rowsum(pre \odot x) $$ 实际开发中需要充分利用昇腾硬件的特性以实现更好的性能，以下将详细介绍当前的解决方案及具体的实现方式。 流水并行 计算流程中第一步是 Vector 计算，而第二步中 $x @ hc\fn$ 是矩阵乘的 Cube 计算，且两者无依赖关系。PyPTO 的框架支持了两个任务的同时执行，无需手动插入同步。 指令优化 在 Sinkhorn-Knopp 算法中，涉及到了大量的重复的归约串联逐元素乘除的计算，在逐元素计算中，通过 pass 优化和 PTO 指令，避免了显式地广播，实现了高性能的计算。 pypto.experimental.setoperationconfig(combineaxis=True) MatMul优化 decode场景下，matmul计算的K轴很长（16K）而M\N轴较小，因此采用切K的方式，将数据切分到不同的核上以充分利用计算资源 pypto.setcubetileshapes([16, 16], [512, 21024], [128, 128], \ enablemultidataload=True, enablesplitk=True) mmres = pypto.matmul(xfp32, hcfn, pypto.DTFP32, btrans=True) 计算优化 Prefill 和 Decode 的最大区别，在 x 入参的的 0 轴大小上。Prefill 场景下，t 通常比较大；而在 Sinkhorn-Knopp 算法中，归约轴很小，为 hcmult=4，且在行归约时为 -1 轴，列归约时为 -2 轴。此时，我们采用数学上等价计算的技巧，在第二步计算中，在矩阵乘中直接计算转置： $$ hc\fn^T @ x^T $$ 从而在进入 Sinkhorn-Knopp 算法中，t 会置于尾轴上，归约轴为 -2, -3 轴，这样能提高计算的效率。 泳道图 在单 die 64 batch, MTP1 的场景下，上板执行结果如下： hcpre泳道图 MlaProlog 该算子是 Multi-Head Latent Attention 将 hidden states 处理为 query 和 kv 的计算操作。 计算过程 1. Query 的计算 包括两次采样和 RmsNorm（其中第二次 RmsNorm 权重恒为 1），最后对 -1 轴的后 rope\dim 维度进行 inplace interleaved rope 计算： $$ c^Q = RmsNorm(x @ wq\a) $$ $$ q = RmsNorm(c^Q @ wq\b) $$ $$ q[..., -rope\dim:] = ROPE(q[..., -rope\dim:]) $$ 2. Kv 的计算 包括一次采样和 RmsNorm，最后对 -1 轴的后 rope\dim 维度进行 inplace interleaved rope 计算： $$ k = RmsNorm(x @ wkv) $$ $$ k[..., -rope\dim:] = ROPE(k[..., -rope\dim:]) $$ 流水并行 PyPTO 采用了 MPMD 的调度方式，在 Decode 场景下，像 x@wqa 和 x@wkv 不会使用满所有的核，因此可以并行执行；同理，query 和 kv 后续的 RmsNorm，亦可并行执行； Unrollist 将动态展开为静态图 在 Prefill 和 Decode 场景中，t 的差异往往是巨大的。通常情况下，一套代码Tile 切分很难在不同场景下均达到较好的性能；但是通过对动态值 t 进行了多分档，以及 Tile 切分采用静态 tTile 的方法，达到了在不同场景下均实现较优性能的结果。 unrolllist = [128, 64, 32, 16, 1] for tIdx, unrollLength in pypto.loopunroll(0, t, 1, name="MLABSLOOP", idxname="bsoffset", unrolllist=unrolllist, ): ... 合图优化 通过设置合图参数，可以将相同结构的子图合并，避免同一结构子图数过大、避免重复搬运，同时可以增大核内流水调度可能性，实现了较优的性能。 passoptions={ "cubenbuffermode": 1, "vecnbuffermode": 2, "vecnbuffersetting": {-1: 2} } MatMul优化 根据输入参与matmul计算的tensor的shape通过设置合适的tileshape，将matmul的任务均衡地分配到各aic 核上。当k轴过大时，使能切k或者手动切k，减少了单个任务的搬运量。在shape较大的情况下，开启大包搬运，提高了带宽利用率。通过以上方式，提升了matmul任务的效率。 xtile.shape=[128, 4096], wkvshape=[4096, 512] pypto.setcubetileshapes([tilebs, tilebs], [256, 512], [128, 128], enablesplitk=True, enablemultidataload=True) kv = pypto.matmul(xtile, wkv, pypto.DataType.DTFP32) 泳道图 在单 die 64 batch, MTP1 的场景下，上板执行结果如下： mlaprolog泳道图 Compressor 新模型引入了 Compressor 模块，PyPTO 对此进行了实现。 计算过程 $$kv = X@W^{KV}$$ $$score = X@W^{Gate}+ape$$ 使用kv和score对kvstate和scorestate进行刷新。推理场景下，当startpos+1为compressratio倍数时，按下面的计算生成压缩的kv： $$kv=(kv\state score\state.\text{softmax(dim=1)).sum(dim=1)}$$ $$kv=\text{ROPE}(\text{RMSNorm}(kv))$$ rotate=true时对kv进行Hadamard变换。 多场景的不同优化 Compressor 模块使用的参数，例如压缩比 compressratio，rotate 等配置，在各层之间有所不同。针对不同的场景配置，PyPTO 在同一个算子中根据不同的分支，在每个分支上进行各自的优化，从而在不同的使用场景下均能达到较为良好的性能。下面以compressratio=4，rotate=false时的场景为例介绍优化方法。 MatMul优化 b = 64 bloop = (bsz + b - 1) // b for bidx in pypto.loop(bloop, name="LOOPCOMP1", idxname="bidx"): xview = pypto.view(x, [bs1, h], [bidxbs1, 0]) ## Matmul pypto.setcubetileshapes([128, 128], [256, 512], [128, 128], True) kvt = pypto.matmul(xview, wkv, pypto.DTFP32, btrans=True) scoret = pypto.matmul(xview, wgate, pypto.DTFP32, btrans=True) 该场景下两个矩阵乘的左右矩阵shape为[batchsizes1, 4096], [4096, 1024]。batchsize是动态的。 1. 如果直接对batch进行循环展开，静态图中矩阵乘的M轴shape将为s1，导致整个算子中右矩阵被重复搬运多次，性能较差。因此，在动态的batch轴，我们使用b=64进行切分。 2. K轴使能大包搬运：cubetileshapes([128, 128], [256, 512], [128, 128], True)代表K轴的L0和L1搬运的tilesize分别设置为256, 512。通过一次搬运较大的数据量进入L1，来提升带宽使用率。 向量操作优化 bvalid = (bsz-bidxb).min(b) for cidx in pypto.loop(bvalid, name="LOOPCOMP2", idxname="cidx"): pypto.setpassoptions(pgskippartition=True) 由于不同batch的startpos不同，它们的vector处理可能进入不同的分支。不同batch所更新的kvstate和scorestate的地址也不同。因此，我们对batch进行loop，对每个batch分别进行vector处理。我们通过设置''pgskippartition=True''，让一个batch的vector处理都在一个子图内。这是因为 1. 断图时中间数据会在GM和UB之间搬入搬出，造成性能劣化。 2. vector处理包括Softmax+ReduceSum和RMSNorm+RoPE，前者在1轴上进行操作，后者在尾轴上进行操作，难以较好地进行多核并行。在高吞吐的大batchsize场景时，由于batch间是独立的操作，因此每个batch作为一个子图，可以多核并行达成较好的性能。 index = cacheindex[:,pos:pos+1] kvstate = scatterupdate3d(kvstate, index, kv) ## b,4,2d scorestate = scatterupdate3d(scorestate, index, score) 对后续vector操作使用的kvstate和scorestate更新时，使用scatterupdate这一OP，可以避免将kvstate和scorestate多次搬入UB以及concat操作导致的性能劣化。 泳道图 在单 die 64 batch，MTP=1，并且每个batch都存在压缩操作的场景中，上板结果如下： compressor泳道图 IndexerProlog 和 DeepSeekV3.2 不同的是，IndexerProlog 只会出现在 compressratio = 4 的层，为后续 LightningIndexer 计算提供输入q、weight 及 qscale。 计算过程 1. Query 的计算 q, qscale的计算公式如下： $$ q\tmp = \text{qr}@{idx\wq\b} \cdot \text{qr\scale} \cdot \text{idx\wq\b\scale} $$ $$ q\hadamard = \text{Cat}(\{q\tmp[:, :nope\dim], Rope(q\tmp[:, nope\dim:])\}, -1)@hadamard $$ $$ q, q\scale = Quant(q\hadamard) $$ 其中，Rope表示旋转位置编码计算，Quant表示量化计算。 2. Weights 的计算 Weights的计算公式如下 $$ weights = x@\text{weights\proj} \cdot {\frac{1}{\sqrt{\text{idx\nq} \cdot \text{head\dim}}}} $$ 泳道图 在单 die 64 batch，MTP=1 的场景下，上板结果如下： indexerprolog泳道图 FA 类算子：SWA、CFA 和 SCFA 本次新模型的一个显著特点就是各层之间根据压缩比的不同，会采用不同的 Attention 计算方式。PyPTO 充分发挥了开发灵活性的特点，将不同层的 attention 实现分为三个不同的 attention 算子进行开发： SWA SWA，是 sliding window attention 的缩写，即滑窗注意力。在 compressratio = 1 的场景下，会采用该算子。通过掩码，实现了在 Prefill 阶段和不同 MTP 配置下的高效实现。 泳道图 在单 die 64 batch，MTP1，kvlen=8k 的场景下，上板结果如下： swa泳道图 CFA CFA，是 compressed flash attention 的缩写。在 compressratio = 128 的场景下，会采用该算子。注意到，CFA 的 kv cache 有两个来源，分别是 orikv 和 cmpkv，其中 orikv 是原始的 kv cache，cmpkv 是经过 compressor 模块压缩后的 kvcache。Orikv 我们采用滑窗选取，而 cmpkv 需要满足因果注意力机制。 泳道图 在单 die 64 batch，MTP，kvlen=8k 的场景下，上板结果如下： cfa泳道图 SCFA SCFA，是 sparse compressed flash attention 的缩写。在 compressratio = 4 的场景下，会采用该算子。和 CFA 不同的是，SCFA 中对 cmpkv 会通过 cmpsparseindices 离散地选取指定的 kv cache。我们通过 UB 将离散的 token 进行连续的聚合，使后续的 Attention 计算高效。 泳道图 在单 die 64 batch，MTP1，kvlen=8k 的场景下，上板结果如下： scfa泳道图 PTO-ISA 支持不同代际芯片的算子兼容 在算子层面，除了像 MXFP8 量化这类由于不同代际芯片本身能力不支持外，算子前端无需感知芯片的代际差异，即一套算子代码即可在不同代际的芯片上运行。而芯片不同代际的能力，通过 pass IR 和后续的 PTO 指令进行区分。 PTO-ISA PyPTO 后端基于 PTO 虚拟指令集（PTO ISA）打造。 PTO ISA 兼容新旧核架构（A2/A3/950D），并做到“兼容不降速”，针对不同代际芯片，统一指令接口，并做到微架构高度适配。 性能方面，封装 DSA 定制优化，结合毕昇 PTO 编译器强大的 VF 融合能力，更好进行micro kernel级别的融合，充分发挥新一代芯片算力。同时PTO ISA及配套毕昇编译器，面向算法快速更新的开发需求，提供了强大的 DFX 能力，提供 TPRINT (打印 Tile 或 GlobalTensor)、算子融合信息统计等功能，方便精度调试与软件优化。 hcpost hc\post 的计算如下： y = post.unsqueeze(-1) x.unsqueeze(-2) + torch.sum(comb.unsqueeze(-1) residual.unsqueeze(-2), dim=2) 只会使用到 Vector 核。在已做其他优化基础上，PTO-ISA 结合毕昇 PTO 编译器强大的 VF 融合能力，通过自动融合性能（相比于未使能自动融合）提升22.7%。

NPU DeepSeek-V4 PyPTO Fused Operator Optimization For the DeepSeek-V4 architecture, this release introduces multiple new fused operators: hcpre, Compressor, and three FA operators, SWA, CFA, and SCFA. MlaProlog and IndexerProlog are also adapted to the new architecture. hcpre is part of the Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC) in the new DeepSeek architecture. This technical report provides an overview of the implementation and optimization of these fused operators in PyPTO. It also describes how PTO-ISA (the PTO virtual instruction set) helps PyPTO provide cross-generation compatibility. For the PyPTO high-performance programming framework code, see the PyPTO repository: Cann-PyPTO . The following table shows measured performance data and code size for each operator on a single die with 64 batches, MTP1, and an 8K sequence. PyPTO can develop complex fused operators with a small amount of code and high development efficiency (3-7 days), while achieving good baseline performance: Operator Lines of Code (KLOC) B S1 S2 D cmpratio coff start pos Duration(us) slidingwindowattention 0.3 64 2 8192 512 N/A N/A N/A 65 compressedflashattention 0.2 64 2 8192 512 128 N/A N/A 90 sparsecompressedflashattention 0.2 64 2 8192 512 4 N/A N/A 160 compressorc4li 0.9 64 2 N/A 128 4 2 8192 55 compressorc4a 64 2 N/A 512 4 2 8192 80 compressorc128a 64 2 N/A 512 128 1 8192 55 compressorc4li 64 2 N/A 128 4 2 8191 75 compressorc4a 64 2 N/A 512 4 2 8191 95 compressorc128a 64 2 N/A 512 128 1 8191 125 mlaprolog 0.5 64 2 N/A N/A N/A N/A N/A 130 hcpre 0.4 64 2 N/A N/A N/A N/A N/A 70 lightningindexerprolog 0.3 64 2 N/A N/A N/A N/A N/A 101 hcpre hcpre is invoked twice in each layer, before attention and ffn computation. Computation Workflow 1. Calculate the denominator of RMSNorm. $$ rsqrt = \sqrt{\frac{1}{\frac{1}{n}\sum{i=1}^n xi^2 + \epsilon}} $$ 2. Calculate mixes. $$ mixes = (x @ hc\fn) \odot rsqrt $$ 3. Apply the Sinkhorn-Knopp algorithm. $$ pre, post, comb = sinkhorn(mixes, hc\scale, hc\base, hc\mult, hc\sinkhorn\iters) $$ In each iteration, the Sinkhorn-Knopp algorithm performs row-wise normalization followed by column-wise normalization. hcsinkhorniters controls the number of iterations. 4. Use pre and x to calculate y. $$ y = rowsum(pre \odot x) $$ In actual development, Ascend hardware features must be fully used to achieve better performance. The following sections describe the current solution and implementation in detail. Pipeline Parallelism The first step in the computation workflow is Vector computation, while $x @ hc\fn$ in the second step is Cube matrix-multiplication computation. The two operations have no dependency. The PyPTO framework supports simultaneous execution of the two tasks without manually inserting synchronization. Instruction Optimization The Sinkhorn-Knopp algorithm contains many repeated reduction operations chained with element-wise multiplication and division. In element-wise computation, pass optimizations and PTO instructions avoid explicit broadcasting and provide high-performance computation. pypto.experimental.setoperationconfig(combineaxis=True) MatMul Optimization In the Decode scenario, the K axis of matmul computation is long (16K), while the M\N axes are small. Therefore, split K to partition data across different cores and fully use computing resources. pypto.setcubetileshapes([16, 16], [512, 21024], [128, 128], \ enablemultidataload=True, enablesplitk=True) mmres = pypto.matmul(xfp32, hcfn, pypto.DTFP32, btrans=True) Computation Optimization The main difference between Prefill and Decode is the size of axis 0 of input x. In the Prefill scenario, t is usually large. In the Sinkhorn-Knopp algorithm, the reduction axis is small, with hcmult=4. The row reduction uses axis -1, and the column reduction uses axis -2. Here, a mathematically equivalent computation technique directly calculates the transpose during matrix multiplication in the second step: $$ hc\fn^T @ x^T $$ As a result, when entering the Sinkhorn-Knopp algorithm, t is placed on the last axis and the reduction axes are -2 and -3, improving computation efficiency. Computation Workflow 1. Query computation Includes two projections and RmsNorm (the weight of the second RmsNorm is always 1), followed by inplace interleaved rope computation on the last rope\dim dimensions of axis -1: $$ c^Q = RmsNorm(x @ wq\a) $$ $$ q = RmsNorm(c^Q @ wq\b) $$ $$ q[..., -rope\dim:] = ROPE(q[..., -rope\dim:]) $$ 2. Kv computation Includes one projection and RmsNorm, followed by inplace interleaved rope computation on the last rope\dim dimensions of axis -1: $$ k = RmsNorm(x @ wkv) $$ $$ k[..., -rope\dim:] = ROPE(k[..., -rope\dim:]) $$ Pipeline Parallelism PyPTO uses MPMD scheduling. In the Decode scenario, operations such as x@wqa and x@wkv do not use all cores and can therefore run in parallel. Similarly, the subsequent RmsNorm operations for query and kv can also run in parallel. Unrollist Expands Dynamic Execution into a Static Graph In Prefill and Decode scenarios, t often differs substantially. In general, it is difficult for one set of code Tile partitions to achieve good performance in different scenarios. By dividing dynamic value t into multiple ranges and using a static tTile for Tile partitioning, good performance is achieved across different scenarios. unrolllist = [128, 64, 32, 16, 1] for tIdx, unrollLength in pypto.loopunroll(0, t, 1, name="MLABSLOOP", idxname="bsoffset", unrolllist=unrolllist, ): ... Graph-Merging Optimization Setting graph-merging parameters merges subgraphs with the same structure, prevents an excessive number of same-structure subgraphs, avoids repeated movement, and increases opportunities for on-core pipeline scheduling, providing good performance. passoptions={ "cubenbuffermode": 1, "vecnbuffermode": 2, "vecnbuffersetting": {-1: 2} } MatMul Optimization Based on the shape of the input tensor participating in matmul computation, set an appropriate tileshape to evenly distribute matmul tasks across AIC cores. When the K axis is too large, enable split K or manually split K to reduce the movement volume of a single task. For large shapes, enable large-block movement to improve bandwidth utilization. These methods improve matmul task efficiency. xtile.shape=[128, 4096], wkvshape=[4096, 512] pypto.setcubetileshapes([tilebs, tilebs], [256, 512], [128, 128], enablesplitk=True, enablemultidataload=True) kv = pypto.matmul(xtile, wkv, pypto.DataType.DTFP32) Swimlane Diagram For a single die with 64 batches and MTP1, the on-device execution result is as follows: mlaprolog Swimlane Diagram Compressor The new model introduces the Compressor module, which PyPTO implements. Computation Workflow $$kv = X@W^{KV}$$ $$score = X@W^{Gate}+ape$$ Use kv and score to refresh kvstate and scorestate. In inference scenarios, when startpos+1 is a multiple of compressratio, generate compressed kv through the following computation: $$kv=(kv\state score\state.\text{softmax(dim=1)).sum(dim=1)}$$ $$kv=\text{ROPE}(\text{RMSNorm}(kv))$$ When rotate=true, perform a Hadamard transform on kv. Different Optimizations for Multiple Scenarios Parameters used by the Compressor module, such as compression ratio compressratio and rotate, differ across layers. For different scenario configurations, PyPTO uses different branches within the same operator and optimizes each branch separately, providing good performance in different usage scenarios. The following example describes optimization methods when compressratio=4 and rotate=false. MatMul Optimization b = 64 bloop = (bsz + b - 1) // b for bidx in pypto.loop(bloop, name="LOOPCOMP1", idxname="bidx"): xview = pypto.view(x, [bs1, h], [bidxbs1, 0]) ## Matmul pypto.setcubetileshapes([128, 128], [256, 512], [128, 128], True) kvt = pypto.matmul(xview, wkv, pypto.DTFP32, btrans=True) scoret = pypto.matmul(xview, wgate, pypto.DTFP32, btrans=True) In this scenario, the shapes of the left and right matrices in the two matrix multiplications are [batchsizes1, 4096] and [4096, 1024]. batchsize is dynamic. 1. If batch is directly unrolled in a loop, the shape of the M axis of matrix multiplication in the static graph is s1. This causes the right matrix to be moved repeatedly many times across the operator, resulting in poor performance. Therefore, the dynamic batch axis is partitioned with b=64. 2. Enable large-block movement on the K axis: cubetileshapes([128, 128], [256, 512], [128, 128], True) means that the L0 and L1 movement tilesizes on the K axis are set to 256 and 512, respectively. Moving a larger amount of data into L1 at a time improves bandwidth utilization. Vector Operation Optimization bvalid = (bsz-bidxb).min(b) for cidx in pypto.loop(bvalid, name="LOOPCOMP2", idxname="cidx"): pypto.setpassoptions(pgskippartition=True) Because the startpos values of different batches differ, their Vector processing may enter different branches. The addresses of kvstate and scorestate updated by different batches also differ. Therefore, loop over batches and process each batch's Vector operations separately. Set ''pgskippartition=True'' so that the Vector processing of one batch remains in one subgraph. This is because: 1. When the graph is split, intermediate data moves between GM and UB, degrading performance. 2. Vector processing includes Softmax+ReduceSum and RMSNorm+RoPE. The former operates along axis 1, while the latter operates along the last axis, making effective multi-core parallelism difficult. In high-throughput, large-batchsize scenarios, operations across batches are independent. Therefore, using each batch as one subgraph enables multi-core parallelism and good performance. index = cacheindex[:,pos:pos+1] kvstate = scatterupdate3d(kvstate, index, kv) ## b,4,2d scorestate = scatterupdate3d(scorestate, index, score) When updating kvstate and scorestate for subsequent Vector operations, use the scatterupdate OP to avoid repeatedly moving kvstate and scorestate into the UB and to avoid performance degradation caused by concat operations. Computation Workflow 1. Query computation The formulas for calculating q and qscale are as follows: $$ q\tmp = \text{qr}@{idx\wq\b} \cdot \text{qr\scale} \cdot \text{idx\wq\b\scale} $$ $$ q\hadamard = \text{Cat}(\{q\tmp[:, :nope\dim], Rope(q\tmp[:, nope\dim:])\}, -1)@hadamard $$ $$ q, q\scale = Quant(q\hadamard) $$ Here, Rope represents rotary position encoding computation, and Quant represents quantization computation. 2. Weights computation The formula for calculating Weights is as follows: $$ weights = x@\text{weights\proj} \cdot {\frac{1}{\sqrt{\text{idx\nq} \cdot \text{head\dim}}}} $$ Swimlane Diagram For a single die with 64 batches and MTP=1, the on-device result is as follows: indexerprolog Swimlane Diagram FA Operators: SWA, CFA, and SCFA A notable feature of the new model is that different Attention computation methods are used across layers based on their compression ratios. PyPTO fully uses its development flexibility and implements attention for different layers as three different attention operators: SWA SWA is short for sliding window attention. This operator is used when compressratio = 1. Masks provide efficient implementation during Prefill and under different MTP configurations. Swimlane Diagram For a single die with 64 batches, MTP1, and kvlen=8k, the on-device result is as follows: swa Swimlane Diagram CFA CFA is short for compressed flash attention. This operator is used when compressratio = 128. The CFA kv cache comes from two sources, orikv and cmpkv. orikv is the original kv cache, while cmpkv is the kvcache compressed by the compressor module. A sliding window is used to select Orikv, while cmpkv must satisfy the causal attention mechanism. Swimlane Diagram For a single die with 64 batches, MTP, and kvlen=8k, the on-device result is as follows: cfa Swimlane Diagram SCFA SCFA is short for sparse compressed flash attention. This operator is used when compressratio = 4. Unlike CFA, SCFA uses cmpsparseindices to discretely select specified kv cache entries from cmpkv. The UB contiguously gathers discrete tokens so that subsequent Attention computation is efficient. Swimlane Diagram For a single die with 64 batches, MTP1, and kvlen=8k, the on-device result is as follows: scfa Swimlane Diagram PTO-ISA Support for Operator Compatibility Across Chip Generations At the operator level, except for capabilities such as MXFP8 quantization that are unsupported by certain chip generations, the operator frontend does not need to be aware of chip-generation differences. One set of operator code can run on different chip generations. The capabilities of different chip generations are distinguished through pass IR and subsequent PTO instructions. PTO-ISA The PyPTO backend is built on the PTO virtual instruction set (PTO ISA). PTO ISA supports both old and new core architectures (A2/A3/950D) while providing compatibility without performance degradation. It uses a unified instruction interface across chip generations and highly adapts to each microarchitecture. For performance, it encapsulates DSA custom optimizations and combines them with the powerful VF fusion capability of the BiSheng PTO compiler to better perform micro-kernel-level fusion and fully use the computing power of next-generation chips. To meet rapid algorithm-update requirements, PTO ISA and the supporting BiSheng compiler also provide powerful DFX capabilities, including TPRINT (printing a Tile or GlobalTensor) and operator-fusion information statistics, facilitating precision debugging and software optimization. hcpost hc\post is calculated as follows: y = post.unsqueeze(-1) x.unsqueeze(-2) + torch.sum(comb.unsqueeze(-1) residual.unsqueeze(-2), dim=2) Only Vector cores are used. Building on other optimizations, PTO-ISA combines with the powerful VF fusion capability of the BiSheng PTO compiler. Automatic fusion improves performance by 22.7% compared with automatic fusion disabled.

NPU DeepSeek SHMEM通信优化实践 简介 在现代大规模语言模型（LLM）的发展中，高效的并行计算与内存管理技术正成为提升模型性能和部署效率的关键因素。随着模型参数规模的不断增长，传统的通信与存储方式在面对高并发、高吞吐场景时逐渐暴露出性能瓶颈。 OpenSHMEM 是一种基于共享地址空间的并行编程模型，支持多线程、多节点环境下的高效数据交换。通过极简接口，实现极低延迟、高可扩展的远程内存访问，是构建下一代超算应用的理想选择。为了弥补传统通信方式的短板，CANN开源社区对标OpenSHMEM概念提供了CANN SHMEM编程接口，基于CANN提供全局内存交互能力。通过封装Host侧与Device侧接口，为模型与算子开发者提供高效、易用的跨设备内存通信能力，简化卡间数据同步与通算融合算子开发流程。 其核心价值在于： 简化分布式场景下的卡间通信逻辑，降低算子开发门槛 集成MTE、xDMA等高性能通信引擎，支持D2D/D2H通信方式，提升多设备协同效率 与CANN生态深度适配，支持通算融合类算子的快速部署 本文主要介绍基于昇腾NPU使能shmem的过程，以及基于其开发高性能算子的实践。更多信息信息可参考SHMEM 开源仓 。 在本篇技术报告中，我们将对SHMEM编程API在昇腾平台的使用方式和具体优化进行细致地阐述，通过dispatch&combine/kvoffload等典型场景为例详细描述shmem接口的调用方法。 Highlights SHMEM API 支持NPU HBM&CPU DDR混合编址，优化KVoffload吞吐； HIXL支持SHMEM API，提供rH2D，d2RH 池化数据访问和通信能力； 通过cann shmem 使能通算融合编程，优化DeepEP中的dispatch&combine的通信调用方式； 通过tilelang，pypto使能shmem 通算融合编程，提升通算融合编程易用性； 使用SHMEM进行KVCache Offload优化 Offload 通过将 LLM 推理过程中的 KV Cache 卸载到 Host 内存中，减轻 Device 内存压力，和稀疏注意力结合，可以应对 LLM 长序列推理面临的内存瓶颈和计算瓶颈，增大 batch size，进而提高推理吞吐量。 在 Offload 过程中，很重要的一环是 KV Cache 在 Host 和 Device 之间的数据搬运，shmem 提供了统一的内存管理能力，使得模型侧无需感知 Host 和 Device 的内存差异，只需调用相应的 torch 接口，就可以实现 h2d 和 d2h 的数据搬运。同时得益于 shmem 对于集群内低延迟，高带宽通信的使能，Offload 过程中 KV Cache 的 h2d 耗时也有所减少，对于提高整网推理时延和吞吐量起到关键作用。 以 DeepSeek V3.2 为例 在模型初始化阶段，调用 shmem 的 torch 接口为将要卸载的 KV Cache 分配 Host 侧内存，并将其地址映射到 Device，模型推理过程中可以直接将这块内存当成 Device tensor 来使用。 cachenopebytes = cachenopetensor.untypedstorage().nbytes() cachenopedataptr = aclshmemmalloc(cachenopebytes, MemType.HOSTSIDE) metadata = { "dataptr": cachenopedataptr, "device": cachedevice, "nbytes": cachenopebytes, "dtype": dtype, "size": cachenopeshape, "stride": cachenopetensor.stride(), "storageoffset": cachenopetensor.storageoffset(), } storage = torchnpu.C.constructstoragefromdatapointer( metadata["dataptr"], metadata["device"], metadata["nbytes"] ) cachenope = torchnpu.C.constructNPUTensorFromStorageAndMetadata(metadata, storage) 在 Prefill 阶段，模型推理生成的 KV Cache 会被异步卸载到这块内存中； 在 Decoding 阶段，Lightning Indexer 生成稀疏注意力的 topk ids 之后，我们会调用 GatherSelectionKVCache
