64卡环境，64K 序列长度下，模型推理支持的最大 batch size 可以从 1024 增长到 2048。 为通过 Offload 进一步提高推理吞吐量，字节提出了 ShadowKV（吞吐提升 3 倍），百度提出了 ESS 系统（吞吐提升 123%），清华大学提出了 NOSA 结构，参考这些方案，未来 Offload + shmem 的优化方向包括： （1）通过将更多高访问量的 Token Cache 缓存在 Device 侧，充分发挥 shmem 高带宽 d2d 的能力，减轻 Decoding 阶段 h2d 的压力，并结合并行掩盖技术，将 Gather 耗时隐藏于前向计算，吞吐量有望翻倍； （2）参考 NOSA 等结构，在算法层面做出创新，突破 DeepSeek V3.2 每步迭代都需实时计算 Topk 并重新 Gather 的限制；（3）借助 shmem 跨机 rH2D、D2rH 的能力，在框架侧实现 Decoding 阶段跨机 Gather，避免全量 KV Cache 的 h2h 传输，进一步降低推理时延。 基于SHMEM实现HIXL单边通信并集成至Mooncake社区 随着LLM上下文窗口持续突破至128K乃至百万级token规模，超长序列在处理长文档分析、多轮复杂对话、代码生成等高阶场景时，其核心瓶颈已从传统的计算算力约束转向存储子系统与数据传输效率的双重挑战。 KV Cache随序列长度呈线性增长特性，在超长序列场景下其容量可达到数十GB级，远超单卡NPU HBM承载上限，进而触发必须将部分或全部KV Cache数据卸载至CPU侧DRAM的部署策略。这一架构适配性调整，虽有效突破了“显存墙”限制、提升了并发请求处理能力，但也引入了NPU与DRAM之间高频次的数据交互需求，其中PUT D2rH（Device to Remote Host）及GET rH2D（Remote Host to Device）的高性能传输诉求，成为制约整体推理吞吐量与延迟表现的核心技术痛点。 HIXL介绍 HIXL（Huawei Xfer Library）是一个灵活、高效的昇腾单边通信库，面向集群场景提供简单、可靠、高效的点对点数据传输能力，并通过简易API开放给用户。HIXL基于SHMEM机制，可高效解决PUT D2rH 与 GET rH2D 场景下的高性能传输问题，为超长序列LLM推理的存储与传输瓶颈提供针对性解决方案。HIXL核心优势体现在三方面： 1. 支持单边零拷贝（One-Sided Zero-Copy）通信机制； 2. 屏蔽硬件差异，兼容多链路实现跨设备高速互联； 3. 极简API设计，深度适配开源生态框架。 HIXL当前已与Mooncake社区深度集成，可实现KV Cache低延迟传输及池化复用等典型业务场景。更多信息信息可参考HIXL开源仓：https://gitcode.com/cann/hixl。 HIXL集成SHMEM HIXL集成SHMEM的核心目标是实现跨进程的全局统一编址，依托SHMEM的内存共享机制，使各进程可直接访问彼此的DRAM内存空间，无需内核态数据拷贝，从而实现高性能传输。其技术实现逻辑如下： 1. 内存申请：各进程独立向本地DRAM申请私有内存段，获取该内存段的虚拟地址与本地物理地址； 2. 地址交换：各进程将自身内存段的物理地址信息（包括基址、长度、权限等）同步至集群内所有参与进程，完成全局物理地址池的构建； 3. 跨进程页表映射：各进程将接收到的其它进程内存物理地址，映射到自身虚拟地址空间，形成全局统一的虚拟——物理地址映射关系，实现 “一处编址、全域可达”； 4. SDMA数据访问：基于全局统一编址，通过SDMA引擎发起远程内存读写操作，直接访问任意进程的DRAM内存，无需进程间显式交互。 HIXL可配置OPTIONENABLEUSEFABRICMEM, 1: 开启SHMEM模式，0：不开启SHMEM模式。 性能测试结果 基于A3超节点，测试HIXL（SHMEM）性能数据如下所示： 1. 双机单卡1对1, 一个block的数据量：模拟DeepSeek-R1 KV大小，即：61x128K + 61x16K = 8784KB, 测试传输100次取平均，剔除第一次带建立链接的时间。（下同） 2. 双机16卡1对1 3. 双机单卡1对1大块数据量测试 基于SHMEM实现Dispatch&Combine并集成至DeepEP Dispatch&Combine介绍 DeepEP的Dispatch和Combine是 Mixture of Experts（MoE, 混合专家）专家并行（EP）中All to All通信的核心操作，分别负责任务分发与结果聚合，适配训练高吞吐与推理低延迟两大场景，是性能的关键保障。 Dispatch 必选输入包括：x，expertIds； x为待分发的原始 token 表示。每个 token 将根据路由结果被发送给一个或多个专家。 expertIds由 Router 生成的专家分配索引。expertIds[i, j] 表示第 i 个 token 的第 j 个被选中的 expert ID（0 ≤ expertId 发状态——>等状态——>本地win区数据拷贝 1. 发数据： 假设当前x的shape为[Bs，H]，expertIds的shape为[Bs, K]，Bs个token中每个token都会发送K次到不同的expert上，因此实现了token往不同rank的不同专家分发的效果即Dispatch 2. 发状态： 状态区的作用是为了标记本rank所需要的接收的来自其他rank的数据的发送状态（即是否发完），主要关注点为两个数据，一个是flag，当flag为1的时候代表来自某rank发往某expert的数据已经发送完毕，并且置为1，cnt表示来自某rank发往某expert的数据的个数 3. 等状态： 由于当前rank也会接受来自其他卡dispatch过来的数据，因此需要不断的通过循环去看当前rank接受的数据是否接受完毕，即去当前rank的状态区，去通过while获取flag的求和结果，如果当前的求和结果满足了对应的要求，则会跳出当前等状态的循环，即代表当前rank已经接受完毕来自其他rank发过来的token 4. 本地win区数据拷贝： 在等状态结束后，即可以去本rank的win区数据区拷贝数据到本rank的UB，然后再通过UB把接收的数据给搬运到本rank的GM上实现Dispatch最终输出数据 win区数据区的大致结构如下： 左边是rank0的win数据区，红色部分代表rank0接收到来自rank0的数据，蓝色部分代表rank0接收到来自rank1的数据，由于等状态已经结束，当前只需要把红色部分的数据和蓝色部分的数据给搬运到本rank0的UB，然后再搬出到rank0的win区，对于右侧的rank1也是同理。 当然，这里面win数据区每一行不仅包含了token的信息，还包含了量化参数信息，三元组信息，把对应的数据通过切片方式搬运即可形成例如expandXOut、assistInfoForCombineOut Combine 通过Dispatch算子后，token被发往不同的专家进行处理，然后Combine的作用则是把这些专家处理后的数据给一一退还回其原来所属rank，combine算子与dispatch算子本质上是一个逆映射的关系。 combine算子的输入包含：expandX、assistInfoForCombine、epSendCounts expandX的含义表示为经过Dispatch发送到本rank数据，经过expert处理后的数据（即要还回原来rank的数据） assistInfoForCombine表示为要还回对应rank的数据的三元组信息，通过该信息即可知道某条token来自哪个rank的哪个token的第几次发送 epSendCounts表示从EP通信域各卡接收的token数，对应MoeDistributeDispatchV2中的epRecvCounts输出。 combine算子的输出为xOut，即通过combine后，把原来从本卡发出去的数据经过来自各个rank的expert处理后的数据 combine算子的执行过程包含：发数据——>发状态——>等状态——>本地数据拷贝 1. 发数据过程： 由于已经有了三元组的信息，存储在assistInfoForCombine，那么久可以根据其中表达的某rank，某专家，第某次发送，通过for循环一条条处理本卡要还的token，把一条条token还到对应的rank的win数据区正确的位置。 2. 发状态： 在发数据的时候就可以发状态，发一条数据就可以发一条状态，和dispatch不同的是，发状态直接把对应该token的整条状态区全部填充为1, 3. 等状态： 本rank除了要通过for循环完成发数据和发状态后，还要通过一个while循环不断的等状态，比如当前rank在dispatch的时候就有A个token，然后每个token发K次，那么理论本rank应该能接受到通过combine返回的AK个token，然后while等待的目标则是去看这些token对应的状态区是否求和等于其目标值，若为目标值则代表本rank所发出去的数据全部都还回来了，此时等状态逻辑完毕 4. 本地数据拷贝与处理： 本rank需要的AK个token已经在本rank的win数据区了，当前就是要把这些数据给搬运到UB进行数据处理后，再搬出到本rank的win区。数据处理的思路为，K个批量处理，一共处理A次对应原本rank的A个token，每一个批次的K个token为当前这个token重复发K次后换回来的K个数据（这K个数据是同一个token被不同rank上不同expert处理后的结果），要做的就是通过某种方式将这K个数据融合，最后得到一个融合了K个专家处理后的该token。然后把这个融合K个token的这一个token搬运到UB上，这个过程执行A次，即完成了combine算子的XOut结果， 指定为当前die分配的内存空间，单位为字节，此区域为数据区和状态区共用。使用内存的总大小不可超过分配的内存大小。 2. “ret = dcbuffer.ShmemInit(16, rank, t)” 规定当前die的rankid以及当前通信的总die数。 3. “shmemcontext = dcbuffer.InitAndGetMC2CommContext() ” 把共享内存信息，封装进shmemcontext，作为入参传给算子 SHMEM使能 算子内通过GetShmemDataAddr和GetShmemSignalAddr接口获取目标对端卡数据区和状态区的内存起始地址。 shmem方案里，状态区紧跟在数据区后面，context->shmemaddr对应当前卡的shmem内存起址。 die集群共享一个全局虚拟地址，die与die之间的内存步距设为1G，用户可根据需要决定分配内存的次数和大小，但单die分配的内存总大小不可超过1G。 整网接入及效果 1. 在modelingdeepseek.py同级目录下，放置基于shmem仓编译出的libcommshmem.so和pyshmem.cpython-311-aarch64-linux-gnu.so动态库文件，以支持封装的shmem API接口调用。 2. 封装initshmemonce函数，确保shmem内存初始化在整网执行流程里只调用一次。当调用超过一次时，函数自动返回（整网里shmem内存初始化次数超过一次会报错）。将该函数放置DeepseekV3ForCausalLM类的init函数下。 3. dispatch和combine的入参里均添加shmemcontext入参，此入参包含了为当前die分配的内存起址和内存大小信息，由shmem接口shmemgetcontext获取。 4. 将原生torchnpu的dispatch和combine替换成shmem版本的dispatch, combine。 使用集成SHMEM的编程框架实现dispatch&combine算子 除原生Shmem NPU DeepSeek SHMEM Communication Optimization Practice Introduction As modern large language models (LLMs) evolve, efficient parallel computing and memory-management technologies are becoming key factors in improving model performance and deployment efficiency. As model parameter scales continue to increase, conventional communication and storage methods increasingly expose performance bottlenecks in high-concurrency, high-throughput scenarios. OpenSHMEM is a parallel programming model based on a shared address space that supports efficient data exchange in multi-threaded and multi-node environments. Through a minimal interface, it provides extremely low-latency, highly scalable remote-memory access and is ideal for building next-generation supercomputing applications. To address the shortcomings of conventional communication methods, the CANN open-source community provides CANN SHMEM programming interfaces based on OpenSHMEM concepts and CANN's global-memory interaction capabilities. By encapsulating Host-side and Device-side interfaces, it provides model and operator developers with efficient, easy-to-use cross-device memory communication, simplifying inter-card data synchronization and the development of communication-computation fused operators. Its core benefits are: Simplifies inter-card communication logic in distributed scenarios and reduces the operator-development barrier. Integrates high-performance communication engines such as MTE and xDMA, supports D2D/D2H communication, and improves multi-device collaboration efficiency. Deeply integrates with the CANN ecosystem and supports rapid deployment of communication-computation fused operators. This document primarily describes the process of enabling SHMEM on Ascend NPUs and practices for developing high-performance operators with it. For more information, see the SHMEM open-source repository . This technical report describes in detail how to use and optimize SHMEM programming APIs on Ascend platforms. It uses typical scenarios such as dispatch&combine/kvoffload to describe SHMEM interface invocations in detail. Highlights The SHMEM API supports hybrid addressing of NPU HBM and CPU DDR to optimize KVoffload throughput. HIXL supports the SHMEM API and provides pooled rH2D and d2RH data-access and communication capabilities. CANN SHMEM enables communication-computation fused programming and optimizes communication invocations for dispatch&combine in DeepEP. Tilelang and PyPTO enable SHMEM communication-computation fused programming and improve its programmability. KVCache Offload Optimization with SHMEM Offload moves the KV Cache in LLM inference to Host memory, relieving Device memory pressure. Combined with sparse attention, it addresses memory and computation bottlenecks in long-sequence LLM inference, increases batch size, and improves inference throughput. During Offload, moving the KV Cache between Host and Device is critical. SHMEM provides unified memory management so that the model does not need to distinguish between Host and Device memory. It only invokes the corresponding torch interface to move data through H2D and D2H. SHMEM also enables low-latency, high-bandwidth communication within a cluster, reducing KV Cache H2D latency during Offload and playing a key role in improving full-network inference latency and throughput. Using DeepSeek V3.2 as an example: During model initialization, invoke the SHMEM torch interface to allocate Host-side memory for the KV Cache to offload and map its address to the Device. During model inference, this memory can be used directly as a Device Tensor. cachenopebytes = cachenopetensor.untypedstorage().nbytes() cachenopedataptr = aclshmemmalloc(cachenopebytes, MemType.HOSTSIDE) metadata = { "dataptr": cachenopedataptr, "device": cachedevice, "nbytes": cachenopebytes, "dtype": dtype, "size": cachenopeshape, "stride": cachenopetensor.stride(), "storageoffset": cachenopetensor.storageoffset(), } storage = torchnpu.C.constructstoragefromdatapointer( metadata["dataptr"], metadata["device"], metadata["nbytes"] ) cachenope = torchnpu.C.constructNPUTensorFromStorageAndMetadata(metadata, storage) During Prefill, the KV Cache generated by model inference is asynchronously offloaded to this memory. During Decoding, after Lightning Indexer generates topk ids for sparse attention, invoke the GatherSelectionKVCache operator to select the KV Cache of the corresponding tokens from Host memory based on the topk ids. During this process, the operator directly accesses the mapped Device Tensor without needing to know its Host-side memory layout, simplifying the algorithm workflow. kv cache constructed by shmem and mapped into device tensor fullkvcache = knope.squeeze(2) fullkrope = kpe.squeeze(2) if not self.kvcachec8 else offloadcache.emptyrope selectionkvactualseq = torchnpu.npugatherselectionkvcache( selectionkrope, selectionkvcache, selectionkvblocktable, selectionkvblockstatus, topkindices, fullkrope, fullkvcache, blocktable, actualseqlengthskv, actualseqqlen, selectiontopkblocksize=1) After Offload + SHMEM is enabled, DeepSeek V3.2 provides significant inference-memory benefits: In an Atlas A3 environment with 64 cards and a 64K sequence length, the maximum batch size supported by model inference increases from 1024 to 2048. To further improve inference throughput through Offload, ByteDance proposed ShadowKV (3x throughput improvement), Baidu proposed the ESS system (123% throughput improvement), and Tsinghua University proposed the NOSA architecture. Based on these solutions, future Offload + SHMEM optimization directions include: (1) Cache more frequently accessed Token Cache entries on the Device side to fully use SHMEM's high-bandwidth D2D capability, relieve H2D pressure during Decoding, and combine parallel-overlap technology to hide Gather latency in forward computation, potentially doubling throughput. (2) Refer to architectures such as NOSA and innovate at the algorithm level to overcome the DeepSeek V3.2 limitation that requires real-time Topk calculation and repeated Gather in every iteration. (3) Use SHMEM's cross-node rH2D and D2rH capabilities to implement cross-node Gather during Decoding at the framework level, avoiding H2H transfer of the entire KV Cache and further reducing inference latency. Implementing HIXL One-Sided Communication with SHMEM and Integrating It into the Mooncake Community As LLM context windows continue to expand to 128K or even millions of tokens, the core bottleneck for ultra-long sequences in advanced scenarios such as long-document analysis, complex multi-turn conversations, and code generation has shifted from conventional computing-power constraints to the dual challenges of the storage subsystem and data-transfer efficiency. The KV Cache grows linearly with sequence length. In ultra-long-sequence scenarios, its capacity can reach tens of GB, far exceeding the HBM capacity of a single NPU card and requiring some or all KV Cache data to be offloaded to CPU-side DRAM. This architectural adaptation overcomes the "global-memory wall" and increases concurrent-request processing capacity, but it also introduces frequent data interaction between the NPU and DRAM. High-performance transfer requirements for PUT D2rH (Device to Remote Host) and GET rH2D (Remote Host to Device) become the core technical bottleneck that limits overall inference throughput and latency. HIXL Introduction HIXL (Huawei Xfer Library) is a flexible and efficient Ascend one-sided communication library that provides simple, reliable, and efficient point-to-point data transfer in cluster scenarios through an easy-to-use API. Based on SHMEM, HIXL efficiently addresses high-performance transfer requirements for PUT D2rH and GET rH2D, providing a targeted solution to storage and transfer bottlenecks in ultra-long-sequence LLM inference. HIXL provides three core advantages: 1. Supports One-Sided Zero-Copy communication. 2. Shields hardware differences and supports multiple links for high-speed cross-device interconnection. 3. Uses a minimal API design and deeply adapts to open-source ecosystem frameworks. HIXL is deeply integrated with the Mooncake community and supports typical service scenarios such as low-latency KV Cache transfer and pooled reuse. For more information, see the HIXL open-source repository: https://gitcode.com/cann/hixl. HIXL Integration with SHMEM HIXL integrates SHMEM to implement unified global addressing across processes. With SHMEM's memory-sharing mechanism, each process can directly access the DRAM memory space of other processes without kernel-mode data copies, providing high-performance transfer. The technical implementation is as follows: 1. Memory allocation: Each process independently requests a private memory segment from local DRAM and obtains its virtual and local physical addresses. 2. Address exchange: Each process synchronizes the physical-address information of its memory segment, including the base address, length, and permissions, to all participating processes in the cluster, constructing a global physical-address pool. 3. Cross-process page-table mapping: Each process maps the received physical memory addresses of other processes to its own virtual-address space, forming a globally unified virtual-to-physical address mapping and enabling "address once, access globally." 4. SDMA data access: Based on globally unified addressing, the SDMA engine initiates remote-memory reads and writes and directly accesses the DRAM of any process without explicit inter-process interaction. HIXL can configure OPTIONENABLEUSEFABRICMEM: 1 enables SHMEM mode, and 0 disables SHMEM mode. Performance Test Results The HIXL (SHMEM) performance data tested on an A3 SuperPod is as follows: 1. Large-block data-volume test with two nodes, one card per node, one-to-one. Implementing Dispatch&Combine with SHMEM and Integrating It into DeepEP Dispatch&Combine Introduction DeepEP Dispatch and Combine are the core All-to-All communication operations in Mixture of Experts (MoE) Expert Parallel (EP). They are responsible for task distribution and result aggregation, respectively, support the two major scenarios of high-throughput training and low-latency inference, and are critical to performance. Dispatch Required inputs include x and expertIds. x is the original token representation to distribute. Each token is sent to one or more experts based on the routing result. expertIds contains expert-assignment indices generated by the Router. expertIds[i, j] represents the j-th selected expert ID for the i-th token (0 ≤ expertId send status ——> wait for status ——> copy local win-region data 1. Send data: Assume that the current shape of x is [Bs, H] and the shape of expertIds is [Bs, K]. Each of the Bs tokens is sent K times to different experts, distributing tokens to different experts on different ranks, which is Dispatch. 2. Send status: The status region marks the transmission status of data that the current rank must receive from other ranks (that is, whether transmission is complete). It primarily contains two values: flag and cnt. When flag is 1, data from a rank to an expert has been completely sent and flag is set to 1. cnt indicates the number of data entries sent from a rank to an expert. 3. Wait for status: Because the current rank also receives data dispatched from other cards, a loop must continually check whether all data for the current rank has been received. In the status region of the current rank, a while loop obtains the sum of flags. If the current sum meets the corresponding requirement, the loop exits, indicating that the current rank has received all tokens sent from other ranks. 4. Copy local win-region data: After status waiting ends, data can be copied from the win-region data area of the current rank to the UB of the current rank. The UB then moves the received data to the GM of the current rank to produce the final Dispatch output. The approximate win-region data-area structure is as follows: The left side is rank0's win data region. The red part represents data received by rank0 from rank0, and the blue part represents data received by rank0 from rank1. Because status waiting has ended, only the red and blue data need to be moved to rank0's UB and then moved out to rank0's win region. The same applies to rank1 on the right. Each row in the win data region contains token information, quantization-parameter information, and tuple information. Moving the corresponding data through slicing forms outputs such as expandXOut and assistInfoForCombineOut. Combine After Dispatch, tokens are sent to different experts for processing. Combine returns the processed data from these experts to the ranks to which the tokens originally belonged. Combine and Dispatch are essentially inverse mappings. Combine inputs include expandX, assistInfoForCombine, and epSendCounts. expandX represents data sent to the current rank through Dispatch and then processed by experts (that is, data to return to the original rank). assistInfoForCombine contains tuple information for data to return to the corresponding rank. It identifies the rank and token from which a token originated and the transmission number for that token. epSendCounts represents the number of tokens received from each card in the EP communication domain and corresponds to the epRecvCounts output of MoeDistributeDispatchV2. Combine outputs xOut, that is, after Combine, data originally sent from the current card after processing by experts on different ranks. The Combine execution workflow includes: send data ——> send status ——> wait for status ——> copy local data 1. Send data: Tuple information is already stored in assistInfoForCombine. Based on the rank, expert, and transmission number it describes, a for loop processes the tokens to return from the current card one by one and returns each token to the correct position in the corresponding rank's win data region. 2. Send status: Status can be sent while data is sent, with one status sent for each data entry. Unlike Dispatch, sending status directly fills the entire status region corresponding to the token with 1. 3. Wait for status: After the current rank sends data and status through the for loop, it must also continually wait for status through a while loop. For example, if the current rank had A tokens during Dispatch and each token was sent K times, the current rank should theoretically receive AK tokens returned through Combine. The while loop checks whether the sum of the status regions corresponding to these tokens equals the target value. When it does, all data sent by the current rank has been returned and status waiting is complete. 4. Copy and process local data: The AK tokens required by the current rank are now in its win data region. They must be moved to the UB for processing and then moved out to the current rank's win region. Process data in batches of K for A iterations corresponding to the original A tokens on the rank. The K tokens in each batch are the K returned data entries after the current token was sent K times. These K entries are results from different experts on different ranks processing the same token. Fuse the K entries to obtain the token after processing by K experts. Then move this one token fused from K entries to the UB. Repeating this process A times produces the XOut result of the Combine operator. The following figure shows rank1 fusing its win data region to obtain the final processed data. The same applies to other ranks. Implementing Dispatch&Combine Operators with SHMEM APIs Based on the symmetric-memory mechanism, SHMEM efficiently supports development of communication-computation fused operators. The following figure shows the basic principle of SHMEM symmetric memory. Operator Development Workflow SHMEM Initialization 1. "pyshmem.MoeDistributeCppBuffer(30010241024, 1)" specifies the memory space allocated for the current die in bytes. The data and status regions share this area. Total memory usage cannot exceed the allocated memory size. 2. "ret = dcbuffer.ShmemInit(16, rank, t)" specifies the rankid of the current die and the total number of dies in the current communication domain. 3. "shmemcontext = dcbuffer.InitAndGetMC2CommContext()" encapsulates shared-memory information in shmemcontext and passes it to the operator as an input parameter. Enabling SHMEM Within an operator, use the GetShmemDataAddr and GetShmemSignalAddr interfaces to obtain the starting memory addresses of the data and status regions on the target remote card. In the SHMEM solution, the status region immediately follows the data region. context->shmemaddr corresponds to the starting SHMEM memory address of the current card. A die cluster shares one global virtual address. The memory stride between dies is set to 1 GB. Users can determine the number and size of memory allocations as required, but total memory allocated per die cannot exceed 1 GB. Full-Network Integration and Results 1. In the directory containing modelingdeepseek.py, place the libcommshmem.so and pyshmem.cpython-311-aarch64-linux-gnu.so dynamic libraries compiled from the SHMEM repository to support invocations of encapsulated SHMEM API interfaces. 2. Encapsulate the initshmemonce function to ensure that SHMEM memory initialization is invoked only once during full-network execution. When invoked more than once, the function returns automatically (initializing SHMEM memory more than once in the full network causes an error). Place this function under the init function of the DeepseekV3ForCausalLM class. 3. Add the shmemcontext input parameter to both Dispatch and Combine. This parameter contains the starting address and size information of the memory allocated for the current die and is obtained through the SHMEM interface shmemgetcontext. 4. Replace the native torchnpu Dispatch and Combine with the SHMEM versions. Implementing Dispatch&Combine Operators with SHMEM-Integrated Programming Frameworks In addition to native SHMEM APIs, CANN SHMEM supports integration with multiple programming frameworks, such as Tilelang and PyPTO. The following sections describe how to develop Dispatch&Combine operators with Tilelang-SHMEM and PyPTO-SHMEM. Implementing Dispatch&Combine Operators with Tilelang-SHMEM Tilelang Introduction TileLang is a tile-level programming DSL that uses Python-like syntax and builds its underlying compiler infrastructure on TVM. It optimizes code for specific hardware, allowing developers to express and optimize underlying kernel behavior at a high level. TileLang allows developers to explicitly control memory allocation, data movement, layout, and parallel execution. It also encapsulates a rich set of APIs to simplify operator development. Tilelang-SHMEM Operator Implementation Workflow The following figure shows the Dispatch&Combine operator implementation workflow. 1. Load the environment required for Tilelang and SHMEM. 2. Use Tilelang primitives to write the Dispatch operator. 3. Use Tilelang primitives to write the Combine operator. 4. Enable multiple threads, construct the input data required by Dispatch, use SHMEM to allocate the required Win-region space, and invoke the Dispatch and Combine operators. Pass the constructed data to the operators to provide cross-card or cross-node functionality. T.shmemubputnbinew(xub, windata, ubsize, destrankid, (rank Bs localexpertnum + destexpertid Bs + tokenrepeatnum[0]) ubsize) # Send status for curexpertid in range(startexpertid, startexpertid + aivexpertnum): ... T.shmemubputnbinew(winstatusubsingle, winstatus, 8, destrankid, localexpertid epworldsize 8 + rank 8) # Wait for status in a loop while (sumofflag[0] != aivexpertfpnum): ... # Copy local Win-region data for i in range(statusnumpercore): ... return maindispatch Basic Parameter Settings moedispatchkernel: Function name that defines the Dispatch operator and is used for subsequent invocations. Bs: Number of tokens per card. H: Token length. The Dispatch output is passed as the Combine input, and Combine produces the final result. Implementing Dispatch&Combine Operators with PyPTO-SHMEM PyPTO Introduction: PyPTO (pronounced "pai p-t-o") is a high-performance programming framework for AI accelerators. It simplifies the development of complex fused operators and even complete model networks while maintaining high-performance computing capabilities. The framework uses the innovative PTO (Parallel Tensor/Tile Operation) programming paradigm, with a Tile-based programming model as its core design principle. Through a multi-level intermediate representation (IR) system, it progressively compiles AI model applications built by users through APIs from high-level Tensor graphs into hardware instructions, ultimately generating executable code that runs efficiently on the target platform. PyPTO-SHMEM API Introduction PyPTO implements some OPENSHMEM communication semantics and encapsulates them as APIs for users: shmemput: Sends local data (local Tensor) to a specified position in symmetric memory (SHMEM Tensor). shmemget: Obtains data from a specified position in symmetric memory (SHMEM Tensor) and stores it in a local Tensor. shmemsignal: Sends a signal to another card. shmemwait: Waits for the signal on the current card until the specified signal equals the specified value. shmembarrierall: Synchronizes cards in the communication domain. Execution continues only after all cards reach this synchronization point. It also implements some non-standard OPENSHMEM semantics: createshmemtensor: Creates a Tensor representing symmetric memory in a specified communication domain. shmemcleardata: Clears data in the SHMEM Tensor. shmemsignaldata: Clears the SHMEM signal. mysymbolicpe: Symbolic rank ID of the current card. PyPTO-SHMEM Operator Implementation Workflow Dispatch Operator Implementation In PyPTO, the Dispatch operator is described as three subgraphs: sendtoken: Uses SHMEM APIs to send tokens and their corresponding token information to shared memory according to the expert table and notifies other ranks after transmission is complete. sendsignal: Notifies other cards after token transmission is complete. receivetoken: Receives tokens from other cards. Tensor tensorTile = View(x, {1, hiddenSize}, {rowIndex, 0}); TileShape::Current().SetVecTile({1, infoSize}); SetTensorData(thisRank, {0, 0}, moeSendMsg); SetTensorData(rowIndex, {0, 1}, moeSendMsg); SetTensorData(colIndex, {0, 2}, moeSendMsg); SymbolicScalar remoteExpertId = GetTensorData(expertIds, {rowIndex, colIndex}); SymbolicScalar tokenOffset = GetTensorData(offsetTable, {rowIndex, colIndex}); SymbolicScalar remoteExpertOffset = remoteExpertId % expertNumPerRank; SymbolicScalar remoteRankId = remoteExpertId / expertNumPerRank; Tensor shmemDataTile = View(shmemData, {1, 1, 1, hiddenSize}, std::vector {remoteRankId, remoteExpertOffset epWorldSize + thisRank, tokenOffset, 0}); Tensor shmemInfoTile = View(shmemInfo, {1, 1, 1, infoSize}, std::vector {remoteRankId, remoteExpertOffset epWorldSize + thisRank, tokenOffset, 0}); TileShape::Current().SetVecTile({1, hiddenSize}); Tensor shmemDataPutOut = ShmemPut(tensorTile, tensorTile, shmemDataTile); TileShape::Current().SetVecTile({1, infoSize}); Tensor shmemInfoPutOut = ShmemPut(moeSendMsg, moeSendMsg, shmemInfoTile); shmemSendOut = Nop({shmemDataPutOut, shmemInfoPutOut}); } } Tensor shmemCountOut(DTINT32, {1, 1}, "shmemCountOut"); LOOP("sendsignal", FunctionType::DYNAMICLOOP, expertId, LoopRange(moeExpertNum)) { TileShape::Current().SetVecTile({1, 1}); SymbolicScalar remoteRankId = expertId / expertNumPerRankScalar; SymbolicScalar remoteExpertOffset = expertId % expertNumPerRankScalar; Tensor shmemCountTile = View(shmemCount, {1, 1, 1, 1}, {remoteRankId, 0, remoteExpertOffset epWorldSize + thisRank + 1, 0}); Tensor totalOffsetTile = View(totalOffset, {1, 1}, {expertId, 0}); Tensor shmemPutOut = ShmemPut(shmemSendOut, totalOffsetTile, shmemCountTile); TileShape::Current().SetVecTile({1, signalCol}); Tensor shmemSignalTile = View(shmemSignal, {1, 1, 1, 1, signalCol}, {remoteRankId, 0, 0, 0, 0}); shmemCountOut = ShmemSignal(shmemPutOut, shmemSignalTile, AtomicType::ADD); } LOOP("receivetoken", FunctionType::DYNAMICLOOP, i, LoopRange(1)) { (void) i; TileShape::Current().SetVecTile({1, signalCol}); Tensor shmemSignalLocalTile = View(shmemSignal, {1, 1, 1, 1, signalCol}, {thisRank, 0, 0, 0, 0}); Tensor waitUntilOut = WaitUntil(shmemCountOut, shmemSignalLocalTile, moeExpertNum, true); TileShape::Current().SetVecTile({expertNumPerRank epWorldSize + 1, 1}); Tensor shmemCountTile = View(shmemCount, {1, 1, expertNumPerRank epWorldSize + 1, countSize}, std::vector {1, 1, expertNumPerRank epWorldSize, 1},{thisRank, 0, 0, 0}); Tensor shmemGetOut = ShmemGet(waitUntilOut, shmemCountTile); Tensor cumSumCurrent = CumSum(shmemGetOut, 0); Tensor cumSumResult = Cast(cumSumCurrent, DTINT32, CASTTRUNC); for (uint32t index = 0; index {1, 1, curCount, hiddenSize}, {thisRank, index, 0, 0}); TileShape::Current().SetVecTile({1, hiddenSize}); Tensor localDataRecvCount = ShmemGet(localExpertRecvCount, curShmemDataTile); Assemble(localDataRecvCount, std::vector {offset, 0}, expandX); auto curShmemInfoTile = View(shmemInfo, {1, 1, batchSize, infoSize}, std::vector {1, 1, curCount, infoSize}, {thisRank, index, 0, 0}); TileShape::Current().SetVecTile({1, infoSize}); Tensor localInfoRecvCount = ShmemGet(localExpertRecvCount, curShmemInfoTile, std::vector {curCount, infoSize}); Assemble(localInfoRecvCount, {offset, 0}, assistInfoForCombine); } } Combine Operator Implementation In PyPTO, the Combine operator is mainly described as two subgraphs: send: Uses assistInfoForCombine to return tokens along the original path to the shared-memory region. receive: Receives processed tokens and calculates a weighted average based on expert weights. The main code is as follows: LOOP("send", FunctionType::DYNAMICLOOP, rowIndex, LoopRange(recvCountsScalar), unrollList) { SymbolicScalar rankId = GetTensorData(assistInfoForCombine, {rowIndex, 0}); SymbolicScalar tokenId = GetTensorData(assistInfoForCombine, {rowIndex, 1}); SymbolicScalar kOffset = GetTensorData(assistInfoForCombine, {rowIndex, 2}); Tensor expandXTile = View(expandX, {1, hiddenSize}, {rowIndex, 0}); Tensor shmemDataTile = View(shmemData, {1, 1, 1, hiddenSize}, {rankId, 0, topK tokenId + kOffset, 0}); Tensor shmemSignalOut = ShmemSignal(shmemPutOut, shmemSignalTile, AtomicType::ADD); Assemble(shmemSignalOut, {rowIndex, 0}, sendOut); } SymbolicScalar thisRank = GetHcclRankId(group); LOOP("receive", FunctionType::DYNAMICLOOP, tokenId, LoopRange(batchSize)) { Tensor shmemSignalTile = View(shmemSignal, {1, 1, 1, 1, hiddenSize}, {thisRank, 0, 0, tokenId, 0}); TileShape::Current().SetVecTile({1, hiddenSize}); Tensor waitUntilOut = WaitUntil(sendOut, shmemSignalTile, topK); TileShape::Current().SetVecTile({topK, hiddenSize}); Tensor shmemDataTile = View(shmemData, {1, 1, topK, hiddenSize}, {thisRank, 0, topK tokenId, 0}); Tensor shmemGetOutFp16 = ShmemGet(waitUntilOut, shmemDataTile); TileShape::Current().SetVecTile({topK / 2, hiddenSize}); Tensor shmemGetOutFp32 = npu::tilefwk::Cast(shmemGetOutFp16, DTFP32); Tensor expertScalesTile = View(expertScales, {1, topK}, {tokenId, 0}); int64t kTileShape = AlignUp(topK, 16); int64t l0bSize = 65536; ASSERT((BytesOf(DTFP32) != 0) && (kTileShape != 0)); int64t nTileShape = l0bSize / BytesOf(DTFP32) / kTileShape; TileShape::Current().SetCubeTile({1, 1}, {kTileShape, kTileShape}, {nTileShape, nTileShape}); Tensor matmulOutFp32 = Matrix::Matmul(DTFP32, expertScalesTile, shmemGetOutFp32); Tensor matmulOutFp16 = npu::tilefwk::Cast(matmulOutFp32, DTBF16); Assemble(matmulOutFp16, {tokenId, 0}, out); } Running Dispatch&Combine See How to Run the Dispatch and Combine Operators in PyPTO .

NPU DeepSeek-V4 TileLang算子开发实践 简介 在大模型异构计算发展背景下，GPU 端成熟模型及新算子向昇腾 NPU 的跨平台迁移，Tilelang-Ascend 作为昇腾 CANN 生态原生算子开发框架，深度契合昇腾 NPU 硬件架构特性，采用声明式编程范式大幅降低开发门槛。框架内置丰富硬件原语与性能优化策略，可充分释放 NPU 算力，同时具备极强的新算子快速适配能力，支持 GPU 算子逻辑高效迁移重构，无需深入底层硬件细节即可完成算子开发优化，显著缩短迁移周期。 Tilelang-Ascend代码仓 ，助力开发者快速开展昇腾平台算子开发工作。同时在此工作中，我们也覆盖了 TileKernels 中的mhc算子。 HighLights Tilelang-Ascend具有适配大模型开发的显著优势。 在开发易用性方面，Tilelang-Ascend致力于实现语法简洁、思路清晰的编程模式，用简单代码实现高性能复杂算子： 易用性强。高性能、低开发门槛，开发者可以专注于算法逻辑，忽略底层同步、内存等细节。 后端语言灵活。灵活后端语言切换，既有稳定的AscendC编程路径，也有跨代际兼容的高性能PTO编程路径，能够自动适配不同层级、硬件场景。 算子快速开发。Tilelang-Ascend用极短的时间实现了DeepSeek新模型中SFA/MHC等复杂融合算子，开发者可以快速利用Tilelang抽象建立算子模型，并且有多种优化路径可选。 在功能支撑方面，Tilelang-Ascend同样以提升框架便捷性和高效性为核心，Developer模式的框架新特性包含了以下新功能： 自动流水同步。CV 核间由硬件流水自动同步，Tilelang-Ascend 自动化分析生成精准同步指令，保障算子执行正确与高效。 自动内存复用。Tilelang-Ascend 自动完成内存规划与复用，分析生命周期并线性扫描分配，提升 NPU 内存利用率与执行效率。 自动拆分跨核指令。Tilelang-Ascend 编译器自动识别 CV 核操作，支持指令混合编写，自动完成同步调度与依赖管理。 流水并行语法糖。T.Pipelined特性在编译时静态分析与代码转换，实现计算与内存的重叠执行，最大化硬件利用率，显著提升计算密集任务的执行性能。 数据并行语法糖。T.Parallel特性用直观语法表达Tile元素向量化计算并实现数据并行，不暴露底层硬件细节，提升编程体验与效率。 Tilelang-Ascend框架特性介绍 Tilelang-Ascend持续致力于在提升开发易用性、降低开发难度和代码量上努力。本次框架升级支持了Developer特性开发模式，包括硬件流水自动同步（核间与核内同步）、内存地址自动复用、自动拆分CV指令，及T.Parallel等核心原语操作，从底层简化算子开发流程。原需手动实现的核间同步、内存规划、算力分配等复杂操作，均由原语自动完成，开发者无需深入硬件底层细节，大幅降低对硬件认知的门槛。同时T.Parallel、T.Pipelined原语高效支撑并行计算开发，从算力调度到资源复用全流程自动化，显著降低开发难度、减少代码量，让开发者聚焦核心算法设计，提升算子开发效率与落地速度。 1、硬件流水自动同步 昇腾NPU芯片集成的Cube、Vector等计算单元是异步执行的，CV核间同步通过硬件流水自动对齐各核执行节拍，避免手动栅栏与等待；核内同步由原语在指令级插入依赖与顺序控制，确保数据就绪与访存一致。开发者只需声明并行与流水边界，即可在多核协同与单核流水间获得稳定、高效的执行。 Tilelang-Ascend通过自动化分析实现同步指令的精准生成，兼顾算子执行的正确性与运行性能。下图介绍了硬件流水自动同步插入的实现逻辑： 硬件流水自动同步流程图 循环与处理：通过将for循环递归展开两份，准确分析嵌套循环中的依赖关系。 Buffer访问分析：结合预定义配置集合，确定指令操作所属的硬件流水线，并解析对Buffer的读写操作。 依赖分析与同步决策：识别数据依赖并根据硬件特性决策同步插入的类型，并通过同步图剔除冗余指令。 识别 RAW（写后读）、WAW（写后写）、WAR（读后写）三类数据依赖。 根据依赖关系和硬件特性，决策同步类型：同流水线用PipeBarrier，跨流水线用EventPair（SetFlag/WaitFlag）。 指令生成与循环重构：展开后的循环进行重构，得到原始嵌套结构并生成指令代码。 硬件流水自动同步开启方式： python passconfigs = { tilelang.PassConfigKey.TLASCENDAUTOCVSYNC: True, # CV核间流水自动同步 tilelang.PassConfigKey.TLASCENDAUTOSYNC: True, # 核内流水自动同步 } 2、内存规划与复用 内存规划与复用由框架自动完成，开发者无需手动分配与回收。传统的手动规划内存与手动复用存在很多挑战，开发效率低下，需要人工计算每个层级的偏移量，且算子迭代成本高；并且开发过程中容易出错、难以调试。Tilelang-Ascend根据算子依赖关系与生命周期分析，智能布局缓冲区与中间张量，减少碎片与冗余拷贝；同时通过地址复用与双缓冲策略，在保持数据一致性的前提下复用空闲内存，显著降低峰值占用。配合流水并行与算力调度，内存访问更连贯，整体带宽利用率与执行效率同步提升。 下图展示了内存自动规划与复用的实现逻辑： 内存规划与复用流程图 Tilelang-Ascend通过Developer模式带来了内存规划与复用特性，它完全替代人工 Offset 计算，开发效率显著提升，维度 / 类型变更无需手动适配。自动规避地址重叠、对齐错误，消除内存超限 / 执行异常的人为因素。自动考虑内存复用降低总占用率 ，最大化利用昇腾 NPU 有限的共享内存资源。该特性 是面向昇腾NPU的核心内存优化组件，通过精准的缓冲区生命周期分析与高效的线性扫描内存分配算法，为每个buffer分配内存空间，提高昇腾NPU内存利用率。 缓存区生命周期分析： 遍历 TIR 抽象语法树（AST），全量采集昇腾 NPU 共享内存缓冲区的访问行为。 标记每个缓冲区的 GEN（生成）/KILL（销毁）事件，精准界定其活跃区间 [start, end]（首次使用→最后一次使用的执行阶段）。 按昇腾硬件内存域分组缓冲区，适配不同分区的内存上限约束。 线性扫描分配算法： 按活跃区间起始位置排序缓冲区，构建线性执行序列。 维护活跃队列与空闲内存块池，循环处理每个缓冲区的分配需求。 智能分配策略：优先复用已释放的空闲内存块，无可用块时分配新内存，所有操作遵循 32 字节硬件对齐规则。 最终生成缓冲区到物理地址 Offset 的映射表（addressmap），固化到函数属性指导执行。 内存自动规划与复用开启方式： python passconfigs = { tilelang.PassConfigKey.TLASCENDMEMORYPLANNING: True, # 内存自动规划与复用 } 3、自动拆分CV指令 在昇腾NPU编程中，开发者面临着一种非自然的编程约束。由于硬件架构的CV分离特性，开发者必须在代码中明确标注每段代码属于Cube还是Vector单元。这种显式作用域声明方式会带来开发困扰：开发的割裂性破坏了代码的连贯性；CV频繁切换导致代码和开发逻辑破碎；同时会导致代码结构重复、调试跳跃性强，定位问题困难。例如在Flash Attention融合算子中，Vector核上的Softmax计算和Cube核上的矩阵乘计算会有多次复用同步的逻辑，人工拆分对开发者并不友好。 为了解决这些问题，CV代码分离优化Pass应运而生。它的核心理念是：让开发者专注于算法逻辑，让编译器处理硬件适配。开发者按算法逻辑自然编写代码，Pass自动识别哪些操作属于Cube，哪些属于Vector。 CV指令自动拆分示意图 如上图所示，Tilelang-Ascend的Developer模式允许用户忽略底层CV核的指令和硬件差异，编写符合正常算法逻辑的代码。 CV自动同步在编译期构建Cube/Vector依赖图，识别跨核读写与数据就绪点，自动插入同步指令与等待机制，并进行流水重排与双缓冲优化，保证核间数据一致与顺序正确。开发者仅需描述算法，编译器即可完成核间调度与核内依赖管理，减少手工拆分与同步代码。 自动拆分CV指令开启方式： python passconfigs = { tilelang.PassConfigKey.TLASCENDAUTOCVCOMBINE: True, # 自动拆分CV指令 } 4、T.Parallel Tilelang-Ascend编程模型中，T.Parallel是用于表达 tile 内元素向量化计算 的核心原语。它在 IR 层以“并行循环”的形式描述数据并行，而不直接暴露底层硬件指令细节，可以让用户用符合编程思维的逐元素编程语法，实现硬件层面Tile级的高性能并行操作，极大的提升用户的算子编程体验。 目前支持的双目运算符、支持的单目运算符、多运算场景、1D / 2D 场景、双目“向量 + 标量”场景、行切分场景、Buffer + 标量广播运算、拷贝场景。 代码使用方式示例： 运算操作： python 一维运算场景 for i in T.Parallel(vblock): mi[i] = T.max(mi[i], miprev[i]) python 二维运算场景 for (i, j) in T.Parallel(vblock, d): accoub[i, j] /= T.exp(attnsinkub[i] - scoresmax[i]) 拷贝操作： python GM -> UB 拷贝&计算场景 for i, j in T.Parallel(blockM // VECNUM, blockN): C[bx blockM + vid blockM // VECNUM + i, by blockN + j] = T.exp(aub[i, j]) 主要算子实现 本章介绍DeepSeek-V4 0Day支持中Tilelang-Ascend实现的四个算子用例。 Tilelang算子优势 多个融合算子已经成功适配并接入DeepSeek模型，Tilelang-Ascend在精细化Tile编程中具有语法简洁、先天适配NPU多级存储模型的优势，开发者可以快速简洁地开发Tilelang算子，结合上述Developer模式新特性，在保持相近性能的前提下，代码量可降低至原后端实现的约20%，开发者能用简短的代码实现高性能的复杂算子。 1、Sparse Flash Attention 概述 SparseFlashAttention算子的整体计算流程如下图所示： SparseFlashAttention计算流程图 在DeepSeek-V4模型中，随着上下文长度不断变大，面对超长序列，注意力机制成为模型中的主要计算瓶颈。为了高效计算注意力，SFA（Sparse Flash Attention）在保留原有稀疏索引筛选功能的基础上，改进计算流程并接入了C4A（Compress-4-Attention）和C128A（Compress-128-Attention）稀疏注意力压缩架构，显著降低了长文本场景中注意力的计算成本。新版的SFA算子还引入了可学习注意力锚点（Attention sink）机制，通过调整每个查询头的注意力分数，保护模型输出序列的稳定性。 算法流程详解 从NPU的块级执行视角，结合具体维度阐述实现细节。输入输出张量以典型维度为例： query: [b, m, h, d]，查询向量集合。 key/value: [b, n, d]，键值向量集合。 topkidxs: [b, m, k]，topk索引向量。 attnsink: [h]，attn sink注意力锚点向量。 output: [b, m, h, d]，注意力权重输出向量。 计算流程： 1、查询块加载 数据并行策略：将batch和m（序列长度）作为核间并行切分维度，分核执行；设置C:V核1:2比例，以[head // 2, block=64]为基础块大小细粒度核内切分张量并行执行。 数据切分细节：按照核间并行-核内切分的双重并行策略进行。 以batchm为逻辑核coreid数，在AiCores上均匀分配任务。 主块大小为dim=512（Shape -> [32, 512]），核内切分块大小为block=64（Shape -> [32, 64]）。 2、稀疏键值索引构建掩码块 索引驱动加载：根据mask规则，对基本块中每个数据的位置，利用topkidxs张量筛选计算得到key/value关联的idxsub索引张量： for i in T.serial(block): idxsub[i] = topkidxs[by, bx, t block + i] if t block + i [64, 64] 注意力掩码累加：将掩码矩阵累加到矩阵乘的注意力分数结果上，得到掩码后的注意力分数值，并与缩放scale相乘。 4、Online Softmax 在注意力分数结果上分块执行在线softmax。 数据并行：利用Tilelang框架新特性T.Parallel，用逐元素计算代码表达Tile块级数据并行计算： for (i, j) in T.parallel(vblock, block): ​ accsub[i, j] -= scoresmax[i] 计算过程中通过规约动态维护最大值(scoremax)和指数和(scoresum)中间统计量，确保数值稳定性。 5、上下文向量计算 完成计算图中注意力权重与value的矩阵乘: attntile = score @ value Shape -> [64, 512] 6、结果累加与重缩放 结果累加：以block=64的基本Tile块进行循环，累加计算结果到accoub buffer中。 在线重缩放：循环结束后，利用在线Softmax维护的统计量(scoremax, scoresum)，通过向量化操作对累加结果进行全局重缩放，校正分块计算引入的偏差。 7、注意力锚点计算 attn sink注意力锚点：对累加结果进行attn sink锚点运算，保留前s个token的注意力权重和KV缓存，使输出保留全局上下文，避免结果仅依赖近期token，导致语义陷入局部陷阱或缺失: for (i, j) in T.Parallel(vblock, d): ​ accoub[i, j] /= T.exp(attnsinkub[i] - scoresmax[i]) 8、结果写回 结果保存：经过缩放与锚点处理的注意力权重结果按块写回全局内存中。 2、Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections 概述 Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections算子的整体计算流程如下图所示： Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections计算流程图 Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections（Mhc）是一种通用残差架构优化方案，融合了流形约束+结构化映射技术，Mhc算子主要包含三类可学习映射：预变换映射pre、后变换映射post和跨流连接映射comb，其将超连接（HC）的多路残差跨流映射约束在双随机矩阵流形上，保留多流表达能力的同时恢复恒等映射特性，解决大规模训练的数值不稳定与信号失控问题。 算法流程详解 算子输入输出典型维度张量分析： mixes: [n, mixhc]，多流特征输入张量。 hcscale: [3]，流级缩放系数向量。 hcbase: [mixhc]，跨流映射初始矩阵向量。 hc: 超参数，流的数量。 sinkhorniters: 超参数，Sinkhorn-Knopp的迭代次数。 eps: 超参数，数值稳定epsilon。 pre: [n, hc]，mixes流级缩放预变换输出张量。 post: [n, hc]，残差融合特征流级缩放的后变换输出张量。 comb: [n, hc]，跨流连接映射输出张量。 计算流程： 1、多流特征缩放 缩放值计算：首先根据流级缩放系数向量及流的数量，构建每条流向量对应的缩放值hcscaleshared。 计算缩放多流特征：按基本块大小，将多流特征乘以缩放值后与跨流初始矩阵相加得到： mixesshared = mixesshared hcscaleshared + hcbaseshared 2、计算预变换张量 预变换张量控制每条流的输入强度。 根据多流特征缩放值，通过Sigmoid缩放+流级参数融合计算预变换张量结果，按基本块Tile，通过乘以scale值控制每条流的输入维度，用 sigmoid 约束结果在稳定区间，然后加eps防止出现零值，计算流程如下： pre = mixes ⊙ sigmoid(scale) + eps 3、计算后变换张量 后变换张量控制每条流的输出幅度。 与预变换处理流程类似，经过Sigmoid缩放+流级参数融合后，后处理张量会乘以2，以适当扩大输出维度： post= (mixes ⊙ sigmoid(scale)) 2 4、指数归一化 按基本块读取跨流融合张量comb，即上述经过缩放的多流特征张量，准备计算跨流映射矩阵的双随机投影。 通过reduce、sub、exp等运算接口对每个基本块实现softmax指数归一化运算逻辑，同样累加eps避免产生零值，实现特征输出的范围稳定： comb = comb.softmax(-1) + eps 5、行列归一化 行归一化：对经过指数归一化的comb基本块首先在行方向做整体归一化： comb = comb / (comb.sum(-2) + eps) 迭代行列归一化：基于Sinkhorn-Knopp算法，按基本块对comb执行总共sinkiter次行列归一化： for i in range(sinkiter): ​ comb = comb / (comb.sum(-1) + eps) ​ comb = comb / (comb.sum(-2) + eps) 最终得到归一化后的comb跨流连接映射输出张量。 6、结果写回 结果保存：将跨流连接映射输出张量结果按块写回全局内存中。 3、Int8 General Matrix Multiplication 概述 Int8 General Matrix Multiplication算子的整体计算流程如下图所示： Int8 General Matrix Multiplication计算流程图 Int8gemm（Int8 General Matrix Multiplication）是带有量化激活输入值的MatMul算子，将int8类型的输入值的矩阵乘结果反量化为fp32，经过缩放因子缩放后，再次量化到目标数据类型，并保存输出结果。 算法流程详解 算子输入输出典型维度张量分析： aint8: [M, K]，int8激活值向量。 ascales: [M, 1]，激活值缩放因子。 bint8: [N, K]，int8权重向量。 bscales: [N, 1]，权重缩放因子。 output: [M, N]，量化gemm输出向量。 计算流程： 1、int8矩阵乘法 矩阵乘：分块读入并使用gemmv0接口计算矩阵乘结果，输入值为int8类型，存储中间结果为int32类型: Ctile = Atile @ Btile.T Shape -> [64, 64] 运算结果传递：利用GM workspace将运算结果写入cub buffer中。 2、数据类型转换 int32->fp32转换：利用cast接口执行数据类型转换： T.tile.cast(cscale, cub) Type: int32 -> float32 3、反量化缩放 加载缩放因子：将激活值和权重缩放因子按基本分块大小拷贝至ub buffer。 转换数据缩放：将转换后的数据与缩放因子相乘，同样从Tile层级数据并行计算： for (i, j) in T.Parallel(blockM2, blockN): ​ cscale[i, j] = scaleaub[i] ​ cscale[i, j] = scalebub[j] 4、结果转换与写回 类型转换：再次通过cast将缩放结果转换为目标输出数据类型（以fp16为例）: T.tile.cast(cout, cscale) Type: float32-> float16 结果保存：经过类型转换与反量化缩放的结果按块写回全局内存中。 4、Activation Quantization 概述 Activation Quantization算子的整体计算流程如下图所示： Activation Quantization计算流程图 Actquant（Activation Quantization）是处理激活量化的算子，负责将模型前向推理时动态生成的激活值从高精度（FP32/FP16）转换为低精度（INT8/INT4），主要在模型反向传播或推理后完成量化。 算法流程详解 算子输入输出典型维度张量分析： xbf16: [M, N] / [batch, seq, N]，待处理输入张量。 roundscale: False，bool值，是否对缩放因子取整为2的幂次。 计算流程： 1、最大值计算 数据预处理：首先把读入的数据转换为fp32类型，然后求取其绝对值数据。 最大值：对列方向进行最大值规约得到输入数据每列的最大值，并存储到maxub buffer中。 2、计算缩放因子 使用每列计算出的最大值除以int8类型的最大值127，根据roundscale判断是否取整为2的幂次，然后得到每个元素的缩放因子： for i in T.Parallel(blockM2): ​ scaleub[i] = maxub[i] / int8absmax 3、int8对称量化 数据缩放：将第一步处理的数据除以缩放因子，并通过clamp接口将数据限制在[-127, 127]范围内。 对称量化：将上述数据四舍五入取整，然后先后量化为fp16和int8类型，得到量化输出结果。 整体计算流程可概括为： y = round(clamp(x / scale, -127, 127)).to(float16).to(int8) 4、结果写回 将结算得到的缩放因子向量scaleub和量化激活值yub写回全局内存中。

NPU DeepSeek-V4 TileLang Operator Development Practice Introduction As heterogeneous computing for large models evolves, mature GPU models and new operators must be migrated across platforms to Ascend NPUs. Tilelang-Ascend, a native operator development framework in the Ascend CANN ecosystem, closely matches Ascend NPU hardware architecture features and uses a declarative programming paradigm to substantially reduce the development barrier. The framework provides rich hardware primitives and performance optimization strategies to fully use NPU computing power. It can also rapidly adapt new operators, efficiently migrate and refactor GPU operator logic, and complete operator development and optimization without requiring detailed knowledge of the underlying hardware, substantially shortening the migration cycle. The Tilelang-Ascend code repository helps developers quickly begin operator development on Ascend platforms. This work also covers the mhc operator in TileKernels . HighLights Tilelang-Ascend provides significant advantages for large-model development. For ease of development, Tilelang-Ascend provides a concise and clear programming model that implements complex, high-performance operators with simple code: Easy to use. It provides high performance and a low development barrier, allowing developers to focus on algorithm logic and ignore underlying synchronization, memory, and other details. Flexible backend languages. It can flexibly switch backend languages, providing both a stable AscendC programming path and a high-performance PTO programming path with cross-generation compatibility, and automatically adapting to different levels and hardware scenarios. Rapid operator development. Tilelang-Ascend implemented complex fused operators such as SFA/MHC in the new DeepSeek model within an extremely short time. Developers can quickly use Tilelang abstractions to build operator models and choose from multiple optimization paths. For functional support, Tilelang-Ascend also focuses on improving framework convenience and efficiency. New framework features in Developer mode include: Automatic pipeline synchronization. Hardware pipelines automatically synchronize CV cores. Tilelang-Ascend automatically analyzes and generates precise synchronization instructions to ensure correct and efficient operator execution. Automatic memory reuse. Tilelang-Ascend automatically performs memory planning and reuse, analyzes lifecycles, and uses linear-scan allocation to improve NPU memory utilization and execution efficiency. Automatic splitting of cross-core instructions. The Tilelang-Ascend compiler automatically identifies CV core operations, supports mixed instruction authoring, and automatically performs synchronization scheduling and dependency management. Pipeline-parallelism syntax sugar. The T.Pipelined feature performs static analysis and code transformation at compile time to overlap computation and memory access, maximize hardware utilization, and substantially improve compute-intensive task performance. Data-parallelism syntax sugar. The T.Parallel feature expresses vectorized Tile-element computation with intuitive syntax and implements data parallelism without exposing underlying hardware details, improving the programming experience and efficiency. Tilelang-Ascend Framework Features Tilelang-Ascend continually works to improve development usability and reduce development difficulty and code volume. This framework upgrade supports the Developer feature-development mode, including automatic hardware-pipeline synchronization (inter-core and intra-core synchronization), automatic memory-address reuse, automatic CV instruction splitting, and core primitive operations such as T.Parallel, simplifying operator development from the underlying layer. Primitives automatically perform complex operations that previously required manual implementation, such as inter-core synchronization, memory planning, and compute allocation. Developers do not need in-depth knowledge of underlying hardware details, substantially reducing the hardware-knowledge barrier. T.Parallel and T.Pipelined also efficiently support parallel-computing development and automate the complete workflow from compute scheduling to resource reuse, substantially reducing development difficulty and code volume and allowing developers to focus on core algorithm design to improve operator development efficiency and implementation speed. 1. Automatic Hardware-Pipeline Synchronization The Cube, Vector, and other compute units integrated into Ascend NPU chips execute asynchronously. Inter-core CV synchronization automatically aligns the execution pace of each core through the hardware pipeline, avoiding manual barriers and waits. For intra-core synchronization, primitives insert dependencies and ordering controls at the instruction level to ensure data readiness and consistent memory access. Developers only need to declare parallel and pipeline boundaries to achieve stable and efficient execution across multi-core collaboration and single-core pipelines. Through automated analysis, Tilelang-Ascend precisely generates synchronization instructions while ensuring operator correctness and runtime performance. The following figure shows the implementation logic for automatically inserting hardware-pipeline synchronization: Automatic Hardware-Pipeline Synchronization Workflow Loop handling: Recursively unroll the for loop into two copies to accurately analyze dependencies in nested loops. Buffer access analysis: Combine predefined configuration sets to determine the hardware pipeline to which an instruction operation belongs and parse Buffer read and write operations. Dependency analysis and synchronization decisions: Identify data dependencies, select the synchronization type based on hardware features, and remove redundant instructions through the synchronization graph. Identify three types of data dependencies: RAW (read after write), WAW (write after write), and WAR (write after read). Select the synchronization type based on dependencies and hardware features: Use PipeBarrier within the same pipeline and EventPair (SetFlag/WaitFlag) across pipelines. Instruction generation and loop reconstruction: Reconstruct the unrolled loops into the original nested structure and generate instruction code. Enabling automatic hardware-pipeline synchronization: python passconfigs = { tilelang.PassConfigKey.TLASCENDAUTOCVSYNC: True, # Automatic inter-core CV pipeline synchronization tilelang.PassConfigKey.TLASCENDAUTOSYNC: True, # Automatic intra-core pipeline synchronization } 2. Memory Planning and Reuse The framework automatically performs memory planning and reuse, so developers do not need to manually allocate and release memory. Conventional manual memory planning and reuse present many challenges: Development is inefficient, offsets at each level must be calculated manually, operator iteration is costly, errors occur easily during development, and debugging is difficult. Based on operator dependencies and lifecycle analysis, Tilelang-Ascend intelligently lays out buffers and intermediate tensors to reduce fragmentation and redundant copies. It also reuses free memory through address reuse and double-buffering strategies while maintaining data consistency, substantially reducing peak usage. Combined with pipeline parallelism and compute scheduling, memory access becomes more contiguous, improving overall bandwidth utilization and execution efficiency. The following figure shows the implementation logic for automatic memory planning and reuse: Memory Planning and Reuse Workflow Developer mode in Tilelang-Ascend provides memory planning and reuse that completely replaces manual Offset calculation and substantially improves development efficiency. Dimension/type changes require no manual adaptation. It automatically prevents address overlap and alignment errors, eliminating human factors that cause memory-limit violations or execution exceptions. Automatic memory reuse reduces total usage and maximizes the use of limited shared-memory resources on Ascend NPUs. This feature is a core memory-optimization component for Ascend NPUs. Through precise buffer-lifecycle analysis and an efficient linear-scan memory-allocation algorithm, it allocates memory space for each Buffer and improves Ascend NPU memory utilization. Buffer lifecycle analysis: Traverse the TIR abstract syntax tree (AST) to collect all access behavior for Ascend NPU shared-memory Buffers. Mark the GEN (creation)/KILL (destruction) event of each Buffer to precisely determine its active interval [start, end] (execution stages from first use to last use). Group Buffers by Ascend hardware memory domain to adapt to memory-capacity constraints in different partitions. Linear-scan allocation algorithm: Sort Buffers by the start positions of their active intervals to construct a linear execution sequence. Maintain an active queue and free-memory-block pool, and process each Buffer allocation request in a loop. Intelligent allocation strategy: Prefer reusing released free memory blocks. Allocate new memory when no block is available. All operations follow the 32-byte hardware-alignment rule. Finally, generate a mapping table from Buffers to physical-address Offsets (addressmap) and store it in function attributes to guide execution. Enabling automatic memory planning and reuse: python passconfigs = { tilelang.PassConfigKey.TLASCENDMEMORYPLANNING: True, # Automatic memory planning and reuse } 3. Automatic CV Instruction Splitting When programming Ascend NPUs, developers face an unnatural constraint. Because the hardware architecture separates CV units, developers must explicitly mark whether each code segment belongs to the Cube or Vector unit. Such explicit scope declarations cause development difficulties: Fragmentation disrupts code continuity, frequent CV switching fragments code and development logic, and the resulting duplicated code structures and abrupt debugging flow make problems difficult to locate. For example, in a Flash Attention fused operator, Softmax computation on Vector cores and matrix-multiplication computation on Cube cores repeatedly reuse synchronization logic. Manual splitting is not developer-friendly. The CV code-separation optimization pass resolves these issues. Its core principle is to let developers focus on algorithm logic while the compiler handles hardware adaptation. Developers write code naturally according to algorithm logic, and the pass automatically identifies which operations belong to Cube and which belong to Vector. Automatic CV Instruction Splitting As shown in the preceding figure, Developer mode in Tilelang-Ascend allows users to ignore instruction and hardware differences between the underlying CV cores and write code that follows normal algorithm logic. Automatic CV synchronization builds a Cube/Vector dependency graph at compile time, identifies cross-core reads/writes and data-ready points, automatically inserts synchronization instructions and wait mechanisms, and performs pipeline reordering and double-buffering optimization to ensure inter-core data consistency and correct ordering. Developers only describe the algorithm, and the compiler performs inter-core scheduling and intra-core dependency management, reducing manual splitting and synchronization code. Enabling automatic CV instruction splitting: python passconfigs = { tilelang.PassConfigKey.TLASCENDAUTOCVCOMBINE: True, # Automatically split CV instructions } 4. T.Parallel In the Tilelang-Ascend programming model, T.Parallel is the core primitive for expressing vectorized computation of elements within a Tile. At the IR layer, it describes data parallelism as a "parallel loop" without directly exposing underlying hardware-instruction details. It allows users to implement high-performance Tile-level parallel operations in hardware through element-wise programming syntax that follows natural programming logic, substantially improving the operator-programming experience. Currently supported scenarios include binary operators, unary operators, multi-operation scenarios, 1D/2D scenarios, binary "vector + scalar" scenarios, row-partitioning scenarios, Buffer + scalar broadcast operations, and copy scenarios. Code usage examples: Computation operations: python 1D computation scenario for i in T.Parallel(vblock): mi[i] = T.max(mi[i], miprev[i]) python 2D computation scenario for (i, j) in T.Parallel(vblock, d): accoub[i, j] /= T.exp(attnsinkub[i] - scoresmax[i]) Copy operations: python GM -> UB copy and computation scenario for i, j in T.Parallel(blockM // VECNUM, blockN): C[bx blockM + vid blockM // VECNUM + i, by blockN + j] = T.exp(aub[i, j]) Main Operator Implementations This chapter describes four operator examples implemented by Tilelang-Ascend for Day-0 support of DeepSeek-V4. Tilelang Operator Advantages Multiple fused operators have been successfully adapted and integrated into the DeepSeek model. In fine-grained Tile programming, Tilelang-Ascend provides concise syntax and native adaptation to the NPU multi-level storage model. Developers can quickly and concisely develop Tilelang operators. Combined with the preceding new Developer-mode features, the code volume can be reduced to approximately 20% of the original backend implementation while maintaining similar performance, allowing developers to implement high-performance complex operators with concise code. 1. Sparse Flash Attention Overview The overall computation workflow of the SparseFlashAttention operator is shown in the following figure: SparseFlashAttention Computation Workflow In the DeepSeek-V4 model, as the context length grows and sequences become ultra-long, the attention mechanism becomes the model's main computation bottleneck. To calculate attention efficiently, SFA (Sparse Flash Attention) improves the computation workflow while retaining the original sparse-index selection function and integrates the C4A (Compress-4-Attention) and C128A (Compress-128-Attention) sparse-attention compression architectures, substantially reducing attention computation costs in long-text scenarios. The new SFA operator also introduces a learnable Attention sink mechanism that adjusts the attention scores of each query head to preserve the stability of model output sequences. Detailed Algorithm Workflow The implementation details are described from the NPU block-level execution perspective using specific dimensions. Typical input and output tensor dimensions are: query: [b, m, h, d], collection of query vectors. key/value: [b, n, d], collection of key/value vectors. topkidxs: [b, m, k], topk index vector. attnsink: [h], attn sink attention-anchor vector. output: [b, m, h, d], attention-weight output vector. Computation workflow: 1. Query Block Loading Data-parallel strategy: Use batch and m (sequence length) as inter-core parallel partitioning dimensions and run them on separate cores. Set the C:V core ratio to 1:2, and use [head // 2, block=64] as the basic block size for fine-grained intra-core partitioning and tensor-parallel execution. Data-partitioning details: Use the two-level parallel strategy of inter-core parallelism and intra-core partitioning. Use batchm as the logical coreid count and evenly distribute tasks across AiCores. The main block size is dim=512 (Shape -> [32, 512]), and the intra-core partition block size is block=64 (Shape -> [32, 64]). 2. Building Mask Blocks from Sparse Key/Value Indices Index-driven loading: Based on mask rules, use the topkidxs tensor to select and calculate the idxsub index tensor associated with key/value for each data position in the basic block: for i in T.serial(block): idxsub[i] = topkidxs[by, bx, t block + i] if t block + i [64, 64] Attention mask accumulation: Accumulate the mask matrix into the matrix-multiplication attention-score result, obtain the masked attention-score value, and multiply it by scaling factor scale. 4. Online Softmax Perform online softmax on the attention-score result in blocks. Data parallelism: Use the new T.Parallel feature of the Tilelang framework to express Tile-block-level data-parallel computation with element-wise computation code: for (i, j) in T.parallel(vblock, block): ​ accsub[i, j] -= scoresmax[i] During computation, dynamically maintain the intermediate statistics maximum (scoremax) and exponential sum (scoresum) through reduction to ensure numerical stability. 5. Context Vector Computation Complete matrix multiplication of the attention weights and value in the computation graph: attntile = score @ value Shape -> [64, 512] 6. Result Accumulation and Rescaling Result accumulation: Loop over basic Tile blocks with block=64 and accumulate computation results into the accoub Buffer. Online rescaling: After the loop, use the statistics maintained by Online Softmax (scoremax and scoresum) to globally rescale the accumulated result through vectorized operations and correct deviations introduced by block-wise computation. 7. Attention Anchor Computation attn sink attention anchor: Apply the attn sink anchor operation to the accumulated result, retain the attention weights and KV cache of the first s tokens, and preserve global context in the output. This prevents the result from depending only on recent tokens, which can cause semantics to become trapped locally or be lost: for (i, j) in T.Parallel(vblock, d): ​ accoub[i, j] /= T.exp(attnsinkub[i] - scoresmax[i]) 8. Writing Back Results Result storage: Write the attention-weight result after scaling and anchor processing back to global memory in blocks. 2. Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections Overview The overall computation workflow of the Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections operator is shown in the following figure: Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections Computation Workflow Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections (Mhc) is a general residual-architecture optimization solution that combines manifold constraints and structured mapping. The Mhc operator mainly contains three types of learnable mappings: pre-transformation mapping pre, post-transformation mapping post, and cross-stream connection mapping comb. It constrains the multi-path residual cross-stream mappings of Hyper-Connections (HC) to a doubly stochastic matrix manifold, preserving multi-stream representation capabilities while restoring identity-mapping properties and resolving numerical instability and uncontrolled signals in large-scale training. Detailed Algorithm Workflow Analysis of typical input and output tensor dimensions for the operator: mixes: [n, mixhc], multi-stream feature input tensor. hcscale: [3], stream-level scaling-coefficient vector. hcbase: [mixhc], initial matrix vector for cross-stream mapping. hc: Hyperparameter specifying the number of streams. sinkhorniters: Hyperparameter specifying the number of Sinkhorn-Knopp iterations. eps: Hyperparameter, numerical-stability epsilon. pre: [n, hc], pre-transformation output tensor after stream-level scaling of mixes. post: [n, hc], post-transformation output tensor after stream-level scaling of residual-fusion features. comb: [n, hc], cross-stream connection-mapping output tensor. Computation workflow: 1. Multi-Stream Feature Scaling Scaling-value calculation: First, construct scaling value hcscaleshared corresponding to each stream vector based on the stream-level scaling-coefficient vector and the number of streams. Scaled multi-stream feature calculation: By basic block size, multiply the multi-stream features by the scaling value and add the initial cross-stream matrix to obtain: mixesshared = mixesshared hcscaleshared + hcbaseshared 2. Calculating the Pre-Transformation Tensor The pre-transformation tensor controls the input intensity of each stream. Based on the multi-stream feature scaling value, calculate the pre-transformation tensor through Sigmoid scaling and stream-level parameter fusion. For each basic-block Tile, multiplication by the scale value controls the input dimension of each stream, sigmoid constrains the result to a stable range, and eps is added to prevent zero values. The computation workflow is as follows: pre = mixes ⊙ sigmoid(scale) + eps 3. Calculating the Post-Transformation Tensor The post-transformation tensor controls the output amplitude of each stream. Similar to the pre-transformation workflow, after Sigmoid scaling and stream-level parameter fusion, multiply the postprocessing tensor by 2 to appropriately increase the output dimension: post= (mixes ⊙ sigmoid(scale)) 2 4. Exponential Normalization Read the cross-stream fused tensor comb by basic block. This tensor is the scaled multi-stream feature tensor described previously. Prepare to calculate the doubly stochastic projection of the cross-stream mapping matrix. Use operation interfaces such as reduce, sub, and exp to implement softmax exponential normalization for each basic block. Also add eps to prevent zero values and stabilize the feature-output range: comb = comb.softmax(-1) + eps 5. Row and Column Normalization Row normalization: First normalize the exponentially normalized comb basic block as a whole along the row direction: comb = comb / (comb.sum(-2) + eps) Iterative row and column normalization: Based on the Sinkhorn-Knopp algorithm, perform a total of sinkiter row and column normalizations on comb by basic block: for i in range(sinkiter): ​ comb = comb / (comb.sum(-1) + eps) ​ comb = comb / (comb.sum(-2) + eps) Finally, obtain the normalized comb cross-stream connection-mapping output tensor. 6. Writing Back Results Result storage: Write the cross-stream connection-mapping output tensor back to global memory in blocks. 3. Int8 General Matrix Multiplication Overview The overall computation workflow of the Int8 General Matrix Multiplication operator is shown in the following figure: Int8 General Matrix Multiplication Computation Workflow Int8gemm (Int8 General Matrix Multiplication) is a MatMul operator with quantized activation inputs. It dequantizes the matrix-multiplication result of int8 input values to fp32, scales it by scaling factors, requantizes it to the target data type, and stores the output result. Detailed Algorithm Workflow Analysis of typical input and output tensor dimensions for the operator: aint8: [M, K], int8 activation vector. ascales: [M, 1], activation scaling factor. bint8: [N, K], int8 weight vector. bscales: [N, 1], weight scaling factor. output: [M, N], quantized gemm output vector. Computation workflow: 1. int8 Matrix Multiplication Matrix multiplication: Read data in blocks and use the gemmv0 interface to calculate the matrix-multiplication result. The input values are int8, and intermediate results are stored as int32: Ctile = Atile @ Btile.T Shape -> [64, 64] Computation result transfer: Use GM workspace to write the computation result into the cub Buffer. 2. Data Type Conversion int32->fp32 conversion: Use the cast interface to perform data type conversion: T.tile.cast(cscale, cub) Type: int32 -> float32 3. Dequantization Scaling Loading scaling factors: Copy the activation and weight scaling factors to the UB Buffer based on the basic block size. Scaling converted data: Multiply the converted data by the scaling factors, also using data-parallel computation at the Tile level: for (i, j) in T.Parallel(blockM2, blockN): ​ cscale[i, j] = scaleaub[i] ​ cscale[i, j] = scalebub[j] 4. Result Conversion and Write-Back Data type conversion: Use cast again to convert the scaled result to the target output data type (using fp16 as an example): T.tile.cast(cout, cscale) Type: float32-> float16 Result storage: Write the result after data type conversion and dequantization scaling back to global memory in blocks. 4. Activation Quantization Overview The overall computation workflow of the Activation Quantization operator is shown in the following figure: Activation Quantization Computation Workflow Actquant (Activation Quantization) processes activation quantization. It converts activations dynamically generated during model forward inference from high precision (FP32/FP16) to low precision (INT8/INT4), primarily completing quantization after model backpropagation or inference. Detailed Algorithm Workflow Analysis of typical input and output tensor dimensions for the operator: xbf16: [M, N] / [batch, seq, N], input tensor to process. roundscale: False, bool indicating whether the scaling factor is rounded to a power of 2. Computation workflow: 1. Maximum-Value Calculation Data preprocessing: First convert the read data to fp32 and then obtain its absolute values. Maximum value: Perform maximum reduction along the column direction to obtain the maximum value in each column of the input data and store it in the maxub Buffer. 2. Calculating the Scaling Factor Divide the maximum value calculated for each column by 127, the maximum int8 value. Based on roundscale, determine whether to round it to a power of 2, and obtain the scaling factor for each element: for i in T.Parallel(blockM2): ​ scaleub[i] = maxub[i] / int8absmax 3. int8 Symmetric Quantization Data scaling: Divide the data processed in step 1 by the scaling factor and use the clamp interface to constrain it to the range [-127, 127]. Symmetric quantization: Round the preceding data and then quantize it to fp16 and int8 in sequence to obtain the quantized output. The overall computation workflow can be summarized as: y = round(clamp(x / scale, -127, 127)).to(float16).to(int8) 4. Writing Back Results Write the calculated scaling-factor vector scaleub and quantized activation yub back to global memory.

基于Atlas A2的GPT-OSS模型推理性能优化实践 概述 本文主要介绍GPT-OSS系列模型基于NPU的推理的优化方式。基于Atlas A2 系列产品，GPT-OSS-120B模型可以采用8卡部署，GPT-OSS-20B模型可以在单device上进行部署。 性能优化 Attention Tensor Parallel (TP)优化 对Attention的张量切分策略可以分为对QKV头的切分和对线性层的切分。 在对QKV头切分时，attention的多头计算机制可以方便进行张量切分，每个头先独立计算，再将结果concat起来。假设模型的attention层需要对numheads个query按照切分数量tpsize进行切分，要求numheads必须能被tpsize整除，每张卡放置query头个数为numheadsperrank = numheads // tpsize；key和value头数相等，且可能小于等于query头个数（在MQA和GQA的场景下会小于）。为了确保每张卡至少放置一个key和value头，每张卡放置的key或value头数计算方法为 numkeyvalueheadsperrank = max(numkeyvalueheads // tpsize, 1)。QKV头在卡上排布情况如下图所示。 attentiontp 针对qproj、kproj和vproj三个线性层，可以进一步合并为一个线性层qkvproj，即在推理中将三个矩阵乘替换为一个矩阵乘，可以最大化使用NPU的计算能力提升性能。随后将结果切分得到Q、K、V，并进行attention计算，最后通过oproj层输出。 MoE Tensor Parallel优化 假设模型的MoE层的切分数量为tpsize，专家个数为expertnum。对MoE层进行张量切分时，对gateproj与upproj进行列切分，对downproj进行行切分。对gateproj和upproj可以采取合并matmul的优化方式，得到gateupproj，实现计算性能优化。 固定KV Cache大小 首先申请一块固定大小的KV Cache tensor，以优化源码动态申请内存的性能损失。KV Cache的大小为(batch seqlen numkeyvalueheadsperrank headdim)，其中seqlen至少为输入和输出的最大总和，以保证在推理过程中KV Cache的更新不会越界。 在计算完Q、K、V后，可以通过scatterupdate算子对指定位置上的KV Cache进行更新，可参考 torchnpu.scatterupdate 接口。 使能融合算子 RMSNorm融合与AddRMSNorm融合 替换GptOssRMSNorm的forward函数，使用融合算子接口 torchnpu.npurmsnorm 和torchnpu.npuaddrmsnorm，将多个算子的计算替换成融合kernel，提升性能。 GMM使能与Routing优化 在GPT-OSS的MoE专家模块中，通过使能融合算子，进一步提升性能，可以参考GptOssMLP类中的实现。 Flash Attention融合算子优化 通过使能 torchnpu.npufusedinferattentionscorev2 推理场景下支持图模式的FlashAttention算子，既可以支持全量计算场景,也可支持增量计算场景。 快速选择专家：在计算专家和token之间的路由分数时，可以使用 torchnpu.npumoegatingtopksoftmax 融合算子，代替原来先topk再softmax的多算子操作，可以更快速地计算出token和专家的分数。 高效排序和token路由： 使能 torchnpu.npumoeinitrouting 融合算子，实现MoE routing计算，获取专家的排序； 使能 torchnpu.npumoecomputeexperttokens 融合算子，获取每个专家需要计算的token数； 使能 torchnpu.npumoefinalizerouting 融合算子，将专家计算完成后的token重新排布并加权求和，获得最终输出。 高性能专家计算：使能 torchnpu.npugroupedmatmul 融合算子，实现多个专家的矩阵乘计算，提高计算和搬运效率。 集合通信使能AIV展开 利用Device的Vector Core计算单元来加速AllReduce操作，可通过环境变量 HCCLOPEXPANSIONMODE 使能AIV，配置如下： shell export HCCLOPEXPANSIONMODE=AIV 附录 环境部署以及样例执行

GPT-OSS Inference Performance Optimization on Atlas A2 Overview This document describes NPU-based inference optimization methods for the GPT-OSS model series. On Atlas A2 series products, the GPT-OSS-120B model can be deployed on eight cards, while the GPT-OSS-20B model can be deployed on a single device. Performance Optimization Attention Tensor Parallel (TP) Optimization The tensor partitioning strategy for Attention can be divided into QKV head partitioning and linear layer partitioning. When QKV heads are partitioned, the multi-head computation mechanism of attention makes tensor partitioning convenient. Each head is computed independently first, and the results are then concatenated. Assume that the attention layer of the model needs to partition numheads query heads by the partition count tpsize. numheads must be divisible by tpsize, and the number of query heads placed on each card is numheadsperrank = numheads // tpsize. The numbers of key and value heads are equal and may be less than or equal to the number of query heads (they are smaller in MQA and GQA scenarios). To ensure that at least one key and one value head are placed on each card, calculate the number of key or value heads placed on each card as follows: numkeyvalueheadsperrank = max(numkeyvalueheads // tpsize, 1). The following figure shows the arrangement of QKV heads on cards. attentiontp The three linear layers qproj, kproj, and vproj can be further merged into one linear layer, qkvproj. This replaces three matrix multiplications with one matrix multiplication during inference and maximizes the use of NPU computing capability to improve performance. Then, partition the result to obtain Q, K, and V, perform attention computation, and finally generate the output through the oproj layer. MoE Tensor Parallel Optimization Assume that the partition count of the model's MoE layer is tpsize and the number of experts is expertnum. When the MoE layer is tensor-partitioned, apply column partitioning to gateproj and upproj, and row partitioning to downproj. gateproj and upproj can use merged matmul optimization to obtain gateupproj, improving computation performance. Fix the KV Cache Size First, allocate a fixed-size KV Cache tensor to avoid the performance loss caused by dynamic memory allocation in the source code. The KV Cache size is (batch seqlen numkeyvalueheadsperrank headdim), where seqlen is at least the maximum sum of input and output lengths to ensure that KV Cache updates do not go out of bounds during inference. After Q, K, and V are computed, use the scatterupdate operator to update the KV Cache at specified positions. For details, see the torchnpu.scatterupdate (Chinese) API. Enable Fused Operators RMSNorm Fusion and AddRMSNorm Fusion Replace the forward function of GptOssRMSNorm and use the fused operator APIs torchnpu.npurmsnorm (Chinese) and torchnpu.npuaddrmsnorm to replace the computation of multiple operators with a fused kernel and improve performance. Enable GMM and Optimize Routing In the MoE expert module of GPT-OSS, enable fused operators to further improve performance. For details, see the implementation in the GptOssMLP class. Flash Attention Fused Operator Optimization Enable the torchnpu.npufusedinferattentionscorev2 (Chinese) FlashAttention operator, which supports graph mode in inference scenarios and supports both full computation and incremental computation scenarios. Fast expert selection: When calculating the routing scores between experts and tokens, use the torchnpu.npumoegatingtopksoftmax (Chinese) fused operator instead of the original multi-operator operation that performs topk before softmax. This calculates the scores between tokens and experts more quickly. Efficient sorting and token routing: Enable the torchnpu.npumoeinitrouting (Chinese) fused operator to perform MoE routing computation and obtain the expert ordering. Enable the torchnpu.npumoecomputeexperttokens (Chinese) fused operator to obtain the number of tokens that each expert needs to compute. Enable the torchnpu.npumoefinalizerouting (Chinese) fused operator to rearrange and calculate the weighted sum of the tokens after expert computation, obtaining the final output. High-performance expert computation: Enable the torchnpu.npugroupedmatmul (Chinese) fused operator to perform matrix multiplication for multiple experts and improve computation and data movement efficiency. Enable AIV Expansion for Collective Communication Use the Device's Vector Core compute units to accelerate AllReduce operations. Enable AIV through the HCCLOPEXPANSIONMODE (Chinese) environment variable as follows: shell export HCCLOPEXPANSIONMODE=AIV Appendix Environment Deployment and Sample Execution (Chinese)

Hy3 昇腾0day适配： 基于CANN的高性能推理优化实践 Hy3 正式版发布，面向真实业务场景打磨，采用 295B 总参数、21B 激活参数架构，原生支持 256K 上下文，并提供nothink（极速响应）、thinklow（快速思考）与 thinkhigh（深度推理） 多档思考模式，兼顾极速响应、复杂推理与调用成本。 Hy3 在 昇腾950PR/DT 与 Atlas A3 两个平台的推理部署样例均已开源。本文主要介绍基于 Ascend950PR 多卡环境的 Hy3 模型 Prefill 推理优化，首先分析了Hy3 模型架构与模型并行策略，并介绍适配昇腾的多卡部署与融合 Kernel 优化方案。基于全套优化方案，本实践 0day 完成 Hy3 模型部署，支持原生 FP8 权重，并进一步支持昇腾亲和的 MXFP8/MXFP4 量化格式，同时兼容 C8 量化方案，全套优化模型与融合 Kernel 均已开源。 针对 Hy3 模型 GQA 推理架构，本次重点完成FA 全 FP8 量化优化，实现QKV 前处理融合算子与FP8 全量化 GQA两个融合算子并完成模型适配集成，进一步提升长序列推理吞吐与时延性能。本次开源包含模型部署实现与AscendC高性能实现。 Highlights 设计实现NPU亲和的并行策略，支持昇腾950PR/DT和Atlas-A3多代际昇腾芯片部署。 模型推理代码 已在cann-recipes-infer开源。 基于AscendC开源发布 QKV 前处理融合算子与 FP8 全量化 GQA 融合算子，高性能计算GQA前处理流程。 基于NpuGraphEx后端，叠加dynamo编译缓存、多流并行等特性，释放昇腾算力，实现极致的图模式加速。 昇腾950PR/DT支持原生FP8量化模式，可实现权重无损平滑迁移。同时本实践支持采用MXFP8替代原生FP8计算，并进一步支持MXFP4量化。 基于上述优化点，CANN已0day支持Hy3推理部署。 模型结构 Hy3 采用GQA+MoE 混合架构，原生支持 256K 上下文。 属性 值 :---:--- 架构 混合专家（MoE） 总参数量 295B 激活参数量 21B MTP层参数量 3.8B 层数（不含MTP层） 80 MTP层数 1 注意力头 64（GQA，8 个 KV 头，head dim 128） 隐藏层维度 4096 FFN 中间层维度 13312 上下文长度 256K 词表大小 120832 专家数量 192 个专家，top-8 激活 并行策略: Prefill优化（Attention SP+TP, MoE EP） 概述 在Prefill推理场景下，模型需要一次性处理完整的输入序列，属于计算密集（compute-bound）场景。为在TTFT时延约束下实现最大吞吐，采用Attention序列并行（SP）+张量并行（TP）与MoE专家并行（EP）的组合策略，结合MXFP8/MXFP4量化与多算子融合，显著降低Prefill阶段的计算与通信开销。同时为了节省LM Head和Embedding Table的内存占用，LM Head和Embedding计算使用TP并行。 Attention SP+TP优化 并行策略选择 Attention部分可以考虑的并行方式包括DP/TP/SP，由于TTFT的时延要求，Attention的并行策略主要考虑TP/SP。Hy3模型为GQA结构（qhead:kvhead=64:8），因此TP并行是比较自然的选择。在TP的基础上对FA前后的算子增加SP并行，进一步减少整体时延。 整体来说一般采用两种方案： 方案一（AllGather + ReduceScatter）：FA 前用 AllGather 将各 Rank 的序列分片聚合成完整序列参与注意力；FA 后经 oproj，再由 ReduceScatter 求和并切回序列分片。 方案二（AlltoAll + AlltoAll）：FA 前后均用 AlltoAll 在「序列分片」与「注意力头分片」两种布局间切换；每张卡始终只持有一份分片、无需像 AllGather 那样将完整序列复制到每张卡，因而通信数据量更小。 两种方案的差异如下图所示： mermaid %%{init: {"flowchart": {"rankSpacing": 18, "nodeSpacing": 320}}}%% flowchart LR subgraph schemeagrs["
