Hy3 Day-0 Adaptation on Ascend: High-Performance Inference Optimization with CANN The official version of Hy3 has been released and refined for real-world business scenarios. It uses an architecture with 295B total parameters and 21B activated parameters, natively supports a 256K context, and provides multiple thinking modes: nothink (ultra-fast response), thinklow (fast thinking), and thinkhigh (deep reasoning). These modes balance response speed, complex reasoning, and invocation cost. Inference deployment samples for Hy3 on both Ascend 950PR/DT and Atlas A3 have been open-sourced. This document primarily describes Prefill inference optimization for the Hy3 model in a multi-card Ascend 950PR environment. It first analyzes the Hy3 model architecture and model parallel strategies, and then introduces multi-card deployment and fused Kernel optimization solutions adapted to Ascend. With the complete optimization solution, this practice completed Hy3 model deployment on day 0, supports native FP8 weights, further supports the Ascend-friendly MXFP8/MXFP4 quantization formats, and is also compatible with the C8 quantization solution. The complete optimized model and fused Kernels have been open-sourced. For the GQA inference architecture of the Hy3 model, this work focuses on fully FP8-quantized FA optimization. It implements and integrates two fused operators, a QKV preprocessing fused operator and fully FP8-quantized GQA, further improving long-sequence inference throughput and latency. This open-source release includes the model deployment implementation and a high-performance Ascend C implementation. Highlights Design and implement an NPU-friendly parallel strategy that supports deployment on multiple generations of Ascend chips, including Ascend 950PR/DT and Atlas-A3. The model inference code (Chinese) is open-sourced in cann-recipes-infer. Open-source the QKV preprocessing fused operator and fully FP8-quantized GQA fused operator based on Ascend C for high-performance GQA preprocessing. Use the NpuGraphEx backend together with features such as the dynamo compilation cache and multi-stream parallelism to unlock Ascend compute power and achieve highly optimized graph-mode acceleration. Ascend 950PR/DT supports native FP8 quantization, enabling smooth weight migration without loss. This practice also supports replacing native FP8 computation with MXFP8 and further supports MXFP4 quantization. Based on the preceding optimizations, CANN supports Hy3 inference deployment on day 0. Model Architecture Hy3 uses a hybrid GQA+MoE architecture and natively supports a 256K context. Attribute Value :---:--- Architecture Mixture of Experts (MoE) Total parameters 295B Activated parameters 21B MTP layer parameters 3.8B Layers (excluding the MTP layer) 80 MTP layers 1 Attention heads 64 (GQA, eight KV heads, head dim 128) Hidden dimension 4096 FFN intermediate dimension 13312 Context length 256K Vocabulary size 120832 Number of experts 192 experts, top-8 activated Parallel Strategy: Prefill Optimization (Attention SP+TP, MoE EP) Overview In the Prefill inference scenario, the model processes the complete input sequence at once and is compute-bound. To maximize throughput under TTFT latency constraints, use a combination of Attention sequence parallelism (SP), tensor parallelism (TP), and MoE expert parallelism (EP). MXFP8/MXFP4 quantization and multi-operator fusion significantly reduce computation and communication overhead in the Prefill stage. To reduce the memory occupied by the LM Head and Embedding Table, LM Head and Embedding computations also use TP. Attention SP+TP Optimization Parallel Strategy Selection The parallel methods available for the Attention component include DP, TP, and SP. Because of TTFT latency requirements, the Attention parallel strategy primarily considers TP and SP. The Hy3 model uses a GQA architecture (qhead:kvhead=64:8), making TP a natural choice. Add SP to the operators before and after FA on top of TP to further reduce overall latency. Two solutions are generally used: Solution 1 (AllGather + ReduceScatter): Before FA, use AllGather to aggregate the sequence shards on all Ranks into a complete sequence for attention. After FA and oproj, use ReduceScatter to sum the results and partition them back into sequence shards. Solution 2 (AlltoAll + AlltoAll): Use AlltoAll before and after FA to switch between the sequence-shard and attention-head-shard layouts. Each card always holds only one shard, without copying the complete sequence to every card as AllGather does, resulting in a smaller communication volume. TP partitions the K or N axis of GMM too finely, reducing computation performance. With EP, each Rank holds some experts and uses InitRouting to match tokens with experts. Communication overhead remains controllable when epsize is small. EP is further divided into the AG-RS (AllGather-ReduceScatter) solution and the Double Routing (AlltoAll) solution: Parallel Strategy Communication Operators Communication Volume Applicable Scenario ------------------- ------------------------- ------------------------- -------------------------------------------- EP (AG-RS) AllGather + ReduceScatter (B,S,H) × 2 Smaller volume when epsize is small and topk > epsize EP (Double Routing) AlltoAll + AlltoAll (BS×topk/epsize, H) × 2 Large-EP scenarios; smaller volume when ep > topk Note: In the table, S and BS both indicate the global complete sequence length. In AG-RS, this is the complete sequence held by each card after AllGather. For the current model, topk=8. When epsize=4, topk > epsize, so the AG-RS solution has a smaller communication volume and is the preferred default. AG-RS Solution EP AG-RS solution: Each rank first obtains all sequence tokens through AllGather. InitRouting routes and computes only local experts. After GMM, FinalizeRouting applies weights and masks non-local experts. Finally, ReduceScatter sums the results and partitions them back into subsequences. This solution exchanges redundant communication of (B,S,H)×2 for regular collective communication and is suitable for small-EP scenarios where topk > epsize. Double Routing Solution EP Double Routing (AlltoAll) solution: Each rank first uses InitRouting to expand and group local tokens by expert. The outbound AlltoAll then accurately sends tokens to the rank containing the target expert. After ReRouting rearranges the tokens and GMM performs computation, the inbound AlltoAll returns the GMM output to the source rank along the original route. Finally, FinalizeRouting multiplies the output by routing weights and combines it. Two precise AlltoAll transfers provide zero redundant communication and zero redundant computation. Shared Expert Multi-Stream Parallelism (Prefill) In each MoE layer of Hy3, every token passes through a shared expert in addition to the top-8 routed experts. The shared expert depends only on the MoE input and not on the Gating result, so it has no data dependency on the dispatch and grouped GMM of the routed experts. In the Prefill stage, split them into two streams accordingly. The main stream sequentially performs Gating, the routed-expert path (the default AG-RS solution: AllGather → InitRouting → grouped GMM → FinalizeRouting → ReduceScatter), and the final combine addition. The shared expert is delivered to the secondary stream, whose start synchronization point is placed after Gating on the main stream. The routed-expert path is the time-consuming part of the MoE block. The shared expert runs concurrently with it and is masked by it, adding almost no latency. NPU Kimi-K2-Thinking Inference Optimization On November 6, Moonshot AI released its latest thinking model, Kimi-K2-Thinking. It excels at deep reasoning and achieves new record benchmark performance. Its model architecture is consistent with Kimi-K2 and natively supports the mixed-precision mode of MOE W4A16 + Attention BF16, balancing inference performance and accuracy. This document primarily describes inference optimization for the Kimi-K2-Thinking model on an A3 cluster. Because its architecture is essentially consistent with Kimi-K2, the basic optimizations can be inherited smoothly. This practice adapted the MOE W4A16 quantization involved in this model on day 0 and provides a recommended deployment strategy for A3 clusters. Performance optimization will continue in the future. Highlights CANN supports Kimi-K2-Thinking inference deployment with a 256K sequence on day 0. The model inference code (Chinese) is open-sourced, and the mainstream open-source inference framework SGLang is also supported. This practice supports the native Kimi-K2-Thinking quantization mode. MOE GroupedMatmul uses W4A16 computation, while Attention retains BF16 precision, balancing inference performance and accuracy. The corresponding GroupedMatmul operator implementation is fully open-sourced. For typical inference scenarios such as small batch sizes and long-sequence production, Decode MLA implements the Flash Decode acceleration mechanism, effectively reducing latency and improving compute utilization. The corresponding FusedInferAttentionScore operator implementation is fully open-sourced. The minimum deployment unit in this practice is a single server, which supports inference tasks with a 4K sequence length. Multi-server large-EP deployment is also supported. Collaborative deployment on a multi-server cluster meets the inference requirements of ultra-long 256K sequences. Outline Parallel Strategy Fused Kernels MTP Future Plan Parallel Strategy The following figure shows the recommended deployment strategy for Atlas A3. Prefill uses M nodes, and Decode uses N nodes. Each node contains eight cards. Adjust M and N dynamically from 1 to 24 based on constraints such as the available resources and SLA. Prefill Parallel Strategy For long-sequence scenarios, Prefill Attention uses Context Parallel (CP). Multiple ranks share the long-sequence computation, so each rank has a smaller computation volume and activation memory footprint. TTFT is more controllable, improving the user experience. The MoE module continues to use the EP parallelism of DeepSeek-V3.1 to balance throughput and latency. Decode Parallel Strategy The Decode stage continues to use the DeepSeek V3.1 deployment strategy with Attention DP + MoE EP. In particular, because the Oproj and LMHead weights occupy substantial memory and present a clear memory-access bottleneck during Decode, this practice uses local TP. The Embedding layer is also partitioned with TP to reduce device memory usage. To minimize the communication overhead introduced by TP, the TP domain is kept within a single server. Fused Kernels The following figure shows the full-network computation flow. This practice uses fused Kernels such as MLAProlog, FusedInferAttentionScore, MoeDistributeDispatch, MoeDistributeCombine, and GroupedMatmul, providing a practical reference for efficient deployment of similar models on the Ascend platform. MTP Compared with DeepSeek V3.1, Kimi-K2-Thinking reduces the number of Attention Heads from 128 to 64, significantly reducing Attention computation and making it more favorable for MTP scenarios. The Decode stage of LLM inference is typically bottlenecked by memory access. MTP can reduce memory-access pressure at a small computation cost. Because Kimi-K2-Thinking has a lighter Attention computation load, it is less likely to reach the computation bottleneck in MTP mode and achieves better performance. The code for this practice supports multi-head MTP. If trained MTP weights are available, enable this feature directly to accelerate inference. Future Plan Quantization: MOE W4A16 inference is currently supported. A low-bit quantization version can be developed for Attention in the future to further reduce system memory usage and latency. Long-sequence performance optimization: TTFT in long-sequence scenarios still has room for improvement. Future work will explore more suitable deployment solutions and specifically optimize fused Kernel performance to comprehensively improve the response speed and operating efficiency of long-sequence inference.

AttnRes（分块注意力残差）作为 Full AttnRes 的可扩展变体。该机制按块聚合跨层表示，以块级表示代替全部历史子层输出作为候选状态，从而在保留跨层选择能力的同时，降低候选状态数量及其显存开销。 具体而言，Kimi K3 将 93 个 Decoder Layer 划分为 8 个 Block，每个 Block 包含约 12 层。对于第 $n$ 个 Block，历史块状态集合记为 $\mathcal{B}n=[\mathbf{b}0,\mathbf{b}1,\ldots,\mathbf{b}{n-1}]$，其中包含初始词嵌入以及此前各 Block 的聚合输出。Block 之间通过 AttnRes 对这些状态进行选择性聚合；Block 内部则采用逐层累加方式维护动态表示 $\mathbf{p}$，下文称为 partial。 进入一个 Block 时，partial 尚未生成，因此第一个 Attention 子层仅对历史块状态集合 $\mathcal{B}n$ 执行 AttnRes 聚合，并以聚合结果作为子层输入。该子层的输出用于初始化 partial。此后，每个 Attention 或 FFN/MoE 子层均将当前 partial 作为新增候选状态，与 $\mathcal{B}n$ 拼接为 $[\mathbf{b}0,\mathbf{b}1,\ldots,\mathbf{b}{n-1}, \mathbf{p}]$ 共同参与 AttnRes 聚合；子层输出随后累加至 partial。Attention 与 FFN/MoE 分别使用独立的 pseudo-query，因此二者具有相互独立的深度权重。 为减少块内重复计算，Block AttnRes 可等价地拆分为以下两个阶段： Phase 1（批量计算块间注意力）：在 Block 入口处，批量计算块内各子层 pseudo-query 与历史块状态集合 $\mathcal{B}n$ 之间的分数。对于每个 AttnRes 位置，分别生成 Softmax 所需的最大分数 $m$、归一化指数和 $Z$ 以及未归一化加权和 $\mathbf{N}$。下式中，$\mathbf{b}i$ 表示第 $i$ 个历史块状态，$\elli$ 表示其对应分数： $$ m=\maxi\elli,\qquad Z=\sumi e^{\elli-m},\qquad \mathbf{N}=\sumi e^{\elli-m}\mathbf{b}i $$ Phase 2（顺序计算块内注意力）：按层执行 Block 内的前向计算。对于每个子层，使用对应的 pseudo-query 计算当前 partial $\mathbf{p}$ 的分数 $r$，再通过 Online Softmax 将 $(\mathbf{p},r)$ 合并到 Phase 1 生成的统计量中，得到该子层的 AttnRes 输出 $\mathbf{h}$： $$ \begin{aligned} M &= \max(m,r), \\ Z' &= e^{m-M}Z+e^{r-M}, \\ \mathbf{N}' &= e^{m-M}\mathbf{N}+e^{r-M}\mathbf{p}, \\ \mathbf{h} &= \mathbf{N}'/Z'. \end{aligned} $$ 以合并后的最大分数 $M$ 为基准平移指数项，可降低指数运算溢出的风险并改善数值稳定性。在精确算术下，两阶段计算与直接对全部候选状态执行 Softmax 聚合严格等价；在有限精度计算中，二者可能因运算顺序不同而产生细微数值差异。各 Block 的统计量相互独立，仅用于对应 Block 的当前次前向计算。 原实现、两阶段优化与融合算子 Kimi 原实现：AttnRes 随 Decoder Layer 逐层更新，将有效块间历史状态与当前 block 表示进行深度 Softmax 聚合，生成 Attention 与 FFN/MoE 输入；核心聚合由 KimiDecoderLayer.forward 中的 applyattnres 完成。 两阶段优化：KimiLinearModel.forwardattnresblock 将 block 内复用的块间历史状态计算前移，批量生成统计量，并在层内通过 Online Softmax 合入动态 partial。该路径与 Kimi 原实现数学等价，由 attnresmode: twophase 启用；Output AttnRes 保持原实现。 融合算子：attnresmode: fused 保持相同的两阶段调度，Phase 1/Phase 2 分别调用 blockattnresprepare 和 blockattnresupdate，由融合算子完成 anchor 打分与统计归约、partial 打分与 Online Softmax 合并，减少中间张量读写与调度开销。默认值为 Kimi K3 Inference Optimization on Ascend NPU Kimi K3 uses a 2.8T-parameter hybrid-attention MoE architecture that interleaves Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) and Gated MLA and introduces Attention Residuals (AttnRes) and Stable LatentMoE. The model natively supports a 1M context. KDA maintains a fixed-size sequence state, AttnRes aggregates historical representations along the network depth, and Stable LatentMoE performs Routed Expert computation in the latent space. cann-recipes-infer provides an implementation reference for Kimi K3 on a four-server, 32-card Ascend 950PR/DT cluster. It uses a combined deployment strategy of Embedding TP, Attention TP, Dense TP, Prefill SP, Decode DP, and Routed Expert EP. KDA, MLA, and MoE all use fused operators. Mamba Cache allocates storage and maps requests for convstate and the KDA ssm state. Stable LatentMoE supports native MXFP4 weights, dynamic MXFP8 activations, and Decode Shared Expert multi-stream execution. The two-phase/fused AttnRes optimization and Decode npugraphex can be enabled as needed; DSpark-based speculative decoding significantly improves Decode throughput. For complete execution instructions, see the model README . Highlights Block AttnRes: Attention and FFN independently calculate Softmax weights for cross-layer representations. In addition to the naive implementation, recipes provides a two-phase computation strategy, implemented through the blockattnresprepare / blockattnresupdate fused operators. Stable LatentMoE and SiTU: Routed Experts compute in the 3584-dimensional latent space, while Shared Experts retain the 7168-dimensional backbone path. Both use SiTU activation. recipes provides reference implementations for Routed Expert EP deployment and Shared Expert TP deployment and supports native MXFP4/MXFP8 Expert computation. Hybrid parallel strategy: recipes uses Embedding TP, Attention TP, Dense TP, Routed Expert EP, Prefill SP, and Decode DP to balance model memory constraints and inference performance. KDA fused operators: Prefill uses the flashkda fused operator, which fuses L2 normalization, gate activation, and beta sigmoid into the operator. Decode uses the fusedrecurrentkda operator, fully fusing L2 norm, gate, and beta during token-by-token recurrence to reduce Python-side preprocessing overhead and intermediate tensor reads and writes. MegaMoE: Routed Expert computation in both Prefill and Decode can switch to the megamoe fused operator, which completes Dispatch, GMM1, SiTU, GMM2, and Combine in a single operator, reducing communication and scheduling overhead in large-EP scenarios. DSpark speculative decoding: The DSpark draft model proposes multiple tokens based on the main model's hidden states. The main model then verifies all draft positions in parallel and commits tokens via acceptance-rate sampling, significantly improving Decode throughput. The draft model and the main model each compile their own Decode graph. Attention selects either KDA or Gated MLA. Layer 1 is followed by a Dense FFN, and layers 2 through 93 are followed by Stable LatentMoE. KDA and Gated MLA use an approximately 3:1 periodic arrangement. Counting from layer 1, the first 92 layers consist of 23 groups of KDA - KDA - KDA - MLA, and the 93rd layer uses one more MLA layer: Attention Residuals AttnRes selects historical representations of the same token along the network depth. Each Attention and FFN sublayer uses an independent learnable pseudo-query to score the RMSNorm results of candidate representations, performs Softmax along the depth direction, and then computes a weighted sum of the raw candidate representations: $$ \elli=\mathbf{w}^{\mathsf T}\operatorname{RMSNorm}(\mathbf{z}i),\qquad \alphai=\frac{e^{\elli}}{\sumj e^{\ellj}},\qquad \mathbf{h}=\sumi\alphai\mathbf{z}i $$ The pseudo-query itself does not depend on the input, but candidate representations change with the token, so the depth weights still vary with the input. RMSNorm is used only to generate scores; the weighted sum uses the raw representations without normalization. Block AttnRes and Two-Phase Computation Kimi K3 uses Block AttnRes (block attention residuals) as a scalable variant of Full AttnRes. This mechanism aggregates cross-layer representations in blocks and uses block-level representations instead of all historical sublayer outputs as candidate states, reducing the number of candidate states and their memory overhead while preserving cross-layer selection capability. Specifically, Kimi K3 divides the 93 Decoder Layers into 8 Blocks, each containing about 12 layers. For the $n$-th Block, the historical block-state set is denoted $\mathcal{B}n=[\mathbf{b}0,\mathbf{b}1,\ldots,\mathbf{b}{n-1}]$, which includes the initial word embedding and the aggregated outputs of all previous Blocks. AttnRes selectively aggregates these states between Blocks; within a Block, a dynamic representation $\mathbf{p}$, called the partial, is maintained by layer-by-layer accumulation. When entering a Block, the partial has not been generated yet, so the first Attention sublayer performs AttnRes aggregation only on the historical block-state set $\mathcal{B}n$ and uses the aggregated result as the sublayer input. The output of this sublayer initializes the partial. Afterward, each Attention or FFN/MoE sublayer appends the current partial as a new candidate state, concatenating it with $\mathcal{B}n$ as $[\mathbf{b}0,\mathbf{b}1,\ldots,\mathbf{b}{n-1}, \mathbf{p}]$ for AttnRes aggregation. The sublayer output is then accumulated into the partial. Attention and FFN/MoE use independent pseudo-queries and therefore have independent depth weights. To reduce repeated computation within a Block, Block AttnRes can be equivalently split into the following two phases: Phase 1 (batch computation of inter-block attention): At the Block entrance, compute the scores between the pseudo-queries of all sublayers in the Block and the historical block-state set $\mathcal{B}n$ in batch. For each AttnRes position, generate the maximum score $m$, the normalized exponential sum $Z$, and the unnormalized weighted sum $\mathbf{N}$ required by Softmax. In the following equations, $\mathbf{b}i$ denotes the $i$-th historical block state and $\elli$ its score: $$ m=\maxi\elli,\qquad Z=\sumi e^{\elli-m},\qquad \mathbf{N}=\sumi e^{\elli-m}\mathbf{b}i $$ Phase 2 (sequential computation of intra-block attention): Execute the forward computation inside the Block layer by layer. For each sublayer, compute the score $r$ of the current partial $\mathbf{p}$ with its pseudo-query, and merge $(\mathbf{p},r)$ into the statistics generated in Phase 1 through Online Softmax to obtain the AttnRes output $\mathbf{h}$ of that sublayer: $$ \begin{aligned} M &= \max(m,r), \\ Z' &= e^{m-M}Z+e^{r-M}, \\ \mathbf{N}' &= e^{m-M}\mathbf{N}+e^{r-M}\mathbf{p}, \\ \mathbf{h} &= \mathbf{N}'/Z'. \end{aligned} $$ Shifting the exponential terms by the merged maximum score $M$ reduces the risk of exponential overflow and improves numerical stability. Under exact arithmetic, the two-phase computation is strictly equivalent to directly performing Softmax aggregation over all candidate states; under finite-precision arithmetic, the two may differ slightly due to different operation orders. The statistics of each Block are independent and used only for the current forward computation of the corresponding Block. Original Implementation, Two-Phase Optimization, and Fused Operators Kimi original implementation: AttnRes is updated layer by layer along the Decoder Layers, performing depth-wise Softmax aggregation between the effective inter-block historical states and the current block representation to generate Attention and FFN/MoE inputs. The core aggregation is completed by applyattnres in KimiDecoderLayer.forward. Two-phase optimization: KimiLinearModel.forwardattnresblock moves the computation of inter-block historical states reused within a Block forward, generates statistics in batch, and merges the dynamic partial through Online Softmax within each layer. This path is mathematically equivalent to the Kimi original implementation and is enabled by attnresmode: twophase; the Output AttnRes keeps the original implementation. Fused operators: attnresmode: fused keeps the same two-phase schedule, and Phase 1/Phase 2 call blockattnresprepare and blockattnresupdate respectively. The fused operators complete anchor scoring and statistical reduction, partial scoring, and Online Softmax merging, reducing intermediate tensor reads and writes and scheduling overhead. The default value is original. Hybrid Attention: KDA and Gated MLA Kimi Delta Attention KDA is a Delta Rule linear attention with per-key-channel decay. Its input is the Output of the Input RMSNorm of the Decoder Layer. The Q/K/V dimension of each head is 128, and KDA maintains a fixed 128 × 128 KDA SSM State. The state is updated token by token: the old state is first decayed by the key channel, K reads the prediction of the current V from it; β scales the difference between the actual V and the prediction and writes the correction back to the state along the corresponding K direction; Q finally reads the updated state. Before entering the KDA core, Q/K undergo L2Norm, Q is additionally scaled by the inverse square root of the key dimension, and V is not normalized. The per-head, per-key-channel gk is generated by faproj, fbproj, dtbias, and the 128-dimensional Alog shared by all heads. The K3 configuration sets gatelowerbound to -5, so gk is in (-5, 0). Both Prefill and Decode use this log-decay; Decode passes it as the gk parameter to the fused operator, and the old state is multiplied by the retention factor corresponding to its exponential. bproj generates β through sigmoid. The KDA output first performs per-head RMSNorm, then multiplies the per-value-channel sigmoid output gate, and finally enters oproj. The three gates control state decay, state write, and output respectively. The long-term state size of KDA is independent of the sequence length. For each request and each KDA layer, only the following needs to be saved: convstate: concatenated along the Q/K/V channels, storing the inputs of the last 3 tokens of the three ShortConv branches; KDA SSM State: a 128 × 128 matrix for each local head. qkvproj generates Q/K/V by channel. The fused QKV ShortConv calls causalconv1dfn in Prefill and causalconv1dupdate in Decode to complete the per-channel causal convolution and SiLU before splitting into three branches. The three channel groups use their own convolution weights and share one concatenated convstate. convstate and the KDA SSM State are registered as MambaCacheEntry respectively, and the framework uniformly allocates and maintains the mapping from requests to state blocks. Prefill clears the corresponding state rows, causalconv1dfn updates convstate, and the Torch chunk KDA computes per request and writes back the KDA SSM State. Decode reuses the same block id and advances the two types of state in place through causalconv1dupdate and npurecurrentgateddeltarule respectively. Gated MLA Gated MLA follows MLA's low-rank Q/KV projection and adds per-head, per-value-channel gating after the Attention output. recipes provides reference implementations of Prefill native and Decode absorb. Both Prefill and Decode use npukvrmsnormropecachev2 (interface reference: npukvrmsnormropecache ) to fuse the RMSNorm of the KV latent and write the normalized latent and the extra K features into two Paged Caches according to slotmapping. In Prefill, kvbproj temporarily expands the current latent into per-head K/V, and npufusedinferattentionscore is called with the NTDTND layout and sparsemode=3 to complete causal Attention over variable-length sequences. In Decode, the K matrix of the KV up-projection is absorbed into the Query side, and npufusedinferattentionscorev2 is called to directly read the NZ-layout latent Paged Cache and complete the absorb Attention. The absorbed V projection then restores the operator output to the value space of each Attention head. Stable LatentMoE Layers 2 through 93 of Kimi K3 use Stable LatentMoE. The input enters three branches: the Sigmoid Router, Latent Down, and Shared Expert. The Routed branch computes in the 3584-dimensional latent space, and the aggregated result is restored to 7168 dimensions through RMSNorm and Latent Up, then added to the Shared Expert branch. When enablemultistreams is enabled in Decode, the Shared Expert runs on an independent stream in parallel with the MC2 path of the Routed Expert and is synchronized before the results are added; Prefill executes on the main stream. The Router selects 16 experts for each token from 896 experts. correctionbias participates only in expert selection. The aggregation weights are obtained by normalizing the sigmoid scores without bias among the selected experts and then multiplying by routedscalingfactor: $$ \begin{aligned} r &= \operatorname{sigmoid}(Wr x), \\ \mathcal{I} &= \operatorname{TopK}(r+b{\mathrm{corr}},16), \\ pi &= s\frac{ri}{\sum{j\in\mathcal{I}}rj},\quad i\in\mathcal{I}, \end{aligned} $$ where s denotes routedscalingfactor. A single Routed Expert has the structure 3584 -> gate/up 3072 each -> 3584; the Shared Expert computes at the backbone width with the structure 7168 -> gate/up 6144 each -> 7168. Dense, Shared, and Routed FFNs all use SiTU as the activation function. In this practice, the Router uses npumoegatingtopk to complete Top-16 expert selection based on sigmoid routing scores and correctionbias, and outputs the expert indices and aggregation weights used for subsequent routing. Prefill uses the AG–EP–RS path. Routed latent is first dynamically quantized to MXFP8, and then AllGather aggregates the activations, scales, and routing results of each SP shard. npumoeinitroutingv2 expands and reorders activations and their scales by expert. Expert computation uses two npugroupedmatmul calls to complete the MXFP4 gate/up projection and down projection respectively. After SiTU, dynamic MXFP8 quantization is performed again before the second GMM. Finally, npumoefinalizerouting restores the token order and aggregates by routing weights, and ReduceScatter returns to the SP layout. Decode uses the MC2 EP path. npumoedistributedispatchv2 dispatches tokens to the corresponding Expert ranks according to the Top-16 results. Local experts continue to use two npugroupedmatmul calls to complete MXFP4 Expert computation. npumoedistributecombinev2 completes cross-EP aggregation, routing-weight weighting, and token-order recovery. When multi-stream is enabled, the Shared Expert runs on an independent stream in parallel with the Routed Expert MC2 path above. MegaMoE path: When enablemegamoe=True and moeepsize > 1, Routed Expert computation in both Prefill and Decode switches entirely to the megamoe fused operator. This operator completes Dispatch, GMM1, SiTU, GMM2, and Combine in a single operator and requires a symmetric communication buffer pre-allocated through getsymmbufferformegamoe, using megamoeepgroup as the communication domain. Compared with calling the MC2/AG–EP–RS path operator by operator, MegaMoE reduces communication and operator scheduling overhead in large-EP scenarios. Parallel Strategy The following parallel configurations apply to a four-server, 32-card Ascend 950PR/DT cluster with all 93 layers and 896 Experts. The framework-level model replica DP is 1; Decoder inter-layer representations use Prefill SP and Decode DP. The recommended parallel configuration is attntpsize=32 (full Attention TP), moetpsize=1 (deriving moeepsize=worldsize locally), oprojtpsize=attntpsize, embedtpsize=16, lmheadtpsize=8, densetpsize=8, and cpsize=1. Routed Experts use MXFP4 weights with E8M0 scales; the remaining major weights are stored in BF16 or FP32. Routed Expert EP shares Routed Expert parameters only along the Expert dimension. Shared Experts are fixed-activated for all tokens and do not belong to the expert set managed by the Router. The KDA/Gated MLA gproj/oproj also lies outside the MoE EP. Each cycle is participated in by the complete Attention TP communication group: prompt tokens perform Sequence Parallel across attntpsize ranks, and Attention performs TP along the head dimension. Decode: KDA uses DP–TP–DP. The Q/KV projections and Attention core of Gated MLA remain DP; the Attention output and gating input are converted to TP before the output gate, and ReduceScatter restores the DP layout after oproj. Routed Experts use MC2 Dispatch–EP–MC2 Combine or MegaMoE, and Shared Experts use AG–TP–RS. The KDA SSM State is sharded with Head TP, and each request holds one state row on every Attention TP rank. The Gated MLA latent Cache is replicated to each TP rank by request during Prefill, and in Decode only the Decode owner rank of the request writes to its local paged blocks. The first-layer Dense FFN and Shared Experts both use AG–TP–RS. Quantization Strategy The w13/w2 of the Kimi K3 Routed Experts use MXFP4 weights and dynamic MXFP8 activations. The remaining checkpoint weights are mainly BF16; the KDA ShortConv, Alog, dtbias, onorm, and Router correction bias remain FP32 in the checkpoint. After loading, the fused qkvconv1d.weight is converted to BF16 for computation. The quantization format of Routed Experts is: Weight elements: MXFP4 E2M1, with every two 4-bit elements packed into one byte; Weight scales: one E8M0 scale shared by every 32 input elements; Activations: dynamically quantized to MXFP8 E4M3FN per token and per group, with runtime scales of E8M0FNU; After SiTU, dynamic quantization is performed again before entering the downproj GMM. The DSpark draft model supports BF16 weights only and does not participate in MXFP4 quantization. The main model and the draft model use independent loading paths. npugraphex Graph Mode npugraphex captures the Decode stage of Kimi K3. Prefill remains eager to handle variable-length packed sequences and establish the initial Cache. Decode uses a fixed token count, fixed Cache addresses, and fixed AttnRes slots for capture/replay. When DSpark is enabled, the main model and the draft model compile independent Decode graphs: Main model: compiles model.decode (normal path) or the Verify path (parallel Decode with width verifysize = nextn + 1) using torch.compile(..., dynamic=True, backend="npugraphex"), with frozenparameter and statickernelcompile enabled. Draft model: compiles model.forwardspecdecode with the npugraphex backend and a fixed graph structure. The firstverify metadata-alias design of DSpark guarantees that the first Verify and subsequent Verify rounds reuse the same compiled main-model graph. When enableprofiler=True, the two-stage profiling writes to prof/prefill and prof/decode respectively. KDA Fused Operators The Prefill and Decode stages of KDA use different fused operators to fuse preprocessing operations such as L2 normalization, gate activation, and beta sigmoid into the NPU operators, reducing intermediate tensor reads and writes and Python-side operator scheduling overhead. The two switches control the Prefill and Decode paths respectively: Switch Default Function :---:---:--- enableflashkda True Select the flashkda fused operator or the torch reference implementation in Prefill enablefusedrecurrentkda True Select the fusedrecurrentkda fused operator or the gdr operator in Decode Prefill: flashkda Fused Operator The Prefill stage computes chunk KDA in blocks of 64 tokens per request. When enableflashkda=True, the flashkda operator is called; otherwise, the pure Python reference implementation (torchchunkkda) is used. When gatelowerbound is None (softplus gate form), flashkda does not support this gate formula and automatically falls back to the torch reference implementation. Fusion range comparison: Operation flashkda (fused operator) torch reference implementation :---:---:--- L2 normalization Fused inside the operator, eps=1e-6 Python-side l2normalize Gate activation Computes lowerbound sigmoid(exp(Alog) (g + dtbias)) inside the operator Same formula on the Python side Beta sigmoid 1/(1+exp(-beta)) inside the operator Python-side .sigmoid() Chunk loop Inside the operator Python for loop Input conventions: flashkda receives raw bf16 Q/K/g/beta (without preprocessing) and requires the bfloat16 dtype; initialstate/Alog/dtbias are fp32. The operator completes L2 norm and converts Q/K to fp32 for computation. The output state is fp32 [B, H, D, D], and the output is bf16 [B, S, H, D]. Padding strategy: When the request token count is not a multiple of 64, Q/K/V are padded with zeros (still zero after L2 norm, contributing zero to the output), and g/beta are padded with -inf (sigmoid(-inf)=0, so a zero gate activation keeps the state undecayed and a zero beta keeps the delta from updating the state), ensuring that padded tokens have no side effects on the recurrent state. After computation, output[:, :tokens] is trimmed to remove the padding. Decode: fusedrecurrentkda Fused Operator The Decode stage updates the KDA SSM State token by token. When enablefusedrecurrentkda=True and gatelowerbound is not None, the fusedrecurrentkda operator is called; otherwise, it falls back to the npurecurrentgateddeltarule (gdr) operator. Fusion range comparison: Operation fusedrecurrentkda (fused operator) gdr (baseline operator) :---:---:--- L2 normalization Fused inside the operator, eps=1e-6 Python-side l2normalize Gate activation lowerbound sigmoid(exp(Alog) (g + dtbias)) inside the operator Precomputed in the Python-side forward Beta sigmoid 1/(1+exp(-beta)) inside the operator Python-side .sigmoid() Input dtype Raw bf16 BSND 4D Preprocessed bf16 TND 3D State update In-place update of recurrentstatecache Same Return value (state, out) tuple; state discarded Single value out Input conventions: fusedrecurrentkda receives raw bf16 Q/K/g/beta in the BSND [B, S, H, D] layout; beta needs a trailing dimension padded to [B, S, H, 1]; Alog/dtbias are fp32; lowerbound is a float in the range [-5, 0]. ssmstateindices must be passed (the values are dynamically allocated block ids and the default arange cannot be used), and numacceptedtokens is passed as None (the default ones(batch) matches the actual value for standard decode with seq=1). State layout: The state layout of both paths is [pool, H, Dv, Dk] fp32, with row indices corresponding to the value dimension (Dv) and column indices to the key dimension (Dk). The state returned by fusedrecurrentkda is the same tensor object as the passed-in recurrentstatecache (updated in place), so the returned state can be discarded directly without writing back to the cache. DSpark Speculative Decoding DSpark (Draft-Speculative) is the speculative decoding solution provided by this sample. With draftmodeltype: dspark enabled, Kimi K3 loads a lightweight draft model (Kimi-K3-DSpark, BF16) in addition to normal Decode. Each iteration proposes nextn draft tokens in parallel, and the main model verifies and commits them at once, improving Decode throughput. Draft Model Architecture The draft model constructs a proposal distribution from the intermediate-layer outputs of the main model. It is a lightweight GQA structure deployed with a fixed TP8 (dsparktpgroup, requiring worldsize % 8 == 0): fc projection: projects the hidden states of the specified layers of the main model (contextwidth = targethiddensize × len(targetlayerids)) to the draft model hidden size as the context representation of the draft; GQA Attention (non-causal): performs non-causal attention over the committed context and the current draft positions. KV is written to the draft model's own Paged Cache (allocated by initdsparkcachedata, independent of the main model's caches). RoPE supports YaRN long-sequence extrapolation; Markov Head: a two-layer Markov head composed of markovw1/markovw2 outputs the vocabulary distribution for each draft position as the proposal distribution. The draft model and the main model share some weights through shared target modules (setsharedtargetmodules). Only BF16 weights are supported during loading (Kimi K3 DSpark supports BF16 weights only). Inference Flow DSpark inference maintains a draft proposal chain outside the main-model Decode graph: 1. Prefill: the main model completes Prefill cycle by mini cycle and routes the target hidden states of each request to the corresponding Decode owner rank through routeprefilltargethidden; 2. First Verify: runs one main-model Decode in parallel with width verifysize = nextn + 1 (firstverify=True), samples anchor tokens, and updates kvlen; 3. Propose: the draft model generates nextn draft tokens and their proposal distribution step by step from the anchor tokens, owner-local target hidden states, and context positions (dsparkpropose; draft positions after eos are filled with pad); 4. Verify & Commit: the main model verifies the draft positions in parallel with a fixed verifysize width. When temperature 0 must divide batchsizeperrank; The DSpark draft model supports BF16 weights only, and worldsize must be divisible by 8. Future Plan Weight prefetch: evaluate the benefit of prefetching MXFP4 expert weights for the memory-bound Routed Expert GMM and large linear layers. DSpark performance tuning: further optimize the draft model structure and proposal length (nextn) selection to improve the average acceptance length.

NPU LongCat-2.0推理优化实践 美团发布了最新的LongCat-2.0模型。模型结构上，在原先LongCat-Flash的ShortCut MOE(SC-MOE)结构基础上，叠加Sink Sliding Window Attention和DeepSeek Sparse Attention(DSA)，同时支持Over Embedding技术和零专家机制，大幅提升模型对超长上下文的处理能力。相关团队在 LongCat-2.0 NPU Inference 实践支持了基于昇腾Atlas A2的LongCat-2.0的服务化部署，提供长达1M序列的高性能推理能力。 在模型体量上，相较于此前发布的LongCat-Flash, LongCat-2.0模型的层数由28层增加到38层，路由专家个数由512增加到768，隐藏层维度从6144增加到8192，模型的参数量依然达到了1.6T。在MOE部分原生支持Int8量化的前提下，显存占用依然高达2.1TB。模型能力增强的同时，为推理部署与性能优化带来新的挑战，本实践对此做了针对性优化。 LongCat推理团队采用业界成熟的PD分离部署，Prefill使用64卡，Decode使用128卡，并分别支持Context Parallel(CP)并行，同时PD之间使用分层Cache传输，释放多专家与超长序列带来的内存压力。 通过Prefill针对性设计Pipeline Parallel(PP)并行与CP并行，Decode使用融合零专家优化流水的MC2 Dispatch/Combine算子并通过多流并行编排与MLP互相掩盖，减少大实例部署带来的通信开销。 在模型执行层面，通过使能Lightning Indexer, MlaProlog, Sparse Flash Attention等融合算子，叠加多流编排与GE静态图，大幅削减调度开销，释放昇腾算力。 Outline 模型结构 融合算子 部署策略 性能优化 Future Plan 模型结构 LongCat-2.0模型使能了 DSA稀疏结构 ，在Attention计算之前，使用Lightning Indexer为每个token选择 topk=2048组KV，极大节约了Attention计算耗时。在SC MOE结构下，每层的两个Sparse Flash Attention (SFA)共用一组topkindices。参照 DSA计算量分析 分析，本次开源的实践样例的Prefill和Decode都使用了absorb模式，亲和DSA的性能。 在DSA基础上，LongCat-2.0模型额外叠加了Sink Sliding Window(3S)设计，在预留的 topk=2048组KV里，固定选择每段请求的init 16（序列维度最前面的16组KV，对应sink）和local 1024（序列维度最后面的1024组KV，对应slidingwindow），再从中段选择top 1008组KV，进一步提升模型能力。3S LI对KV Pair的筛选方式如下图示例。 Over Embedding LongCat-2.0模型支持了基于美团技术报告的Over Embedding实现，可以通过在推理开始时的Embedding计算环节小幅增加计算量，得到模型效果的提升。OE计算的步骤如下图所示。 每个token与前序oen - 1个token计算，得到(oen - 1)个带有前序Token信息的n-gram，再对它们分别进行Ngram Embedding计算。Ngram Embedding的计算过程被拆解为oek张子表，每张子表对应自己的Embedding和Projection，用增加子表个数的方式减少不同n-gram映射到词表同一行的概率，并提升n-gram表达的自由度。从计算流的视角来看，OE计算为oek张子表，将每个token与前序oen - 1个token通过哈希计算，得到(oen - 1) oek个oetoken，再对oetoken做OE Embedding和OE Projection计算。最后将得到的oehiddenstates与原始Embedding计算的hiddenstates加权平均，做为后续Layer计算的输入。计算步骤可参考下方公式。 $$ ei =\frac{1}{(N-1)K + 1}\left(E0(ti)+\sum{n=2}^{N}\sum{k=1}^{K}W{n,k}E{n,k}\left(H{n,k}(t{i-n+1}, \ldots, ti)\right)\right) $$ Ngram的哈希计算参考下方公式，其中$\mathrm{ti}$指代Token, $\mathrm{V}$指代哈希参数。 $$ \mathrm{H{nk}} = (\mathrm{\sum{j=0}^{n-1}} \mathrm{t{i-j}} \mathrm{V{k}^j} ) \% \mathrm{Vn} $$ MTP投机推理 LongCat-2.0依然提供了原生的Multi-Token Prediction(MTP)机制。MTP机制允许在一次主模型推理过程中同时计算验证多个Token，在未达到计算瓶颈前，可以通过较少的时延增加，有机会获得更多的输出Token，从而降低单Token的平均推理耗时。LongCat-2.0由于采用了新的3S DSA结构，MTP加速相对于LongCat-Flash会更复杂。 Full Attention场景下，开启MTP几乎不会增加MLA的KV Cache的搬运量，因此MTP能够提高计算访存比，从而提高算力利用率。而对于Sparse Flash Attention算子，每个qtoken都会选择topk=2048组KV，极端情况下mtptoken选择的KV与maintoken不重合，反而增加了离散访存的代价。 在长序列场景中Lightning Indexer算子耗时长于SFA算子，其需要的K Cache搬运与稠密MLA相似，可以利用MTP机制提高计算访存比。同时由于DSA稀疏计算显著降低了长序列Attention的计算量，而剩下的算子（如Matmul等）都能在使能MTP后达到更好的计算访存比，因此使用MTP对整个推理有比较可观的加速。 本次开源的实践支持了MTP 3，在每次推理Step，MTP模型额外推理三次，有效降低平均每Token的推理时延。 融合算子 Attention AllToAll方案进行了针对性优化，将节点间低带宽通信的范围限制在进行topk=12扩展前的原始Token（模型此处每个Token对应一个hiddenstates，本节使用Token指代）。新方案步骤如下。 在进行MOE计算前，在不同节点间，localrankid相同的卡间做allgather汇集Token，使得每个节点内都有全部的Token。 对汇集后的Token做topkgating后，再在各自节点内做EP域的alltoall通信和专家计算。每个节点内只有局部的专家。 在MOE计算完成后，在不同节点间，localrankid相同的卡间做reducescatter，汇聚不同节点的专家信息，并返还各自Token。 通过在进行torch.compile时指定backend使用静态图gegraph可以削减Decode阶段的算子下发开销，获得更好的推理性能。GE是CANN平台的图模式实现，对标的是Torch-TensorRT，其核心优势在于对静态计算图的编译优化。即代码不会立即执行，而是先将所有计算步骤（操作、变量依赖）定义为一个“静态的计算图”（类似流程图），然后由框架对整个图进行优化（如算子融合、内存规划），最后再将优化后的图提交给NPU执行。 使能图编译缓存 torch.compile是一种即时编译器（Just-In-Time compiler），成图首次编译时间通常较长，在时延敏感的模型推理场景下，使能图编译缓存可以缓存编译后的静态图，有效缩短服务启动后的首次推理时延，从而提高推理性能。可参考下方示例，配置完缓存路径后，下次编译时会默认从配置路径下加载，无额外调用动作。 python if self.enablecachecompile: casename = "compilecache/" + os.getenv("CASENAME") cachemodel = self.model.decode if self.ismtp: casename += "spec" cachemodel = self.model.mtpcompiledecode cachedir = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(file)), casename) self.model.decode = tng.inference.cachecompile(cachemodel, cachedir=cachedir, config=compilerconfig, dynamic=False, fullgraph=True, gecache=True) 主模型缓存默认路径为./compilecache/CASENAME，mtp模型缓存默认路径为./compilecache/CASENAMEspec。 多流并行与控核 大模型推理场景下，对于一些可并行的场景，可以划分多个stream做并行计算，多个stream上的计算形成overlap，从而降低整体计算耗时。多流并行技术的详细介绍，请参考 官方文档 多流场景下，会出现所有核（Core）都被一个流占用的情况，导致算子执行并行度降低，因此需要把核分给不同的流用，从而保证算子并行执行的收益。控核技术的详细介绍，请参考 官方文档 原始的 LongCat-Flash模型 在论文中提供了四阶段的并行策略，其方案图如下所示。 我们对并行策略进行了调整，调整后的多流并行和控核方案图如下所示。将第二段Attention和FFN专家提前执行，并通过控制多流上的Cube核和Vector核数量，使得双流的计算时间接近，无明显拖尾，提升性能。其中Stage1不做控核，默认占用全部的Cube核和Vector核，Stage2里的stream0和stream1都采用c12v24控核方案。 实现多流并行和控核可以参考以下伪代码。 python attn layernorm with npustreamswitch(True, "1"): with limitcorenum(True, "12", "24"): router dispatch gmm combine with limitcorenum(True, "12", "24"): dense attn layernorm dense 权重预取 该优化提供网络Weight预取功能，在前序算子计算的同时，利用空闲的带宽，提前将一些访存Bound算子的权重从HBM搬运到L2 Cache中，提升算子性能。npuprefetch技术的详细介绍，请参考 官方文档 。 以下图为例，Matmul的权重有20 MB，前序的算子RmsNorm对内存带宽的需求较小，执行时间为10us，此时可以通过预取技术，将Matmul的权重提前写入到L2 Cache中，理想情况下，最大可预取的大小为 HBMbandwidth timeavailable，实际可预取大小因网络与前序算子对带宽的占用程度而异。假设此时可预取的大小为10 MB，与RmsNorm并行执行，则在Matmul算子执行时，只需要再额外读10 MB权重，访存的耗时开销减少明显。 可以通过Profiling分析预取的大小和位置是否合理.如果与预取并行的算子性能有明显劣化，则需要进一步调整预取的位置（可以将预取的位置提前开始，或与劣化算子错开），如没有可调整的位置，则需要减少预取的大小使得并行算子尽量不劣化。如果想要获取最大化的预取收益，可以通过实验对比调整。如果前序算子是访存密集型，如Matmul等，则不适合并行，避免带宽抢占导致劣化。 预取分析和调试的通用流程如下： NPU LongCat-2.0 Inference Optimization Meituan released the latest LongCat-2.0 model. Architecturally, it adds Sink Sliding Window Attention and DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA) to the ShortCut MOE (SC-MOE) architecture of LongCat-Flash, while supporting Over Embedding and the zero-expert mechanism. These features substantially improve the model's ability to process ultra-long contexts. The related team supported service deployment of LongCat-2.0 on Ascend Atlas A2 in the LongCat-2.0 NPU Inference (Chinese) practice, providing high-performance inference for sequences up to 1M. In model scale, compared with the previously released LongCat-Flash, LongCat-2.0 increases the number of layers from 28 to 38, the number of routed experts from 512 to 768, and the hidden dimension from 6144 to 8192, while the model parameter count still reaches 1.6T. Even with native Int8 quantization in the MOE component, memory usage remains as high as 2.1 TB. The improved model capabilities introduce new challenges for inference deployment and performance optimization, which this practice addresses with targeted optimizations. The LongCat inference team uses mature PD-disaggregated deployment, with 64 cards for Prefill and 128 cards for Decode. Both support Context Parallel (CP), while hierarchical Cache transfer between PD releases the memory pressure introduced by many experts and ultra-long sequences. Prefill uses a targeted design that combines Pipeline Parallel (PP) and CP. Decode uses MC2 Dispatch/Combine operators with a fused zero-expert optimization pipeline and overlaps them with the MLP through multi-stream scheduling, reducing the communication overhead of large-instance deployment. At the model execution layer, enabling fused operators such as Lightning Indexer, MlaProlog, and Sparse Flash Attention, together with multi-stream scheduling and the GE static graph, substantially reduces scheduling overhead and unlocks Ascend compute power. Each Layer contains two rounds of Attention and FFN computation, and the number of MOE experts is further increased. It contains 768 routed experts and 128 zero experts. Each token activates 12 experts at a time, averaging eight routed experts and four zero experts. In this open-source LongCat-2.0 practice, the MOE and MLP components natively use Int8 quantization, effectively reducing model storage overhead and improving computation efficiency compared with Bfloat16. ModuleNumber of ExpertsIntermediate SizeActivated Parameters per ExpertBF16 Weight SizeInt8 Weight SizeActivated Weight Size per Token ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- MLP112288288M42.8GB21.4GB21.3GB MOE768204848M2.67TB1.34TB14.3GB Attention Sparsity and Sliding Window LongCat-2.0 enables the DSA sparse architecture . Before Attention computation, Lightning Indexer selects topk=2048 KV groups for each token, substantially reducing Attention computation time. In the SC-MOE architecture, the two Sparse Flash Attention (SFA) operations in each layer share one set of topkindices. According to the DSA computation analysis , both Prefill and Decode in this open-source practice use absorb mode, which is favorable for DSA performance. On top of DSA, LongCat-2.0 additionally uses the Sink Sliding Window (3S) design. Among the reserved topk=2048 KV groups, it always selects init 16, the first 16 KV groups along the sequence dimension corresponding to sink, and local 1024, the last 1024 KV groups corresponding to slidingwindow. It then selects top 1008 KV groups from the middle section, further improving model capabilities. The following figure shows an example of how 3S LI filters KV Pairs. Over Embedding LongCat-2.0 supports Over Embedding based on the Meituan technical report. It slightly increases computation in the Embedding stage at the start of inference to improve model quality. The following figure shows the OE computation steps. Each token is computed with the preceding oen - 1 token to obtain (oen - 1) n-gram containing preceding Token information, after which Ngram Embedding is performed on each. Ngram Embedding computation is divided into oek subtables, each with its own Embedding and Projection. Increasing the number of subtables reduces the probability that different n-gram map to the same row in the vocabulary and increases the freedom of n-gram representation. From the computation-flow perspective, OE computation uses oek subtables and hashes each token with its preceding oen - 1 token to obtain (oen - 1) oek oetoken. OE Embedding and OE Projection are then performed on the oetoken. Finally, the resulting oehiddenstates and the hiddenstates from the original Embedding computation are averaged with weights and used as the input to subsequent Layer computation. See the following formula for the computation steps. $$ ei =\frac{1}{(N-1)K + 1}\left(E0(ti)+\sum{n=2}^{N}\sum{k=1}^{K}W{n,k}E{n,k}\left(H{n,k}(t{i-n+1}, \ldots, ti)\right)\right) $$ The following formula shows the Ngram hash computation, where $\mathrm{ti}$ indicates a Token and $\mathrm{V}$ indicates a hash parameter. $$ \mathrm{H{nk}} = (\mathrm{\sum{j=0}^{n-1}} \mathrm{t{i-j}} \mathrm{V{k}^j} ) \% \mathrm{Vn} $$ MTP Speculative Inference LongCat-2.0 continues to provide a native Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) mechanism. MTP allows multiple Tokens to be computed and verified simultaneously during one main-model inference operation. Before reaching the computation bottleneck, a small latency increase can potentially produce more output Tokens, reducing the average inference time per Token. Because LongCat-2.0 uses the new 3S DSA architecture, MTP acceleration is more complex than in LongCat-Flash. In Full Attention scenarios, enabling MTP barely increases MLA KV Cache movement, so MTP can improve the compute-to-memory-access ratio and compute utilization. For the Sparse Flash Attention operator, each qtoken selects topk=2048 KV groups. In the extreme case, the KV selected by mtptoken does not overlap with the KV selected by maintoken, increasing the cost of discrete memory access instead. In long-sequence scenarios, the Lightning Indexer operator takes longer than the SFA operator. Its required K Cache movement is similar to dense MLA, so the MTP mechanism can improve the compute-to-memory-access ratio. DSA sparse computation substantially reduces long-sequence Attention computation, while the remaining operators, such as Matmul, achieve a better compute-to-memory-access ratio after MTP is enabled. Therefore, MTP provides considerable acceleration for the entire inference process. This open-source practice supports MTP 3. In each inference Step, the MTP model performs three additional inference operations, effectively reducing the average inference latency per Token. Fused Operators Attention As shown in the following figure, the DSA computation process consists of MLAProlog, IndexerProlog, Lightning Indexer, Sparse Flash Attention, and MLAEpilog. Note: Because of space limitations, the figure appropriately simplifies model information and does not show MLP/MOE or the second Attention computation group. Lightning Indexer: Includes operations such as Score Batchmatmul, ReLU, ReduceSum, and TopK. In long-sequence scenarios, TopK becomes a bottleneck. Pipeline the TopK computation time to mask the time of other operations and obtain computation-pipeline benefits. Sparse Flash Attention: Selects TopK-related Tokens from the complete KVCache and performs sparse Flash Attention. The main bottleneck is discrete gather memory access. Use this time to mask other operations and accelerate them through pipeline parallelism. MLAProlog and IndexerProlog: Include operations such as Q/KV LoRA, RoPE, Norm, and KVCache update, providing substantial space for Cube/Vector parallel pipelines. MLAEpilog: Includes Oproj and V dimension expansion. In this open-source sample, MLAProlog, Lightning Indexer, and Sparse Flash Attention use NPU fused operators to improve computation performance. The following operators are open-sourced in the CANN/ops-transformer repository: lightningindexer and its quantized version quantlightningindexer , and sparseflashattention and its quantized version kvquantsparseflashattention . MOE Because the MOE component of LongCat-series networks includes special zero experts, the moedistributecombine operator used by Decode supports the zero-expert feature. It can use the pipeline inside the fused operator to mask zero-expert computation time and improve MOE performance. Over Embedding This open-source practice implements two fused operators for the Over Embedding feature of LongCat-2.0 to improve computation efficiency in key steps. Update Token Table: Over Embedding needs to hash the current token with preceding token. To quickly obtain historical token information during Decode, all historical token are maintained in a Token Table data structure. When a new request is input or a new token is derived or accepted, the new token information must be written to the Token Table. For discrete update operations in multi-request scenarios, this practice implements the updatetokentable operator, which efficiently writes token from multiple requests to specified positions in the Token Table. Compute N-Gram Ids: During Embedding computation in each Step, each token must be hashed with its preceding (oen - 1) token for the oek subtables to generate new oetoken. This generates (oen - 1) oek oetoken for each token as the input to subsequent OE Embedding computation. The computengramids operator implemented in this practice generates these oetoken. For the computation flow, see OE parallelism . The related operator implementations are open-sourced in LongCat-2.0 NPU Inference (Chinese). Deployment Strategy This open-source release is a PD-disaggregated serving framework sample. Prefill is deployed on 64 Atlas A2 cards, and Decode is deployed on 128 Atlas A2 cards. Prefill LongCat-2.0 has up to 1.6T parameters, occupies more than 2 TB of memory during inference, and supports long-sequence requests of 1M through features such as 3S DSA. The Prefill stage therefore has a high risk of device memory OOM, while TTFT also presents a major challenge during inference-service deployment. Optimizing memory usage and TTFT is therefore the primary goal of the parallel strategy. This open-source practice uses Context Parallel Pipeline deployment, dividing 64 Atlas A2 cards into m x n groups. Pipeline parallelism is applied along dimension m, and Context Parallel (CP) is applied along dimension n. The preceding figure shows Pipeline parallelism, which partitions the model by Layer for parallel execution. Note: Because of space limitations, the figure appropriately simplifies model information and does not show MLP/MOE or the second Attention computation group. As shown in the preceding figure, CP partitions input requests in parallel along the sequence dimension. Before Indexer and SFA computation, perform allgather communication for the Indexer Key Cache and KV Cache, respectively. During LI and SFA computation, each rank has part of q and the complete Cache. MLA Naive Vs Absorb In the Prefill stage, using 1 Batch 64K inference as an example, Lightning Indexer selects TopK=2048 kvtoken for each qtoken. The MLA computation flow has three options: Solution 1: MLA Naive + Sparse Mask. Prefill MLA uses Naive mode. Each qtoken computes Attention with all historical kvtoken, and an Attention Mask filters out token outside TopK only before softmax. The two batchmatmul Shapes in Attention are as follows: Solution 1 Batch M K N :---------: :---: :--: :--: :--: BMM1(QK^T) 1128 64K 192 64K BMM2(PV) 1128 64K 64K 128 This solution has the same computation volume as the original Full Attention but cannot obtain DSA sparse-computation benefits, resulting in poor performance in long-sequence scenarios. Solution 2: MLA Naive + Sparse Attention. Prefill MLA uses Naive mode, and each qtoken computes Attention with TopK=2048 kvtoken. Because each qtoken independently selects the 2048 KV groups to compute, the 64K sequence length must be moved to the Batch axis, and the M-axis size is 1. Solution 2 Batch M K N :---------: :--------: :--: :--: :--: BMM1(QK^T) 1\64K128 1 192 2048 BMM2(PV) 1\64K128 1 2048 128 Solution 2 has a smaller BMM computation volume, reduced to 2048/64K=1/32 of the original Full Attention computation volume, but has the following problems: The BMM M axis is 1, resulting in low matrix-multiplication efficiency. Compared with the original Full Attention, BMM increases HBM access to kv by topk=2048 times, causing a memory-access bottleneck. Solution 3: MLA Absorb + Sparse Attention. Prefill MLA uses Absorb mode, consistent with Decode. Similarly, each qtoken computes Attention with TopK=2048 kvtoken. Solution 3 Batch M K N :---------: :----: :--: :--: :--: BMM1(QK^T) 1\64K 128 576 2048 BMM2(PV) 1\64K 128 2048 512 The comparison between Solution 3 and Solution 2 is as follows: Solution 3 increases computation by approximately three times, reflected in the K axis of BMM1 and the N axis of BMM2. However, its BMM M axis is 128, which is more suitable for matrix multiplication. Solution 3 benefits from reduced memory access in Absorb mode compared with Naive mode. KV HBM access is tens of times lower than in Solution 2, resulting in less execution time. Considering computation and memory-access time and long-sequence application scenarios, this practice selects Solution 3, MLA Absorb + Sparse Attention, for Prefill deployment, unifying the MLA computation flows of Prefill and Decode. Decode LongCat-2.0 3S DSA uses Lightning Indexer to select topk=2048 KV groups for each token, so subsequent SFA computation is no longer the bottleneck. In long-sequence scenarios, the Lightning Indexer (LI) operator becomes the new computation bottleneck. Under Decode DP, different requests in real-world business scenarios have different sequence lengths. KV must be partitioned in parallel to effectively balance the LI computation load among Ranks. Therefore, this open-source practice uses KV Parallel deployment, storing the Indexer Key Cache and KV Cache of different requests on different rank. Each rank computes with complete q and part of the Cache, and allgather then aggregates the computation results. The following figure shows the complete computation flow. Note: Because of space limitations, the figure appropriately simplifies model information and does not show MLP/MOE or the second Attention computation group. MOE Because intra-node communication bandwidth in an Atlas A2 cluster is higher than inter-node bandwidth, this practice specifically optimizes the conventional Attention DP - AllToAll - MOE EP - AllToAll solution. It limits low-bandwidth inter-node communication to the original Tokens before topk=12 expansion. At this point in the model, each Token corresponds to one hiddenstates; this section uses Token to refer to it. The new solution consists of the following steps. Before MOE computation, perform allgather among cards with the same localrankid on different nodes to aggregate Tokens, so each node contains all Tokens. After topkgating is performed on the aggregated Tokens, perform EP-domain alltoall communication and expert computation within each node. Each node contains only local experts. After MOE computation, perform reducescatter among cards with the same localrankid on different nodes to aggregate expert information from different nodes and return each Token. Assume that four Ranks form a complete EP domain and each Rank deploys one expert. rank1 and rank2 are on one node, while rank3 and rank4 are on another node. The following figure shows an example of the communication and computation flow. Note: Because of space limitations, the figure appropriately simplifies the model information and computation flow. Over Embedding To reduce the memory occupied by the Over Embedding Table, Over Embedding computation uses TP, while other computations are not parallelized. Therefore, after the computengramids operator produces oetoken, perform allgather to aggregate the oetoken from all DP Ranks. Because the Over Embedding weights are partitioned into TP parts, after Over Embedding computation, perform reducescatter on oehiddenstates to aggregate Over Embedding information and restore the DP distribution of requests. Using oen=5, oek=4, and ngram=(oen - 1) oek=16 as an example, the computation flow is as follows. Performance Optimization Enable Graph Mode Specifying the static graph gegraph as the backend for torch.compile reduces operator delivery overhead in the Decode stage and improves inference performance. GE is the graph-mode implementation of the CANN platform and corresponds to Torch-TensorRT. Its core advantage is compilation optimization of static computation graphs. Code is not executed immediately. Instead, all computation steps, including operations and variable dependencies, are first defined as a static computation graph, similar to a flowchart. The framework then optimizes the complete graph, such as through operator fusion and memory planning, and finally submits the optimized graph to the NPU for execution. Enable the Graph Compilation Cache torch.compile is a Just-In-Time compiler. Initial graph compilation usually takes a long time. In latency-sensitive model inference scenarios, enabling the graph compilation cache stores compiled static graphs and effectively reduces the latency of the first inference operation after service startup, improving inference performance. In the following example, after the cache path is configured, subsequent compilation loads from the configured path by default without additional calls. python if self.enablecachecompile: casename = "compilecache/" + os.getenv("CASENAME") cachemodel = self.model.decode if self.ismtp: casename += "spec" cachemodel = self.model.mtpcompiledecode cachedir = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(file)), casename) self.model.decode = tng.inference.cachecompile(cachemodel, cachedir=cachedir, config=compilerconfig, dynamic=False, fullgraph=True, gecache=True) The default cache path of the main model is ./compilecache/CASENAME, and the default cache path of the mtp model is ./compilecache/CASENAMEspec. Multi-Stream Parallelism and Core Control In large-model inference scenarios, divide parallelizable scenarios into multiple streams for parallel computation. Computations on multiple streams overlap, reducing overall execution time. For details about multi-stream parallelism, see the official documentation (Chinese). In multi-stream scenarios, one stream may occupy all Cores, reducing operator execution parallelism. Therefore, allocate cores to different streams to ensure the benefits of parallel operator execution. For details about core control, see the official documentation (Chinese). The original LongCat-Flash model paper provides a four-stage parallel strategy, shown in the following figure. We adjusted the parallel strategy. The following figure shows the adjusted multi-stream parallelism and core-control solution. Execute the second Attention and FFN experts earlier and control the number of Cube and Vector cores on multiple streams so the execution times of the two streams are close, with no significant tail, improving performance. Stage1 does not use core control and occupies all Cube and Vector cores by default. In Stage2, both stream0 and stream1 use the c12v24 core-control solution. See the following pseudocode for implementing multi-stream parallelism and core control. python attn layernorm with npustreamswitch(True, "1"): with limitcorenum(True, "12", "24"): router dispatch gmm combine with limitcorenum(True, "12", "24"): dense attn layernorm dense Weight Prefetch This optimization provides network Weight prefetch. While preceding operators compute, it uses idle bandwidth to move the weights of some memory-Bound operators from HBM to L2 Cache in advance, improving operator performance. For details about npuprefetch, see the official documentation (Chinese). In the following example, Matmul weights are 20 MB. The preceding RmsNorm operator has a low memory-bandwidth requirement and executes for 10 us. Prefetch can write the Matmul weights to L2 Cache in advance. Ideally, the maximum prefetch size is HBMbandwidth timeavailable. The actual prefetch size varies with the bandwidth used by the network and preceding operators. Assume that 10 MB can be prefetched and executes in parallel with RmsNorm. When the Matmul operator executes, it only needs to additionally read 10 MB of weights, substantially reducing memory-access time. Use Profiling to analyze whether the prefetch size and position are appropriate. If the performance of an operator running in parallel with prefetch degrades significantly, further adjust the prefetch position by starting prefetch earlier or moving it away from the degraded operator. If the position cannot be adjusted, reduce the prefetch size so that the parallel operator degrades as little as possible. To maximize prefetch benefits, adjust the configuration through comparative experiments. If the preceding operator is memory-intensive, such as Matmul, parallel execution is unsuitable because bandwidth contention may cause degradation. 基于Atlas A3集群的LongCat-Flash模型推理性能优化实践 概述 本文主要介绍基于Atlas A3系列产品的LongCat-Flash模型的优化方式。 性能优化 通用优化 LongCat-Flash结构中的与Llama类似的部分，可参考通用优化点 Llama 的改动，如固定KV Cache大小、cos/sin优化、AddRMSNorm融合等。 使能图模式 使用静态图可以获得更好的推理性能。LongCat-Flash使用推理框架的图编译流程，在 modelworker.py 的ModelWorker.compilemodel中触发，并调用 graphutils.py 中的compilemodelforward完成编译。 执行模式通过YAML中modelconfig.exemode配置，当前支持eager、gegraph和npugraphex。其中gegraph和npugraphex会在Decode阶段使用编译后的model.forward，Prefill阶段按eager模式执行。 使能图编译缓存 torch.compile是一种即时编译器（Just-In-Time compiler），成图首次编译时间通常较长，在时延敏感的模型推理场景下，使能图编译缓存可以缓存编译后的静态图，有效缩短服务启动后的首次推理时延，从而提高推理性能。当前编译入口如下： python self.modelcompiled = compilemodelforward( self.model.forward, exemode=self.exemode, enablecachecompile=self.enablecachecompile, cachedir=os.path.join(self.inferconfig.modelconfig.outputpath, "cachecompile"), enablestatickernel=self.enablestatickernel, ) 图编译缓存通过YAML中modelconfig.enablecachecompile开关使能，缓存目录为modelconfig.outputpath/cachecompile。gegraph模式下使用torchair.inference.cachecompile，npugraphex模式下使用torch.npu.npugraphex.inference.cachecompile；npugraphex还可通过modelconfig.enablestatickernel使能静态kernel编译。 多流并行与控核 大模型推理场景下，对于一些可并行的场景，可以划分多个stream做并行计算，多个stream上的计算形成overlap，从而降低整体计算耗时。多流并行技术的详细介绍，请参考 官方文档 多流场景下，会出现所有核（Core）都被一个流占用的情况，导致算子执行并行度降低，因此需要把核分给不同的流用，从而保证算子并行执行的收益。控核技术的详细介绍，请参考 官方文档 原始的 LongCat-Flash模型 在论文中提供了四阶段的并行策略，其方案图如下所示。 我们对并行策略进行了调整，调整后的多流并行和控核方案图如下所示。将第二段attention和FFN专家提前执行，并通过控制多流上的ai core和vector core核数，使得双流的计算时间接近，无明显拖尾，提升性能。其中stage1不做控核，默认占用全部的ai core和vector core核数，stage2里的stream0采用c16v32控核方案，stream1采用c8v16。 当前代码中通过modelconfig.customparams.enablemultistreams控制该优化：0表示关闭，1表示采用上述非对称控核方案，2表示stream0和stream1均采用c12v24方案。该优化只在Decode阶段生效，且不支持exemode: eager。 实现多流并行和控核可以参考以下伪代码。 python attn layernorm with npustreamswitch(True, "1"): with limitcorenum(True, "8", "16"): router dispatch gmm combine with limitcorenum(True, "16", "32"): dense attn layernorm dense 权重预取 该优化提供网络weight预取功能，在算子计算的同时，利用空闲的带宽，提前将一些访存bound算子的权重从HBM搬运到L2 Cache中，提升算子性能。npuprefetch技术的详细介绍，请参考 官方文档 。npuprefetch优化功能可通过modelconfig.customparams.enableprefetch开关使能；当前LongCat-Flash中该开关依赖多流优化，需要同时设置enablemultistreams > 0。 以下图为例，Matmul的权重有20 MB，前序的算子RmsNorm对内存带宽的需求较小，执行时间为10us，此时可以通过预取技术，将Matmul的权重提前写入到L2 Cache中，理想情况下，最大可预取的大小为 HBMbandwidth / timeavailable，实际可预取大小因网络与前序算子对带宽的占用程度而异。假设此时可预取的大小为10 MB，与RmsNorm并行执行，则在Matmul算子执行时，只需要再额外读10 MB权重，访存的耗时开销减少明显。 判断预取的大小和位置是否合理，可以通过profiling分析，如果与预取并行的算子性能有明显劣化，则需要进一步调整预取的位置（可以将预取的位置提前开始，或与劣化算子错开），如没有可调整的位置，则需要减少预取的大小使得并行算子尽量不劣化。如果想要获取最大化的预取收益，可以通过实验对比调整。如果前序算子是访存密集型，如Matmul等，则不适合并行，避免带宽抢占导致劣化。 预取分析和调试的通用流程如下： npufusedinferattentionscore 融合kernel，实现对MLA计算的加速。 oproj Tensor Parallelism K轴切分 对线性层oproj进行行切分处理，oproj的输入维度为numheads vheaddim，输出维度为hiddensize。在进行oproj TP时，将这一输入维度按照oprojtpsize进行切分，要求numheads vheaddim能被oprojtpsize整除，每个rank上只保存一部分输入通道对应的权重。在推理过程中，attnoutput先经过alltoall，使得每个rank只拿到自己负责的那一段输入特征，然后每个rank对局部张量执行线性层变换，得到局部输出，最后通过reducescatter对各rank的局部输出按元素求和，并在batch维度切分，得到各rank的输出。 MoE (Mixture of Experts)模块实现Expert Parallel (EP)及使能融合算子 MoE计算阶段采用EP (Expert Parallelism)切分策略，将路由专家和零计算专家均匀分布到每张卡上。当前实现位于 modelinglongcatflash.py 的LongcatFlashMoE；AFD场景下FFN侧独立模型位于 ffn.py ，并在框架中注册为longcatflashffn。 Router使能融合算子 使用 torchnpu.npumoegatingtopk 算子，对router计算的结果排序，并选取前top-k个专家。 Prefill阶段优化 Prefill阶段路由专家采用Double-Routing的计算策略完成计算,具体计算步骤可参见 基于Atlas A3集群的DeepSeek-R1模型prefill阶段推理性能优化实践 的MoE部署策略优化章节。 Decode阶段优化 高性能专家计算：使用 torchnpu.npugroupedmatmul 算子，可以同时处理多个专家的计算，提高计算和搬运效率； 多卡间高性能通信路由：使能 torchnpu.npumoedistributedispatchv2 和 torchnpu.npumoedistributecombinev2 算子，实现EP并行下多卡间的通信。通过传入参数copyexpertnum使能dispatchv2和combinev2算子支持零专家处理，计算公式为：MoE(orix) = orix。在使用前可参考上述的算子文档，检查HCCLBUFFSIZE等环境变量的配置是否合理，了解该算子的使用场景和约束。 MLP线性层优化 MLP线性层计算合并 原始LongCatFlashMLP实现中，存在gateproj、upproj与downproj三个matmul运算，可通过将gateproj与upproj进行合并计算，得到gateupproj提升整体计算效率。 MLP线性层TP切分 在MLP的计算中，gateupproj和downproj需要全量存储到每一个device上，造成device内存压力，本优化将gateupproj沿N轴切分、downproj沿K轴切分到densetp域内的不同device上，以完成MLP线性层的TP切分，降低单个device的内存使用，并减少matmul矩阵运算时的权重搬运开销。需要注意的是，MLP阶段采用TP切分，但前后的Attention模块采用的是DP切分，在MLP计算前后需要分别进行AllGather和ReduceScatter，完成DP -> TP -> DP的并行方式转化。虽然有额外的通信开销，但整体具有较好的性能收益。在当前的优化实践中，Dense FFN专家采用TP8切分。 支持Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) 实现了MTP投机推理，在未达到计算bound的场景下，MTP计算可以实现较好的推理加速效果。可通过YAML中modelconfig.nextn参数使能MTP。框架会在nextn > 0时加载LongcatFlashModelMTP并由 mtpworker.py 执行投机推理流程。当前支持MTP1和MTP2。 Attention-FFN Disaggregation(AFD)优化 优化出发点 在非分离场景中，Attention 模块和 MoE 模块部署在同一个卡上，由于 ScMoE 结构的固有特性，为了获取最佳的性能，在 多流并行与控核 小节中对 Stage2 设计了多流并行策略，通过分配不同的核数将 Attention 计算流和 MoE 计算流进行了并行流水，达到最佳性能。 然而，对 Stage2 通过控核后，由于两条计算流在计算时只能使用部分 Cube 和 Vector 核，算子执行时会受到算力的约束。在 Atlas A3 环境上实测对比发现，在不控核情况下，MLAProlog/FA/MM/TBMM/QBMM算子耗时相比控核时均有所下降，耗时对比如下表格。 CubeVector核数 MLAProlog (μs) FA (μs) MM (μs) TBMM (μs) QBMM1 (μs) QBMM2 (μs) 12C24V 68.1 118 18 19.6 18.7 20.1 24C48V 45.2 91.8 14.2 12.5 14.6 16.3 以上数据除了核数不同，其他都在相同的配置情况下从整网中采集拆解得到的。 根据以上分析，针对 LongCat-Flash-560B 模型，为了在 Decode 阶段进一步降低 TPOT 耗时，可采用 Attention-FFN Disaggregation(AFD) 技术方案，它将 MoE 模块从整网中剥离出来进行独立部署，也即 Attention 模块 和 MoE 模块单独部署在不同的节点上，中间通过 Send/Recv 算子进行节点间的数据交互。AFD通过modelconfig.customparams.enableafd使能，框架会将worldsize一分为二：低半区rank加载longcatflashffn，高半区rank加载longcatflash主模型，二者通过dist.send/dist.recv完成Attention侧和FFN侧的数据交互。使能
