DeepSeek-V3网络的MoE结构计算路由专家与共享专家的激活值，其中，路由专家的权重被EP切分，需要在GroupedMatmul计算前后做卡间的AlltoAll通信（由MC2算子实现）；共享专家权重被TP切分，需要在Matmul计算后做卡间AllReduce通信，且路由专家与共享专家的计算无数据依赖关系。 在vLLM Ascend的原生实现中，共享专家计算和路由专家计算串行执行，对应如下图所示的Profiling，可见其在计算与通信的编排上存在以下两个问题： MC2算子（同时包含通信与Vector计算）执行时，Cube运算单元闲置。 共享专家计算耗时较短，但其后AllReduce操作与MC2并发，导致通信带宽抢占。 MLA多流-CV并行 与MoE结构类似，DeepSeek-V3网络的MLA结构中亦存在部分无数据依赖的计算步骤。原生vLLM Ascend的实现未考虑这一特点，将所有算子串行执行，因而存在进一步的优化空间。 6.2.2 优化方案 针对MoE部分，本实践基于TorchAir的多流能力将共享专家的计算拆分到并行的计算流上作重新排布。将共享专家的"gate\up\proj"矩阵运算与路由专家的"dispatch"通信算子并行，共享专家的"down\proj"矩阵运算与路由专家的"combine"通信算子并行，通过通算并行的方式优化Decode耗时。 moeoptimization1 同时，为了避免共享专家"down\proj"计算结束后的AllReduce通信拖尾，本实践额外通过保存共享专家冗余权重的方式消除张量并行带来的AllReduce通信。由于共享专家本身矩阵运算规模较小，即使不做TP切分也可以被MC2算子基本掩盖，获得进一步的性能收益。 类似地，针对MLA部分，同样可以经过一定的流水排布将无数据依赖的Cube与Vector计算作多流并行执行，提升Decode性能。 为了突破单设备内存限制，本实践推理阶段针对MLA层与MoE层分别使用TP和EP切分，将DeepSeek-V3完整模型拆分到多个设备运行。在vLLM Ascend的原生实现中，MLA层通过AllReduce完成张量并行场景下的数据汇聚，MoE层通过Split算子从中取出本卡需要的数据完成TP切分到EP切分的转化，此处AllReduce + Split的组合引入了通信量和计算量的双重冗余。 6.3.2 优化方案 本实践采用零冗余的TP转EP的通信方案，在Decode阶段将MLA层的AllReduce算子替换为ReduceScatter算子，使MoE层仅接收本卡计算所必需的数据，并将MoE层末尾的AllGather通信移至MLA层，保证原本的TP切分逻辑的正确性。由于AllReduce算子的通信量与ReduceScatter与AllGather算子的通信量之和相当，从而本方案在MLA层整体通信量保持不变的前提下，消除了MoE部分原本的AllGather通信与Split算子。 6.3.3 优化效果 开启零冗余TP转EP通信优化后，MoE层内的StridedSlice和AllGather算子被消除。另一方面，MoE层通信的减少还进一步缓解了卡间通信不均衡问题，最终推理TPOT优化2ms以上，Decode吞吐提升超过3%。 6.4 KVCache支持NZ 6.4.1 现象分析 NZ是NPU上的一种特殊的私有数据格式，如下图所示，其将完整数据划分为数据块，并采取块之间列优先，块内行优先的内存排布方式。 在矩阵进行分块计算时，NZ格式可以使计算单元访问连续的数据内存，因而能够最大程度挖掘出NPU Cube 单元的性能。算子一般包含将数据格式转化为NZ的步骤，通过预先将KVCache按照NZ格式进行存储，可以消除FusedInferAttentionScore算子内部的格式转换阶段，并优化推理Decode阶段FA算子的性能。 6.4.2 优化方案 在Prefill与Decode阶段指定KvRmsNormRopeCache算子的cache\mode参数为"PA\NZ"，即可按照NZ格式存储KVCache。同时亦需要对KV作相关变换，以满足NZ格式场景下FA算子对输入参数shape及layout的约束。 6.4.3 优化结果 本实践在vLLM Ascend中torchair\graph\config下新增了用于控制KVCache NZ优化的配置项enable\kv
z。该优化的收益随序列长度上升而增长，具体结果如下图所示，序列长度为3K时Decode TPOT收益将超过1ms。 6.5 大EP的冗余算子消除 6.5.1 现象分析 冗余Transpose算子 DeepSeek-V3模型普遍使用大EP的推理部署方式，通过减少MoE部分参与GroupedMatmul计算的路由专家数量，以降低单次Decode耗时。然而，在分析EP256配置下的profiling时发现，GroupedMatmul算子执行前出现了额外的Transpose操作，导致性能反而出现较大劣化。 上图的profiling信息显示，单层MoE中的Transpose算子总耗时高达175us。经过模型代码排查、对比EP128无Transpose场景的dump图，发现问题由以下原因导致： 在EP256单卡1专家的配置下，由于专家权重shape中存在值为1的维度，导致针对权重的Transpose算子触发TorchAir的"enable\view\optimize"优化（详见 PyTorch图模式使用指导 > View类算子优化功能 ）而被插入了额外的Reshape算子。 新引入的Reshape算子使融合Pass "GroupedMatmulTransFusionPass"无法检测到其预定目标模式，最终导致Transpose算子被保留到图执行阶段。 冗余Cumsum算子 DeepSeek-V3网络的多路由专家计算由GroupedMatmul算子实现，该算子用于批量处理多个矩阵乘法操作，通过将具有相同或相似形状的矩阵乘法操作组合在一起，减少内存访问开销和计算资源的浪费，从而提高计算效率。对应的torch
pu接口“npu\grouped\matmul”依赖入参“group\list”获取每个子矩阵运算中实际M轴的大小，并支持以“累加和数列”或“逐维度指定”两种形式提供这一参数。vLLM Ascend的模型脚本中使用了“累加和数列”模式而非后者，因而在MoE层中引入了用于实现累加和的Cumsum算子。 实际上，这一累加过程是多余的，通过配置"npu\grouped\matmul"接口的"group\list	ype=1"参数可以将group\list按照"逐维度指定"的方式提供，从而省去Cumsum算子的开销。 6.5.2 优化方案 优化项"enable\view\optimize"在TorchAir中默认开启，目标是为了融合连续的view类算子。由于DeepSeek-V3网络不涉及这一目标场景，所以选择将其在"additional\config"配置中显式关闭，避免因此导致的Transpose/Gmm算子融合失败。 同时，修改vLLM Ascend的网络脚本，调整"npu\grouped\matmul"接口的"group\list	ype"配置，以消除原本的Cumsum操作。 6.5.3 优化效果 调整TorchAir的优化功能开关"enable\view\optimize"和torch
pu接口"npu\grouped\matmul"的配置后，MoE阶段关键路径上的Transpose/Cumsum算子即被消除。尽管GroupedMatmul算子耗时有所增加，仍能获得单层158us，整网9ms的Decode性能收益，在3K推理长度下可将rollout总耗时优化超过28s。 6.6 RL推理调度bound优化 6.6.1 现象分析 在对Decode模型侧进行较大性能优化之后，纯模型耗时在整体Rollout中的占比显著减低，这意味着如果仅仅优化纯模型的性能，后续在整体Rollout吞吐量的提升上面将面临较大局限。基于此，结合当时Rollout耗时373s（对应吞吐547 token/p/s）的数据，对整体RL推理过程进行了重新拆解与分析，结果如下： 上图中可以看到，Prefill和Decode的纯模型计算时间在RL推理的整体耗时占比已不足60%，其余40%耗时集中在Decode的前后处理、vLLM V1 Engine调度以及RL训推切换前权重内存卸载等调度操作上。为了进一步提升Rollout性能，需要从单纯关注模型性能优化转向优化此类推理场景下的“调度bound”问题。经过深入分析，得到如下结果： 1. vLLM Sche部分：耗时集中在调度前的全卡DP域间的EOS检测同步，通过CPU的AllReduce通信来获取"has\unfinishedequests"的结果，决定是否需要执行dummy atch。此CPU通信单次平均耗时10ms，推理3000次后叠加耗时高达30s。 2. DeepSeek-R1 Model RL Training Optimization Practice Based on the verl Frontend & A3 Cluster 1. Introduction 1.1 Background After the release of DeepSeek-R1, RL training of large models has received widespread attention. Major vendors and the open-source community have carried out extensive RL training practices, striving to build more efficient RL training systems. This article, based on the open-source verl framework, combined with the MindSpeed and vLLM Ascend frameworks, achieves high-throughput performance on Atlas A3 SuperPoD super-nodes through in-depth optimization and adaptation. The open-source frameworks involved in this article are shown in the following table. Framework Name Description ----- ---- verl Open-source LLM reinforcement learning framework that combines the advantages of single-controller (control flow) and multi-controller (computation flow), simplifying the implementation of RL algorithms (such as PPO, GRPO). Its training supports FSDP, FSDP2, and Megatron-LM, and its inference supports vLLM, SGLang, and Hugging Face Transformers. vLLM Open-source engine providing high-throughput and memory-efficient inference services for large language models, using PagedAttention technology to efficiently implement KV cache memory management and supporting numerous inference features. vLLM Ascend The Ascend NPU adaptation plugin for vLLM, supporting many optimizations on NPUs. Some optimizations from this practice were contributed to this open-source repository. Megatron-LM Ultra-large-scale language model training framework supporting multiple distributed parallel strategies. MindSpeed Large-model training acceleration library for NPUs, providing basic functionality adaptation of the Megatron-LM framework to NPUs as well as some NPU-affine optimization features. MindSpeed RL Reinforcement learning acceleration framework based on the Ascend ecosystem; this optimization practice draws some references from it. 1.2 Technology Path Selection 1.2.1 Why Choose Full Co-residency Deployment? Each training step of DeepSeek R1 can be roughly divided into three compute-intensive phases: inference generating complete Q&A data (rollout/generate) -> the reference model computing reference probability distributions (ref) -> the training model computing loss and performing backward updates (update). For DeepSeek R1, a large model with 671B parameters, all three phases require substantial computational resources. Therefore, deploying the three models — rollout/ref/update — on shared cards and time-sharing computational resources is a simple and efficient deployment strategy. In addition, for the rollout part we did not adopt the PD separation deployment strategy commonly used in inference (i.e., instantiating and deploying the Prefill phase and Decode phase on different machine resources separately), because the inference Prefill part accounts for only a small proportion of the time in the entire RL training, and the optimization benefit is not high. 1.2.2 Why Choose vLLM Ascend? vLLM Ascend decouples the framework from hardware dependencies through a hardware plugin mechanism. Users can deploy models on Ascend NPUs without modifying core code. The code is fully open source and continuously adapted for new features. Currently, vLLM Ascend already supports vLLM's V1 mode and has been optimized for DeepSeek R1's TorchAir graph mode, which is essential for optimizing the rollout part. 1.3 Overview of verl Adaptation and Optimization Practice ------------------------- We performed NPU adaptation on the verl open-source code and carried out some key performance optimizations. The core adaptations mainly include: Training engine: enable Megatron-LM through MindSpeed on NPUs to obtain better NPU training performance. Inference engine: adapt vLLM Ascend graph mode and large-EP inference; since the sleep feature is not yet supported in multi-machine scenarios, offload and onload, init\cache and free\cache need to be manually implemented. Framework Adaptation 2.1 verl + MindSpeed Adaptation The current verl version natively supports the MindSpeed training backend. Through the repatch mechanism embedded in the MegatronWorker initialization phase, it implements the conversion and parsing of verl configuration parameters to MindSpeed configuration parameters, as well as the replacement of MindSpeed's NPU-affine training implementations within Megatron-LM. Based on this mechanism, this practice configured MindSpeed's various functional and performance optimization features in the verl launch script, and completed functional verification of the DeepSeek-R1 model reinforcement learning training phase on the NPU environment. 2.2 verl + vLLM Ascend Adaptation This practice builds on the Ascend-affine adaptation of the DeepSeek R1 model structure performed by the vLLM community's vLLM Ascend project, achieving excellent performance. To make verl compatible with vLLM Ascend, this practice modified some interface parameters, with the modifications mainly concentrated in the vllm\rollout\spmd.py file used to initialize the vLLMRollout object. Performance Optimization: Inter-Model Scheduling 3.1 Slow Training Task Dispatch Problem --------------------- 3.1.1 Abnormal Communication Phenomenon on the Training Side During debugging, we found that the performance of the verl training side (compute\ref\log\prob, update\actor) was not as expected. Profiling of these two phases showed that the first communication on some cards took extremely long: the first communication of compute\ref\log\prob took about 50s+, and the first communication of update\actor took about 90s+. As shown in the figure below, in 256-Die training, the first communication time of card 0 in ref profiling is abnormal. 3.1.2 Excessive Start Time Differences of Training-Side Tasks We added detailed timestamps before and after generate\sequences, compute\ref\log\prob, and update\actor on each card, and observed that the end times of generate\sequences and compute\ref\log\prob are consistent across cards, but the start times of compute\ref\log\prob and update\actor are inconsistent across cards. The specific phenomenon is that card 0 always starts earliest, the last card starts latest, each card starts serially, and the maximum start time difference on the training side is very close to the time of the first extremely long communication in profiling. As shown in the figure below, in 256-Die training, the update start time difference between card 0 and card 255 can reach 96 seconds. 3.1.3 Analysis of verl Controller Logic At this point, we can conclude that the poor performance of the verl training side is due to significant time differences in task dispatch, which may be related to verl's controller logic. According to the func\generator function in base.py , after verl calls a task interface in the CPU-side main process, it actually executes the following 3 steps: dispatch\fn: the main process splits the held task input data into multiple parts along the batch dimension according to the task DP size. execute\fn: the main process dispatches tasks to each worker process. collect\fn: the main process collects the output results from each worker and concatenates them along the batch dimension into a complete result. dispatch\fn and collect\fn respectively perform the split of input tensors and the concat of output tensors, which in practice take very little time. Further analyzing execute\fn, which corresponds to the execute\all\async function in base.py , as shown in the figure below. The code logic here matches the previously observed phenomenon of each worker serially starting tasks. Adding timestamps before line 586 can confirm that it is the serial task dispatch that causes time differences in task start times across workers, which in turn leads to the poor performance exhibited on the training side. 3.1.4 Analysis Conclusion on the Performance Problem Ray dispatching a task to a worker involves at least three steps: input data serialization, data transmission, and output data serialization. Therefore, when the input tensor data volume of a task is large, the task dispatch time across many workers accumulates continuously, creating a training performance bottleneck. In addition, compared with training-side tasks, the dispatch time of the generate\sequences task is within one second, which also proves from the side that task dispatch time is related to data volume. As shown in the figure below, the gen input data volume is far smaller than the training-side input data volume, for several reasons: The DP used by gen when partitioning data in dispatch\fn equals the total number of cards (e.g., 256), far larger than the training-side DP size (e.g., 8). In GRPO training, the input batch\size of gen is not amplified by the n\sample multiplier. The input of gen is only the prompt, while the sequence length of some training-side inputs equals prompt+response. 3.1.5 Summary of verl Controller Logic Based on the above analysis, for a single worker, the inter-task scheduling logic of the verl controller can be described by the following flow chart: The following sequence diagram shows the performance bottleneck caused by task dispatch in the verl framework more clearly. 3.2 Performance Optimization: D2D Data Transfer 3.2.1 Optimization Approach Based on the previous analysis, the goal of this practice is to improve the task dispatch performance of the verl training side, so that in large-scale training all workers start executing tasks as simultaneously as possible, reducing the resource waste caused by workers waiting for each other, and improving training-side throughput. In addition, this practice attempted to change ray task dispatch in verl to multithreaded parallelism, but measurements showed it could not meet the requirements: The ref computation task dispatch could only be reduced from 66 seconds to 24 seconds, making it difficult to fully eliminate task dispatch time. Multithreaded parallel task dispatch can cause tensor data serialization errors on some workers, which are difficult to resolve. After reviewing the design directions of optimization schemes, this practice decided to focus mainly on the following two goals. Goal 1: Reduce the time consumed in transferring data between tasks. According to the previous analysis, verl's poor performance in large-scale training on NPUs is mainly because serial task dispatch includes serialization, ray transmission, and deserialization of each worker's input data. But in fact, the input data of most training-side tasks is generated on the device side by preceding tasks; sending the data to the host side, adjusting it in the main process, and then sending it back to the device side is unreasonable from a performance perspective. We can consider using the AlltoAllV collective communication to directly implement D2D data transfer to accelerate the data flow between verl tasks, i.e., the original logic of the main process collecting and dispatching data is directly implemented through AlltoAllV during device-to-device communication. In addition, because the actor model and the ref model in our verl training use the same parallel strategy and the DP rank layout is completely identical, the input/output data used by ref is completely identical to the input data required by update, so the collective communication operations can even be eliminated. Goal 2: Task control maintains verl's single-controller logic. verl uses Ray for scheduling at the upper layer, transferring data between workers to implement the control flow of RL algorithms, which is the so-called single controller. The advantage of verl's single controller is its clear architecture, simplifying the implementation of different RL algorithms within the framework: one only needs to write the worker methods and then call them at appropriate points in the main process training flow. However, data being directly communicated and transferred between multiple workers belongs to multi-controller logic, which would complicate the implementation of inter-task control logic in RL training and conflict with the verl framework's original design philosophy. We can consider decoupling verl's control flow from its data flow: accelerate the data flow as much as possible with D2D direct transfer, while keeping the control flow logic unchanged. Using a cache approach, data that subsequent tasks will also use is cached in place on the device side, and later tasks pull it from the cache on demand. Other data that must be returned to the CPU side or must be obtained from the CPU side retains its original logic coupled with the control flow. 3.2.2 Overall Flow We use TensorCache to manage tensors shared between preceding and subsequent tasks on the device, thereby accelerating transfer speed and reducing task dispatch time. Each worker instance holds a TensorCache, i.e., each device has a TensorCache managing tensor data. Attribute or Method Description ----- ---- minibs The batchsize of a single training step in GRPO, used together with the batch-axis size of tensors in the cache to compute their src DP size. tensorcached The dictionary of tensors cached in the cache, where the key is the tensor's name. cachedtensors() Given DataProto data, cache the tensors within it. Certain tensors can be specified not to be cached, and certain tensors can be specified to be cached while not being deleted (they will be passed to the CPU side for use later). getcachedtensors() Fetches the tensor with the given name from the cache and returns a DataProto instance. clear() Clears the cache, generally called after updateactor finishes. get\cached\tensors() may involve AlltoAllV communication, specifically in two cases: The current task and the preceding task have the same DP rank layout This situation occurs when the update task uses the cache updated by the ref computation task. The current verl does not support this feature. This practice supplemented verl with the old\log\prob-free computation feature. Setting config.actor\rollout\ref.actor.recompute\old\log\prob to False enables this optimization. 6. Performance Optimization: Inference The data generation inference phase has always been the top priority of RL training performance optimization. In long-sequence scenarios, the inference phase can account for more than 80% of the total time; in the current DeepSeek-R1 1K-to-3K scenario, the inference phase also accounts for nearly half of the total time. Therefore, this practice focused on performance optimization across framework scheduling, communication, model operator affinity, and other aspects of RL inference, ultimately achieving an inference throughput of 610+ token/p/s in the DeepSeek-R1 randomly initialized weights 1K-forced-to-3K scenario. The main journey is shown in the following figure: All the above optimization code has been merged into the vLLM Ascend community repository . This section will introduce, one by one, the features with significant benefit contributions, including TorchAir full-graph sinking enablement, MoE/MLA multi-stream, zero-redundancy TP-to-EP communication optimization, KV cache supporting NZ, Transpose/Cumsum elimination for large EP, and RL inference scheduling bound optimization. 6.1 TorchAir Full-Graph Sinking 6.1.1 Phenomenon Analysis PyTorch's Eager mode can seamlessly connect to Ascend hardware through the Ascend Extension for PyTorch (torch\npu), but the total inference time is dragged down by the operator dispatch scheduling overhead, resulting in a so-called scheduling Bound phenomenon that greatly impacts performance. The following figure uses the MLA structure of DeepSeek-V3 as an example to provide an intuitive demonstration of PyTorch's scheduling overhead in Eager mode: the NPU remains idle most of the time, and the CPU-side operator scheduling overhead has become the main factor in inference time. 6.1.2 Optimization Scheme To address this problem, PyTorch 2.0 released the major feature torch.compile, which implements native CPU/GPU-based graph mode capability based on TorchDynamo, supporting the capture of operators in the network into graphs with unified scheduling, eliminating scheduling latency during Decode inference. Correspondingly, TorchAir (Torch Ascend Intermediate Representation) is middleware that adapts TorchDynamo to Ascend IR, providing the foundation for PyTorch's graph mode in NPU environments. This practice enables the TorchAir graph mode in vLLM, eliminating the operator dispatch overhead of the inference Decode part during the rollout phase. 6.1.3 Optimization Effect After enabling the TorchAir graph mode, the profiling of a single-layer model is shown in the following figure, where it can be seen that the scheduling overhead is completely eliminated: In measurements, the double-layer Dense + MoE network inference time is reduced by 9.5ms in graph mode, and Decode throughput is doubled in the 671B full-parameter network. 6.2 MoE/MLA Multi-Stream 6.2.1 Phenomenon Analysis The TorchAir graph mode supports expressing the semantics of multi-stream operator execution in network scripts. Based on this feature, combined with the structural characteristics of the DeepSeek-V3 network, some operators can be executed concurrently across multiple streams to improve Decode performance. MoE Multi-Stream - Communication-Computation Parallelism The MoE structure of the DeepSeek-V3 network computes the activations of routed experts and shared experts. The weights of routed experts are partitioned by EP, requiring AlltoAll communication between cards before and after the GroupedMatmul computation (implemented by the MC2 operator); the weights of shared experts are partitioned by TP, requiring AllReduce communication between cards after the Matmul computation. Moreover, the computations of routed experts and shared experts have no data dependency. In the native vLLM Ascend implementation, shared expert computation and routed expert computation execute serially, corresponding to the profiling shown in the following figure. It can be seen that there are the following two problems in its computation-communication orchestration: While the MC2 operator (which contains both communication and Vector computation) executes, the Cube compute unit is idle. Shared expert computation takes a short time, but the subsequent AllReduce operation runs concurrently with MC2, causing communication bandwidth contention. MLA Multi-Stream - CV Parallelism Similar to the MoE structure, the MLA structure of the DeepSeek-V3 network also contains some computation steps without data dependencies. The native vLLM Ascend implementation does not consider this characteristic and executes all operators serially, leaving further room for optimization. 6.2.2 Optimization Scheme For the MoE part, this practice uses TorchAir's multi-stream capability to split shared expert computation onto parallel computation streams and rearrange it. The shared expert's "gate\up\proj" matrix operation is parallelized with the routed expert's "dispatch" communication operator, and the shared expert's "down\proj" matrix operation is parallelized with the routed expert's "combine" communication operator, optimizing Decode time through communication-computation parallelism. moeoptimization1 At the same time, to avoid the AllReduce communication tail after the shared expert's "down\proj" computation, this practice additionally eliminates the AllReduce communication brought by tensor parallelism by storing redundant shared expert weights. Since the shared expert's matrix operations are inherently small in scale, they can be basically hidden by the MC2 operator even without TP partitioning, yielding further performance gains. Similarly, for the MLA part, through certain pipeline arrangement, the Cube and Vector computations without data dependencies can be executed in parallel across multiple streams, improving Decode performance. moeoptimization2 6.2.3 Optimization Effect The profiling of the network segment after enabling the MoE multi-stream and MLA multi-stream optimizations is shown in the following figure: It can be seen that the MoE layer shared expert computation and MLA layer Vector computation have been offloaded to secondary streams, and the related time is hidden by the corresponding communication operators and Cube computation operators. This corresponds to a 6ms TPOT optimization for single-step Decode and a 7% improvement in end-to-end inference throughput. 6.3 Zero-Redundancy TP-to-EP Communication Optimization 6.3.1 Phenomenon Analysis To break through the single-device memory limit, this practice uses TP and EP partitioning for the MLA layer and the MoE layer respectively during inference, splitting the complete DeepSeek-V3 model across multiple devices. In the native vLLM Ascend implementation, the MLA layer completes data aggregation in tensor parallel scenarios through AllReduce, and the MoE layer uses the Split operator to extract the data needed by the current card, completing the conversion from TP partitioning to EP partitioning. Here, the combination of AllReduce + Split introduces double redundancy in both communication volume and computation volume. 6.3.2 Optimization Scheme This practice adopts a zero-redundancy TP-to-EP communication scheme. During the Decode phase, the AllReduce operator in the MLA layer is replaced with a ReduceScatter operator, so that the MoE layer only receives the data necessary for the current card's computation, and the AllGather communication at the end of the MoE layer is moved to the MLA layer, ensuring the correctness of the original TP partitioning logic. Since the communication volume of the AllReduce operator is equivalent to the sum of the communication volumes of the ReduceScatter and AllGather operators, this scheme eliminates the original AllGather communication and the Split operator in the MoE part while keeping the overall communication volume of the MLA layer unchanged. 6.3.3 Optimization Effect After enabling the zero-redundancy TP-to-EP communication optimization, the StridedSlice and AllGather operators in the MoE layer are eliminated. On the other hand, the reduction of MoE layer communication further alleviates the inter-card communication imbalance problem, ultimately optimizing inference TPOT by more than 2ms and improving Decode throughput by more than 3%. 6.4 KV Cache Supporting NZ 6.4.1 Phenomenon Analysis NZ is a special private data format on NPUs. As shown in the following figure, it divides complete data into data blocks and adopts a memory layout that is column-major between blocks and row-major within each block. When matrices undergo block computation, the NZ format allows compute units to access contiguous data memory, thereby maximizing the performance of the NPU Cube units. Operators generally include a step to convert the data format to NZ. By pre-storing KV cache in the NZ format, the internal format conversion stage of the FusedInferAttentionScore operator can be eliminated, optimizing the performance of the FA operator during the inference Decode phase. 6.4.2 Optimization Scheme By specifying the cache\mode parameter of the KvRmsNormRopeCache operator as "PA\NZ" in both the Prefill and Decode phases, KV cache can be stored in the NZ format. At the same time, the KV also needs to undergo relevant transformations to satisfy the FA operator's constraints on the shape and layout of input parameters in the NZ format scenario. 6.4.3 Optimization Result This practice added a new configuration item enable\kv\nz under torchair\graph\config in vLLM Ascend to control the KV cache NZ optimization. The benefit of this optimization grows as the sequence length increases. The specific results are shown in the following figure; when the sequence length is 3K, the Decode TPOT benefit exceeds 1ms. 6.5 Redundant Operator Elimination for Large EP 6.5.1 Phenomenon Analysis Redundant Transpose Operator DeepSeek-V3 models commonly use large-EP inference deployment, which reduces the number of routed experts participating in GroupedMatmul computation in the MoE part to lower single-Decode time. However, when analyzing profiling under the EP256 configuration, we found that an extra Transpose operation appears before the GroupedMatmul operator executes, causing significant performance degradation instead. The profiling information in the above figure shows that the total time of the Transpose operator in a single MoE layer is as high as 175us. After inspecting the model code and comparing the dump graphs of the EP128 scenario without Transpose, we found the problem is caused by the following reasons: Under the EP256 single-card-1-expert configuration, because the expert weight shape contains dimensions with a value of 1, the Transpose operator on the weights triggers TorchAir's "enable\view\optimize" optimization (see PyTorch Graph Mode Usage Guide > View-type Operator Optimization Feature (Chinese)), causing an extra Reshape operator to be inserted. The newly introduced Reshape operator prevents the fusion Pass "GroupedMatmulTransFusionPass" from detecting its intended target pattern, ultimately causing the Transpose operator to be retained into the graph execution phase. Redundant Cumsum Operator The multi-routed expert computation in the DeepSeek-V3 network is implemented by the GroupedMatmul operator, which is used to batch-process multiple matrix multiplication operations. By combining matrix multiplication operations with the same or similar shapes, it reduces memory access overhead and the waste of compute resources, thereby improving computational efficiency. The corresponding torch\npu interface "npu\grouped\matmul" relies on the input parameter "group\list" to obtain the actual M-axis size in each sub-matrix operation, and supports providing this parameter in either the "cumulative sum sequence" or "per-dimension specification" form. The model script of vLLM Ascend uses the "cumulative sum sequence" mode rather than the latter, thus introducing the Cumsum operator used to implement the cumulative sum in the MoE layer. In fact, this accumulation process is redundant. By configuring the "group\list\type=1" parameter of the "npu\grouped\matmul" interface, group\list can be provided in the "per-dimension specification" manner, thereby eliminating the overhead of the Cumsum operator. 6.5.2 Optimization Scheme The optimization item "enable\view\optimize" is enabled by default in TorchAir, aiming to fuse consecutive view-type operators. Since the DeepSeek-V3 network does not involve this target scenario, we choose to explicitly disable it in the "additional\config" configuration to avoid the resulting Transpose/Gmm operator fusion failure. At the same time, modify the network script of vLLM Ascend to adjust the "group\list\type" configuration of the "npu\grouped\matmul" interface, eliminating the original Cumsum operation. 6.5.3 Optimization Effect After adjusting TorchAir's optimization feature switch "enable\view\optimize" and the configuration of the torch\npu interface "npu\grouped\matmul", the Transpose/Cumsum operators on the critical path of the MoE phase are eliminated. Although the GroupedMatmul operator time increases, it still achieves a Decode performance benefit of 158us per layer and 9ms for the entire network, optimizing the total rollout time by more than 28s at a 3K inference length. 6.6 RL Inference Scheduling Bound Optimization 6.6.1 Phenomenon Analysis After significant performance optimization on the Decode model side, the proportion of pure model time in the overall Rollout is significantly reduced, which means that if only the pure model performance is optimized, subsequent improvements in overall Rollout throughput will face major limitations. Based on this, combined with the then-current Rollout time of 373s (corresponding to a throughput of 547 token/p/s), we re-decomposed and analyzed the overall RL inference process, with the results as follows: It can be seen in the above figure that the pure model computation time of Prefill and Decode accounts for less than 60% of the overall RL inference time, and the remaining 40% is concentrated in scheduling operations such as the pre/post-processing of Decode, vLLM V1 Engine scheduling, and weight memory offloading before RL training-inference switching. To further improve Rollout performance, we need to shift from focusing solely on model performance optimization to optimizing the "scheduling bound" problem in such inference scenarios. After in-depth analysis, the following results were obtained: 1. vLLM Sche part: the time is concentrated in the EOS detection synchronization across the entire DP domain before scheduling, which uses CPU AllReduce communication to obtain the result of "has\unfinished\requests" and decide whether to execute dummy\batch. This CPU communication takes an average of 10ms per call, accumulating to as much as 30s after 3000 inference iterations. 2. Decode prepare input part: the time is concentrated in the P/D detection synchronization across the entire DP domain, similar to the "vLLM Sche part" above, taking 10ms per call and accumulating to a total of as much as 30s after 3000 Decode iterations. It is worth mentioning here that the deployment scheme for RL inference is P/D co-residency, so during the Sche phase it is necessary to determine whether PD hybrid deployment exists among the current DP ranks, to decide whether to use the Prefill AlltoAll or the Decode Dispatch/Combine, preventing blocking caused by inconsistent communication operators between DP ranks. Later, if this practice scheme switches to P/D separated deployment, this communication will no longer be needed. 3. RL Sche part: after inference ends and before switching to training, the RL framework first needs to offload the inference-phase memory, then reshard the model weights for the training phase. However, testing found that calling the "torch.cuda.empty\cache()" interface to offload memory also takes about 4s. Investigating the reason, we found it calls the underlying "aclrtFreePhysical" interface, releasing the torch memory pool to the operating system. The memory released per call is about 26G, and two memory releases occur during the inference-to-training and training-to-inference processes, for a total of about 8s. In principle, reducing operations that directly release memory to the OS and reusing memory in the memory management of the Ascend Extension for PyTorch (Chinese) will help further improve the overall efficiency of training-inference switching. 6.6.2 Optimization Scheme For the CPU AllReduce communication of EOS detection and P/D detection synchronization across all DP ranks, we plan to change it from CPU-side communication on the Gloo backend to NPU-side communication on the HCCL backend. 基于鲲鹏 CPU、昇腾 950 和灵衢协同的 Agentic RL 训练实践 随着 DeepSeek 等大规模基座模型的发展，大模型技术正经历从“生成文本”向“自主决策智能体”的演进。早期模型主要依靠预训练获得通用语言能力，并通过 SFT、RLHF 等后训练方法提升指令遵循和偏好对齐能力。进一步地，Agentic RL 将强化学习引入智能体场景，使模型能够通过任务规划、工具调用和环境交互，根据反馈不断优化行为策略。围绕这一方向，业界正在构建面向 Agent 的大规模 RL 基础设施，以支持长程任务、多环境交互和持续学习能力的发展。 然而，Agentic RL 的发展仍面临多方面挑战： 长序列和超大规模模型带来的内存与通信挑战。 Agentic RL 中的任务轨迹通常包含大量交互历史、工具调用记录以及中间推理过程，导致训练序列长度显著增加。同时，随着千亿甚至万亿参数规模模型的发展，模型参数、梯度、优化器状态以及 KV Cache 均带来了巨大的存储压力和通信开销。 高频工具调用对 Agent 环境基础设施提出更高要求。 与传统 LLM 训练不同，Agentic RL 需要模型频繁调用外部工具，大量工具交互会引入额外的环境执行开销，使 Rollout 阶段成为影响整体训练效率的重要瓶颈。因此，需要构建高性能、安全可靠的 Agent 沙箱环境，实现模型推理、工具执行和环境反馈之间的高效协同。 RL 训练稳定性与训推一致性挑战。 RL 训练过程中，训练与推理阶段的计算差异可能导致策略偏移，影响奖励评估准确性、训练稳定性和可复现性。在大规模分布式训练环境下，算子实现、数值精度以及并行策略的不一致，都可能造成训推结果偏差。因此，需要从算法设计和 Kernel 实现等多个层面保证训推一致性，从而提升 RL 训练过程的稳定性、可复现性以及调试效率。 面对上述挑战，我们发布了鲲鹏 CPU、昇腾 950 和灵衢协同的 Agentic RL 训推一致性保障 低精度训练 长序列训练优化 Agentic RL 训练流程 Future Plan RL Framework 及部署方案 本实践基于 Vime RL 训练框架进行扩展：Rollout 侧沿用 Vime 的 vLLM 集成方案，训练侧采用 TorchTitan 替换 Megatron 作为训练后端。模型定义、FSDP2 并行策略以及 Optimizer 等核心训练组件均基于 TorchTitan 构建，同时保持与 Vime 一致的训练流程和接口设计，实现 RL 训练链路的平滑迁移。 整体架构与 Vime 保持一致，主要包含 Training、Rollout 和 Data Buffer 三个核心模块： Training（TorchTitan）： 负责 RL 主训练流程，从 Data Buffer 获取训练数据，完成模型优化更新，并将最新权重同步至 Rollout 模块； Rollout（vLLM + Router）： 负责推理采样流程，通过 vLLM 推理引擎生成轨迹数据，并结合 Router 完成请求调度，产出包含 reward/verifier 信息的新数据； Data Buffer： 作为训练与 Rollout 的数据桥梁，负责管理 Prompt 初始化、自定义数据以及 Rollout 生成数据。 当前支持训推共卡/分离和推理侧 PD 共卡/分离等多种部署模式，用户可以结合集群资源规模、模型特点及训推负载特征灵活选择，进一步优化 Agentic RL 系统的资源利用效率。本实践实际部署中采用“训推分离 + PD 共卡”的组合部署形态。 训推分离： 训练侧与 Rollout 侧部署在独立 NPU 资源域中。训练侧保留模型参数、activation、gradient 和 optimizer state；Rollout 侧独立管理推理权重、请求调度和 KV Cache，两侧通过权重同步衔接每一轮 RL 更新，保障训练稳定性与训推资源边界清晰。 PD 共卡： Rollout 内部将 Prefill 和 Decode 共卡部署，按阶段复用 NPU 资源与显存，降低部署复杂度。 PD 分离： Rollout 内部将 Prefill 和 Decode 分别部署在独立的推理资源域，Prefill 负责处理输入上下文，Decode 负责生成输出 token；两侧通过 KV connector 传输 KV Cache。 训推一致性保障 在 RL 后训练流程中，推理引擎负责生成训练轨迹，训练引擎负责计算策略概率（Logprobs）并更新模型参数。理论上，两侧加载相同权重后，对同一输入应该得到一致的输出概率。但在实际大模型系统中，由于训练和推理框架在框架调度、算子调用、Kernel实现、计算精度、并行策略以及权重处理流程等方面存在差异，即使使用完全相同的模型参数，也可能产生不同的计算结果。 对于 RL 训练而言，这类差异会直接影响策略优化过程：轻微的数值误差可能进一步放大为 MoE 路由选择变化、Lightning Indexer KV选择差异等，最终导致 logprobs 偏差。因此，训推一致性不仅是数值精度问题，更是保证 RL 训练稳定性和结果可复现性的基础能力。 本实践基于 CANN 软件栈，对 TorchTitan-NPU 训练引擎和 vLLM-Ascend 推理引擎进行了从框架到算子的系统性对齐。最终在相同权重条件下，通过算法、框架到 CANN 算子 Kernel 的层层校准，实现训推全链路 bitwise 一致，logprob MAE 为 0.0。 基础设施 训推一致性的建设并非单点优化，而是由底层基础能力逐步向上收敛。整体按照如下路径推进： CANN 基础能力建设 → 单引擎内部一致性 → 训推引擎间一致性 其中两项基础能力是后续所有对齐工作的基石：CANN 算子 Batch 一致性、MoE Routing Replay。 CANN 算子 Batch 一致性支持 在实际 RL 场景中，同一个样本可能由于 Batch 内位置和 Batch 大小变化、动态调度策略变化等原因，进入不同的计算路径。如果算子本身无法保证 Batch 一致性，则即使输入数据和权重完全相同，仅改变样本在 Batch 中的位置，也可能产生不同结果。因此，首先需要保证底层算子的 Batch 一致性。 CANN 软件栈针对计算算子和通信算子均提供了 Batch 一致性支持能力，通过统一开关使能后，可以保证同一输入在不同 Batch 排布情况下得到一致结果。 python export HCCLDETERMINISTIC=strict torchnpu.npu.setdeterministiclevel(3) 可通过如上开关使能。在此基础上，我们结合实际训推场景，对关键算子进行了验证，确保后续框架级一致性问题不会受到底层算子非确定性的干扰。 MoE Routing Replay 对于 MoE 模型，Router 根据每个 token 的 Router Logits 选择 Top-K 专家参与计算。由于 Router Logits 对数值误差敏感，即使训推两侧使用相同权重，微小计算差异也可能导致不同专家选择。 一旦专家路径发生变化，后续计算结果已经不再是简单的数值误差，而是离散计算路径差异。为隔离这一因素，推理侧需要返回每个 token、每一层选择的逻辑专家 ID，训练侧使用这些 ID 重放相同的专家路径。 推理侧捕获逻辑专家 ID。 vLLM-Ascend 在 MoE Router 产生 topkids 后、专家 ID 映射到各 EP Rank 的本地编号前完成捕获，保证返回的是训练侧可以直接使用的逻辑专家 ID。DP、TP 和 SP 会改变当前 Rank 上看到的 token 排布，因此捕获时还要恢复原始 token 顺序，并裁掉通信或图执行引入的 padding。最终每个请求返回的数据形状为 [numreturnedtokens, numhiddenlayers, numexpertspertok]，分别对应返回 token、MoE 层和 Top-K 位置。 mermaid flowchart LR A[推理侧 MoE Router] --> B[捕获逻辑 topkids] B --> C[按原始 Token 映射到物理 KV Slot] C --> D[Scheduler 持久化并按请求恢复] D --> E[返回 Routed Experts] E --> F[训练侧重放相同专家路径] F --> G[比较训推 Logprobs] 按原始 token 持久化。 路由数据按逻辑 token 产生，需要建立从逻辑 token 到物理 slot 的映射来保存路由数据。对于 DeepSeek-V4 一类使用 MLA compressed KV Cache 的模型，Attention 路径不会为每个原始 token 区间分配一个物理 slot；routed-expert capture 却必须为每个原始 token 保存一行数据。因此，compressed KV slot 不能直接作为 routed-expert slot。另外，压缩 KV 可能尚未为尾部 token 分配新的物理 block，但这些 token 仍然各自需要一行路由记录。为解决这两个问题，本实践根据已申请的 compressed 物理 block 重建非压缩的物理 block ID，将非尾块 token 的路由信息写入全局 host buffer 的 block 中；暂时无法落盘的尾部保存在请求级 pending buffer 中，返回时再按逻辑 token 顺序拼接。由于 Prefix Cache 和 Chunked Prefill 的复用单位是物理 KV block，该方案既能复用 Prefix Cache 中已有的路由信息，也能覆盖跨多个 Prefill chunk 的请求。 Async Scheduling 下保持数据对应。 Async Scheduling 允许多个 forward 同时处于执行或回传阶段，而路由捕获 buffer 会被下一轮 forward 清空并复用。为避免数据被覆盖，每轮 forward 都先生成独立的 device snapshot，再执行异步 D2H；同时将物理 block snapshot 保存在对应的 SchedulerOutput 中，使 SchedulerOutput N 与 ModelRunnerOutput N 一一对应。 关键问题与解决方案 完成基础能力建设后，我们按照训推单引擎内部一致性 → 训推引擎间一致性的顺序逐步推进一致性验证。以下是我们在对齐过程中遇到的关键问题。 框架侧问题 a\) PD 分离场景下 MoE 路径不一致 在 PD 分离架构中，Prefill 和 Decode 使用不同执行路径： Prefill 通常采用标准 AllToAll 完成 MoE Dispatch； Decode 为降低延迟，会采用 Dispatch/Combine 融合算子。 在 PD 混部场景下，Decode token 可能与 Prefill token 被调度进入同一个 Batch，从而在 Prefill 路径执行，导致同样的 token 在不同 Batch 组合下走不同 MoE 计算路径，产生训推差异。 针对该问题，我们统一了推理引擎中的 MoE Dispatch/Combine 实现，全部切换到 CANN 提供的 融合 Kernel ，保证不同阶段、不同 Batch 组合下执行路径一致。 b\) 权重与 Activation 数据类型不一致 LLM 训练和推理通常需要复杂的细粒度数据类型控制，以 DeepSeek\-V4 Flash 为例： MoE Router、Compressor、mHC 等模块需要保持 FP32 精度 Embedding、LMHead、Lightning Indexer 等模块采用 BF16 Attention 和 MoE Router Expert 权重采用 MXFP8 MoE Expert 权重采用 MXFP4 如果训推两侧在权重加载、反量化方式、FSDP 通信精度、模型内部 Forward 输入类型转换等任一环节存在差异，都会导致最终结果不一致。针对该问题，我们实现了细粒度的数据类型对齐，使训练侧实际参与计算的数据类型与推理侧保持一致。 c\) 算子融合粒度差异 推理引擎为了追求极致性能，通常会采用更大粒度融合 Kernel，训练框架不一定采用相同融合策略。因此，即使数学公式一致，不同融合方式仍可能由于中间结果精度、计算顺序、归约顺序等问题产生数值差异。我们针对该类差异逐点权衡性能： 优先训练侧复用推理融合算子，并实现对应反向传播融合 Kernel 或者小算子； 对难以复用的融合算子，推理侧回退到基础小算子实现； 算子侧问题 在 CSA Kernel 的 PageAttention 场景中，我们发现即使逻辑 KV 和 Top\-K 顺序一致，仅改变 BlockTable 排布，也会导致计算结果变化。 进一步分析发现，PageAttention 过程中，CSA Kernel 会根据 Top\-K 结果连续搬运两个 token。由于搬运过程按照物理地址排序，导致搬运后的 token 顺序与原始 Top\-K 顺序不一致。最终在 Attention 累加过程中，由于归约顺序变化，引入浮点计算误差，导致输出存在差异。 针对该问题，我们修复 Kernel 内部搬运逻辑，保证计算顺序与逻辑 Top\-K 顺序一致，消除了 BlockTable 变化导致的精度波动。 低精度训练 本实践支持 MXFP8 和 MXFP4 两种低精度 RL 训练模式，用户可根据模型结构和性能需求灵活参考。依托 Ascend 950 原生 MXFP8/MXFP4 计算能力，实现低精度矩阵计算加速，有效提升 Rollout 和在线服务推理效率，同时降低大模型训推过程中的静态内存占用和权重传输开销，缓解超大规模模型部署中的内存瓶颈。 MXFP8 训练 MXFP8 训练流程如上图所示。为保证 RL 训推一致性，训练阶段与 Rollout 推理阶段采用严格一致的数据类型和量化策略。 在训练正向阶段， BF16 Activation 分别沿 M 维和 K 维进行 MXFP8 量化，生成 row\-wise 和 col\-wise 的 FP8 Activation。其中，FP32 Master Weight 按 32×32 block 进行量化，得到 FP8 Weight 以及对应的 E8M0 Scale。Block\-wise Scale 在计算前广播为 row\-wise 的 1×32 Scale，方便直接调用 MXFP8 Matmul Kernel，完成 FP8 Activation 与 FP8 Weight 的矩阵乘计算。 在训练反向阶段， BF16 Gradient 分别沿 M 维和 N 维进行 MXFP8 量化，生成 row\-wise 和 col\-wise 的 FP8 Gradient。其中，col\-wise FP8 Gradient 与正向缓存的 col\-wise FP8 Activation 进行矩阵乘，计算权重梯度 dW，用于后续优化器更新；row\-wise FP8 Gradient 与缓存的 FP8 Weight 进行矩阵乘，计算得到输入梯度 dX，完成梯度反向传播。与正向类似，FP8 Weight 对应的 Scale 会广播为 col\-wise Scale。 在训推权重同步阶段， 由于 TorchTitan 训练引擎仅保留 FP32 Master Weight，不驻留低精度权重副本，RL Framework 从 TorchTitan 获取 FP32 Master Weight，并按照与训练正向阶段一致的量化流程转换为 FP8 Weight 后传输至 Rollout 引擎。 在 Rollout 阶段， 推理引擎获取更新后的低精度权重，调用 W8A8 Matmul Kernel 完成推理计算，实现低精度推理加速。 值得注意的是，本实践对权重量化采用FP8 32×32 Per Block 量化。相比 DeepSeek-V4 原生的 128×128 粒度，该方案能提供更细粒度的 Scale 表征，从而获得更高的量化精度；同时，生成的 Block-wise E8M0 Scale 经广播后，可直接复用 Ascend 950DT 上的 MXFP8 Kernel（该 Kernel 为 per-group 粒度），无需引入额外计算路径，进而提升算子执行效率。 在 MXFP8 计算中，Ascend 950DT 硬件支持在 L0C 内完成随路反量化，无需将数据搬出至 UB 再由 Vector 单元执行反量化，避免受 UB buffer 容量、Vector算力及带宽的制约，进一步提升低精度矩阵计算效率。 此外，本实践没有直接采用 MXFP8 per group 权重量化，主要还基于以下两点考虑： 1. 保证训推一致性与训练稳定性 MXFP8 量化会导致前向与反向阶段权重量化轴不一致，引入权重数值偏差，存在影响 RL 训练稳定性的风险。采用 FP8 per-block 权重量化，可保证前向、反向计算过程中的权重表示完全一致。 2. 提升计算复用效率，降低量化开销 前向阶段生成的 FP8 Weight 可缓存，并复用于 Recompute 与反向传播，避免在反向阶段重复执行权重量化操作，减少额外计算开销，提升训练效率。 综合上述原因，本实践对权重量化采用FP8 32×32 Per Block 量化，也和后续的 DeepSeek-V4.1 原生量化策略保持一致。 MXFP4 训练 MXFP4 训练主要应用于 MoE 模型的 GroupedMatmul，其整体数据流与 MXFP8 基本保持一致。主要区别在于：训练正向阶段，FP32 Master Weight 首先量化为 MXFP4 格式，后续重量化为 per-block FP8 权重，用于训练过程中的重计算和反向传播。 在训推权重传输阶段，采用 MXFP4 格式传输权重，相较于 MXFP8 可进一步降低权重传输带宽需求和存储开销。推理阶段，推理引擎直接调用 W4A8 GroupedMatmul Kernel 完成计算，在保持计算效率的同时进一步优化 MoE 模型权重访存效率。 DSV4 Flash MXFP8 训练效果 本次实践基于 GRPO、DSV4 Flash MXFP8，在 dapo-math-17k 数据集完成 60 步训练，实现了 logprob MAE 为 0.0 的训推对齐效果。实验采用 --rollout-batch-size=128、n-samples-per-prompt=8、rollout-max-response-len=3072的参数配置，reward 逐步收敛，gradient norm 整体稳定，效果如下图所示。 DSV4 Flash MXFP8 发布的权重在dapo-math-17k 数据集上效果很好，初始 reward=0.7，每个 prompt 生成 8 个样本下大量样本全 0 或 1，训练信号太弱。为了方便观测训练收敛效果，本次实验先离线收集该数据集的 reward 评分（每个 prompt 生成 8 个样本），将 reward 之和在区间 [1, 6] 的样本过滤出来用于训练。 长序列训练优化 Agentic RL 场景多轮工具调用通常会导致序列长度显著增加，除 Prefix Cache、Partial Rollout 等常见优化外，针对 1M 超长序列的 RL 训练，我们重点优化了以下两个方面：一是降低训练过程中的局部内存峰值；二是采用上下文并行（Context Parallelism，CP）将长序列计算分散到多个设备上，并完成 RL 训练中 CP 场景下数据准备、loss 处理及权重同步等相关环节的适配。 激活峰值内存优化 Activation Checkpoint 调整 激活重计算通过减少前向阶段保存的中间结果来节省内存，但反向恢复这些结果时，仍可能出现局部峰值。因此，除了检查保存了多少激活，还需要关注重计算发生时有哪些张量同时驻留。我们针对 hchead 调整了 activation checkpoint 的位置，使激活保存与重计算的边界更适合长序列场景。在 32K 序列长度配置下，该阶段的局部峰值降低近 20%。 Chunked loss 为保持数值精度，我们在 loss 的 softmax 与 log 相关计算中使用 FP32。长序列下，这部分操作会产生较大的词表维度中间结果。为降低一次计算的内存需求，我们沿 token 维度将其拆成多个 chunk，逐块计算 log\-probability，再按原顺序重排结果。分块保持了每个 token 的词表归一化范围不变；使用lm\head TP 时，也保留了对应的跨设备归约。 chunk 大小需要在内存和执行效率之间取舍，较小的 chunk 可以减少单次操作的临时空间，但会增加算子调用，并可能增加通信次数。本次使用的 chunk 大小为 8192，32K序列长度配置下，loss 计算阶段峰值由 45 GB 降至 38 GB。 RL 训练的 CP 适配 为进一步减少长序列下激活的内存占用，我们考虑在RL场景引入了 CP 并行。CP 将一条长序列切分到多个Rank计算，使每个 Rank 主要处理本地 token 对应的激活，在Attention阶段通过通信获取完整序列的KV信息。 我们接入了 TorchTitan-NPU 后端已有的 CP 训练能力，采用连续序列切分。框架将完整 packed tokens、位置信息和 CP 通信组交给模型，由模型统一构造 Forward 输入并完成切分，避免框架和模型各切一次。由于 Rollout 过程产生的 Response 长度并不固定，因此框架将对不满足 CPdegree 倍数的训练输入做 padding 处理，并且 padding 部分不参与 loss 计算。 对齐 token 归属与训练目标。 CP 方案还需要保证 response、mask、advantage 和 log\-probability 与本地 logits 一一对应，其关键是区分输入位置与预测目标：位置 g 的 logit 预测位置 g\+1 的 token。因此，分片最后一个 logit 可能负责预测下一分片的第一个 token，不能直接按输入边界切分所有训练字段。我们按全局预测目标映射分配这些字段，并将 old/reference 前向的局部 log\-probability 恢复为完整 response，供后续 advantage 计算和指标统计使用。 保持 loss 与梯度尺度不变。 CP 的多个 Rank 共同处理同一组输入，各 Rank 只需计算本地有效 token 的 loss；按 rollout 归一化时保留完整 rollout 的有效 token 分母，按 token 归一化时使用全局唯一有效 token 数。CP 汇总 loss 的前向值，反向保留本地贡献，并与 FSDP 的梯度归约配套，避免额外乘除 CP\degree。在恢复完整 response 的数据布局下，advantage 和样本分母只按独立的数据并行样本统计，避免重复计数。 CP 场景下的 Routing Replay 支持 在已有 Routing Replay 的基础上，CP 主要增加了路由布局和重计算管理两方面的适配，对应图中的橙色路径。 路由与输入使用同一映射。 若推理侧也进行了分片，需先将路由恢复到请求内的逻辑 token 顺序，去除 padding 和重复行；训练侧再按模型提供的 localtoglobal 映射取出本地路由，避免重复实现切分规则。路由按输入位置 g 取 route[g]，loss 则对应目标 token[g+1]。缺失记录和末 token 需显式标记；没有 response target 的 Rank 仍可能有 prompt 路由和通信，不能直接跳过。 重计算复用本地路由。 将推理记录的 routed experts 绑定到对应的 microbatch、层和 CP 布局，保证原前向与 checkpoint 重计算读取同一份记录，避免调用顺序变化造成错位。 Agentic RL 训练流程 本实践以 Qwen3.5 和 SWE-Gym 代码修复任务为例，基于鲲鹏平台部署 AgentENV 与 Codex Harness，使能多轮模型推理、工具执行、独立评测和策略更新，形成从任务采样到训练更新的端到端 Agentic RL 流程。 沙箱环境与 RL 框架解耦，支持多种 Harness 本实践实现了环境执行与 RL 训推分离部署下的稳定训练：AgentENV 沙箱环境在 CPU 侧承载代码执行与工具交互，TorchTitan 和 vLLM-Ascend 在 NPU 侧完成策略优化与推理采样，两侧通过环境控制和模型请求接口协同。框架将任务环境、Harness 与模型协议适配分开，支持 Codex、Claude Code 等不同 Harness 复用同一套训练主干，使 Agent 执行方式的扩展无需重写 RL 后端。 AgentENV 在鲲鹏 CPU 上的适配和优化 与传统 Reasoning RL 不同，Agentic RL 的 Rollout 采样过程不仅包含模型自身的推理，也涉及与外部环境进行持续、多轮的高并发交互。本实践基于 AgentENV，在鲲鹏 CPU（ARM64 架构）上完成部署和 SWE-Gym 训练环境的构建；基于 openEuler OS 完成 PVspinlock 优化，提升 vCPU 在超高并发下的资源利用率，同时提升沙箱的恢复和调度效率。 PVspinlock 实战优化： 在 AgentENV 所用的 KVM 虚拟化场景中，Host 与 Guest 分别进行独立调度。当 vCPU 存在超分时，如果持有 spinlock 的 vCPU 被 Host 调度出去，其余 vCPU 会持续等待，造成无效 CPU 消耗。Agentic RL 场景下，沙箱在高并发场景下通常存在较高的 vCPU 超分比例，因此该问题会直接影响沙箱的执行效率和性能。 openEuler OLK-6.6 已在 ARM 平台支持 PVspinlock。当 Guest vCPU 抢锁超时后，可通过 WFI 陷出至 Host 并暂时退出运行队列；锁释放后，再由 Guest 通知 Hypervisor 定向唤醒等待 vCPU，从而减少无意义自旋并提升物理 CPU 利用率。本实践基于 AgentENV MicroVM，在 Host 和 Guest 均使用支持 PVspinlock 的 openEuler OLK-6.6 内核，并构造两种 CPU 调度场景： 1:1：2 个 vCPU 分别绑定至两个独立 pCPU； 1:2 超分：2 个 vCPU 共同绑定至同一个 pCPU。 使用 hackbench 进行高并发进程通信压测。每组实验执行 13 次，前 3 次预热，取后 10 次平均值。同时通过 Guest 启动参数 nopvspin 控制 PVspinlock 开关，以进行对比测试。 测试结果数值越小越好。在 1:2 vCPU 超分场景下，开启 PVspinlock 后 hackbench 完成时间由 8\.2052 s 降低至 7\.2483 s，性能提升约 11\.66%。相比之下，在无超分的 1:1 场景中收益并不明显，说明 PVspinlock 的主要价值体现在高超分、强锁竞争场景下。 CONFIGHZ 优化实践：缩短沙箱恢复调度时延 CONFIGHZ 是 Linux 内核的编译配置项，用于定义内核每秒的时钟 tick 频率，并影响调度器定时处理、线程唤醒及时间管理等机制的时间粒度。HZ=250 对应约 4 ms 的 tick 间隔，而 HZ=1000 对应约 1 ms。 在 AgentEnv 的 concurrentresume 测试中，每个 sample 会并发恢复 50 个沙箱。测试发现，openEuler 内核默认 CONFIGHZ=250 时，大部分恢复耗时位于 40–60 ms，但会出现较多 100 ms 以上的长尾异常点，最大时延达到 147 ms，整体方差和长尾延迟均明显高于 Ubuntu。 分析发现，沙箱恢复过程中需要并发创建和删除 ublk 设备，多个线程会竞争全局 ublkctlmutex。未获取锁的线程进入睡眠并在锁释放后重新参与调度。在此类高并发锁竞争场景下，提高 HZ 可以提供更细粒度的调度机会，降低等待线程重新获得 CPU 的调度延迟，从而减少多个锁竞争阶段累积形成的 resume 长尾时延。 以 openEuler 6\.6\.0、每组 150 个 samples 为例： 将 CONFIGHZ 从 250 调整至 1000 后，openEuler 的平均 resume 时延由 57\.6 ms 降低至 37\.9 ms，下降约 34%；超过 80 ms 的长尾 sample 从 13 个下降至 1 个。剩余异常点主要出现在每轮第一个 sample，属于缓存未热等因素带来的冷启动开销；除冷启动外，测试结果基本稳定在 25–60 ms。 Ubuntu 6\.8\.12 上也观察到了相同趋势：将 HZ 从 250 调整至 1000 后，平均时延由 53\.9 ms 降至 45\.2 ms（约 16%），剔除每轮首个冷启动 sample 后，超过 80 ms 的长尾样本由 5 个降至 0 个。 因此，对于 Agent 沙箱这类包含大量并发恢复、锁竞争和线程唤醒的低时延场景，将 CONFIGHZ 提升至 1000 可以明显改善调度响应速度，尤其能够有效降低沙箱 resume 的平均时延和长尾抖动。 准确的优势估计与信用分配 针对多轮交互中轨迹分支、上下文重写和请求重试带来的训练数据偏差，本实践保留模型实际采样的 token 与 logprob，通过 loss mask 和共享前缀去重，明确参与策略优化的输出范围。该训练实践引入 Turn Disposition 机制判断多轮轨迹片段的训练资格，减少训练噪声，并最终在任务级结果奖励与 token 级优化之间建立一致的归属关系，为 advantage 计算与 credit assignment 提供可信的数据基础。 Turn Disposition：从响应采纳到训练资格 Agent 在多轮执行中可能重试同一请求、压缩上下文或并发发起模型调用。在 RL 训练过程中，模型产生的行为并非全部都值得训练。以常见的 Coding Agent 为例，正确的思考方向 + 被迫截断的上下文（reward = 0）并不能作为合适的训练样本。本实践引入 Turn Disposition，以会话为单位，为每个已生成响应维护状态，并根据后续协议事件确定其训练资格。 先记录，暂不训练。 模型响应生成后进入 pending，保留原始 token 和 logprob，但设置 trainable=False，等待下一次请求或会话收尾。 请求推进或会话结束时确认。 仅有一个待定响应、且未发生长度截断时，后续请求若未重试同一请求，上一响应转为 accepted；若会话直接结束，则转为 terminal，保留最后一次输出的训练资格。 重试、截断和归属不明时排除。 相同请求再次出现、响应因长度限制截断，或同时存在多个无法明确关联的待定响应时，相关响应转为 discarded。排除的是其训练损失贡献，原始交互记录仍可保留。 状态更新最终写入轨迹节点：accepted 和 terminal 获得训练资格，再结合 token 对齐与共享前缀去重形成最终 loss mask；pending 和 discarded 不贡献该响应的训练损失。Turn Disposition 因而负责明确“哪些模型输出可以承接学习信号”，任务奖励仍由独立评测产生，优势值由后续 RL 逻辑计算。即使一次任务失败，被采纳的输出仍可以参与训练，从失败反馈中更新策略。 求解与验证隔离 Agentic RL 与 AgentENV 协同管理两类独立沙箱：执行沙箱承载 Agent 的代码修改与工具调用，验证沙箱从相同模板重新创建，仅接收候选补丁并执行评测。两者保持一致的任务起点，同时隔离可写工作区、临时文件和后台进程，使奖励依据可复现的测试结果生成。隔离的执行和验证环境，保证了奖励信号的准确性，并规避模型 Reward Hacking 的风险。 SWE-Gym 任务上的稳定奖励收敛 本实践基于 GRPO、Qwen3.5-4B 模型以及 NovaSky-AI/SkyRL-v0-293-data 数据集，完成了基于 Codex 的 SWE-Gym Agentic RL 训练，并实现了训练 Reward 的稳定收敛。该结果表明，环境交互、轨迹处理、奖励计算以及训推权重更新等关键环节已实现端到端打通与稳定协同。如下图所示，Reward 在训练过程中逐步提升，并且 gradient norm 整体稳定，进一步体现了本实践在长流程训练 + 长程 Agent 交互中的稳定性与可用性，也为后续面向更复杂任务及更大规模模型的训练实践提供了工程基础和验证依据。 Future Plan 1. 支持 DeepSeek-V4.1 等新模型的 Agentic RL 训练 当前实践仅支持 DeepSeek-V4 Flash 的 Reasoning RL 和 Qwen3.5 的 Agentic RL 训练，后续将持续扩展模型适配范围，支持 DSV4.1 等新一代大模型的 Agentic RL 训练流程。 2. 提升训练稳定性与可靠性保障 开展长稳运行与可靠性测试，完善故障监控、问题定位与恢复机制，保障 Agentic RL 训练稳定可靠。 3. 完善训推一致性问题定位与调试能力 增强精度问题分析与维测能力，围绕训推一致性问题沉淀算法/框架问题定位 Skill，并提供 Kernel 级 Dump 与分析工具，实现问题快速定界。 4. 完善异步 RL 性能分析与优化能力 建设性能问题维测能力，针对异步 RL 训练流程开展端到端效率分析，快速识别 Rollout、通信、训练等环节瓶颈，持续优化系统性能。 5. 提升 Agentic RL 任务的规模化和丰富度 当前版本主要展示了 SWE-Gym 的训练效果，之后该训练实践将聚焦“多任务 + 多 Harness”的 Agentic RL 训练场景。基于已有的稳定训推精度和轻量解耦的环境，该训练实践将继续演进并提升模型后训练能力的泛化性。

Qwen3-235B 32K长序列RL训练优化实践 本文系统总结了基于verl框架与A3集群的Qwen3-235B模型32K长序列强化学习训练优化实践，详细介绍了对RL长序列场景下特有的长尾序列负载不均、显存瓶颈等问题进行的多项优化。通过文中所述技术，本实践成功将系统吞吐从个位数大幅度提升至122TPS/卡。同时，本文还与近期发布的Seer长序列RL训练系统中的相关优化思路进行了对比分析，揭示了技术路线上的共识与差异。 1. 前言 1.1 背景 长序列处理能力是推动大型语言模型走向实用化的关键。以具备32K上下文长度处理能力的Qwen3-235B模型为例，它能够有效应对长篇文章解析、复杂多轮对话和大规模代码编写等现实任务，在金融研报分析、法律条文解读以及科研文献理解等多个领域都展现出重要的应用价值。因此，如何高效处理训练与推理过程中的长序列数据，已成为影响模型部署效率的关键因素。 特别地，在强化学习场景中，模型不仅需要在超长上下文中进行复杂的思维链（CoT）推理与奖励训练，还面临HBM内存消耗随序列长度线性增长、长尾序列分布导致负载不均等挑战，这无疑对训练与推理系统的效率及稳定性提出了更高要求。 针对上述问题，本实践在 前序工作 基础上，沿用verl的前端，采用vLLM Ascend作为推理引擎，MindSpeed作为训练引擎，在64卡A3集群上对Qwen3-235B模型进行了32K长序列GRPO算法的强化学习训练优化。本实践系统性地从模型切分策略、长序列负载均衡、计算与通信效率等多个维度入手，显著提升了长序列训练吞吐，最终实现122TPS/卡的系统性能。 值得一提的是，近期月之暗面&清华发布的论文 《Seer: Online Context Learning for Fast Synchronous LLM Reinforcement Learning》 中，也提出了多项针对长序列强化学习的优化策略，与本实践的思路高度契合。本文也对其中的一部分策略进行了对比分析。 1.2 优化实践总览 本实践对verl开源代码进行了以下关键功能的适配与优化： 训练引擎适配：verl框架当前已经原生支持MindSpeed训练引擎，但在开启moe\alltoall\overlap后会出现专家权重加载异常问题，本实践针对该问题进行了修复与适配。 推理引擎优化：推理过程中的sleep模式依赖torch
pu的虚拟内存动态切换，目前采用 前序工作 的方法实现推理权重及kv\cache的加载与卸载。 框架适配：参考 前序工作 修改了verl框架，在GRPO这类on-policy训练算法中实现了old\log\prob免计算。 本实践针对长序列推理和训练中的性能瓶颈与内存占用，进行了系统性地优化，具体方法如下图所示： 1.3 详细性能结果 1.3.1 GRPO算法 在Atlas 在强化学习训练中，数据生成推理阶段一直是性能优化的重中之重，在长序列场景下，推理阶段的耗时可占总体耗时的70%以上；在当前Qwen3-235B模型的2K推32K场景下，推理阶段耗时亦是如此。为攻克此难题，我们针对RL推理的框架调度、通信、负载均衡等多方面进行了深度优化，最终在Qwen3-235B的2K推32K场景，将推理吞吐提升至233 的切分配置中，模型权重共占用约7.09GB内存空间。 TPDPEP模型权重(GB)Embedding/LmHead(GB)QKV(GB)O(GB)MoE(GB)Gate(GB) ------------------ 4321287.090.581.651.473.300.09 2. 预留激活内存/KV Cache：预留激活内存由初始化阶段的实测决定；KV Cache 内存则在激活内存与模型权重之外，按照预设比例在剩余内存中分配。 在推理的预热阶段，框架使用一批预设数据执行模型，并记录模型推理时网络计算过程中分配的峰值激活内存，这一过程通常被称为profilingun。如下图所示，在profilingun结束之后： 1. 通过 torch
pu 的内存系列接口 mem\get\info/memory\stats，可以查询当前设备使用内存 used(1) ，当前 Torch 分配内存 current(2) ，其差值即为模型执行时非 torch 管理内存的数量 others(3) 。此值与Torch 峰值内存 peak(4) 叠加，可以获取网络执行过程中对 NPU 内存的最大占用量，其中包含了外部内存、模型权重内存以及 profilingun 中测量到的峰值激活内存。 2. vLLM 启动时会指定其最大使用的 NPU 内存量(5)，在除去前述的各内存占用项后，由 vLLM 申请，专用于存储 KVCache(6) 。 在 Prefill 阶段，系统使用初始 prompt 数据填充 KV Cache，本实践RL场景下输入序列通常较短，对 KV Cache 的内存需求并不突出。为提升效率，推理框架通常会将多个 prompt 拼接在一起，在一次 prefill 中完成多个序列 KV Cache 的填充。拼接后 prompt 的最大长度由参数 max
um atched	okens 控制。一方面，在 DP-Attention/EP-MoE 的模型部署下， MoE 层往往会因为专家负载不均衡而出现较大显存激活值挤占 KV Cache 内存空间，在显存受限场景下通常不能将 max
um atched	okens 设置过大，而本实践适配了Chunk-MoE的新特性有效降低了prefill阶段的峰值内存，因此配置了较大的max
um atched	okens，具体适配代码可参考 cann-recipes-train 。另一方面，由于RL step间可能产生的内存碎片，后续step中Prefill阶段的实际峰值内存往往会出现增长，因而KV Cache内存也需要在合理的范围内进行分配，为后续step的Prefill激活内存空间留出一定的裕度。基于以上考虑，本实践最终采取了max
um atched	okens=32768 和 gpu\memory\utilization=0.87 的参数配置，用于满足Prefill和Decode阶段各自的内存需求。 在 Decode 阶段，由于每次处理的序列长度为 1，且并发序列数 max
um\seq 通常比 max
um atched	okens 低一个数量级，因此产生的激活内存占用较低。这一阶段的主要矛盾在于，随着序列逐渐变长，对 KV Cache 的内存需求可能超出预分配上限。理论上，可根据 KV Cache 总大小反推出给定序列长度下可支持的最大序列数 max
um\seqs。以Qwen3-235B-A22B模型在TP4切分下的32K长序列场景为例：单个BS对应的KV Cache占用高达1.47GB，导致单卡BS上限仅在30\40量级，与离线推理场景下的大BS诉求相违背，示例如下图所示。 实际上，以上的单卡最大BS推算是过于保守的 —— 下方左图展示了DeepScalar数据集一次推理过程中256条回复的实际长度分布，可以发现仅有少数长尾样本会达到最大长度，大多数序列会在早期退出并释放 KVCache。若按最大序列长度严格限制 max
um\seqs，会导致推理初期吞吐量严重受损。 我们进一步尝试以样本平均推理序列长度（7K）估算合理的 max
um\seqs，发现结果（约为128）仍然保守。实际测试中，即使将 max
um\seqs 设置为256（已经达到预估值的2倍），在这一数据集中依然未触发 KVCache 的OOM。为探究其原因，我们采集了推理过程中各 DP 域内全部 256 个回复的长度，统计"各长度下剩余序列的数量"，并将其与"给定KVCache容量下序列长度-最大序列数量"的反比例曲线绘制在一起，如上方右图所示。可以看到，随着部分序列推理完成并释放 KVCache，剩余序列得以继续增长至最大长度，在任何一个时刻下，这一样本中的各蓝色曲线均处于红色反比例曲线下方，因而未触发KVCache内存不足的问题。尽管如此，上图也同时表明，在推理长度到达5K\10K时，KVCache内存已经相当紧张，正是因为当前样本中序列结束的速度足够快，系统才在初始高并发下持续运行而未触发OOM。可以预见，在极端情况下，即使按照样本最小序列长度来计算初始BS，只要推理过程中剩余序列数量贴合前述反比例函数下降，理论上依然有可能使用有限的KVCache完成推理。 因此，为优化长序列场景下的吞吐性能，我们对 Qwen3-235B 模型采用了 TP4 切分策略：在 Decode 访存 bound 的前提下，用更大的 TP 降低单卡权重占比，从而预留更多 KV cache 空间，同时缓解访存瓶颈（见 切分策略优化 ）；同时通过上述的内存分析，我们将max
um\seq设置为256，在不触发OOM前提下进一步充分利用内存，大幅提高推理吞吐。 2.2 计算与调度优化​ 本实践针对框架的计算和调度做了大量的优化，其中部分的通信及调度问题与 前序工作 的优化是通用的， 此处复用，具体实现参考 相关技术解析 。 1. 针对vLLM框架侧的调度优化：我们将其从Gloo后端的CPU侧通信修改为HCCL后端的NPU侧通信，显著降低通信延时，提升了整体的吞吐，具体参考 前序工作 的 “RL推理调度bound优化”。 2. 开启零冗余TP转EP通信优化，将MoE层内的StridedSlice和AllGather算子消除，具体参考 前序工作 的 “零冗余TP转EP通信优化”。 本节则着重介绍在长序列场景下实现的4个新优化点。 2.2.1 切分策略优化 现象分析 面对复杂的长序列推理场景，路由专家部分我们默认选择大EP的方案，即EP128的策略；但是对于TP切分策略的选择需要进一步分析。 我们采集了一份长序列下开启多档位编图的profiling数据，取其中一个Matmul计算来分析，如下表所示： 算子名称decodelengthshapeWall Duration -------- MatMul2k"256,2048;4096,2048"32us MatMul4k"256,2048;4096,2048"32us MatMul8k"128,2048;4096,2048"23us MatMul16k"32,2048;4096,2048"19us MatMul24k"4,2048;4096,2048"15us 发现随着较多的request推理结束，图的shape不断变小，Matmul计算量明显降低，但是耗时并没有随着计算量的减少等比例变化。 我们猜测长序列的长尾场景下，计算并没有bound，反而绝大部分耗时都在搬运权重，存在明显的访存bound。 优化方案 对于非MoE部分采用更大的TP切分策略，使得每张卡仅加载较小的权重，提高计算在整体耗时中的占比。 为了验证该方案的可行性，我们做了下表所示的实验： step推理模型切分GBS采样数910C卡数数据集序列长度多档位编图maxnumseqprompt lenresponse lengeneratesequence/s ------------------------ 1TP4DP32EP128641664deepscaler2K推32K开3276.363601369.4 1TP1DP128EP128641664deepscaler2K推32K开876.36330.61614.2 上述实验在推理输入数据保持不变的情况下，两种切分策略对应rank上的Matmul的计算量是完全一致的；但是从总耗时以及profiling上可以明显看到TP1切分的Matmul存在严重访存bound，单次执行耗时更久。 根据以上分析，我们采用TP4DP32的切分策略，整网性能更优。 优化效果 1. TP4DP32的切分策略，减少了权重搬移带来的访存开销，在访存Bound场景下，带来了比较明显的性能收益，结果如上表所示。 2. 当前使用TP4切分，模型在单卡上占用更少的权重，可以预留更多的KVCache空间。实际训练中，TP4配置下更不容易出现KVCache不够用导致的request换出的情况，推理更稳定。 2.2.2 图模式路径选择 现象分析 在RL推理场景下，如果PyTorch处于Eager模式，那么NPU在大部分时间里都会空闲，CPU侧算子调度开销会成为推理主要耗时。因此通常会使能图模式来减少CPU侧的调度开销，具体分析可以参考 前序工作 的TorchAir整图下沉章节。 目前在verl+vLLM的框架下存在5种可用的图模式路径，我们主要对比了其中两种图模式，并选择了更适合本实践场景的GE图模式。 两种图模式路径差异如下，左边路径为Full\decode\only ACLGraph，右边路径是TorchAir GE： Full\decode\only ACLGraph: 该图模式的主要方案是将整个模型的的前向计算函数封装为一个可运行对象，并捕获前向过程中所有NPU操作序列，当前该方案已经在最新的vLLM Ascend实现了Qwen3 235B模型的适配。 TorchAir GE图模式： TorchAir GE是TorchAir的max-autotune模式。TorchAir将torch.compile生成的FX graph转换为昇腾中间表示（IR，Intermediate Representation），即Ascend IR计算图，并通过GE（Graph Engine，图引擎）实现计算图的编译、优化和执行。同时为了使模型获得最优执行性能，GE提供了计算图优化、多流并行、内存复用、静态kernel和SuperKernel等技术手段。 方案选择 本实践在Qwen3 235B的长序列训练中的rollout阶段，对两种图模式做了性能对比分析： stepmodeGBS采样数910C卡数数据集序列长度多档位编图maxnumseqInferDPprompt lenresponse lengeneratesequence/s -------------------------- 1Fulldecodeonly ACLGraph5121664deepscaler2K推30K关643273.77089.66690 1TorchAir GE5121664deepscaler2K推30K关483273.77099.59123.3 1TorchAir GE5121664deepscaler2K推30K关643273.77069.58145 1TorchAir GE5121664deepscaler2K推30K关2563273.77130.36836.2 1TorchAir GE5121664deepscaler2K推30K开2563273.77110.84918.9 从结果中可以明显的看到以下结论： 1. 当两种图模式的max

um\seq并开启多档位编图，反而能获得最优的总体推理耗时（上表中1,5行的消融实验）。 此外，由于Full graph要求所有kernel输入地址固定为capture时地址，因此必须使用vLLM原生的sleep mode来保证地址不变更。然而sleep mode依赖关闭PyTorch的虚拟内存，但训练阶段若禁用该功能会引发很多内存碎片，极易引发OOM，同时会导致训练性能也比较差。当前torch
pu支持动态开启虚拟内存的功能尚在开发中，因此Full\decode\only ACLGraph还无法在大集群场景的RL训练中正常运行。 相对应的，如 前言 提到的 Seer论文 所述，实际部署中常因内存不足，无法一次完成所有prompt推理，就会处于我们消融实验1,2,3行所描述的场景，需要依赖continuous batching来调度所有的请求。针对此场景，该研究提出了一种有效策略来缓解continuous batching带来的长尾问题： 基于"同一 group 内不同输出长度高度相关"的实验结论，优先从每个group中选择一个prompt组成"探测响应"，来实时估计该组其余请求的长度；接着调度器根据预估长度，执行近似 Longest-First Scheduling，优先推理长文本，从而显著压缩长尾。这为内存受限场景下的长尾优化提供了一种新思路。 优化效果 综上所述，考虑到TorchAir GE在大Batchsize场景下的推理性能优势，且无需依赖sleep mode、可以开启Torch的虚拟内存，不影响训练性能，因此本实践最终选择基于TorchAir GE作为推理阶段的图模式方案。 2.2.3 FA算子负载均衡优化 现象分析 本次FA算子优化的核心目标是改善多核负载均衡。具体方案是将IFA算子（IncreFlashAttention）替换为FIA算子（FusedInferAttention），FIA算子当前支持更优的负载均衡逻辑。关于FIA算子的适配实现，请参考 开源仓库 。 负载均衡优化面临的关键问题如下： 分块：不同大小的负载具有不同的开销（权重），不能统一视为1。 分核：所有核数默认全部启动，没有考虑调度以及同步的开销，可能导致性能劣化。 本次优化主要从如下两个方面着手： 1. 确定最优核数： 增加核数可降低单核负载，缩短慢核计算时间。 过多核数会引入调度与同步开销，反而导致 FA 总耗时上升。 2. 优化块分配策略： 将块合理分配到每个核，确保各核上的总计算开销基本均衡。 本实践最终采用基于核数的循环模拟方案，具体实现流程如下： 1. 计算最优核数。 关键设计点1：Rebalance的条件检测方法与实现逻辑 为了实现精准的调度决策，系统设计了全局负载状态的同步机制。该机制通过HCCL在DP组间进行高效通信，每个Rank（计算单元）会周期性地向全局共享其调度器的核心状态信息。这些信息主要包括： 请求队列深度：正在运行（Running）和等待（Waiting）队列中的请求数量，直观反映了各节点的任务压力。 KVCache使用率：KVCacheManager的内存占用情况，是衡量长序列推理中显存资源是否紧张的关键指标。 通过汇总这些信息，每个Rank就都能够感知全局的负载视图，为是否启动Rebalance提供决策依据。 考虑到DP组间的状态同步会引入额外的通信开销（实验测定小于2毫秒），过于频繁的检测会影响整体推理效率。为了在"调度及时性"与"性能开销"之间取得平衡，我们引入了可配置的周期性检测机制。 基于Step的同步：利用大模型推理中各DP组间Step基本同步的特性，调度器对每个Rank的推理Step前进行是否需要做Rebalance同步的检查。 可配置的检测策略：用户可以通过配置文件设定全局状态感知的方式，如检测方式（伴随step计数检测、异步线程周期检测）、间隔步长（每1000个Step检测、每隔30s检测）。 这种设计将周期性检测带来的性能影响降至最低，实现了开销的有效控制。 关键设计点2：两阶段均衡调度策略 为了确保调度既高效又稳定，我们设计了一套两阶段的均衡调度算法。 阶段一 ：排队请求的跨DP组间及时调度 因为RL推理阶段，请求任务是提前分配到了各个DP组内，在DP组内存在排队任务的场景下，可能其他DP组已有空闲资源，因此阶段的核心目标是最大化资源利用率，优先解决"忙闲不均"的问题。 触发条件：当系统中部分DP组存在空闲推理容量，而其他DP组的Waiting队列中仍有积压任务时，触发此策略。 调度逻辑：调度器会将等待中的任务优先从高负载节点迁移至有空闲容量的节点，快速消化积压请求，提升系统的吞吐。 阶段二：运行时请求的负载均衡调度 此阶段的目标是通过降低KV Cache的内存占用（档位），获取更高的计算性能收益。 触发条件：仅当全局所有DP组的负载水平均满足"最大档位可下降"的条件时，才会触发此策略。 调度逻辑：该策略通过全局协同，确保所有节点都能从档位下降中获益。这种"全体一致"的原则，大幅减少了因局部优化而引发的频繁Rebalance，避免了不必要的KV Cache搬运开销，保证了调度的稳定性。 KV Cache的搬运是调度过程中开销最大的环节。为保证传输效率，算法在选择调度目标时遵循以下原则： 最小化点对点连接：优先选择能一次性完成多个任务交换的节点对，减少通信链路的建立开销。 避免"多对一"拥塞：精心设计任务分发路径，防止多个发送方同时向单个接收方传输数据，从而避免网络拥塞和接收端排队，保障数据传输的高效性。 关键设计点3：请求（Sequence）迁移方案 为确保所有节点对调度任务有一致的认知并协同执行，我们设计了以下流程： 1. 本地运算，全局共识：每个Worker（工作进程）根据全局状态信息，独立运行相同的均衡调度算法，得出一份初步的调度任务清单（例如，节点A需要向节点B发送2个任务）。 2. 任务详情同步：由于初始清单只包含任务数量，缺乏具体的请求状态信息，系统会通过一次HCCL的All2AllSingle通信，将需要迁移任务的具体信息（如请求ID、已推理输出的tokens等）在所有Worker间实现数据交换。 3. 角色判定与有序执行：每个Worker根据交换后的详细任务列表，判定自己是发送方还是接收方，并按照全局统一的顺序执行迁移操作，确保了整个调度过程的有序性和一致性。 针对正在运行（Running）的任务，其KV Cache也须随之迁移，不然搬迁后的rePrefill将带来较大的负向性能开销，在调度任务同步后，需要进行KV Cache迁移的Worker会建立一次独立的点对点Send/Recv通信来高效传输数据。接收方利用vLLM框架的请求与BlockTable管理机制，在本地NPU上精准地还原KV Cache的状态，确保任务可以无缝地在新的节点上继续推理。 关键设计点4：对外无感知的推理结果还原 为了使Rebalance过程对上层应用完全透明，系统在所有Worker完成推理后，会执行一次统一的All2All通信。通过这次通信，所有被迁移过的任务的最终推理结果，都会被准确地传回其原始的Rank。这样，从外部框架来看，请求的处理流程与未发生调度时完全一致，实现了真正的无感知调度。 Seer论文 中也提到了他们解决长序列场景下KV Cache不均衡的问题，是基于Mooncake技术，构建 DRAM/SSD 两级 KV Cache池，允许跨实例迁移请求 chunk 时无需 Prefill 重算，和我们的rollout rebalance实现了类似的功能。同时他们提出了一种Divided Rollout策略，将长序列的请求切分为多个子块，每块最多推理8K个token，推理完放回缓存池，再分配给其他实例，直到请求推理完毕；这是一种针对continuous batching场景非常有效推理加速方案，解决了OOM以及中途preempt请求的风险，未来对于Device侧内存不够的场景，使用该方案将会带来很大的收益；但是本实践通过分析推理侧的实际内存，配置了合适的max

MoE模型门控网络会将样本分配给适配专家，导致专家负载两极分化：极端场景下，头部20%"热专家"承担80%以上计算任务，队列长期饱和；尾部30%"冷专家"调用率常低于5%，多数时间闲置。且"冷热"身份会随数据批次切换动态转移，形成负载热点漂移。 计算节点：NPU利用率两极失衡 专家并行架构中，专家固定分配至NPU节点，"冷热分化"直接传导为节点负载不均：极端场景下，承载热专家的节点利用率长期超90%，易现NPU内存溢出；承载冷专家的节点利用率多低于30%，甚至不足10%。节点负载还会随专家"冷热"切换动态波动，静态调度无法适配。 优化方案 EPLB（Expert Parallelism Load Balancer，专家并行负载均衡器）最早是DeepSeek针对大规模混合专家（MoE）模型训练中"负载不均"核心痛点推出的动态负载均衡解决方案。其核心目标是通过智能调度策略与技术优化，消除专家模块及计算节点间的负载差异，最大化NPU资源利用率，突破MoE模型规模化训练的效率瓶颈。 1. 双模式负载均衡调度 EPLB提供分层与全局两种调度模式，适配不同训练场景： 分层负载均衡策略 当专家组数量可以被服务器节点数整除时，EPLB会采用分层负载均衡策略，充分利用 DeepSeek-V3 中的组限制路由（Group-Limited Expert Routing）的特性。 1. 将专家组均匀分配到各个节点，确保节点间的负载平衡。 2. 在每个节点内复制冗余专家。 3. 节点内将专家分配到不同的 NPU 上，确保 NPU 间的负载均衡。 全局负载均衡策略 在其他情况下（如解码阶段），EPLB会切换到全局负载均衡策略，忽略专家组的限制，直接在所有 NPU 上复制和分配专家。 适用于更大规模的专家并行场景。 灵活应对复杂的负载分布情况。 2. 实时负载估计与动态调整 依托历史计算数据（如任务耗时、调用频率）构建负载估计模型，通过移动平均值等算法实时输出各专家及节点的负载值。基于该估计结果，EPLB动态调整专家复制策略与分配方案，快速适配训练数据分布变化（如批次切换、领域迁移）导致的负载热点漂移。 优化效果 实验一 实验设置：基于Qwen3-30B加载真实权重，测试开启EPLB前后的推理耗时。 实验结果：开启EPLB并无性能提升。 所述，为了优化长尾阶段低batch场景下的推理吞吐，我们在attention侧选择了访存bound友好的TP4DP32EP128推理切分配置。基于这一切分方案，我们进一步选择了BS256+DataBalance的输入组织方式以实现较高的端到端推理吞吐。 现象分析 Roofline模型描述了理想情况下算子执行耗时受计算量和访存量的影响，如下图所示，固定访存量大小，设备计算吞吐会随计算强度的提升出现"先线性上升后趋于平稳"的变化趋势。 对于Matmul/GroupedMatmul等矩阵乘法算子，不难得到其计算强度恰巧为输入左矩阵bs维度的大小，在理论上可以通过提升bs的方式提升整网Matmul算子的计算吞吐；FIA算子由于每个bs维度拥有独立的KV Cache缓存，其计算强度不随bs增长而变化。另一方面，RL训练所依赖的离线推理场景仅关心一批给定数据的端到端完成耗时，不会受到在线推理场景中各类SLO（Service Level Objective，如TPOT等）条件的制约，因而无需关注bs提升导致的单token推理时延上升。基于这一思路，我们在Qwen3-235B-A22B网络中尝试逐步扩大推理batch size，在Deepscaler数据集中得到了如下的测试结果： GBS实际推理BS推理总耗时首DP完成时间首DP空闲时间首DP空闲时间占比 ------------ 2562402:27:1101:08:5301:16:1850.84% 2566401:22:3200:40:5700:41:3550.38% 25612801:18:1800:27:3200:50:4664.84% 可以看出： 1. 在bs提升的初期阶段(24-\>64)，首DP完成时间和推理总耗时都有较为明显的下降。 2. 随着bs进一步扩大(64-\>128)，首DP完成时间进一步降低，而推理总耗时仅降低了5%，几乎未变化。 第一阶段的现象契合了Roofline模型的分析，在算子的访存bound阶段提升计算强度，可以在相近时间内完成更多的数据批次的计算 —— 提示在离线推理场景下应选择最优的BS参数，充分利用硬件算力提升整体吞吐。而结合MoE大EP部署下各个DP锁步执行的特性，第二阶段的现象表明推理任务在不同DP间的数据生成长度存在较为显著的差别，致使部分卡在整个推理任务超过64%的时间里处于空闲 —— 提示在同步RL场景下应尝试缓解推理数据集负载不均的问题，避免推理阶段长尾问题导致的巨大算力浪费。 优化方案 在数据集负载均衡问题的处理上，verl默认将推理的prompt数据按照采样数n复制后作相邻排布，使得各DP域处理间处理的prompt输入完全不同。当倾向于生成长回复和倾向于生成短回复的prompt被分配至不同的DP域时，便会出现极其严重的负载不均现象。对此，我们通过DataBalance的方式，将prompt数据按照采样数n复制后作间隔排布，尽可能地将各prompt数据均匀分散到不同DP域中，一定程度上缓解了原本的数据不均衡现象。在训练阶段开始前，再将各个DP域生成的response数据按照原本的方式作重排，保证同一条prompt的不同采样结果依然彼此相邻。 相对应的，在前言提到的 Seer论文 中，他们也发现同一prompt的多个输出有强相关性，即一个组内的输出长度具有强相关性，如下图所示： 因此他们将一组prompt请求，进一步切成chunk，并将每一个chunk调度到最空闲的实例，从而解决部分推理实例的OOM以及长尾问题，达到实例间的均衡: 在prompt排布顺序经过调整后，BS128配置下的推理长尾情况出现了较大程度的改善，各个DP域负载更加均衡，实现了25%的端到端时延降低。 进一步地，在开启DataBalance缓解负载不均衡带来的长尾瓶颈后，为进一步扩大BS提升吞吐创造了更大的空间。将BS从128逐步提升至192和256的过程中，我们观察到端到端的推理性能实现了进一步的增长。 上下文并行（Context Parallelism，CP）通过将批次中的序列沿序列长度的维度进行切分，并将其分配至不同设备并行计算，从而有效解决了超长序列的训练问题。在模型训练中，为处理不同长度序列并防止内存溢出（OOM），通常会将多个序列打包成一个达到最大序列长度 max\packing	oken\size的序列，并配置足够的 context\parallel\size。 然而，该方法存在明显的效率缺陷：无论序列长短，所有序列均需经历相同的划分与通信过程。当短序列与长序列一同被打包并进行CP处理时，短序列本不需拆分的部分也被强制划分，引入不必要的通信开销，造成计算资源浪费与训练效率下降。在训练数据包含大量短序列时，该问题尤为突出。 优化方案 为了解决上述问题，我们采用了一种新的优化算法 —— 混合数据并行（HDP）。HDP算法将数据并行（DP）和上下文并行（CP）融合，统一进行调度。内置装箱算法将根据序列长度自动选择最优并行策略，动态调整 DP 和 CP 组，保证对长序列进行 CP 的同时，将短序列尽可能划分至 DP 组从而避免其进行不必要的通信计算。 1. HDP装箱分组算法设计 对于给定的micro atch，本算法根据各序列长度以及总rank数对序列进行分组，以图示batch2：\[seq0\length, seq1\length\] = \[24k, 8k\] ， cp\size = 4 的情况为例，最终的分组结果为：\[\[1, 2, 3\], \[4\]\]，seq0占用rank0ank2执行CP3，seq1单独占用rank3。具体算法流程如下： 对于给定的micro atch，首先根据序列长度及总rank数计算序列预计占用的rank数量。 根据每个序列占用rank数量来进行动态装箱，算法在初次遍历中会对各序列进行整体划分，并保留序列在装箱过程中溢出的部分及其对应的序列索引。 对于序列的溢出部分，算法将根据剩余rank数量进行轮转合并或均衡分组，得到最终的hdp\group。 另外，算法设定了上、下阈值来保证算法的鲁棒性。 2. 跨Rank序列拆分与聚合 为保障上下文并行（CP）的正确执行，序列在输入模型前与输出模型后需分别进行前处理与后处理。 前处理步骤： 获取当前卡在 batch\hdp\group 的hdp\group和对应索引。 根据索引从batch得到对应sequence，并按照hdp\group的size进行cp切分。 设置实际序列长度，用于 FA 的 TND 模式和 Ring Attention 的 q/k/v 索引。 后处理步骤： 通过多次 AllGather操作 收集得到所有卡的序列长度和输出数据。 将每张卡上的输出数据按前处理的逆过程进行还原。 3. 框架适配 为支持HDP，需对模型框架进行以下针对性修改： Positional Embedding：由于HDP对固定的cp\size进行了划分，在RoPE位置编码时，需将原有的CP通信范围调整为当前hdp group的组内CP通信范围。 Ring Attention：同样，在Ring attention计算中，需对参数 rank\cpank\cp\globalanks\cp\outeranks 等进行调整。 实验结果 Memory）：该技术无需修改RL训练目标与奖励函数，在RL场景下，由于模型还未完全收敛，尤其适用这种draft-model-free的投机策略；同时在长序列缓存场景下draft-model会具有更高的接受率，这将会极大的助力长序列场景下的RL的推理吞吐提升。在前言提到的 Seer论文 Cache分布到多个NPU，使得单个NPU能够处理比其显存容量大得多的序列，从而直接提升单BS的吞吐量；同时动态调整DP域大小，充分利用序列推理完成后空闲DP域的NPU，进一步均衡负载，提高推理吞吐。 2. 注意力机制的不断革新或将重塑长序列处理范式。 以线性注意力（Linear Attention）、状态空间模型（如Mamba2）、近似注意力为代表的新兴技术，有望从根本上解决二次复杂度问题。 以DeepSeek代表的DSA(token-based)/NSA（block-based）等稀疏注意力、以及滑动窗口注意力等优化方案，可在长序列的场景下，保持性能的同时大幅降低计算开销。 百万级别。在算法与系统的双重驱动下，持续构建基于昇腾的超长序列训练与推理下一代技术体系，仍面临诸多挑战。我们将持续跟踪前沿进展，为昇腾生态下的长序列RL训练贡献力量。

Qwen3-235B 32K Long-Sequence RL Training Optimization Practice This document systematically summarizes the optimization practice for Qwen3-235B 32K long-sequence reinforcement learning training based on the verl framework and the A3 cluster, and describes in detail several optimizations carried out for the issues unique to RL long-sequence scenarios, such as long-tail sequence load imbalance and NPU memory bottlenecks. Through the techniques described in this document, this practice successfully increased the system throughput from single digits to 122 TPS/card. In addition, this document also compares and analyzes the relevant optimization ideas in the recently released Seer long-sequence RL training system, revealing the consensus and differences in technical approaches. 1. Preface 1.1 Background Long-sequence processing capability is the key to making large language models practical. Taking the Qwen3-235B model, which has 32K context-length processing capability, as an example, it can effectively handle real-world tasks such as long-article parsing, complex multi-turn dialogues, and large-scale code writing, and demonstrates important application value in multiple fields including financial research report analysis, legal provision interpretation, and scientific literature comprehension. Therefore, how to efficiently process long-sequence data in training and inference has become a key factor affecting model deployment efficiency. In particular, in reinforcement learning scenarios, the model not only needs to perform complex chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning and reward training over extremely long contexts, but also faces challenges such as HBM memory consumption growing linearly with sequence length and load imbalance caused by long-tail sequence distribution, which undoubtedly places higher demands on the efficiency and stability of the training and inference system. To address the above problems, this practice builds on prior work , reuses the verl frontend, uses vLLM Ascend as the inference engine and MindSpeed as the training engine, and performs 32K long-sequence GRPO algorithm reinforcement learning training optimization for the Qwen3-235B model on a 64-card A3 cluster. This practice systematically improves long-sequence training throughput from multiple dimensions, including model sharding strategy, long-sequence load balancing, and compute and communication efficiency, ultimately achieving a system performance of 122 TPS/card. It is worth mentioning that the paper Seer: Online Context Learning for Fast Synchronous LLM Reinforcement Learning recently released by Moonshot AI & Tsinghua also proposes several optimization strategies for long-sequence reinforcement learning, which are highly consistent with the ideas of this practice. This document also provides a comparative analysis of some of those strategies. 1.2 Overview of the Optimization Practice This practice adapted and optimized the verl open-source code for the following key features: Training engine adaptation: the verl framework currently natively supports the MindSpeed training engine, but when moe\alltoall\overlap is enabled, an abnormal expert weight loading problem occurs. This practice fixed and adapted this problem. Inference engine optimization: the sleep mode in the inference process depends on the dynamic switching of torch
pu virtual memory. This practice currently uses the method of prior work to implement the loading and unloading of inference weights and kv\cache. Framework adaptation: referring to prior work , the verl framework was modified to implement old\log\prob-free computation in on-policy training algorithms such as GRPO. This practice carried out systematic optimization for the performance bottlenecks and memory usage in long-sequence inference and training. Key design point 1: Rebalance condition detection method and implementation logic To achieve precise scheduling decisions, the system designs a synchronization mechanism for the global load state. This mechanism performs efficient communication between DP groups through HCCL, and each Rank (compute unit) periodically shares the core state information of its scheduler with the global scope. This information mainly includes: Request queue depth: the number of requests in the running (Running) and waiting (Waiting) queues, which directly reflects the task pressure of each node. KVCache usage: the memory usage of the KVCacheManager, which is a key indicator for measuring whether the NPU memory resources are tight in long-sequence inference. By aggregating this information, each Rank can perceive the global load view, providing a decision basis for whether to start Rebalance. Considering that the state synchronization between DP groups introduces additional communication overhead (measured to be less than 2 ms in experiments), overly frequent detection will affect the overall inference efficiency. In order to strike a balance between "scheduling timeliness" and "performance overhead", we introduced a configurable periodic detection mechanism. Step-based synchronization: leveraging the feature that the Steps of different DP groups in large-model inference are basically synchronized, the scheduler checks before each Rank's inference Step whether Rebalance synchronization needs to be performed. Configurable detection strategy: users can set the manner of global state awareness through the configuration file, such as the detection method (step-count-based detection, asynchronous-thread periodic detection) and the interval step (detect every 1000 Steps, detect every 30s). This design minimizes the performance impact of periodic detection and achieves effective overhead control. Key design point 2: two-phase balanced scheduling strategy To ensure that scheduling is both efficient and stable, we designed a two-phase balanced scheduling algorithm. Phase 1: timely scheduling of queued requests across DP groups Since in the RL inference phase, request tasks are pre-allocated to each DP group, in scenarios where there are queued tasks within a DP group, other DP groups may already have idle resources. Therefore, the core goal of this phase is to maximize resource utilization and prioritize solving the "uneven busy/idle" problem. Trigger condition: this strategy is triggered when some DP groups in the system have idle inference capacity while the Waiting queues of other DP groups still have backlogged tasks. Scheduling logic: the scheduler migrates waiting tasks from high-load nodes to nodes with idle capacity first, quickly digesting backlogged requests and improving the system throughput. Phase 2: load balancing scheduling of runtime requests The goal of this phase is to obtain higher compute performance gains by reducing the KV Cache memory usage (tier). Trigger condition: this strategy is triggered only when the load levels of all DP groups globally satisfy the condition that "the maximum tier can be decreased". Scheduling logic: through global coordination, this strategy ensures that all nodes benefit from the tier decrease. This "all-consistent" principle greatly reduces frequent Rebalance caused by local optimization, avoids unnecessary KV Cache migration overhead, and ensures the stability of scheduling. KV Cache migration is the most expensive step in the scheduling process. To ensure transmission efficiency, the algorithm follows the following principles when selecting scheduling targets: Minimize point-to-point connections: preferentially select node pairs that can complete multiple task exchanges at once, reducing the communication link establishment overhead. Avoid "many-to-one" congestion: carefully design the task distribution paths to prevent multiple senders from transmitting data to a single receiver at the same time, thereby avoiding network congestion and receiver-side queuing and ensuring efficient data transmission. Key design point 3: request (Sequence) migration scheme To ensure that all nodes have a consistent understanding of the scheduling tasks and execute collaboratively, we designed the following flow: 1. Local computation, global consensus: each Worker (work process) independently runs the same balanced scheduling algorithm based on the global state information and produces a preliminary scheduling task list (for example, node A needs to send 2 tasks to node B). 2. Task detail synchronization: since the initial list only contains the number of tasks and lacks specific request state information, the system exchanges the specific information of the tasks to be migrated (such as request ID, tokens already inferred and output, etc.) among all Workers through one HCCL All2AllSingle communication. 3. Role determination and orderly execution: based on the exchanged detailed task list, each Worker determines whether it is a sender or a receiver and executes the migration operation in a globally uniform order, ensuring the orderliness and consistency of the entire scheduling process. For running (Running) tasks, their KV Cache must also be migrated accordingly; otherwise, the rePrefill after migration will bring significant negative performance overhead. After the scheduling tasks are synchronized, the Workers that need to migrate the KV Cache establish an independent point-to-point Send/Recv communication to transmit data efficiently. The receiver uses the vLLM framework's request and BlockTable management mechanism to precisely restore the KV Cache state on the local NPU, ensuring that the task can seamlessly continue inference on the new node. Key design point 4: externally transparent inference result restoration To make the Rebalance process completely transparent to the upper-layer application, the system performs a unified All2All communication after all Workers complete inference. Through this communication, the final inference results of all migrated tasks are accurately transmitted back to their original Ranks. In this way, from the perspective of the external framework, the request processing flow is exactly the same as when no scheduling occurs, achieving truly transparent scheduling. The Seer paper also mentions that its solution to the KV Cache imbalance problem in long-sequence scenarios is based on Mooncake technology, building a two-level DRAM/SSD KV Cache pool that allows request chunks to be migrated across instances without Prefill recomputation, achieving similar functionality to our rollout rebalance. At the same time, they proposed a Divided Rollout strategy that splits long-sequence requests into multiple sub-chunks, each chunk inferring at most 8K tokens; after inference, the chunks are put back into the cache pool and then allocated to other instances until the request inference is completed. This is a very effective inference acceleration solution for continuous batching scenarios, solving the risks of OOM and mid-process request preemption. In the future, for scenarios with insufficient Device-side memory, this solution will bring great benefits; however, this practice configures an appropriate max
um\seq by analyzing the actual memory on the inference side, does not trigger continuous batching, and is more effective at solving the long-tail problem. Moreover, the "hot/cold" identity dynamically shifts with data batch switching, forming load hotspot drift. Compute nodes: NPU utilization polarization imbalance In the expert parallel architecture, experts are statically assigned to NPU nodes, and the "hot/cold differentiation" is directly transmitted as node load imbalance: in extreme scenarios, the utilization of nodes hosting hot experts is above 90% for a long time, and NPU memory overflow is likely; the utilization of nodes hosting cold experts is mostly below 30%, or even below 10%. The node load also fluctuates dynamically with the "hot/cold" switching of experts, and static scheduling cannot adapt. Optimization Approach EPLB (Expert Parallelism Load Balancer) is a dynamic load balancing solution first introduced by DeepSeek for the core "load imbalance" pain point in large-scale Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model training. Its core goal is to eliminate the load differences between expert modules and compute nodes through intelligent scheduling strategies and technical optimizations, maximize NPU resource utilization, and break through the efficiency bottleneck of MoE model scaling training. 1. Dual-mode load balancing scheduling EPLB provides two scheduling modes, hierarchical and global, to adapt to different training scenarios: Hierarchical load balancing strategy When the number of expert groups is divisible by the number of server nodes, EPLB adopts the hierarchical load balancing strategy, fully leveraging the Group-Limited Expert Routing feature in DeepSeek-V3. 1. Evenly allocate the expert groups to each node to ensure load balance between nodes. 2. Replicate redundant experts within each node. 3. Allocate the experts to different NPUs within the node to ensure load balance among NPUs. Global load balancing strategy In other cases (such as the decode phase), EPLB switches to the global load balancing strategy, ignoring the expert group restrictions and directly replicating and allocating experts on all NPUs. Suitable for larger-scale expert parallel scenarios. Flexibly handle complex load distribution situations. 2. Real-time load estimation and dynamic adjustment Relying on historical compute data (such as task time and call frequency), a load estimation model is built, and algorithms such as moving average output the load value of each expert and node in real time. Based on the estimation result, EPLB dynamically adjusts the expert replication strategy and allocation scheme, quickly adapting to load hotspot drift caused by changes in training data distribution (such as batch switching and domain migration). The experiments show that when the load is not obviously unbalanced, EPLB cannot bring performance gains. 2.3.3 Input Data Reordering As described in Split Strategy Optimization , to optimize the inference throughput in the low-batch scenario of the long-tail stage, we chose the memory-access-bound-friendly TP4DP32EP128 inference sharding configuration on the attention side. Based on this sharding scheme, we further selected the BS256+DataBalance input organization method to achieve higher end-to-end inference throughput. Phenomenon Analysis The Roofline model describes how, in the ideal case, operator execution time is affected by the computation volume and the memory-access volume. As shown in the figure below, with the memory-access volume fixed, the device compute throughput shows a trend of "rising linearly first and then leveling off" as the compute intensity increases. Optimization Approach In handling the dataset load balancing problem, verl by default replicates the inference prompt data by the sampling count n and then arranges it adjacently, so that the prompt inputs processed by different DP domains are completely different. When prompts that tend to generate long responses and prompts that tend to generate short responses are assigned to different DP domains, extremely severe load imbalance occurs. To address this, we use the DataBalance method to replicate the prompt data by the sampling count n and then arrange it in an interleaved manner, distributing the prompt data as evenly as possible across different DP domains, alleviating the original data imbalance to a certain extent. Before the training phase begins, the response data generated by each DP domain is rearranged in the original manner to ensure that different sampling results of the same prompt remain adjacent to each other. Correspondingly, in the Seer paper mentioned in the preface, they also found that multiple outputs of the same prompt are strongly correlated, i.e., the output lengths within a group are strongly correlated, as shown in the figure below: Therefore, they further cut a group of prompt requests into chunks and schedule each chunk to the most idle instance, thereby solving the OOM and long-tail problems of some inference instances and achieving balance between instances: Compared with our solution, Seer needs to schedule requests between instances, while we only need to replicate the prompts by the sampling count n and arrange them in an interleaved manner before prompt distribution to achieve a similar effect. The implementation is very simple; although the current practice has only one instance and we achieve data balance between DP domains, it can also be very conveniently extended to multi-instance schemes across multiple clusters in the future.
